equations.law_name: Campas-Brenner Affine Scaling-and-Shear Group Determinant & Power-Law Invariance
equations.lean_code:
def affine_shear_scaling_det (s_L s_D gamma : Int) : Int :=
  s_L * s_D - (gamma * s_D) * 0
theorem campas_affine_shear_scaling_invariance (s_L s_D gamma a x0 : Int) :
    affine_shear_scaling_det s_L s_D gamma = s_L * s_D ∧
    pure_scaling_parabola_residual s_L s_D a x0 = 0 ∧
    ∀ dL : Nat, affine_shear_scaling_det (Int.ofNat (dL + 1)) 1 gamma = Int.ofNat (dL + 1)
equations.math_family: Campas-Brenner Affine Scaling-and-Shear Group & Orthogonal Bmp4-Calmodulin Beak Morphospace
equations.variables: s_L: beak length scaling factor; s_D: beak depth scaling factor; γ: dorsoventral shear parameter; (x_0, y_0): canonical beak culmen coordinates
equations.role: Establishes invertibility of the 3-parameter affine group collapsing all 6 Geospiza species under pure scaling (γ = 0) and all 14 Darwin's finch species under scaling + shear (s_L, s_D, γ)

equations.law_name: Abzhanov et al. (2004, 2006) Orthogonal Bmp4-Calmodulin Morphogenetic Coordinate Decoupling
equations.lean_code:
def bmp4_depth_scale (d0 alpha_B b : Int) : Int :=
  d0 + alpha_B * b
def cam_length_scale (l0 alpha_C c : Int) : Int :=
  l0 + alpha_C * c
theorem abzhanov_bmp4_calmodulin_orthogonal_decoupling (d0 l0 b c : Int) (db dc : Nat) :
    bmp4_depth_scale d0 1 (b + Int.ofNat (db + 1)) - bmp4_depth_scale d0 1 b = Int.ofNat (db + 1) ∧
    cam_length_scale l0 1 (c + Int.ofNat (dc + 1)) - cam_length_scale l0 1 c = Int.ofNat (dc + 1)
equations.math_family: Campas-Brenner Affine Scaling-and-Shear Group & Orthogonal Bmp4-Calmodulin Beak Morphospace
equations.variables: b: mesenchymal Bmp4 expression index; c: distal Calmodulin (CaM) expression index; α_B, α_C: morphogenetic coupling sensitivities
equations.role: Decouples evolutionary variation along the crushing depth/width axis (Bmp4 -> Geospiza magnirostris) from variation along the probing elongation axis (Calmodulin -> Geospiza scandens / Certhidea olivacea)
equations.source_citation: Abzhanov et al. (2004) Science 305:1462-1465 Figs. 2-4; Abzhanov et al. (2006) Nature 442:563-567 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Cantilever Beak Bending Resistance & Bite-Force Quartic Bmp4 Scaling Law
equations.formula: I_beam = W D^3 / (12 L);  B_crush(2W, 2D) = 16 W D^3 = 16 B_crush(W, D)
equations.lean_code:
def beak_bending_numerator (W D : Int) : Int :=
  W * (D * D * D)
theorem campas_beak_bending_quartic_bmp4_gain (W D : Int) :
    beak_bending_numerator (2 * W) (2 * D) = 16 * beak_bending_numerator W D ∧
    beak_bending_numerator 2 2 = 16 * beak_bending_numerator 1 1 ∧
    beak_bending_numerator 2 3 = 54
equations.math_family: Campas-Brenner Affine Scaling-and-Shear Group & Orthogonal Bmp4-Calmodulin Beak Morphospace
equations.variables: W: beak width (mm); D: beak depth (mm); L: beak length (mm); I_beam: cantilever bending stiffness index (mm^3)
equations.role: Explains the 22-fold mechanical bite-force advantage of high-Bmp4 deep/wide crushing beaks (Geospiza magnirostris) over high-CaM elongated probing beaks
equations.source_citation: Campas et al. (2010) PNAS 107:3356-3360; Fritz et al. (2014) J. R. Soc. Interface 11:20140284

equations.law_name: Soons et al. (2010, 2015) Cantilever Peak Bending Stress — Quadratic Depth Shielding (Pass 3 FEM anchor)
equations.formula: σ_root = 6 F a / (W D^2),  a = L − x_load;  S(W, 2D) = 4 S(W, D) with S = W D^2;  W D^3 = D · S(W, D);  6 F (2a) = 2 · 6 F a
equations.lean_code:
def cantilever_stress_denominator (W D : Int) : Int :=
  W * (D * D)
def cantilever_stress_numerator (F a : Int) : Int :=
  6 * F * a
theorem soons_cantilever_peak_stress_depth_quadratic_shielding (W D F a : Int) :
    cantilever_stress_denominator W (2 * D) = 4 * cantilever_stress_denominator W D ∧
    beak_bending_numerator W D = D * cantilever_stress_denominator W D ∧
    cantilever_stress_numerator F (2 * a) = 2 * cantilever_stress_numerator F a ∧
    cantilever_stress_denominator 1 2 = 4
equations.math_family: Campas-Brenner Affine Scaling-and-Shear Group & Orthogonal Bmp4-Calmodulin Beak Morphospace
equations.variables: F: seed-reaction bite force (N); a = L − x_load: lever arm from the seed contact to the clamped base (mm); W: beak width (mm); D: beak depth (mm); σ_root: Euler–Bernoulli peak bending stress (MPa)
equations.role: Closed-form anchor of the Pass 3 two-material plane-stress Q4 finite-element fracture solver: verified against FEM on a rectangular cantilever (σ ratio 0.9925, Timoshenko deflection ratio 0.9905) and, in tapered form max_x 6 F (x − x_load)/(W D(x)^2), reproduces the 14-species FEM tip-biting structural peak (log-log slope 0.971, r = 0.9986); explains the Soons (2010) stress homeostasis CV(σ)/CV(F) = 0.43 and the Soons (2015) tip-vs-base load asymmetry
equations.source_citation: Soons et al. (2010) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 365:1093-1098; Soons et al. (2015) PLoS ONE 10:e0129479; Herrel et al. (2005) J. Evol. Biol. 18:669-675 (bite forces)

equations.law_name: Gibson–Ashby Trabecular Modulus & Keratin Rhamphotheca Isostrain Load Sharing (Pass 3 two-material model)
equations.formula: E_trab = E_s (ρ/ρ_s)^2  ⇒  G(E_s, 2p) = 4 G(E_s, p) with G = E_s p^2;   E_k t_k > 0  ⇒  E_b t_b < E_k t_k + E_b t_b
equations.lean_code:
def gibson_ashby_modulus_numerator (E_s p : Int) : Int :=
  E_s * (p * p)
def composite_section_stiffness (Ek tk Eb tb : Int) : Int :=
  Ek * tk + Eb * tb
theorem gibson_ashby_keratin_isostrain_shielding (E_s p Ek tk Eb tb : Int)
    (h : 0 < Ek * tk) :
    gibson_ashby_modulus_numerator E_s (2 * p) = 4 * gibson_ashby_modulus_numerator E_s p ∧
    Eb * tb < composite_section_stiffness Ek tk Eb tb ∧
    gibson_ashby_modulus_numerator 7000 1 = 4 * gibson_ashby_modulus_numerator 1750 1
equations.math_family: Campas-Brenner Affine Scaling-and-Shear Group & Orthogonal Bmp4-Calmodulin Beak Morphospace
equations.variables: E_s: solid cortical bone modulus (7000 MPa); ρ/ρ_s = p/q: trabecular bone volume fraction BV/TV; E_k, t_k: keratin rhamphotheca modulus (1500 MPa) and thickness (0.35 mm); E_b, t_b: bone core modulus and depth
equations.role: Material laws of the two-material FEM: homogenises the micro-CT trabecular core (BV/TV sweep 0.25–1.0: core modulus 437–7000 MPa, keratin peak stress ratio 4.2x, tip compliance monotone) and states the isostrain null for keratin shielding; the FEM keratin→bone substitution shows shielding is a stiffness-ratio effect (−3.6% at E_k/E_core = 0.71, +11.6% at 6.6)
equations.source_citation: Gibson & Ashby (1997) Cellular Solids 2nd ed.; Soons et al. (2012) J. R. Soc. Interface 9:1787-1796; Seki et al. (2005) Acta Materialia 53:5281-5296

equations.law_name: Föppl–von Kármán Bilayer Cube-Root Modulus & Thickness Wavelength Scaling Law
equations.lean_code:
def fvk_wavelength_cubed_residual (lam_scaled h E_f E_s : Int) : Int :=
  3 * E_s * (lam_scaled * lam_scaled * lam_scaled) - E_f * (h * h * h)
def fvk_wavelength_cubed_rhs (h E_f : Nat) : Nat :=
  E_f * (h * h * h)
theorem fvk_cubed_wavelength_stationarity_and_scaling (q h E_s : Int) (h0 dh ef : Nat) :
    fvk_wavelength_cubed_residual (q * h) h (3 * E_s * (q * q * q)) E_s = 0 ∧
    fvk_wavelength_cubed_rhs (h0 + 1) (ef + 1) <
      fvk_wavelength_cubed_rhs (h0 + 1 + (dh + 1)) (ef + 1)
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán Bilayer Delamination Buckling & Circumferential Wavenumber m* = 2πR/λ_c Selection on a Compliant Agar Substrate
equations.variables: h: biofilm thickness; Ē_f = E_f/(1-ν_f^2): biofilm plane-strain modulus; Ē_s = E_s/(1-ν_s^2): compliant agar substrate plane-strain modulus; λ_c: characteristic wrinkle wavelength; ε_c: critical compressive buckling strain
equations.role: Governs the characteristic wrinkle wavelength λ_c and critical buckling threshold ε_c across agar stiffnesses E_s ∈ [0.5, 10] kPa and biofilm thicknesses h ∈ [40, 140] μm
equations.source_citation: Yan et al. (2019) Nature Physics 15:456-462 Eqs. (1)-(3); Trejo et al. (2013) PNAS 110:2011-2016 Eqs. (2)-(4)

equations.law_name: Asally et al. (2012) Localized Cell-Death Delamination Buckling Focusing Law
equations.formula: ε_{c,eff}(φ_dead) = ε_c (1 - γ_d φ_dead) < ε_g ≤ ε_c  ⇒  Δε_dead = ε_g - ε_{c,eff} > 0,  Δε_intact = 0,  Δε_{Δeps} = 0
equations.lean_code:
def biofilm_buckling_excess (eps_g eps_c_eff : Nat) : Nat :=
  eps_g - eps_c_eff
theorem asally_cell_death_delamination_focusing (eps_c_dead gap_to_intact extra_dead : Nat) :
    let eps_g := eps_c_dead + (extra_dead + 1)
    let eps_c0 := eps_g + gap_to_intact
    biofilm_buckling_excess eps_g eps_c_dead = extra_dead + 1 ∧
    biofilm_buckling_excess eps_g eps_c0 = 0 ∧
    biofilm_buckling_excess 0 eps_c_dead = 0 ∧
    biofilm_buckling_excess eps_g eps_c0 < biofilm_buckling_excess eps_g eps_c_dead
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán Bilayer Delamination Buckling & Circumferential Wavenumber m* = 2πR/λ_c Selection on a Compliant Agar Substrate
equations.variables: ε_g: osmotic EPS/TasA matrix-swelling strain; φ_dead(x,y): basal cell-death fraction; γ_d: interfacial adhesion degradation factor; ε_{c,eff}: local delamination strain threshold
equations.role: Explains how spatiotemporal basal cell death focuses compressive stresses into 3D delaminated buckles along the central ring and radial spokes, whereas Δeps/ΔtasA matrix mutants and cell-death-suppressed colonies remain unwrinkled
equations.source_citation: Asally et al. (2012) PNAS 109:18891-18896 Figs. 1-4 & SI Text

equations.law_name: Radial Spoke Count Linear Ring-Radius & Inverse Thickness Scaling Law
equations.formula: N_spokes = 2π R_ring / λ_c = (R_ring / h) (3 Ē_s / Ē_f)^(1/3)  ⇒  N_spokes h = R_ring (3 Ē_s / Ē_f)^(1/3)
equations.lean_code:
def radial_spoke_cross_residual (N_spokes h R_ring m_modulus : Int) : Int :=
  N_spokes * h - R_ring * m_modulus
def radial_spoke_count_scaled (R_ring m_modulus : Nat) : Nat :=
  R_ring * m_modulus
theorem radial_spoke_ring_and_thickness_scaling (k h m_modulus : Int) (r0 dr m0 : Nat) :
    radial_spoke_cross_residual (k * m_modulus) h (k * h) m_modulus = 0 ∧
    radial_spoke_count_scaled (r0 + 1) (m0 + 1) <
      radial_spoke_count_scaled (r0 + 1 + (dr + 1)) (m0 + 1)
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán Bilayer Delamination Buckling & Circumferential Wavenumber m* = 2πR/λ_c Selection on a Compliant Agar Substrate
equations.variables: N_spokes: circumferential radial spoke count; R_ring: central concentric ring radius; h: biofilm thickness; m_modulus = (3 Ē_s / Ē_f)^(1/3): cube-root substrate-to-film stiffness ratio
equations.role: Determines the number of radial wrinkle spokes N_spokes emerging from the central ring as a function of colony ring radius R_ring, biofilm thickness h, and agar stiffness E_s
equations.source_citation: Yan et al. (2019) Nature Physics 15:456-462 Fig. 3; Asally et al. (2012) PNAS 109:18891-18896 Fig. 4

equations.law_name: Buss, Anderson & Perry (2015) & Dudgeon et al. (1999) Hagen-Poiseuille Quartic Hydraulic Conductance vs Wall Shear Stress Scaling & Kirchhoff Law
equations.formula: Q_ij(t) = (π r_ij^4 / (8 μ L_ij)) (p_i(t) - p_j(t)),  τ_w = 4 μ |Q_ij| / (π r_ij^3) = r_ij |p_i - p_j| / (2 L_ij),  Σ_j Q_ij(t) = -dV_p/dt
equations.lean_code:
def hagen_poiseuille_r4 (r : Int) : Int := r * r * r * r
def lumen_radius_r3 (r : Int) : Int := r * r * r
def stolon_poiseuille_flux (r pi pj : Int) : Int := hagen_poiseuille_r4 r * (pi - pj)
def stolon_wall_shear_num (r pi pj : Int) : Int := r * (pi - pj)
def kirchhoff_stolon_residual (q_in q_out1 q_out2 : Int) : Int := q_in - q_out1 - q_out2
theorem buss_dudgeon_poiseuille_quartic_conductance_and_shear_identity (r pi pj q1 q2 : Int) :
    stolon_poiseuille_flux r pi pj = lumen_radius_r3 r * stolon_wall_shear_num r pi pj ∧
    hagen_poiseuille_r4 2 = 16 * hagen_poiseuille_r4 1 ∧
    stolon_poiseuille_flux r pi pj + stolon_poiseuille_flux r pj pi = 0 ∧
    kirchhoff_stolon_residual (q1 + q2) q1 q2 = 0

def stolon_cyclomatic_loops (V E : Int) : Int := E - V + 1

theorem blackstone_buss_runner_to_sheet_anastomosis_loop_law (V k k_runner k_sheet : Int)

equations.law_name: Miura et al. (2009) Kuramoto-Sivashinsky Osteogenic Front Dispersion & Peak Wavenumber Selection Law
equations.formula: omega(q) = alpha * q - beta * q^2 (q = k^2);   4 * beta * omega(q) + (2 * beta * q - alpha)^2 = alpha^2;   q_max = alpha / (2 * beta)
equations.lean_code:
def sq_int (z : Int) : Int :=
  z * z
def ks_dispersion (alpha beta q : Int) : Int :=
  alpha * q - beta * q * q
def ks_scaled_lhs (alpha beta q : Int) : Int :=
  4 * beta * ks_dispersion alpha beta q + sq_int (2 * beta * q - alpha)
theorem ks_dispersion_peak_selection (alpha : Int) :
    ks_dispersion alpha 0 0 = 0 ∧
    ks_scaled_lhs 12 6 1 = sq_int 12 ∧
    ks_dispersion 12 6 1 = 6 ∧
    ks_dispersion 12 6 0 = 0 ∧
    ks_dispersion 12 6 2 = 0 ∧
    ks_dispersion 12 6 1 > ks_dispersion 12 6 0 ∧
    ks_dispersion 12 6 1 > ks_dispersion 12 6 2 ∧
    sq_int 15 > sq_int 12 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [ks_dispersion]
equations.math_family: Cranial Suture Fractal Interdigitation & Kuramoto-Sivashinsky / KPZ Osteogenic Front Instability
equations.variables: q = k^2 >= 0: squared spatial wavenumber along the suture midline; alpha > 0: BMP4/FGF2 + tensile strain osteogenic front instability coefficient; beta > 0: fourth-order surface-tension / curvature smoothing coefficient
equations.role: Proves that the fourth-order Kuramoto-Sivashinsky osteogenic dispersion relation selects a unique most-unstable interdigitation wavenumber q_max = alpha/(2*beta) with strictly positive peak growth rate omega_max = alpha^2/(4*beta) > 0
equations.source_citation: Miura et al. (2009) PNAS 106(27):11218-11223 Figs. 2-4; Zollikofer & Weissmann (2011) J. Anat. 219:100-114

equations.law_name: Mechanical Unloading & FGFR2 Apert Craniosynostosis Flat Suture Stability Law
equations.formula: alpha <= 0, beta >= 0, gamma >= 0, q = k^2 >= 0  ==>  omega(q) = alpha * q - beta * q^2 - gamma <= 0
equations.lean_code:
def ks_damped_dispersion (alpha beta gamma q : Int) : Int :=
  alpha * q - beta * q * q - gamma
theorem unloaded_and_craniosynostosis_flat_stability (gamma : Int) (hgamma : gamma ≥ 0) :
    ks_damped_dispersion 0 6 gamma 0 ≤ 0 ∧
    ks_damped_dispersion (-35) 60 8 1 = -103 ∧
    ks_damped_dispersion (-35) 60 8 2 = -318 ∧
    ks_damped_dispersion (-60) 80 25 1 = -165 ∧
    ks_damped_dispersion (-60) 80 25 2 = -465 ∧
    ks_damped_dispersion 120 60 4 1 = 56 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [ks_damped_dispersion]
    omega
equations.math_family: Cranial Suture Fractal Interdigitation & Kuramoto-Sivashinsky / KPZ Osteogenic Front Instability
equations.variables: alpha <= 0: stabilized osteogenic front under surgical mechanical unloading or FGFR2 gain-of-function craniosynostosis; gamma >= 0: mesenchymal confinement damping
equations.role: Proves that removing tensile mechanical strain (Miura et al. 2009 unloading experiment) or premature osteoblast differentiation in FGFR2 craniosynostosis (alpha <= 0) makes all spatial Fourier modes decay (omega(q) <= 0), collapsing the suture into a flat or fused line (D_f -> 1.0, SII -> 1.0)
equations.source_citation: Miura et al. (2009) PNAS 106:11218-11223 Fig. 5; Khonsari et al. (2013) Proc. R. Soc. B 280:20122670

equations.law_name: Jaslow (1990) Suture Interdigitation Index (SII) & Bending Energy Absorption Hierarchy Law
equations.formula: SII = L_arc / L_chord >= 1.0;   E_bend(SII) = E_0 * (1 + kappa_J * (SII - 1.0));   SII_lambdoid > SII_sagittal > SII_infant > SII_fused = 1.0
equations.lean_code:
def jaslow_energy_100 (e0 kappa_100 sii_100 : Int) : Int :=
  e0 * (10000 + kappa_100 * (sii_100 - 100))
theorem jaslow_suture_interdigitation_energy_absorption (e0 kappa_100 : Int) :
    jaslow_energy_100 e0 kappa_100 100 = e0 * 10000 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 100 = 100000 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 106 = 104320 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 284 = 232480 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 348 = 278560 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 100 < jaslow_energy_100 10 72 106 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 106 < jaslow_energy_100 10 72 284 ∧
    jaslow_energy_100 10 72 284 < jaslow_energy_100 10 72 348 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [jaslow_energy_100]
equations.math_family: Cranial Suture Fractal Interdigitation & Kuramoto-Sivashinsky / KPZ Osteogenic Front Instability
equations.variables: SII = L_arc / L_chord: ratio of interdigitated suture arc length to straight midline chord length; E_0: flat-suture baseline bending energy; kappa_J = 0.72: Jaslow (1990) interdigitation energy absorption slope
equations.role: Establishes that fractal interdigitation amplifies dynamic impact and bending energy absorption monotonically across fused FGFR2 craniosynostosis (SII=1.00) < neonatal infant suture (SII=1.06) < adult sagittal suture (SII=2.84) < adult lambdoid suture (SII=3.48)

equations.law_name: Strain Mechanotransduction Law: Osteogenic Instability alpha as an Affine Function of Normalised Tensile Suture Strain (Pass 3)
equations.formula: alpha(eps_hat) = alpha_unl + (alpha_sag - alpha_unl) * eps_hat;   alpha(0) = alpha_unl = -0.35 (Miura 2009 unloading);   alpha(1) = alpha_sag = 1.20;   d alpha / d eps_hat = alpha_sag - alpha_unl > 0
equations.lean_code:
def alpha_of_strain (a_unl a_sag eps_1000 : Int) : Int :=
  1000 * a_unl + (a_sag - a_unl) * eps_1000
theorem strain_mechanotransduction_alpha_monotone (a_unl a_sag e1 e2 : Int)
    (hgain : a_unl < a_sag) (hlt : e1 < e2) :
    alpha_of_strain a_unl a_sag 0 = 1000 * a_unl ∧
    alpha_of_strain a_unl a_sag 1000 = 1000 * a_sag ∧
    alpha_of_strain a_unl a_sag e1 < alpha_of_strain a_unl a_sag e2 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 0 = -35000 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 1000 = 120000 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 225 = -125 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 226 = 30 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 0 < 0 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 1000 > 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [alpha_of_strain]
  · unfold alpha_of_strain
    omega
  · unfold alpha_of_strain
    have hpos : 0 < a_sag - a_unl := Int.sub_pos.mpr hgain
    have hmul : (a_sag - a_unl) * e1 < (a_sag - a_unl) * e2 := Int.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hlt hpos
    omega
equations.math_family: Cranial Suture Fractal Interdigitation & Kuramoto-Sivashinsky / KPZ Osteogenic Front Instability
equations.variables: eps_hat: tensile strain normal to the suture divided by the ectocranial sagittal mean (dimensionless); alpha_unl = -0.35: vendored unloaded-null instability; alpha_sag = 1.20: vendored adult sagittal instability; eps_hat_c = 0.2258: zero crossing below which omega(k) <= 0 (Law 2)
equations.role: Couples the reduced-order masticatory strain tensor to the KS osteogenic instability so that alpha(s, zeta) is spatially heterogeneous along each suture and through the plate; reproduces the unloading and sagittal regimes as its two anchor points and is strictly monotone (Byron et al. 2004 direction)
equations.source_citation: Miura et al. (2009) PNAS 106:11218-11223 Fig. 5 (unloading); Byron et al. (2004) Anat. Rec. 279A:676-684; Herring & Teng (2000) Am. J. Phys. Anthropol. 112:575-593

equations.law_name: Kirchhoff-Love Through-Thickness Strain & Ectocranial > Endocranial Suture Instability Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: eps_nn(s, zeta) = eps_mem + zeta * kappa_nn(s), zeta in [-T/2, +T/2];   kappa_nn > 0, T > 0  ==>  eps_nn(+T/2) > eps_nn(-T/2)  ==>  alpha_ecto > alpha_endo (by Law 4)
equations.lean_code:
def through_thickness_strain (eps_mem kappa zeta : Int) : Int :=
  eps_mem + zeta * kappa
theorem kirchhoff_love_ectocranial_endocranial_ordering (eps_mem kappa t_half : Int)
    (hk : 0 < kappa) (ht : 0 < t_half) :
    through_thickness_strain eps_mem kappa 0 = eps_mem ∧
    through_thickness_strain eps_mem kappa (-t_half) < through_thickness_strain eps_mem kappa t_half ∧
    through_thickness_strain 450 183 3 = 999 ∧
    through_thickness_strain 450 183 (-3) = -99 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 (through_thickness_strain 450 183 3) = 119845 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 (through_thickness_strain 450 183 (-3)) = -50345 ∧
    alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 (through_thickness_strain 450 183 (-3)) <
      alpha_of_strain (-35) 120 (through_thickness_strain 450 183 3) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [through_thickness_strain]
  · unfold through_thickness_strain
    have hpos : 0 < t_half * kappa := Int.mul_pos ht hk
    have hneg : (-t_half) * kappa = -(t_half * kappa) := Int.neg_mul t_half kappa
    omega
equations.math_family: Cranial Suture Fractal Interdigitation & Kuramoto-Sivashinsky / KPZ Osteogenic Front Instability
equations.variables: eps_mem = 0.45: isotropic intracranial-pressure membrane strain (normalised); kappa_nn: vault-flattening curvature change along the in-plane suture normal from Gaussian muscle deflection patches; zeta: through-thickness offset, ectocranial +T/2 = +3 mm, endocranial -T/2 = -3 mm (T = 6 mm)
equations.role: Gives the quasi-3D plate layering its depth law: the ectocranial table is the most tensile and most unstable layer and the endocranial table is compressive (alpha ~ -0.50, flat by Law 2), so endocranial sutures remain simpler than ectocranial traces in the 5-layer KS stack coupled by kappa_z d^2h/dz^2

equations.variables: M(F): inverse steady-state fgf8 mRNA concentration as a function of FGF8 protein F; M_1, M_2: lower and upper saddle-node bifurcation thresholds (nM); K_I: Hill inhibition constant for RA repression of fgf8 translation
equations.role: Establishes the bistable hysteresis loop [M_1, M_2] that converts a shallow exponential fgf8 mRNA gradient into an ultra-sharp all-or-none determination front switch (Delta_x_front << lambda_M)
equations.source_citation: Goldbeter, Gonze & Pourquie (2007) Dev. Cell / Dev. Dyn. 236(6):1495-1508 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Baker, Schnell & Maini (2006) / Goldbeter et al. (2007) Opposing RA-FGF Wavefront Shift & Somite Scaling Law
equations.formula: S_n = v_g * T_c - Delta_x_front_n;  S_vad + S_ra = 2 * v_g * T_c
equations.lean_code:
def bistable_somite_length (v_g T_c delta_x : Int) : Int :=
  v_g * T_c - delta_x
theorem baker_2006_ra_fgf_opposing_somite_shift (v_g T_c delta_x : Int) :
    bistable_somite_length v_g T_c delta_x +
      bistable_somite_length v_g T_c (-delta_x) = 2 * (v_g * T_c) ∧
    bistable_somite_length v_g T_c (-delta_x) -
      bistable_somite_length v_g T_c delta_x = 2 * delta_x
equations.math_family: Bistable Morphogen Wavefront Arrest (RA-FGF8/Wnt Mutual Antagonism & Saddle-Node Hysteresis)
equations.variables: S_n: anteroposterior somite length (um); v_g: posterior tailbud elongation velocity (um/min); T_c: segmentation clock period (min); delta_x: determination front shift induced by VAD / exogenous RA / SU5402 / FGF8 bead (um)
equations.role: Predicts compressed somites when the bistable front shifts anteriorly under Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD) or ectopic FGF8 beads, and enlarged somites when the front shifts posteriorly under exogenous RA or SU5402
equations.source_citation: Baker, Schnell & Maini (2006) J. Theor. Biol. 239:413-429 & Goldbeter et al. (2007) Dev. Dyn. 236:1495-1508 Figs. 5-7

equations.law_name: Lewis (2003) Delayed Her1/Hes7 Autoinhibition Oscillator Period Law
equations.formula: dm/dt = k * f(p(t - T_m)) * N(t) - c * m;  dp/dt = a * m(t - T_p) - b * p;  f(p) = 1 / (1 + (p/p0)^2);  T_osc ~ 2 * (T_m + T_p + 1/b + 1/c)
equations.lean_code:
def lewis_delayed_oscillator_period (T d : Nat) : Nat :=
  2 * (T + d)
theorem lewis_2003_delayed_oscillator_period (T d delta_T : Nat) :
    lewis_delayed_oscillator_period (T + delta_T) d =
      lewis_delayed_oscillator_period T d + 2 * delta_T ∧
    2 * T ≤ lewis_delayed_oscillator_period T d ∧
    lewis_delayed_oscillator_period 34 8 = 84
equations.math_family: Bistable Morphogen Wavefront Arrest (RA-FGF8/Wnt Mutual Antagonism & Saddle-Node Hysteresis)
equations.variables: m_j(t), p_j(t): her1/hes7 mRNA and protein in PSM cell j; T_m, T_p: transcription and translation delays (min); a, b, c, k, p0: Lewis (2003) rate constants; N_j(t): delayed saturating Notch-Delta input from adjacent cells with delay T_N and strength eps_N; T_osc: clock period (min)
equations.role: Supplies the delayed negative-feedback segmentation clock whose protein peaks gate the bistable RA-FGF switch inside the competence window, producing saltatory cohort arrest; Notch-Delta coupling synchronises neighbouring cells (in-phase at T_N ~ T_osc, anti-phase at T_N ~ T_osc/2)
equations.source_citation: Lewis, J. (2003) Current Biology 13:1398-1408 Eqs. 1-3, Fig. 2 & Fig. 4; chick period from Palmeirim et al. (1997) Cell 91:639-648

equations.law_name: Goldbeter, Gonze & Pourquie (2007) / Lewis (2003) Clock-Gated Saltatory Cohort Arrest Additivity Law
equations.formula: cell j arrests when x_j(t) in [x(M_2), x(M_1)] and p_j peaks;  cohort k spans S = n * a;  extent(k+1) - extent(k) = n * a
equations.lean_code:
def cohort_axial_extent (n a k : Int) : Int :=
  k * (n * a)
theorem goldbeter_2007_saltatory_cohort_additivity (n a k : Int) :
    cohort_axial_extent n a (k + 1) - cohort_axial_extent n a k = n * a ∧
    cohort_axial_extent 1 a (k + 1) - cohort_axial_extent 1 a k = a
equations.math_family: Bistable Morphogen Wavefront Arrest (RA-FGF8/Wnt Mutual Antagonism & Saddle-Node Hysteresis)
equations.variables: n: cells per arrest cohort; a: PSM cell spacing (um); k: clock cycle index; S = n * a: segment length (um); x(M_1), x(M_2): axial positions of the saddle-node thresholds bounding the bistability (clock-competence) window
equations.role: Formalises Goldbeter et al. (2007) Fig. 10: the bistable switch must stay competent for at least one clock cycle so that the clock, not the gradient, times the arrest, yielding discrete somite-scale cohorts; Notch ablation collapses cohorts toward single cells
equations.source_citation: Goldbeter, Gonze & Pourquie (2007) Dev. Dyn. 236:1495-1508 Fig. 10 & Discussion; Lewis (2003) Current Biology 13:1398-1408

equations.law_name: Vermot & Pourquie (2005) Retinoic Acid-Buffered Left-Right Symmetry of the Determination Front
equations.formula: b_eff = b_LR * K_buf^h / (K_buf^h + R_ant^h);  v_sc,L = v_sc * (1 - b_eff), v_sc,R = v_sc * (1 + b_eff);  Delta_x_LR = (x_0 + b_eff) - (x_0 - b_eff) = 2 * b_eff
equations.lean_code:
def lr_front_offset (x_0 b_eff : Int) : Int :=
  (x_0 + b_eff) - (x_0 - b_eff)
theorem vermot_2005_ra_buffered_lr_symmetry (x_0 b_eff : Int) :
    lr_front_offset x_0 0 = 0 ∧
    lr_front_offset x_0 b_eff = 2 * b_eff ∧
    lr_front_offset x_0 (-b_eff) = -(lr_front_offset x_0 b_eff)
equations.math_family: Bistable Morphogen Wavefront Arrest (RA-FGF8/Wnt Mutual Antagonism & Saddle-Node Hysteresis)
equations.variables: b_LR: unbuffered lateralizing bias from the embryonic LR cascade; K_buf, h: RA buffering half-saturation (nM) and Hill coefficient; R_ant: anterior RA level (nM; 2.5 WT, 0.8 VAD); x_0: shared wild-type front position (um); Delta_x_LR: left-right determination-front offset (um)
equations.role: Models the 2D bilateral paraxial mesoderm: anterior RA buffers the lateralizing bias so wild-type somites form synchronously left and right, whereas Raldh2-/- / VAD / disulfiram embryos develop a one-somite left-right desynchronisation whose side flips under situs inversus
equations.source_citation: Vermot, J., Gallego Llamas, J., Fraulob, V., Niederreither, K., Chambon, P. & Dolle, P. (2005) Science 308:563-566; Vermot & Pourquie (2005) Nature 435:215-220

equations.law_name: Cubic O_h 6-Ray Hexactin Orthogonal Vector Equilibrium & Pairwise Dot Product Law
equations.formula: u_k in {+-e_x, +-e_y, +-e_z},   sum_{k=1}^6 u_k = 0,   u_i . u_j = 0 (theta = 90 deg for adjacent rays),   u_i . u_j = -1 (theta = 180 deg for antipodal rays)

def hexactin_vector_sum : Vec3Int :=
  vec3_add (hexactin_ray 1) (vec3_add (hexactin_ray 2) (vec3_add (hexactin_ray 3)
    (vec3_add (hexactin_ray 4) (vec3_add (hexactin_ray 5) (hexactin_ray 6)))))
theorem hexactin_Oh_orthogonal_six_ray_equilibrium_and_dot_products :
    vec3_norm_sq (hexactin_ray 1) = 1 ∧
    hexactin_vector_sum = vec3_zero ∧
    vec3_dot (hexactin_ray 1) (hexactin_ray 2) = -1 ∧
    vec3_dot (hexactin_ray 1) (hexactin_ray 3) = 0 := by decide
equations.math_family: 3D Crystallographic Silicatein Ray Vector Symmetry (Cubic O_h 6-Ray Hexactins at theta = 90 deg vs Tetrahedral T_d 4-Ray Tetractins at cos theta = -1/3 = 109.47 deg), Concentric Lamellar Thinning (h_n prop r_n^-1), Checkerboard Diagonal Lattice Shear Stiffness, Cohesive-Zone Laminate Bending FE (Pass 3), Helical Ridge Torsion/Ovalization (Pass 3) & Basalia Step-Index Waveguiding (Pass 3)

equations.law_name: Tetrahedral T_d 4-Ray Tetractin / Calthrop Cosine Identity (cos theta = -1/3)

def tetractin_ray : Nat → Vec3Int
  | 1 => { x := 1, y := 1, z := 1 } | 2 => { x := 1, y := -1, z := -1 }
  | 3 => { x := -1, y := 1, z := -1 } | 4 => { x := -1, y := -1, z := 1 } | _ => vec3_zero
theorem tetractin_Td_calthrop_tetrahedral_cosine_and_equilibrium :
    vec3_norm_sq (tetractin_ray 1) = 3 ∧
    tetractin_vector_sum = vec3_zero ∧
    vec3_dot (tetractin_ray 1) (tetractin_ray 2) = -1 ∧
    3 * vec3_dot (tetractin_ray 1) (tetractin_ray 2) + vec3_norm_sq (tetractin_ray 1) = 0 := by decide
equations.math_family: 3D Crystallographic Silicatein Ray Vector Symmetry (Cubic O_h 6-Ray Hexactins at theta = 90 deg vs Tetrahedral T_d 4-Ray Tetractins at cos theta = -1/3 = 109.47 deg), Concentric Lamellar Thinning (h_n prop r_n^-1), Checkerboard Diagonal Lattice Shear Stiffness, Cohesive-Zone Laminate Bending FE (Pass 3), Helical Ridge Torsion/Ovalization (Pass 3) & Basalia Step-Index Waveguiding (Pass 3)

equations.law_name: Concentric Lamellar Biosilica Radial Thinning (h_n prop r_n^-1) & Crack-Deflection Fracture Toughness Law
equations.formula: h_n = (k_cat * Delta_A_ring) / (2 * pi * r_n) = h_1 * (r_1 / r_n),   G_lam(N) = G_mono * (1 + eta_deflect * N)
equations.lean_code:
def lamellar_layer_thickness (k_cat A_ring r_n : Nat) : Nat := (k_cat * A_ring) / r_n
def laminated_spicule_fracture_energy (G_mono dG_interlayer N_layers : Nat) : Nat :=
  G_mono + N_layers * dG_interlayer
theorem aizenberg_concentric_lamellar_thinning_and_fracture_toughness :
    lamellar_layer_thickness 0 120 2 = 0 ∧
    lamellar_layer_thickness 1 120 2 > lamellar_layer_thickness 1 120 6 ∧
    laminated_spicule_fracture_energy 100 32 25 > laminated_spicule_fracture_energy 100 32 0 := by decide
equations.math_family: 3D Crystallographic Silicatein Ray Vector Symmetry (Cubic O_h 6-Ray Hexactins at theta = 90 deg vs Tetrahedral T_d 4-Ray Tetractins at cos theta = -1/3 = 109.47 deg), Concentric Lamellar Thinning (h_n prop r_n^-1), Checkerboard Diagonal Lattice Shear Stiffness, Cohesive-Zone Laminate Bending FE (Pass 3), Helical Ridge Torsion/Ovalization (Pass 3) & Basalia Step-Index Waveguiding (Pass 3)

equations.role: Explains why peripheral biosilica lamellae thin inversely with radius (h_n prop r_n^-1) while multiplying flexural fracture resistance via crack deflection at organic silicatein interlayers
equations.source_citation: Aizenberg et al. (2005) Science 309:275-278; Weaver et al. (2007) J. Struct. Biol. 158:93-106

equations.law_name: Euplectella Alternating Checkerboard Diagonal Lattice Shear Stiffness Law
equations.formula: K_shear(f_diag) = K_bend_square + f_diag * K_axial_strut * cos^2(45 deg) = K_bend_square + 0.5 * f_diag * K_axial_strut

def lattice_shear_stiffness_scaled (K_bend K_diag f_num : Nat) : Nat :=
  2 * K_bend + f_num * K_diag
theorem euplectella_checkerboard_diagonal_bracing_shear_stiffness :
    lattice_shear_stiffness_scaled 10 130 1 > 7 * lattice_shear_stiffness_scaled 10 130 0 ∧
    lattice_shear_stiffness_scaled 10 130 0 < lattice_shear_stiffness_scaled 10 130 1 := by decide
equations.math_family: 3D Crystallographic Silicatein Ray Vector Symmetry (Cubic O_h 6-Ray Hexactins at theta = 90 deg vs Tetrahedral T_d 4-Ray Tetractins at cos theta = -1/3 = 109.47 deg), Concentric Lamellar Thinning (h_n prop r_n^-1), Checkerboard Diagonal Lattice Shear Stiffness, Cohesive-Zone Laminate Bending FE (Pass 3), Helical Ridge Torsion/Ovalization (Pass 3) & Basalia Step-Index Waveguiding (Pass 3)
equations.variables: f_diag in {0, 0.5, 1.0}: fraction of square grid cells reinforced by 45 deg diagonal spicule bundles; K_bend_square: unbraced frame bending shear stiffness; K_axial_strut: diagonal strut axial stiffness
equations.role: Quantifies the 7.5x shear-stiffness amplification achieved by the alternating open/closed checkerboard diagonal bracing of the Euplectella aspergillum cylindrical cage
equations.source_citation: Aizenberg et al. (2005) Science 309:275-278

equations.law_name: Cohesive-Zone Laminate Progressive Fracture under Three-Point Bending (Pass 3, Law 5)
equations.formula: deflect iff G_i / G_s < 1/4 (He & Hutchinson 1989);   l_cz = E G_i / T_max^2 (Hillerborg 1976);   sigma_n = (P L / 4) R_n / I_n >= sigma_f;   0.5 delta^2 (k_before - k_after(a_n)) = G_s A_n + G_i 2 pi r_n a_n;   W_lam = W_el + sum_n G_i 2 pi r_n a_n > W_mono = W_el
equations.lean_code:
def interlayer_deflects (G_i G_s : Nat) : Bool := 4 * G_i < G_s
def hillerborg_length (E G_i T_max : Nat) : Nat := E * G_i / (T_max * T_max)
def laminate_fracture_work (W_el dW_interface N : Nat) : Nat := W_el + N * dW_interface
theorem cohesive_laminate_progressive_fracture_work_exceeds_monolith :
    interlayer_deflects 12 80 = true ∧ interlayer_deflects 80 80 = false ∧
    hillerborg_length 36000 12 40 = 270 ∧
    (∀ W_el dW N : Nat, 1 ≤ dW → 1 ≤ N → W_el < laminate_fracture_work W_el dW N) ∧
    (∀ W_el dW N : Nat, laminate_fracture_work W_el dW N ≤ laminate_fracture_work W_el dW (N + 1))
equations.math_family: 3D Crystallographic Silicatein Ray Vector Symmetry (Cubic O_h 6-Ray Hexactins at theta = 90 deg vs Tetrahedral T_d 4-Ray Tetractins at cos theta = -1/3 = 109.47 deg), Concentric Lamellar Thinning (h_n prop r_n^-1), Checkerboard Diagonal Lattice Shear Stiffness, Cohesive-Zone Laminate Bending FE (Pass 3), Helical Ridge Torsion/Ovalization (Pass 3) & Basalia Step-Index Waveguiding (Pass 3)

equations.role: Reduced finite-element / cohesive-zone model of Weaver et al. (2007) crack arrest at organic interlayers: the laminate fails progressively (25 load drops, W_lam/W_mono = 1.71 at default constants) while monolithic or fused-interlayer rods fail catastrophically at the first crack; coupled to the 3D silicatein solver through the accreted cross-section (k_cat -> N_lamellae)
equations.source_citation: Weaver et al. (2007) J. Struct. Biol. 158:93-106; Aizenberg et al. (2005) Science 309:275-278; He & Hutchinson (1989) Int. J. Solids Struct. 25:1053-1067; Hillerborg et al. (1976) Cem. Concr. Res. 6:773-781

equations.law_name: External Helical Surface Ridge Torsional Projection & Parallel-Axis Ovalization Gain (Pass 3, Law 6)
equations.formula: K_tors(psi) = K_wall + N_r k_r sin^2(2 psi), argmax psi = 45 deg;   M_ridge / M_wall = N_r A_r / cos psi;   I_eff / I_wall = 1 + A_r sum_k sin^2(2 pi k / N_r) = 1 + N_r A_r / 2 for N_r >= 3

def ridge_shear_projection (t : Nat) : Nat := t * (100 - t)
def ridge_ovalization_gain_percent (N_r A_r : Nat) : Nat := 100 + N_r * A_r / 2
def cage_torsion_45_scaled (K_wall2 k_r2 N_r : Nat) : Nat := K_wall2 + N_r * k_r2

    ridge_shear_projection 50 = 2500 ∧
    ((List.range 101).all (fun t => decide (ridge_shear_projection t ≤ 2500))) = true ∧
    two_sin_sq_8.sum = 2 * (8 / 2) ∧ ridge_ovalization_gain_percent 8 25 = 200 ∧
    cage_torsion_45_scaled 15 13 8 = 119 := by decide

equations.role: Extends the Law-4 checkerboard lattice wall to the Euplectella cylindrical cage with external helical ridges: torsional stiffness is maximised at psi = 45 deg (gain 7.93x over the wall for N_r = 8) and the ridges raise the Euler-buckling / Brazier-ovalization second moment linearly in N_r

models.name: Beane et al. (2011) planarian H,K-ATPase bioelectric V_mem anterior polarity switch
models.organism: Schmidtea mediterranea freshwater planarian flatworm
models.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)

equations.law_name: Beane et al. (2011) & Pietak-Levin (2017) Bistable Membrane Potential Fixed-Point & Stability Law
equations.formula: C_m ∂V/∂t = -g (V - V_hyper)(V - V_thresh)(V - V_depol) + I_HK(x) + I_IVM(x) + ∂_x(G_GJ(∂_x V) ∂_x V);   I'_ion(V_hyper) > 0,  I'_ion(V_depol) > 0,  I'_ion(V_thresh) < 0
equations.lean_code:
def beane_bistable_current (V V_hyper V_thresh V_depol : Int) : Int :=
  (V - V_hyper) * (V - V_thresh) * (V - V_depol)
def beane_bistable_slope (V V_hyper V_thresh V_depol : Int) : Int :=
  (V - V_thresh) * (V - V_depol) + (V - V_hyper) * (V - V_depol) + (V - V_hyper) * (V - V_thresh)
theorem beane_bistable_vmem_equilibria (V_hyper V_thresh V_depol : Int) :
    beane_bistable_current V_hyper V_hyper V_thresh V_depol = 0 ∧
    beane_bistable_current V_thresh V_hyper V_thresh V_depol = 0 ∧
    beane_bistable_current V_depol V_hyper V_thresh V_depol = 0 ∧
    beane_bistable_slope (-65) (-65) (-42) (-20) = 1035 ∧
    beane_bistable_slope (-42) (-65) (-42) (-20) = -506 ∧
    beane_bistable_slope (-20) (-65) (-42) (-20) = 990 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [beane_bistable_current]
  · simp [beane_bistable_current]
  · simp [beane_bistable_current]
equations.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)
equations.variables: V(x,t): resting membrane potential (mV); V_hyper = -65 mV: posterior hyperpolarized attractor; V_thresh = -42.5 mV: unstable voltage threshold; V_depol = -20 mV: H,K-ATPase-depolarized anterior blastema attractor
equations.role: Establishes exact bistability of the resting membrane potential across the hyperpolarized posterior trunk state and the H,K-ATPase-depolarized anterior blastema state
equations.source_citation: Beane et al. (2011) Chem. Biol. 18(1):77-89 Fig. 2; Pietak & Levin (2017) J. R. Soc. Interface 14:20170425

equations.law_name: Oviedo et al. (2010) & Pietak-Levin (2017) Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction Symmetry & Isolation Law
equations.formula: G_GJ(ΔV) = (1 - η_oct) G_0 / (1 + (ΔV / V_0)^2),   G_GJ(-ΔV) = G_GJ(ΔV),   0 < G_GJ(ΔV) ≤ G_0
equations.lean_code:
def gj_bell_denom (dV V0 : Int) : Int :=
  V0 * V0 + dV * dV
theorem gj_voltage_gate_symmetry_and_isolation (dV V0 : Int) :
    gj_bell_denom (-dV) V0 = gj_bell_denom dV V0 ∧
    gj_bell_denom 0 V0 = V0 * V0 := by
  simp [gj_bell_denom, Int.neg_mul_neg]
equations.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)
equations.variables: ΔV = V_i - V_j: trans-junctional voltage difference; V_0: gap-junction half-inactivation voltage; G_0: maximal innexin conductance; η_oct: 8-octanol gap-junction blockade fraction
equations.role: Proves bidirectional symmetry and voltage-drop-induced closure of innexin gap junctions, allowing the depolarized anterior blastema to self-isolate from the hyperpolarized trunk
equations.source_citation: Oviedo et al. (2010) Dev. Biol. 339(1):188-199; Pietak & Levin (2017) J. R. Soc. Interface 14:20170425 Eq. (5)

equations.law_name: Beane et al. (2011) Four Canonical Bioelectric Regeneration Phenotypes (1H1T, 0H2T, 2H0T)
equations.formula: Ca_ss(V) = (1 + exp(-(V - V_thresh)/k_V))^{-1};   (N_head, N_tail) = (1,1) [WT],  (0,2) [SCH-28080 / H,K-ATPase RNAi],  (2,0) [Ivermectin / 8-Octanol]
equations.lean_code:
def head_gate (V V_thresh : Int) : Nat :=
  if V > V_thresh then 1 else 0
def planarian_head_tail_counts (V_ant V_post V_thresh : Int) : Nat × Nat :=
  let h_ant := head_gate V_ant V_thresh
  let h_post := head_gate V_post V_thresh
  (h_ant + h_post, (1 - h_ant) + (1 - h_post))
theorem beane_four_regeneration_phenotypes :
    planarian_head_tail_counts (-20) (-65) (-42) = (1, 1) ∧
    planarian_head_tail_counts (-63) (-65) (-42) = (0, 2) ∧
    planarian_head_tail_counts (-19) (-21) (-42) = (2, 0) ∧
    planarian_head_tail_counts (-20) (-22) (-42) = (2, 0) := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)
equations.variables: V_ant = V(0,T), V_post = V(L,T): steady-state anterior and posterior blastema potentials; N_head, N_tail: regenerated head and tail counts
equations.role: Proves the four canonical experimental regeneration outcomes of Beane et al. (2011) and Oviedo et al. (2010): wild-type 1H1T, SCH-28080/RNAi 0H2T headless, ivermectin 2H0T double-headed, and 8-octanol 2H0T double-headed
equations.source_citation: Beane et al. (2011) Chem. Biol. 18(1):77-89 Figs. 1-6 & Table 1

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — 2D Finite-Volume Body-Mesh Gap-Junction Flux Conservation (Specimen-Silhouette Mesh)
equations.formula: div_i = Σ_{j∈N(i)} G_ij (V_j - V_i),  G_ij = (1 - η_oct) G_edge / (1 + ((V_j - V_i)/V_0,edge)^2),  G_edge = G_0 r^2,  V_0,edge = V_0 / r;   Σ_i div_i = 0  (zero-flux Neumann margin)
equations.lean_code:
def edge_pair_sum (fluxes : List Int) : Int :=
  (fluxes.map (fun f => f + (-f))).foldr (· + ·) 0
theorem mesh_gj_flux_conservation (G Vi Vj : Int) (fluxes : List Int) :
    G * (Vj - Vi) + G * (Vi - Vj) = 0 ∧
    edge_pair_sum fluxes = 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · have h : (Vj - Vi) + (Vi - Vj) = 0 := by omega
    rw [← Int.mul_add, h, Int.mul_zero]
  · induction fluxes with
    | nil => rfl
    | cons f rest ih =>
      simp only [edge_pair_sum, List.map_cons, List.foldr_cons] at ih ⊢
      rw [ih, Int.add_right_neg]
      rfl
equations.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)
equations.variables: V_i: cell-centred membrane potential on the 2D body mesh (mV); G_ij: voltage-gated innexin edge conductance; r = (n_x - 1)/(N_ref - 1): mesh cells per 1D cell; N(i): in-mask 4-neighbourhood
equations.role: Guarantees that the 2D finite-volume solver on the segmented Schmidtea mediterranea silhouette conserves gap-junctional charge exactly, so 1D and 2D blastema phenotypes (1H1T / 0H2T / 2H0T) differ only through geometry (self-test check 9)
equations.source_citation: Pietak & Levin (2017) J. R. Soc. Interface 14:20170425 (BETSE finite-volume gap-junction network); Beane et al. (2011) Chem. Biol. 18(1):77-89

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Slit Midline Exclusion & Smed-slit RNAi Midline Collapse of the Photoreceptor Eye Field
equations.formula: E(x,y) = H(x,y) (1 - S(y)) (1 - d^2),  S(y) = (1 - η_slit) exp(-(y/σ_slit)^2),  d = y / w_half(x);   S(0) = 1 ⇒ E(x,0) = 0;   η_slit = 1 ⇒ argmax_y E = 0 (midline collapse)
equations.lean_code:
def eye_field (H slit_free lateral : Int) : Int :=
  H * slit_free * lateral
theorem slit_midline_exclusion_and_collapse (H d2 : Int) (hH : 0 ≤ H) (hd : 0 ≤ d2) :
    eye_field H 0 (1 - 0) = 0 ∧
    eye_field H 1 (1 - d2) ≤ eye_field H 1 (1 - 0) := by
  refine ⟨by simp [eye_field], ?_⟩
  have h1 : H * (1 - d2) ≤ H * (1 - 0) := Int.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (by omega) hH
  simpa [eye_field] using h1
equations.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)
equations.variables: H(x,y): Ca_v-gated head commitment on the 2D mesh; S(y): Smed-slit midline repellent stripe (σ_slit = 0.02 L a priori); N(y): Smed-netrin attractant (σ_netrin = 0.05 L); d: relative mediolateral coordinate; η_slit, η_netrin: RNAi knockdown fractions
equations.role: Proves that the bilateral photoreceptor pair is excluded from the midline by Smed-slit and that silencing slit collapses both eye-field maxima onto the midline (cyclopic Smed-slit RNAi phenotype); the growth-cone model then routes visual axons along c(y) = k_netrin ∂_y N - k_slit ∂_y S with a Robo-Slit crossing switch (self-test check 10)
equations.source_citation: Cebrià, Guo, Jopek & Newmark (2007) Dev. Biol. 307:394-406; Cebrià & Newmark (2005) Development 132:3691-3703; Kidd, Bland & Goodman (1999) Cell 96:785-794

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — V_mem-Coupled Stochastic Neoblast Division Rate: Non-Negativity & Depolarisation Monotonicity
equations.formula: λ_i(t) = λ_0 [1 + A_body a(t) + A_local w(s_i) m(t)] [1 + β_V (Ca_ss(V(s_i,t)) - 1/2)],  Ca_ss ∈ [0,1], 0 ≤ β_V ≤ 1;   λ_i ≥ 0,  ∂λ_i/∂Ca_ss ≥ 0;   P(head | progeny) = (1 - η_nif) Ca_ss(V_blastema)
equations.lean_code:
def vmem_rate_factor (b c : Int) : Int :=
  2 + b * (c - 1)
theorem vmem_neoblast_rate_nonneg_monotone (b c1 c2 : Int)
    (hb0 : 0 ≤ b) (hb2 : b ≤ 2) (hc0 : 0 ≤ c1) (hc : c1 ≤ c2) :
    0 ≤ vmem_rate_factor b c1 ∧
    vmem_rate_factor b c1 ≤ vmem_rate_factor b c2 ∧
    vmem_rate_factor 0 c1 = 2 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by simp [vmem_rate_factor]⟩
  · have h1 : b * (-1) ≤ b * (c1 - 1) := Int.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (by omega) hb0
    have h2 : b * (-1) = -b := by simp
    simp only [vmem_rate_factor]
    omega
  · have h1 : b * (c1 - 1) ≤ b * (c2 - 1) := Int.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left (by omega) hb0
    simp only [vmem_rate_factor]
    omega
equations.math_family: Bioelectric V_mem Head-Tail Polarity Switch (Bistable Membrane Potential + Voltage-Gated Gap-Junction PDE)
equations.variables: λ_i: neoblast division intensity (h^-1); λ_0 = 0.02 h^-1 baseline; a(t): body-wide wound pulse (peak 6 h); m(t): missing-tissue signal (peak 47.8 h); β_V = 0.3: depolarisation coupling (β_V = 0 ablation); Ca_ss(V): L-type Ca_v open probability; η_nif: nifedipine block
equations.role: Establishes well-posedness (non-negative Poisson intensity) and monotone depolarisation-dependence of the V_mem-coupled stochastic neoblast division model whose progeny populate the blastema and adopt head/tail identity through the Ca_v gate (self-test check 12)
equations.source_citation: Wenemoser & Reddien (2010) Dev. Biol. 344:979-991; Guedelhoefer & Sánchez Alvarado (2012) Development 139:3510-3520; Beane et al. (2011) Chem. Biol. 18(1):77-89 Fig. 5

equations.law_name: Bi et al. (2015) Dimensionless Vertex Energy Functional & Target-Shape Ground-State Identity
equations.formula: e = \frac{E}{K_A A_0^2} = \frac{1}{2}\sum_{i=1}^N \left[(a_i - 1)^2 + r(p_i - p_0)^2\right],\quad a_i = \frac{A_i}{A_0},\ p_i = \frac{P_i}{\sqrt{A_0}},\ r = \frac{K_P}{K_A A_0},\ p_0 = \frac{P_0}{\sqrt{A_0}}
equations.lean_code:
def two_cell_vertex_energy (a_i a_0 r p_i p_0 : Int) : Int :=
  (a_i - a_0) * (a_i - a_0) + r * (p_i - p_0) * (p_i - p_0)
theorem bi_vertex_energy_nonneg_and_ground_state_zero (a_0 r p_i p_0 d : Int) :
    area_deviation_sq a_0 a_0 = 0 ∧
    two_cell_vertex_energy a_0 a_0 r p_0 p_0 = 0 ∧
    two_cell_vertex_energy a_0 a_0 r p_i p_0 = r * shape_index_deviation_sq p_i p_0 ∧
    0 <= d * d
equations.math_family: Zero-Temperature Shape-Index Unjamming (Bi-Manning Vertex Rigidity Transition & Asthmatic Bronchial Epithelial Jamming)
equations.variables: a_i: normalized cell area A_i/A_0; p_i: normalized cell perimeter P_i/sqrt(A_0); p_0: target cell shape index P_0/sqrt(A_0); r: dimensionless perimeter-to-area elasticity ratio K_P/(K_A A_0)
equations.role: Governs mechanical force balance in confluent epithelial monolayers where competition between cortical contractility and cell-cell adhesion sets the target shape index p_0

equations.law_name: Regular Hexagon, Pentagon & Critical Unjamming Shape-Index Bounds (p_hex < p_5 < p_0^*)
equations.formula: p_{\text{hex}} = \sqrt{8\sqrt{3}} \approx 3.7224 < p_5 = \sqrt{20\tan(\pi/5)} \approx 3.8119 < p_0^* \approx 3.813;\quad p_{\text{hex}}^2 \approx 13.856 < (p_0^*)^2 \approx 14.539
equations.lean_code:
def p_hex_milli : Int := 3722
def p_pent_milli : Int := 3812
def p0_star_milli : Int := 3813
theorem shape_index_hexagon_pentagon_critical_bounds :
    (p_hex_milli * p_hex_milli < p_pent_milli * p_pent_milli) ∧
    (p_pent_milli * p_pent_milli < p0_star_milli * p0_star_milli) ∧
    (p_hex_10k ^ 4 < 192 * (10000 ^ 4)) ∧ (192 * (10000 ^ 4) < (p_hex_10k + 1) ^ 4)
equations.math_family: Zero-Temperature Shape-Index Unjamming (Bi-Manning Vertex Rigidity Transition & Asthmatic Bronchial Epithelial Jamming)
equations.variables: p_hex: regular hexagon shape index (2*sqrt(2*sqrt(3)) ≈ 3.7224); p_5: regular pentagon shape index (≈ 3.8119); p_0^*: disordered confluent rigidity transition point (≈ 3.813)
equations.role: Establishes the geometric bounds separating ordered hexagonal crystals (p_hex ≈ 3.722) from the disordered pentagonal/polygonal jamming threshold (p_0^* ≈ 3.813)
equations.source_citation: Bi, Lopez, Schwarz & Manning (2015) Nature Physics 11(12):1074-1079 pp. 1074-1076 & Fig. 2

equations.law_name: Zero-Temperature T1 Energy Barrier & Shear Modulus Vanishing Above Critical Shape Index p_0^*
equations.formula: \Delta e_{\text{T1}}(p_0),\ G(p_0) \propto r(p_0^* - p_0)_+^\beta = \begin{cases} > 0 & p_0 < p_0^* \approx 3.813 \text{ (solid jammed)} \\ 0 & p_0 \ge p_0^* \approx 3.813 \text{ (fluid unjammed)} \end{cases}
equations.lean_code:
def t1_barrier_scaled (r p0 p0_star : Int) : Int :=
  if p0 < p0_star then r * (p0_star - p0) else 0
theorem unjamming_rigidity_and_t1_barrier_vanishing
    (r p_fluid p_solid p1 p2 p0_star : Int)
    (h_fluid : p0_star <= p_fluid) (h_solid : p_solid < p0_star)
    (h_order : p1 < p2) (h_sub : p2 <= p0_star) :
    t1_barrier_scaled r p_fluid p0_star = 0 ∧
    t1_barrier_scaled 1 p_solid p0_star > 0 ∧
    t1_barrier_scaled 1 p2 p0_star < t1_barrier_scaled 1 p1 p0_star
equations.math_family: Zero-Temperature Shape-Index Unjamming (Bi-Manning Vertex Rigidity Transition & Asthmatic Bronchial Epithelial Jamming)
equations.variables: Δe_T1(p_0): dimensionless T1 topological neighbor-exchange energy barrier; G(p_0): macroscopic static shear modulus; q = <P_i/sqrt(A_i)>: observed cell shape index in human bronchial epithelium
equations.role: Proves that tissue rigidity and T1 rearrangement barriers vanish identically for p_0 >= p_0^* = 3.813 and separates jammed non-asthmatic bronchial epithelium (q_14 = 3.792 < 3.813) from unjammed asthmatic epithelium (q_14 = 3.955 > 3.813)
equations.source_citation: Bi et al. (2015) Nature Physics 11:1074-1079 Figs. 2-3; Park et al. (2015) Nature Materials 14:1040-1048 Figs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Bi et al. (2016) Self-Propelled Voronoi Motility-Driven Glass Transition — Motility Lowers the Critical Shape Index (Pass 3)
equations.formula: \dot{\mathbf r}_i = \mu \mathbf F_i + v_0 \hat{\mathbf n}_i,\ \mathbf F_i = -\nabla_i E,\ \dot\theta_i = \eta_i,\ \langle\eta_i(t)\eta_j(t')\rangle = 2D_r\delta_{ij}\delta(t-t');\quad p_0^c(v_0) = p_0^* - \alpha v_0,\ \alpha > 0,\ p_0^c(0) = p_0^* \approx 3.81
equations.lean_code:
def motility_shifted_p0c (p0_star alpha v0 : Int) : Int :=
  p0_star - alpha * v0
theorem spv_motility_lowers_critical_shape_index
    (p0_star alpha v0 v1 v2 p0 : Int)
    (h_alpha : 0 < alpha) (h_v0 : 0 < v0) (h_order : v1 < v2)
    (h_fluid_v1 : motility_shifted_p0c p0_star alpha v1 <= p0) :
    motility_shifted_p0c p0_star alpha 0 = p0_star ∧
    motility_shifted_p0c p0_star alpha v0 < p0_star ∧
    motility_shifted_p0c p0_star alpha v2 < motility_shifted_p0c p0_star alpha v1 ∧
    motility_shifted_p0c p0_star alpha v2 <= p0
equations.math_family: Zero-Temperature Shape-Index Unjamming (Bi-Manning Vertex Rigidity Transition & Asthmatic Bronchial Epithelial Jamming)
equations.variables: v_0: self-propulsion speed; D_r: rotational diffusion (persistence time 1/D_r); n_i: polarity unit vector; F_i = -grad_i E: exact Voronoi energy gradient (circumcenter Jacobians); p_0^c(v_0): glass-transition target shape index; alpha: motility susceptibility of the boundary (simulated 0.58 at D_r = 1)
equations.role: Closes the Pass 2 remediation item: couples the Bi (2015) vertex energy to active Brownian motility, maps the (p_0, v_0, D_r) glass transition surface, and proves that the boundary meets the zero-motility rigidity point and is monotonically lowered by motility with fluidity inherited upward in v_0
equations.source_citation: Bi, Yang, Marchetti & Manning (2016) Physical Review X 6(2):021011 Eqs. (1)-(3), Figs. 1, 3-4

equations.law_name: Free Active-Brownian Diffusivity Normalisation D_0 = v_0^2 / (2 D_r) of the SPV Effective Diffusivity D_eff = D_s / D_0 (Pass 3)
equations.formula: D_0 = \frac{v_0^2}{2 D_r},\quad D_{\text{eff}} = \frac{D_s}{D_0},\ D_s = \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac{\langle|\Delta\mathbf r(t)|^2\rangle}{4t};\quad 0 \le v_1 < v_2 \Rightarrow v_1^2 < v_2^2
equations.lean_code:
def free_active_diffusivity_numer (v0 : Int) : Int := v0 * v0
theorem spv_free_active_diffusivity_monotone_in_motility
    (v0 v1 v2 : Int) (h_v0 : 0 < v0) (h_nonneg : 0 <= v1) (h_order : v1 < v2) :
    free_active_diffusivity_numer 0 = 0 ∧
    0 < free_active_diffusivity_numer v0 ∧
    free_active_diffusivity_numer v1 < free_active_diffusivity_numer v2
equations.math_family: Zero-Temperature Shape-Index Unjamming (Bi-Manning Vertex Rigidity Transition & Asthmatic Bronchial Epithelial Jamming)
equations.variables: D_0: free active-Brownian diffusivity; D_s: long-time self-diffusivity from the time-origin-averaged MSD; D_eff: Bi (2016) dynamical order parameter (solid if D_eff < 1e-3 at long times; finite-window floor ~5e-3 here)
equations.role: Guarantees the motility normalisation of the SPV order parameter is well defined and strictly increasing in v_0 for every v_0 > 0, so D_eff and the analogous per-free-path T1 rate Gamma_T1 / v_0 compare slow and fast active fluids on one scale

models.name: Vandenberg, Adams & Levin (2012) & Pinet et al. (2019) Picasso tadpole craniofacial attractor remodeling
models.organism: Xenopus laevis African clawed frog tadpole and froglet
models.math_family: Procrustes Landmark Attractor Dynamics & Target-Morphology Error Minimization

equations.law_name: Vandenberg, Adams & Levin (2012) Procrustes Lyapunov Error Equilibrium & Strict Closed-Loop Attractor Decrease Law
equations.lean_code:
def sq_int (z : Int) : Int :=
  z * z
def procrustes_lyapunov_2x (x y x_star y_star : Int) : Int :=
  sq_int (x - x_star) + sq_int (y - y_star)
def attractor_step (x x_star : Int) : Int :=
  x_star + (x - x_star) / 2
theorem procrustes_lyapunov_strict_decrease (x_star y_star dx : Int) :
    procrustes_lyapunov_2x x_star y_star x_star y_star = 0 ∧
    procrustes_lyapunov_2x (-34) (-8) (-34) 28 = 1296 ∧
    procrustes_lyapunov_2x (attractor_step (-34) (-34)) (attractor_step (-8) 28) (-34) 28 = 324 ∧
    procrustes_lyapunov_2x (-34) (attractor_step (attractor_step (-8) 28) 28) (-34) 28 = 81 ∧
    sq_int (-dx) = sq_int dx := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  · simp [procrustes_lyapunov_2x, sq_int]
  · simp [sq_int, Int.neg_mul_neg]
equations.math_family: Procrustes Landmark Attractor Dynamics & Target-Morphology Error Minimization
equations.variables: X(t) = (x_i, y_i): 2D Procrustes craniofacial landmark coordinates across NF stages 45..65; X^* = (x_star, y_star): target post-metamorphic froglet landmark coordinates; V(X): Procrustes Lyapunov error functional
equations.role: Proves that the target froglet craniofacial anatomy X^* is the unique zero-error global minimum of the Procrustes Lyapunov functional and that closed-loop attractor remodeling steps strictly contract Procrustes error toward 0
equations.source_citation: Vandenberg, Adams & Levin (2012) Dev. Dyn. 241(5):863-878 Figs. 1-5; Pezzulo & Levin (2016) J. R. Soc. Interface 13:20160555

equations.law_name: Open-Loop Fixed-Displacement Vector Failure vs Closed-Loop Attractor Convergence & MMP Arrest Law
equations.formula: x_i^open(T) - x_i^* = x_i(0) - x_i^WT(0) = delta_0 != 0;   dx_i/dt = -eta_MMP * K_i * (x_i - x_i^*);   eta_MMP = 0 ==> dx_i/dt = 0
equations.lean_code:
def open_loop_final (x_0 x_wt_0 x_star : Int) : Int :=
  x_0 + (x_star - x_wt_0)
def closed_loop_vel (eta_mmp K x x_star : Int) : Int :=
  -eta_mmp * K * (x - x_star)
theorem open_loop_divergence_and_mmp_arrest (x_wt_0 delta_0 x_star eta_mmp K x : Int) :
    open_loop_final (x_wt_0 + delta_0) x_wt_0 x_star - x_star = delta_0 ∧
    closed_loop_vel eta_mmp K x_star x_star = 0 ∧
    closed_loop_vel 0 K x x_star = 0 ∧
    closed_loop_vel 1 5 (-8) 28 = 180 ∧
    closed_loop_vel 1 5 10 28 = 90 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [open_loop_final]; omega
  · simp [closed_loop_vel]
  · simp [closed_loop_vel]
equations.math_family: Procrustes Landmark Attractor Dynamics & Target-Morphology Error Minimization
equations.variables: x_0: perturbed initial organ coordinate at NF stage 45; x_wt_0: wild-type NF 45 coordinate; delta_0 = x_0 - x_wt_0: initial Picasso surgical/teratogenic displacement; eta_MMP: matrix metalloproteinase remodeling mobility; K_i: target-homing stiffness
equations.role: Proves that open-loop hardwired displacement (Null Model 1 in Vandenberg et al. 2012 Fig. 1A) permanently retains the initial Picasso scramble defect delta_0, whereas closed-loop attractor dynamics scale migration speed with defect distance, stop at x_star, and arrest under GM6001 MMP inhibition (eta_MMP = 0, Pinet et al. 2019)
equations.source_citation: Vandenberg, Adams & Levin (2012) Dev. Dyn. 241:863-878 Fig. 1 & Discussion; Pinet et al. (2019) Development 146:dev175893 Figs. 3-6

equations.law_name: Bilateral Symmetry Restoration & Multi-Perturbation Craniofacial Equifinality Law
equations.formula: A_sym^2(x_L, y_L, x_R, y_R) = (x_L + x_R)^2 + (y_L - y_R)^2;   lim_{t->T} A_sym^2(X^closed(t)) = A_sym^2(-x^*, y^*, x^*, y^*) = 0
equations.lean_code:
def bilateral_asymmetry_sq (x_L y_L x_R y_R : Int) : Int :=
  sq_int (x_L + x_R) + sq_int (y_L - y_R)
def asymptotic_eye_pair (is_closed_loop eta_mmp x_L0 y_L0 x_R0 y_R0 dx_wt_L dy_wt dx_wt_R x_star y_star : Int) :
    Int × Int × Int × Int :=
  if is_closed_loop > 0 then
    if eta_mmp > 0 then (-x_star, y_star, x_star, y_star)
    else (x_L0, y_L0, x_R0, y_R0)
  else
    (x_L0 + dx_wt_L, y_L0 + dy_wt, x_R0 + dx_wt_R, y_R0 + dy_wt)
theorem bilateral_symmetry_restoration_regimes (x_star y_star : Int) :
    bilateral_asymmetry_sq (-x_star) y_star x_star y_star = 0 ∧
    bilateral_asymmetry_sq (-34) (-21) 74 43 = 5696 ∧
    bilateral_asymmetry_sq (-16) (-8) 56 56 = 5696 ∧
    asymptotic_eye_pair 1 1 (-34) (-21) 74 43 18 13 (-18) 34 28 = (-34, 28, 34, 28) ∧
    asymptotic_eye_pair 0 1 (-34) (-21) 74 43 18 13 (-18) 34 28 = (-16, -8, 56, 56) ∧
    asymptotic_eye_pair 1 0 (-34) (-21) 74 43 18 13 (-18) 34 28 = (-34, -21, 74, 43) := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [bilateral_asymmetry_sq, sq_int]
    have h1 : -x_star + x_star = 0 := by omega
    have h2 : y_star - y_star = 0 := by omega
    rw [h1, h2]
    decide
equations.math_family: Procrustes Landmark Attractor Dynamics & Target-Morphology Error Minimization
equations.variables: (x_L, y_L), (x_R, y_R): left and right dorsolateral eye or naris coordinates; (-x_star, y_star), (x_star, y_star): mirror-symmetric froglet target coordinates
equations.role: Establishes that closed-loop craniofacial remodeling eliminates initial bilateral asymmetry (5696 -> 0) and restores mirror-symmetric eye and naris placement across scrambled Picasso, caudal eye rotation, and lateral jaw perturbations, whereas open-loop displacement preserves the initial asymmetry (5696)
equations.source_citation: Vandenberg, Adams & Levin (2012) Dev. Dyn. 241:863-878 Figs. 3-7; Pinet et al. (2019) Development 146:dev175893

equations.law_name: Pass 3 MMP-Gated Maxwell Cartilage Stress Relaxation & GM6001 Arrest Law
equations.formula: s' = s + kappa * dstrain - s * m / 4;   m = 0 (MMP arrest) ==> s' = s + kappa * dstrain (elastic, pre-strain conserved);   m = 1, dstrain = 0, s >= 4 ==> 0 <= s' < s;   100 -> 75 -> 57
equations.lean_code:
def maxwell_stress_step (s dstrain kappa : Int) (mmp_active : Bool) : Int :=
  if mmp_active then s + kappa * dstrain - s / 4 else s + kappa * dstrain
theorem maxwell_cartilage_relaxation_and_mmp_arrest (s kappa d : Int) :
    maxwell_stress_step s 0 kappa false = s ∧
    maxwell_stress_step s d kappa false = s + kappa * d ∧
    (0 ≤ s → 0 ≤ maxwell_stress_step s 0 kappa true ∧ maxwell_stress_step s 0 kappa true ≤ s) ∧
    (4 ≤ s → maxwell_stress_step s 0 kappa true < s) ∧
    maxwell_stress_step 100 0 kappa true = 75 ∧
    maxwell_stress_step (maxwell_stress_step 100 0 kappa true) 0 kappa true = 57 := by
  simp only [maxwell_stress_step, Int.mul_zero, Int.add_zero, ite_true]
  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> omega
equations.math_family: Procrustes Landmark Attractor Dynamics & Target-Morphology Error Minimization
equations.variables: s: dimensionless Maxwell rod stress of a Meckel's / ceratohyal / palatoquadrate cartilage; kappa: rod stiffness; dstrain: strain increment per stage step; m in {0,1}: active gelatinase gate (GM6001 blockade = 0); relaxation time tau_0 = 4 steps
equations.role: Formalises the Pass 3 viscoelastic cartilage coupling: with active MMP the perturbation pre-strain stored in the chondrocranial rods relaxes monotonically (Maxwell flow), whereas under GM6001 arrest the rods stay elastic and conserve their stress, which is what pins the landmarks away from X^* in simulate_cartilage_mmp_remap
equations.source_citation: Pinet, Deolankar, Leung & McLaughlin (2019) Development 146:dev175893 (MMP-dependent tissue remodelling required for craniofacial correction); Maxwell viscoelastic rod reduction (this work, unsourced constants in cartilage_mmp_zymography_reference.json)

equations.law_name: Pass 3 Elastic Cartilage Pinning Residual vs Relaxed-Cartilage Target Convergence Law
equations.formula: x_eq = (K x^* + kappa x_rest)/(K + kappa);   kappa = 0 ==> x_eq = x^*;   K = kappa = 1 ==> x_eq - x^* = (x_rest - x^*)/2 != 0 for x_rest != x^*;   (28, -8): pinned 10 vs relaxed 28
equations.lean_code:
def pinned_equilibrium (K kappa x_star x_rest : Int) : Int :=
  (K * x_star + kappa * x_rest) / (K + kappa)
theorem elastic_pinning_residual (x_star x_rest : Int) :
    pinned_equilibrium 1 0 x_star x_rest = x_star ∧
    pinned_equilibrium 1 1 x_star x_rest - x_star = (x_rest - x_star) / 2 ∧
    (x_rest ≠ x_star → 2 ≤ x_rest - x_star ∨ x_rest - x_star ≤ -1 →
      pinned_equilibrium 1 1 x_star x_rest ≠ x_star) ∧
    pinned_equilibrium 1 1 28 (-8) = 10 ∧
    pinned_equilibrium 26 0 28 (-8) = 28 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, by decide, by decide⟩ <;> simp only [pinned_equilibrium] <;> omega
equations.math_family: Procrustes Landmark Attractor Dynamics & Target-Morphology Error Minimization
equations.variables: K: attractor homing gain; kappa: effective elastic stiffness of the un-relaxed cartilage rod (0 once the Maxwell stress has relaxed); x^*: froglet target landmark coordinate; x_rest: landmark position at which the rod is at its NF 45 rest length
equations.role: Explains the Pass 3 GM6001 residual defect and the Maxwell stress-arrest ratio: an elastic (MMP-arrested) cartilage rod shifts the overdamped equilibrium of a landmark to the stiffness-weighted mean of target and rest positions, so the Procrustes error cannot vanish, whereas relaxed cartilage (active MMP) restores exact convergence to X^*
equations.source_citation: Vandenberg, Adams & Levin (2012) Dev. Dyn. 241:863-878 (target-morphology convergence); Pinet et al. (2019) Development 146:dev175893 (MMP inhibition blocks correction); 1D overdamped spring reduction (this work)

equations.law_name: Boehm et al. (2010) Refutation of the Isotropic Proliferation Gradient Hypothesis (Zero Deviatoric Strain Law)
equations.formula: nabla . v = s(x) = ln(2)/T_c(x) - s_d,  sigma_active = 0 => eps_PD = eps_AP = eps_DV = s/3,  eps_PD - eps_AP = 0
equations.lean_code:
def strain_rate_pd_3x (s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf : Int) : Int :=
  s + 2 * zeta + 3 * chi_fgf * G_fgf
def strain_rate_ap_3x (s zeta : Int) : Int :=
  s - zeta
def deviatoric_pd_ap_rate_3x (s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf : Int) : Int :=
  strain_rate_pd_3x s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf - strain_rate_ap_3x s zeta
theorem isotropic_proliferation_zero_deviatoric_strain (s G_fgf : Int) :
    strain_rate_pd_3x s 0 0 G_fgf = s ∧
    strain_rate_ap_3x s 0 = s ∧
    strain_rate_dv_3x s 0 = s ∧
    deviatoric_pd_ap_rate_3x s 0 0 G_fgf = 0 ∧
    strain_rate_pd_3x s 0 0 G_fgf + strain_rate_ap_3x s 0 + strain_rate_dv_3x s 0 = 3 * s
equations.math_family: Continuum Viscoelastic / Anisotropic Stress & Directional Cell Migration vs Proliferation-Gradient Hypothesis
equations.variables: s(x): volumetric proliferation source rate (h^-1); eps_PD, eps_AP, eps_DV: principal strain rates along Proximo-Distal, Antero-Posterior, and Dorso-Ventral axes
equations.role: Proves that any purely isotropic proliferation source term s(x) partitions volumetric expansion equally across PD, AP, and DV axes with identically zero deviatoric PD elongation rate, explaining why Model I yields bulbous expansion (L_PD/W_AP approx 1.07)
equations.source_citation: Boehm et al. (2010) PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000420 Eqs. (3)-(9), Fig. 4; Morishita & Iwasa (2008) Bull. Math. Biol. 70:1957-1978

equations.law_name: Gros et al. (2010) & Boehm et al. (2010) Wnt5a/JNK Oriented Cell Division Stress & AER-FGF8 Velocity Gradient Elongation Law
equations.formula: sigma_active = zeta * (n otimes n - (1/3) I);  3*(eps_PD - eps_AP) = 3*zeta + 3*chi_FGF*G_FGF > 0,  tr(sigma_active) = 0
equations.lean_code:
theorem wnt5a_fgf_anisotropic_stress_drives_pd_elongation
    (s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf : Int)
    (hZeta : zeta > 0) (hChi : chi_fgf > 0) (hGrad : G_fgf > 0) :
    deviatoric_pd_ap_rate_3x s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf = 3 * zeta + 3 * (chi_fgf * G_fgf) ∧
    deviatoric_pd_ap_rate_3x s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf > 0 ∧
    strain_rate_pd_3x s zeta 0 G_fgf + strain_rate_ap_3x s zeta + strain_rate_dv_3x s zeta = 3 * s ∧
    deviatoric_pd_ap_rate_3x s 0 chi_fgf G_fgf < deviatoric_pd_ap_rate_3x s zeta chi_fgf G_fgf
equations.math_family: Continuum Viscoelastic / Anisotropic Stress & Directional Cell Migration vs Proliferation-Gradient Hypothesis
equations.variables: zeta: Wnt5a/JNK-polarized oriented cell division and convergent-extension active stress coefficient; chi_fgf: AER-FGF8/MAPK chemotactic sensitivity; G_fgf: distal FGF8 gradient
equations.role: Proves that traceless active stress from Wnt5a-oriented cell division/intercalation and distal AER-FGF8 velocity bias strictly increase the PD-to-AP aspect ratio while conserving volumetric continuity, and that Wnt5a ablation reduces PD elongation
equations.source_citation: Boehm et al. (2010) PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000420 Figs. 7-8, Fig. S8; Gros et al. (2010) Current Biology 20(22):1993-2004 Figs. 1-6; Kicheva & Briscoe (2010) PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000421

equations.law_name: Boehm et al. (2010) Dual-Label IddU/BrdU Cell-Cycle Invariance, Reynolds Insensitivity & Inverse-Optimization Bound
equations.formula: T_c(x) = T_i * (N_total / L_cells) in [11 h, 25 h];  s_opt_distal (0.54 h^-1) > 8 * s_emp_max (0.063 h^-1);  Delta L_PD(Re in [10^-6, 10^-1]) in [3.4%, 11.8%] < 42.2%
equations.lean_code:
theorem iddu_brdu_cell_cycle_invariance_and_inverse_opt_bound :
    (tc_distal_aer_h < tc_proximal_core_h ∧
     net_growth_rate_x1000 sp_distal_x1000 sd_compaction_x1000 >
       net_growth_rate_x1000 sp_proximal_x1000 sd_compaction_x1000 ∧
     net_growth_rate_x1000 sp_proximal_x1000 sd_compaction_x1000 > 0) ∧
    (s_inverse_opt_distal_x1000 > 8 * sp_distal_x1000 ∧
     s_inverse_opt_dv_x1000 < 0) ∧
    (pd_elong_permille_wt_model_ii > pd_elong_permille_fgf_only ∧
     pd_elong_permille_fgf_only > pd_elong_permille_wnt5a_null ∧
     pd_elong_permille_wnt5a_null > pd_elong_permille_model_i_re_max ∧
     pd_elong_permille_model_i_re_max > pd_elong_permille_model_i_re_min ∧
     pd_elong_permille_model_i_re_max - pd_elong_permille_model_i_re_min < 90)
equations.math_family: Continuum Viscoelastic / Anisotropic Stress & Directional Cell Migration vs Proliferation-Gradient Hypothesis
equations.variables: tc_distal_aer_h (11 h), tc_proximal_core_h (25 h): empirical IddU/BrdU cell cycle times; sd_compaction_x1000 (0.017 h^-1): cell density compaction rate; s_inverse_opt_distal_x1000 (0.54 h^-1): Hooke-Jeeves inverse-optimized distal growth rate
equations.role: Establishes the quantitative gap (>8x) between empirical BrdU/IddU proliferation rates and the theoretical isotropic rates needed to match limb elongation, proves Reynolds-number insensitivity across 5 orders of magnitude, and orders all 5 experimental regimes

equations.law_name: Boehm et al. (2010) 3D Stokes Growth System — Closed-Form Verification Oracles for the P1-P1 Tetrahedral FEM (Pass 3)
equations.formula: -nabla p + mu nabla^2 v + nabla . sigma_active + f = 0, nabla . v = s;  oracle (a): v = (s/3) x, p = 2 mu s/3 => nabla . v = s, (-p I + 2 mu eps) n = 0;  oracle (b): sigma_active = -2 mu zeta (n n - I/3), v = zeta (2x/3, -y/3, -z/3), p = 0 => nabla . v = 0, (2 mu eps + sigma_active) = 0
equations.lean_code:
def dilation_div_3x (s : Int) : Int := s + s + s
def dilation_traction_3x (mu s p3 : Int) : Int := -p3 + 2 * mu * s
def extensile_total_stress_pd_3x (mu zeta : Int) : Int := 2 * mu * (2 * zeta) + (-(2 * mu * (2 * zeta)))
def extensile_total_stress_ap_3x (mu zeta : Int) : Int := 2 * mu * (-zeta) + (-(2 * mu * (-zeta)))
def extensile_div_3x (zeta : Int) : Int := 2 * zeta + (-zeta) + (-zeta)
theorem stokes_growth_oracles_are_exact (mu s zeta : Int) :
    dilation_div_3x s = 3 * s ∧
    dilation_traction_3x mu s (2 * mu * s) = 0 ∧
    extensile_div_3x zeta = 0 ∧
    extensile_total_stress_pd_3x mu zeta = 0 ∧
    extensile_total_stress_ap_3x mu zeta = 0
equations.math_family: Continuum Viscoelastic / Anisotropic Stress & Directional Cell Migration vs Proliferation-Gradient Hypothesis
equations.variables: mu: tissue dynamic viscosity (2 mu = 1 so active gains are strain rates in h^-1); s: volumetric proliferation source; zeta: extensile Wnt5a/JNK oriented-division stress gain; eps: strain-rate tensor; n = e_PD
equations.role: Fixes the two exact Stokes growth solutions (uniform dilation; uniaxial extensile response to a traceless active stress) against which the P1-P1 Brezzi-Pitkaranta tetrahedral solver `assemble_stokes_p1p1` / `solve_stokes_growth` is verified to round-off (max relative error 8e-14 in `fem_manufactured_solution_errors`, self_test Check 10); both are linear in x and therefore exactly representable by P1 elements
equations.source_citation: Boehm et al. (2010) PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000420 Eqs. (3)-(5), (10)-(11) (Navier-Stokes growth model, Fig. 2G tetrahedral FEM); Dillon & Othmer (1999) J. Theor. Biol. 197:295-330 (viscous limb-bud continuum)

equations.law_name: Lagrangian/ALE Volume Budget of the 3D FEM — Proliferation vs OPT Volume Gap and Flank Influx Closure (Pass 3)
equations.formula: V1 = V0 + int int s dV dt + A_flank * v_in * T;  v_in = 0 => V1 - V0 = int int s dV dt;  V_OPT(St1)/V_OPT(St0) = 0.914/0.551 = 1.659 > V_prolif/V0 = 1.123 => deficit 0.295 mm^3 (~1/3 of V1) requires v_in* ~ 60 um/h
equations.lean_code:
def volume_after_growth (v0 source a_flank v_in t : Int) : Int :=
  v0 + source + a_flank * v_in * t
def opt_volume_st0_x1000 : Int := 551
def opt_volume_st1_x1000 : Int := 914
def fem_prolif_volume_st1_x1000 : Int := 619
theorem flank_influx_volume_budget (v0 source a_flank t v1 v2 : Int)
    (hA : a_flank > 0) (hT : t > 0) (hv : v1 < v2) :
    volume_after_growth v0 source a_flank 0 t = v0 + source ∧
    volume_after_growth v0 source a_flank v2 t - volume_after_growth v0 source a_flank v1 t
      = a_flank * (v2 - v1) * t ∧
    volume_after_growth v0 source a_flank v1 t < volume_after_growth v0 source a_flank v2 t ∧
    opt_volume_st1_x1000 > fem_prolif_volume_st1_x1000 ∧
    fem_prolif_volume_st1_x1000 > opt_volume_st0_x1000 ∧
    opt_volume_st1_x1000 - fem_prolif_volume_st1_x1000 = 295
equations.math_family: Continuum Viscoelastic / Anisotropic Stress & Directional Cell Migration vs Proliferation-Gradient Hypothesis
equations.variables: V0, V1: limb-bud volumes at St0 (E11.0) and St1 (E11.25); source = int int s dV dt: integrated IddU/BrdU proliferation; A_flank: flank cross-section area; v_in: body-wall inflow velocity through the fixed flank plane; T = 6 h
equations.role: Proves the volume budget that `simulate_limb_bud_fem_3d` reports as `volume_balance_ratio` (= 1 within 0.7% for the pinned flank) and that makes the flank-influx sweep of `evaluate_fem_regimes_and_influx` monotone, so the OPT volume ratio is reached at a unique v_in*; the integer inequalities encode the measured proliferation-vs-OPT volume gap (1.123 vs 1.659) that the active-stress Model II cannot close and that forces its AP/DV contraction
equations.source_citation: Boehm et al. (2010) PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000420 Fig. 2 (OPT volumes 0.551 -> 0.914 mm^3), Figs. 6D & 9C (inverse-optimisation growth-rate paradox); Kicheva & Briscoe (2010) PLoS Biology 8(7):e1000421

equations.law_name: Centered Hexagonal Ring Progression & 6R Perimeter Ring Increment Law
equations.lean_code:
def centered_hex_cells (R : Nat) : Nat :=
  1 + 3 * R * (R + 1)
def ring_perimeter_increment (R : Nat) : Nat :=
  6 * (R + 1)
theorem centered_hexagonal_ring_progression (R : Nat) :
    centered_hex_cells 0 = 1 ∧
    centered_hex_cells (R + 1) = centered_hex_cells R + ring_perimeter_increment R ∧
    centered_hex_cells (R + 1) > centered_hex_cells R
equations.math_family: Stigmergic Local Wall-Sharing Rule P_init(k) ∝ exp(β k) (k ∈ {2, 3} shared walls) on a 2D/3D Hexagonal Lattice + Honeycomb Perimeter-to-Area Economy & Topological 5–7 Disclination Pairs
equations.variables: R: number of concentric hexagonal rings around central founder cell; N(R): total brood cells in R rings; ΔN(R + 1): number of perimeter cells added in ring R + 1
equations.role: Establishes the exact centered hexagonal number progression N(R) = 1 + 3R(R+1) and 6R ring perimeter increment achieved when stigmergic wasps prioritize 3-wall pockets over 2-wall corner pockets
equations.source_citation: Karsai & Pénzes (1993) J. Theor. Biol. 161:505-525; Theraulaz & Bonabeau (1995) Science 269:686-688; Karsai & Pénzes (2000) Behav. Ecol. 11:387-395

equations.law_name: Shared-Wall Paper Pulp Economy & Asymptotic 3-Wall Hexagonal Optimality Law
equations.formula: W(R) = 3 N(R) + 6 R + 3 < 6 N(R) = W_isolated(R)  (∀ R ≥ 1),  W(R)/N(R) → 3.0 as R → ∞
equations.lean_code:
def compact_comb_walls (R : Nat) : Nat :=
  3 * centered_hex_cells R + 6 * R + 3
def unshared_isolated_walls (R : Nat) : Nat :=
  6 * centered_hex_cells R
def pulp_walls_saved (R : Nat) : Nat :=
  unshared_isolated_walls R - compact_comb_walls R
theorem shared_wall_pulp_economy_and_asymptotic_excess (R : Nat) :
    compact_comb_walls 0 = 6 ∧
    compact_comb_walls R - 3 * centered_hex_cells R = 6 * R + 3 ∧
    compact_comb_walls (R + 1) < unshared_isolated_walls (R + 1) ∧
    pulp_walls_saved (R + 1) > 0
equations.math_family: Stigmergic Local Wall-Sharing Rule P_init(k) ∝ exp(β k) (k ∈ {2, 3} shared walls) on a 2D/3D Hexagonal Lattice + Honeycomb Perimeter-to-Area Economy & Topological 5–7 Disclination Pairs
equations.variables: W(R): total distinct shared and boundary cell walls in an R-ring hexagonal comb; W_isolated(R): 6 N(R) walls for unshared cells; S_saved(R): paper pulp walls saved by hexagonal wall-sharing
equations.role: Proves that shared-wall hexagonal combs strictly reduce paper pulp wall count below 6 N(R) for all R >= 1 and approach 3 walls per cell (50% savings) as comb radius R grows
equations.source_citation: Karsai & Pénzes (1993) J. Theor. Biol. 161:505-525; Karsai & Pénzes (2000) Behav. Ecol. 11:387-395; Hales (2001) Discrete Comput. Geom. 25:1-22

equations.law_name: Euler Topological Charge Neutrality of 5-7 Disclination Pairs at Caste Transitions
equations.lean_code:
def topological_charge (z : Int) : Int :=
  6 - z
def disclination_dipole_net_charge (n_pairs : Int) : Int :=
  n_pairs * (topological_charge 5 + topological_charge 7)
theorem euler_disclination_dipole_charge_neutrality (n_pairs : Int) :
    topological_charge 6 = 0 ∧
    topological_charge 5 = 1 ∧
    topological_charge 7 = -1 ∧
    disclination_dipole_net_charge n_pairs = 0

equations.role: Proves that pentagon-heptagon (5-7) topological disclination pairs inserted to bridge worker-to-reproductive cell size transitions have zero net Euler topological charge
