equations.law_name: [Pass 3] Planar-Cell-Polarity Frizzled/Strabismus Bond-Asymmetry Tensor & PCP-Modulated Junction Tension
equations.formula: c_{ab} = \mathrm{relu}(\mathbf{p}_a\cdot\mathbf{n})\,\mathrm{relu}(\mathbf{p}_b\cdot\mathbf{n}) + \mathrm{relu}(-\mathbf{p}_a\cdot\mathbf{n})\,\mathrm{relu}(-\mathbf{p}_b\cdot\mathbf{n});\quad Q_{ab} = 2c_{ab}\,(\mathbf{n}\otimes\mathbf{n} - \tfrac{1}{2}I),\ \mathrm{tr}\,Q_{ab}=0;\quad a_{ab} = \mathbf{n}\cdot Q_{ab}\cdot\mathbf{n} = 2c_{ab}-1 \to \cos 2\theta_n;\quad \Lambda_{ab} = \bar{\Lambda}\,(1 + \varepsilon_{\mathrm{PCP}}\, a_{ab});\quad a(\theta) + a(\theta + \pi/2) = 0
equations.lean_code:
def pcp_bond_quadratic_form (a b c s : Int) : Int :=
  a * (c * c) - a * (s * s) + 2 * b * (c * s)
def pcp_bond_tension_permille (eps1000 a1000 : Int) : Int :=
  1000 + eps1000 * a1000 / 1000
theorem pcp_bond_tensor_traceless_and_perpendicular_cancellation
    (a b c s eps1000 : Int) (h0 : 0 < eps1000) (h1 : eps1000 < 1000) :
    pcp_bond_tensor_trace a = 0 ∧
    pcp_bond_quadratic_form a b c s + pcp_bond_quadratic_form a b (-s) c = 0 ∧
    pcp_bond_quadratic_form 1 0 c s = c * c - s * s ∧
    pcp_bond_tension_permille eps1000 (-1000) < pcp_bond_tension_permille eps1000 1000 ∧
    0 < pcp_bond_tension_permille eps1000 (-1000)
equations.math_family: Apical Epithelial Vertex Mechanics & Topological Polygon Packing (Farhadifar-Jülicher Vertex Functional & Lewis's Law)
equations.variables: p_a, p_b: Frizzled (distal) polarity unit vectors of the two cells sharing a bond; n: outward bond normal (angle theta_n to the proximal-distal axis); c_ab: intercellular Fz-Stbm bridge density in [0, 1]; Q_ab: traceless symmetric bond tensor; a_ab: asymmetry in [-1, 1]; eps_PCP: PCP coupling (0 = fz / stbm mutant); Lambda_ab: per-bond adherens-junction line tension
equations.role: Couples the explicit tri-cellular vertex network to a per-bond PCP tensor so AP-oriented (PCP-complex-bearing) junctions are stiffened exactly as much as PD-oriented junctions are softened (zero-trace), producing oriented T1 rearrangements and anisotropic blade elongation under pupal hinge contraction
equations.source_citation: Classen et al. (2005) Dev. Cell 9:805-817; Aigouy et al. (2010) Cell 142:773-786 (doi:10.1016/j.cell.2010.07.042, recorded offline); Farhadifar et al. (2007) Eq. 1 with bond-resolved Lambda_ij

equations.law_name: [Pass 3] Hinge-Contraction Pure-Shear Boundary Strain & Etournay (2015) Tissue-Shear Decomposition
equations.formula: F(t) = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda(t), 1/\lambda(t)),\ \det F = 1;\quad \ln\lambda(t) = \Delta\langle Q_{xx}\rangle(t) + R_{\mathrm{T1}}(t);\quad |Q| = \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(a/b);\quad \mathbf{F}_i = -\partial E/\partial\mathbf{r}_i,\ \partial A_\alpha/\partial\mathbf{r}_k = \tfrac{1}{2}(y_{k+1}-y_{k-1},\ x_{k-1}-x_{k+1})

def shear_rearrangement_residual (total elong : Int) : Int := total - elong
theorem hinge_contraction_shear_decomposition_balance
    (total elong_pcp elong_ctrl p q Lx Ly : Int) (h : elong_pcp < elong_ctrl) :
    elong_pcp + shear_rearrangement_residual total elong_pcp = total ∧
    shear_rearrangement_residual total elong_ctrl < shear_rearrangement_residual total elong_pcp ∧
    (p * Lx) * (q * Ly) = (p * q) * (Lx * Ly)

equations.variables: lambda(t): proximal-distal stretch of the blade margin (smoothstep ramp to exp(gamma_PD)); Q_xx: tissue-mean cell-elongation nematic along PD; R_T1: rearrangement residual of the shear decomposition; a/b: long/short cell axes; r_i: vertex positions; A_alpha: cell area
equations.role: States the area-preserving hinge-contraction strain, the closure of the Etournay et al. (2015) shear bookkeeping (imposed shear = cell-elongation change + rearrangement residual) and that lowering residual cell elongation strictly raises the rearrangement share, as measured for eps_PCP = 0.5 vs the eps_PCP = 0 control

models.name: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) PIN1 efflux carrier canalization on a Lockhart (1965)-growing hexagonal leaf blade with Scarpella et al. (2004/2006) procambial commitment: sequential 1°→4° vein-order emergence, open trees vs closed areoles vs decelerating no-branching
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (dicot leaf lamina and procambial venation network)
models.math_family: PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation & Intracellular Pool Conservation on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices

equations.law_name: Feugier et al. (2005) Hexagonal Intracellular PIN1 Carrier Pool Conservation Law
equations.lean_code:
def cytoplasmic_pin_pool (P_total P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 : Int) : Int :=
  P_total - (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6)
def membrane_face_rhs (k1 k2 Phi_j P_cyt P_j : Int) : Int :=
  k1 * Phi_j * P_cyt - k2 * P_j
theorem feugier_2005_hexagonal_pin_pool_conservation
    (P_total k1 k2 Phi1 Phi2 Phi3 Phi4 Phi5 Phi6 P_cyt P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 : Int) :
    cytoplasmic_pin_pool P_total P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 + (P1 + P2 + P3 + P4 + P5 + P6) = P_total ∧
    cytoplasmic_pool_rhs k1 k2 Phi1 Phi2 Phi3 Phi4 Phi5 Phi6 P_cyt P1 P2 P3 P4 P5 P6 +
      (membrane_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi1 P_cyt P1 +
       membrane_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi2 P_cyt P2 +
       membrane_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi3 P_cyt P3 +
       membrane_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi4 P_cyt P4 +
       membrane_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi5 P_cyt P5 +
       membrane_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi6 P_cyt P6) = 0
equations.math_family: PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation & Intracellular Pool Conservation on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices
equations.variables: P_{i,cyt}: cytoplasmic PIN1 carrier pool in cell i; P_{ij} (j=1..6): membrane PIN1 carrier density on face j of hexagonal cell i; P_{total}: conserved total cellular carrier pool; k_1, k_2: exocytosis and endocytosis rates; Φ(J_{i→j}): flux-dependent carrier recruitment function
equations.role: Proves exact state and rate conservation of total intracellular + membrane PIN1 efflux carriers across all 6 faces of each hexagonal leaf lamina cell, creating resource competition among faces for cytoplasmic PIN1 vesicles
equations.source_citation: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236(4):366-375 Eqs. 4-6

equations.law_name: Feugier et al. (2005) Winner-Take-All Open Tree vs Saturating Co-Polarized Face Law (Pass 3 note: the closed-loop attribution to Feugier is withdrawn; loop closure is Scarpella 2004/2006 commitment)
equations.formula: P_2 dP_1/dt - P_1 dP_2/dt = k_1 P_{cyt} (ΔS)^2 P_1 P_2 (P_1 - P_2) (Model A, Φ(J)=J^2, open tree β_1=0)  vs  k_1 Φ_{max} P_{cyt} (P_2 - P_1) (Model B, Φ(J)=J^n/(K^n+J^n)→Φ_{max}, bipolar loop closure β_1>0)
equations.lean_code:
def model_a_quadratic_face_rhs (k1 k2 P_cyt dS P : Int) : Int :=
  k1 * (P * dS) * (P * dS) * P_cyt - k2 * P
def model_b_saturated_face_rhs (k1 k2 Phi_max P_cyt P : Int) : Int :=
  k1 * Phi_max * P_cyt - k2 * P
theorem feugier_2005_winner_take_all_vs_saturating_bipolar
    (k1 k2 Phi_max P_cyt dS P1 P2 : Int) :
    P2 * model_a_quadratic_face_rhs k1 k2 P_cyt dS P1 -
      P1 * model_a_quadratic_face_rhs k1 k2 P_cyt dS P2 =
      k1 * P_cyt * dS * dS * P1 * P2 * (P1 - P2) ∧
    P2 * model_b_saturated_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi_max P_cyt P1 -
      P1 * model_b_saturated_face_rhs k1 k2 Phi_max P_cyt P2 =
      k1 * Phi_max * P_cyt * (P2 - P1)
equations.math_family: PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation & Intracellular Pool Conservation on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices
equations.variables: P_1, P_2: PIN1 carrier concentrations on two efflux faces of a hexagonal cell; P_{cyt}: shared cytoplasmic PIN1 pool; ΔS: downstream auxin concentration drop; Φ_{max}: saturated Hill exocytosis ceiling; β_1 = E - V + C: venation graph Betti-1 loop count
equations.role: Proves the two-face competition algebra: non-saturating superlinear exocytosis (Φ(J) = J^2) forces winner-take-all polarization onto a single efflux face per cell (open dendritic trees, β_1 = 0), whereas a saturated exocytosis ceiling lets two high-flux faces co-polarize (bipolar cells). Pass 3 correction: Feugier (2005) reports that decelerating/saturating Φ yields NO branching (the growing-blade `decelerating_no_branching` regime reproduces this, vein fraction -> ~0.9); the bipolar-cell loop closure in the leaf is attributed to Scarpella et al. (2004/2006) procambial commitment, formalised as Law 6. Code loci: templated scaffold #L421-L693, emergent growing-blade regimes #L862-L1076
equations.source_citation: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236(4):366-375 (PMID 15899502) Eqs. 7-11 & Figs. 3-7 (accelerating -> branching; decelerating -> no branching); Scarpella et al. (2006) Genes Dev. 20:1015-1027 Figs. 3-5 (bipolar PIN1 cells)

equations.law_name: Feugier et al. (2005) Directional Carrier-Mediated Auxin Flux Antisymmetry Law
equations.formula: J_{i→j} = P_{ij} S_i - P_{ji} S_j + D(S_i - S_j)  ⇒  J_{i→j} + J_{j→i} = 0  ∧  J_{i→j}(S,S) = (P_{ij} - P_{ji}) S
equations.lean_code:
def carrier_auxin_flux (P_ij P_ji D S_i S_j : Int) : Int :=
  P_ij * S_i - P_ji * S_j + D * (S_i - S_j)
theorem feugier_2005_flux_antisymmetry_and_polarity (P_ij P_ji D S_i S_j S : Int) :
    carrier_auxin_flux P_ij P_ji D S_i S_j +
      carrier_auxin_flux P_ji P_ij D S_j S_i = 0 ∧
    carrier_auxin_flux P_ij P_ji D S S = (P_ij - P_ji) * S
equations.math_family: PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation & Intracellular Pool Conservation on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices
equations.variables: J_{i→j}: net intercellular auxin flux from hexagonal cell i to neighbor j; P_{ij}, P_{ji}: opposing plasma-membrane PIN1 carrier densities; S_i, S_j: intracellular auxin concentrations; D: passive apoplastic permeability
equations.role: Proves exact pairwise intercellular auxin flux conservation across every hexagonal cell-wall edge while demonstrating pure carrier-driven polar transport at homogeneous auxin concentration. Code loci: graph topology #L351-L419, growing-blade flux kernel #L933-L1003
equations.source_citation: Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236(4):366-375 Eqs. 1-3

equations.law_name: Lockhart (1965) Yield-Threshold Biomechanical Blade Growth Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: (1/A) dA/dt = φ · max(0, P − Y(t)),   Y(t) = Y_0 + κ t   ⇒   A(t) = A_0 exp(φ[(P − Y_0) t − κ t²/2]) for t ≤ (P − Y_0)/κ, growth arrest thereafter
equations.lean_code:
def lockhart_growth_rate (phi P Y : Int) : Int :=
  if Y < P then phi * (P - Y) else 0
theorem lockhart_1965_yield_threshold_growth (phi P P' Y : Int) (hphi : 0 < phi) :
    (P ≤ Y → lockhart_growth_rate phi P Y = 0) ∧
    (Y < P → 0 < lockhart_growth_rate phi P Y) ∧
    (P ≤ P' → lockhart_growth_rate phi P Y ≤ lockhart_growth_rate phi P' Y)
equations.math_family: PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation & Intracellular Pool Conservation on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices
equations.variables: A: blade area; φ: wall extensibility; P: turgor pressure; Y(t) = Y_0 + κ t: time-hardening wall yield threshold; κ: hardening rate; arrest at t* = (P − Y_0)/κ = 8 DAG with the script defaults (φ = 1.0, P = 0.6, Y_0 = 0.2, κ = 0.05)
equations.role: Drives the growing hexagonal blade mesh on which the Feugier ODEs are integrated: blade area follows the Lockhart law (closed form A(7)/A(2) = 2.399, Euler check within 1e-3), new marginal cells are born as the allometric blade mask (half-width ∝ g^1.5, half-length ∝ g^0.5) expands, so vein orders emerge sequentially rather than from a prescribed template
equations.source_citation: Lockhart (1965) J. Theor. Biol. 8(2):264-275 Eq. 1 (doi 10.1016/0022-5193(65)90077-9); Kuchen et al. (2012) Science 335(6072):1092-1096 (growth-field framing)

equations.law_name: Vein-Graph Growth-Event Betti-1 Bookkeeping Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: β_1 = E − V + C;  free-end extension (E+1,V+1,C): Δβ_1 = 0;  new seed (E,V+1,C+1): Δβ_1 = 0;  same-component fusion (E+1,V,C): Δβ_1 = +1;  cross-component fusion (E+1,V,C−1): Δβ_1 = 0
equations.lean_code:
def betti1 (E V C : Int) : Int := E - V + C
theorem vein_graph_growth_event_betti1 (E V C : Int) :
    betti1 (E + 1) (V + 1) C = betti1 E V C ∧
    betti1 E (V + 1) (C + 1) = betti1 E V C ∧
    betti1 (E + 1) V C = betti1 E V C + 1 ∧
    betti1 (E + 1) V (C - 1) = betti1 E V C
equations.math_family: PIN1 Efflux Carrier Allocation & Intracellular Pool Conservation on Hexagonal Leaf Lamina Lattices
equations.variables: E: strand edges (vein-cell pairs joined by a PIN1 face with P ≥ P_vein); V: vein cells; C: connected components; β_1: closed areole count
equations.role: Classifies every canalization event during blade growth by its effect on the areole count: only fusion of a freely-ending strand with its own component (Scarpella et al. 2004) closes an areole, which is why the open-tree regime stays at β_1 = 0 across all four stages and the committed regime accumulates β_1 ≥ 1 after the lock activates
equations.source_citation: Scarpella, Francis & Berleth (2004) Development 131(14):3445-3455 (freely-ending domain fusion); Kang & Dengler (2004) Int. J. Plant Sci. 165(2):231-242 (vein-order hierarchy); standard graph cycle-rank identity

equations.law_name: Scarpella et al. (2004) Irreversible Procambial Commitment Lock Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: timer_ij ← (P_ij ≥ P_commit) ? timer_ij + dt : 0;   locked_ij ← locked_ij ∨ (timer_ij ≥ τ_commit);   P_ij ← locked_ij ? max(P_ij, P_commit) : P_ij
equations.lean_code:
def commitment_lock (locked : Bool) (P P_commit : Int) : Int :=
  if locked then (if P < P_commit then P_commit else P) else P
theorem procambial_commitment_lock_monotone (P P_commit : Int) :
    P_commit ≤ commitment_lock true P P_commit ∧
    P ≤ commitment_lock true P P_commit ∧
    (P_commit ≤ P → commitment_lock true P P_commit = P) ∧
    commitment_lock false P P_commit = P

def gauss_stretching_penalty (kx ky k_init : Int) : Int :=
  (kx * ky - k_init * k_init) * (kx * ky - k_init * k_init)
theorem forterre_gauss_stretching_bistable_wells (ky k_init : Int) :
    gauss_stretching_penalty k_init k_init k_init = 0 ∧
    gauss_stretching_penalty (-k_init) (-k_init) k_init = 0 ∧
    (∀ k : Nat, 0 < gauss_stretching_penalty 0 ky ((k : Int) + 1))

def flat_pass_stiffness (alpha alpha_c : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_c - alpha
theorem forterre_cusp_catastrophe_threshold (alpha alpha_c : Int) :
    (alpha < alpha_c ↔ 0 < flat_pass_stiffness alpha alpha_c) ∧
    flat_pass_stiffness alpha_c alpha_c = 0 ∧
    (alpha_c < alpha ↔ flat_pass_stiffness alpha alpha_c < 0)

    alpha_quartic_numerator 0 k_init_sq = 0 ∧
    alpha_quartic_numerator (16 * L_sq_sq) k_init_sq = 16 * alpha_quartic_numerator L_sq_sq k_init_sq ∧

equations.lean_code:
def gm_activator_num_residual (a h_scaled mu_h : Int) : Int :=
  (a * a) * mu_h - a * h_scaled
def gm_inhibitor_num_residual (a h_scaled mu_h : Int) : Int :=
  (a * a) * mu_h - mu_h * h_scaled
theorem gierer_meinhardt_homogeneous_steady_state (mu_h : Int) :
    gm_activator_num_residual mu_h (mu_h * mu_h) mu_h = 0 ∧
    gm_inhibitor_num_residual mu_h (mu_h * mu_h) mu_h = 0 := by
  simp [gm_activator_num_residual, gm_inhibitor_num_residual, Int.mul_assoc]
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Polarity (Gierer-Meinhardt Short-Range Activator / Long-Range Lateral Inhibitor PDE)
equations.variables: a(x,t): head/tentacle activator concentration; h(x,t): long-range inhibitor concentration; ρ(x): morphogen source density; μ_a, μ_h: turnover rates; D_a, D_h: diffusivities
equations.role: Establishes the exact algebraic homogeneous steady state of the nonlinear Gierer-Meinhardt reaction kinetics prior to diffusive symmetry breaking

equations.formula: tr(J_0) = μ_a - μ_h < 0  (μ_h > μ_a),   det(J_0) = μ_a μ_h > 0;   D_a = D_h = D ⟹ det(J_0 - q D I) = (Dq)^2 + Dq(μ_h - μ_a) + μ_a μ_h > 0  ∀ q ≥ 0

def gm_equal_diff_neg_trace (d_mu D q : Nat) : Nat :=
  (d_mu + 1) + 2 * D * q
def gm_equal_diff_det (d_mu d_pos D q : Nat) : Nat :=
  (D * q) * (D * q) + (D * q) * (d_mu + 1) + (d_pos + 1)
theorem gierer_meinhardt_equal_diffusion_stable (d_mu d_pos D q : Nat) :
    gm_equal_diff_neg_trace d_mu D q ≥ 1 ∧
    gm_equal_diff_det d_mu d_pos D q ≥ d_pos + 1 := by
  simp [gm_equal_diff_neg_trace, gm_equal_diff_det]
  omega

equations.variables: J_0: homogeneous reaction Jacobian; q = k^2: squared spatial wavenumber; D: common diffusivity
equations.role: Proves that faster inhibitor turnover (μ_h > μ_a) stabilizes the homogeneous state against oscillations and that equal diffusion (D_a = D_h) can never generate spatial Hydra polarity peaks

theorem gierer_meinhardt_lateral_inhibition_instability :
    gm_fourier_det 2 3 1 1 0 = 6 ∧
    gm_fourier_det 2 3 1 1 1 = 8 ∧
    gm_fourier_det 2 3 1 5 1 = 4 ∧

equations.variables: d = D_h / D_a: inhibitor-to-activator diffusivity ratio; d_c = (√2 + 1)^2 ≈ 5.8284: critical lateral-inhibition threshold; q = k^2: unstable spatial mode

equations.law_name: Meinhardt (1993) Thresholded Subsystem Firing Law (basal inhibitor production ⇒ drive threshold w_c)
equations.formula: b' = w (c b^2 / c_i + ρ_act) − μ b,  c_i' = c' b^2 − μ_inh c_i + ρ_inh;  off state exists ⟺ μ^2 ρ_inh − 4 w^2 c μ_inh ρ_act ≥ 0 ⟺ w ≤ w_c = (μ/2)·sqrt(ρ_inh / (c μ_inh ρ_act)) = 0.1633 (shell defaults)
equations.lean_code:
def meinhardt_off_state_disc (mu w c mu_inh rho_act rho_inh : Nat) : Nat :=
  mu * mu * rho_inh - 4 * w * w * c * mu_inh * rho_act
theorem meinhardt_three_system_off_state_discriminant_antitone
    (mu c mu_inh rho_act rho_inh w₁ w₂ : Nat) (h : w₁ ≤ w₂) :
    meinhardt_off_state_disc mu w₂ c mu_inh rho_act rho_inh ≤
      meinhardt_off_state_disc mu w₁ c mu_inh rho_act rho_inh := by
  unfold meinhardt_off_state_disc
  apply Nat.sub_le_sub_left
  apply Nat.mul_le_mul _ (Nat.le_refl rho_act)
  apply Nat.mul_le_mul _ (Nat.le_refl mu_inh)
  apply Nat.mul_le_mul _ (Nat.le_refl c)
  apply Nat.mul_le_mul _ h
  exact Nat.mul_le_mul (Nat.le_refl 4) h
theorem meinhardt_three_system_threshold_instance :
    meinhardt_off_state_disc 200 1 50 30 5 2 = 50000 ∧
    meinhardt_off_state_disc 200 2 50 30 5 2 = 0 := by
  decide

equations.formula: φ_t(σ, a) = H_t(σ) / (1 + κ_a a),  H_t(σ) = σ^p / (σ_t^p + σ^p);  ∂φ_t/∂σ ≥ 0, ∂φ_t/∂a ≤ 0  (integer form: σ K / (K + a) monotone in σ, antitone in a)

def meinhardt_tentacle_drive (sigma K a : Nat) : Nat :=

theorem meinhardt_tentacle_drive_monotone (K a σ₁ σ₂ a₁ a₂ σ : Nat)
    (hσ : σ₁ ≤ σ₂) (ha : a₁ ≤ a₂) :

    meinhardt_tentacle_drive σ (K + 1) a₂ ≤ meinhardt_tentacle_drive σ (K + 1) a₁ := by
  unfold meinhardt_tentacle_drive
  constructor
  · exact Nat.div_le_div_right (Nat.mul_le_mul hσ (Nat.le_refl K))
  · apply Nat.div_le_div_left
    · omega
    · omega

equations.law_name: Meinhardt (2012) Head–Foot Source-Density Exclusion Law
equations.formula: head drive = σ,  foot drive φ_f = 1 / (1 + (σ/σ_f)^2);  σ₁ ≤ σ₂ ⟹ φ_f(σ₂) ≤ φ_f(σ₁): the two drives are anti-monotone in σ

theorem meinhardt_head_foot_source_density_exclusion (K σ₁ σ₂ : Nat) (h : σ₁ ≤ σ₂) :
    σ₁ ≤ σ₂ ∧ meinhardt_foot_drive (K + 1) σ₂ ≤ meinhardt_foot_drive (K + 1) σ₁ := by

def keller_segel_fgf20_det (D_n r_n D_c mu_c chi n_0 f_c q : Int) : Int :=
  (D_n * q + r_n) * (D_c * q + mu_c) - chi * n_0 * f_c * q
def scaleless_neg_trace (D_n D_c r_n mu_c q : Nat) : Nat :=
  (D_n + D_c) * q + (r_n + 1) + (mu_c + 1)
def scaleless_pos_det (Dq_prod D_n_mu D_c_r r_pos : Nat) : Nat :=
  Dq_prod + D_n_mu + D_c_r + (r_pos + 1)
theorem keller_segel_fgf20_chemotactic_instability (D_n D_c r_n mu_c q Dq_prod D_n_mu D_c_r r_pos : Nat) :
    scaleless_neg_trace D_n D_c r_n mu_c q ≥ 2 ∧
    scaleless_pos_det Dq_prod D_n_mu D_c_r r_pos ≥ r_pos + 1 ∧
    keller_segel_fgf20_det 1 1 1 2 0 1 3 1 = 6 ∧
    keller_segel_fgf20_det 1 1 1 2 1 1 3 1 = 3 ∧
    keller_segel_fgf20_det 1 1 1 2 4 1 3 1 = -6 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [scaleless_neg_trace]; omega
  · simp [scaleless_pos_det]

equations.formula: g = [[1 + h_u², h_u h_v], [h_u h_v, 1 + h_v²]],  det g = (1 + p)(1 + q) - s² = 1 + p + q ≥ 1  (p = h_u², q = h_v², s² = p q)
equations.lean_code:
def monge_metric_det (p q s_sq : Nat) : Nat :=
  (1 + p) * (1 + q) - s_sq
theorem monge_metric_determinant (p q s_sq : Nat) (h_cross : s_sq = p * q) :
    monge_metric_det p q s_sq = 1 + p + q ∧ 1 ≤ monge_metric_det p q s_sq := by
  subst h_cross
  have h_expand : (1 + p) * (1 + q) = 1 + p + q + p * q := by
    simp [Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_add, Nat.one_mul, Nat.mul_one]
    omega
  constructor
  · simp only [monge_metric_det]
    omega
  · simp only [monge_metric_det]
    omega

equations.law_name: Zero-Link Topological Conservation & Opposite-Handed Chiral Helix Cancellation Law
equations.formula: ΔLk = Tw + Wr = 0  ⇒  N_+(+τ_h) + N_-(-τ_h) = 0,  τ(-s) = -τ(s),  τ(0) = 0 at the perversion kink
equations.lean_code:
def net_chiral_link (tau_plus tau_minus L_half : Int) : Int :=
  tau_plus * L_half + tau_minus * L_half
theorem goriely_zero_link_chiral_cancellation (tau_h L_half : Int) :
    net_chiral_link tau_h (-tau_h) L_half = 0 ∧
    net_chiral_link (-tau_h) tau_h L_half = 0
equations.math_family: Kirchhoff Elastic Rod Hamiltonian Mechanics, Zero-Link Topological Conservation (ΔLk = 0), Pitchfork Bifurcation, G-Fiber Overwinding & Contact-Gated Thigmotropic Coiling with Coulomb Friction

equations.role: Explains why a tethered climbing plant tendril that cannot rotate its ends must coil into two mirror-symmetric helices of opposite chirality (+τ and -τ) joined by a central perversion inversion kink
equations.source_citation: Goriely & Tabor (1998) Phys. Rev. Lett. 80:1564-1567; McMillen & Goriely (2002) J. Nonlinear Sci. 12:241-281

equations.law_name: Goriely & Tabor (1998) Critical Tension Pitchfork Bifurcation & Heteroclinic Perversion Soliton Law
equations.formula: T_c = B κ_0^2 / (1 + Γ),  cos θ_helix = 1 - ((1 + Γ)/Γ)(1 - √(T / T_c))  (T ≤ T_c),  θ(s) = θ_helix tanh(s / ξ),  ξ = √(B / (T_c - T))
equations.lean_code:
def pitchfork_bifurcation_residual (T gamma_plus_1 B kappa0 : Int) : Int :=
  T * gamma_plus_1 - B * (kappa0 * kappa0)
theorem goriely_pitchfork_critical_tension (B kappa0 gamma_plus_1 : Int) :
    pitchfork_bifurcation_residual (B * (kappa0 * kappa0)) 1 B kappa0 = 0 ∧
    pitchfork_bifurcation_residual 0 gamma_plus_1 B 0 = 0

equations.role: Determines the exact critical tension T_c below which an intrinsically curved rod bifurcates into left- and right-handed helices and governs the spatial width ξ of the central tendril perversion
equations.source_citation: Goriely & Tabor (1998) Phys. Rev. Lett. 80:1564-1567 Eq. 11; McMillen & Goriely (2002) J. Nonlinear Sci. 12:241-281 Sec. 3-4

equations.law_name: Gerbode et al. (2012) Soft vs Mature Lignified Tendril Over-Winding Susceptibility Law
equations.formula: S_overwind = B - C = B(1 - Γ);  Γ = C/B < 1 (young soft G-fiber ribbon) ⇒ dN/dz > 0 (initial axial stretching overwinds coil);  Γ > 1 (old lignified tendril) ⇒ dN/dz < 0 (monotonic unwinding)
equations.lean_code:
def gerbode_overwinding_susceptibility (B C : Int) : Int :=
  B - C
theorem gerbode_soft_vs_lignified_overwinding (B dC : Int) :
    gerbode_overwinding_susceptibility B B = 0 ∧
    (∀ k : Nat, gerbode_overwinding_susceptibility (B + Int.ofNat (k + 1)) B = Int.ofNat (k + 1)) ∧
    gerbode_overwinding_susceptibility B (B + dC) = -dC

equations.law_name: Contact-Gated Thigmotropic Intrinsic Curvature Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: κ0_i(t) = κ_contact · [t ≥ t_arrive_i] · (1 − exp(−(t − t_arrive_i)/τ_thigmo)),  t_arrive_i = min_j (t_touch_j + |s_i − s_j| / v_signal);  no touch ⇒ κ0 ≡ 0 ⇒ no coiling;  0 ≤ κ0_i ≤ κ_contact
equations.lean_code:
def gated_curvature (touched : Bool) (kappa_contact r : Nat) : Nat :=
  if touched then kappa_contact * r else 0
theorem thigmotropic_contact_gating (kappa_contact r d : Nat) (h : r ≤ d) :
    gated_curvature false kappa_contact r = 0 ∧
    gated_curvature true kappa_contact d = kappa_contact * d ∧
    gated_curvature true kappa_contact r ≤ kappa_contact * d

theorem coulomb_grip_capacity (mu1 mu2 N : Nat) (h : mu1 ≤ mu2) :
    coulomb_capacity 0 N = 0 ∧
    coulomb_capacity mu1 0 = 0 ∧
    coulomb_capacity mu1 N ≤ coulomb_capacity mu2 N

models.name: Graner & Glazier (1992) / Glazier & Graner (1993) extended large-Q Cellular Potts Model cell sorting + Ouchi et al. (2003) cortical tension

models.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)

equations.law_name: Graner & Glazier (1992) Cellular Potts Surface Tension Relations & Equal-Adhesion Null Identity
equations.lean_code:
def two_gamma_LD (J_LL J_DD J_LD : Int) : Int :=
  2 * J_LD - (J_LL + J_DD)
theorem cpm_equal_adhesion_null_tension (J J_M : Int) :
    two_gamma_LD J J J = 0 ∧ two_spreading_diff J J J_M J_M = 0
equations.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)
equations.variables: J_{LL}, J_{DD}, J_{LD}: homotypic and heterotypic Potts bond energies; J_{LM}, J_{DM}: cell-medium bond energies; γ_{LD}: heterotypic surface tension
equations.role: Maps microscopic lattice bond energies J(τ, τ') to macroscopic tissue interfacial tensions and proves that equal adhesion zeroes the sorting force
equations.source_citation: Graner & Glazier (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 69(13):2013-2016 Eqs. (2)-(3); Glazier & Graner (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47(3):2128-2154 Eqs. (3)-(5)

equations.law_name: Graner & Glazier (1992) / Glazier & Graner (1993) Four Canonical Phase Regimes (Complete Engulfment, Partial Lens, Checkerboard, Dissociation)
equations.formula: Complete engulfment: 0 < γ_{LD} < γ_{DM} - γ_{LM};  Partial lens: γ_{LD} > |γ_{LM} - γ_{DM}| > 0;  Checkerboard: γ_{LD} < 0;  Dissociation: γ_{αM} < 0
equations.lean_code:
theorem graner_glazier_four_phase_regimes :
    two_gamma_LD 14 2 11 = 6 ∧
    two_spreading_diff 14 2 16 16 = 12 ∧
    (0 < two_gamma_LD 14 2 11 ∧ two_gamma_LD 14 2 11 < two_spreading_diff 14 2 16 16) ∧
    two_gamma_LD 14 2 16 > two_spreading_diff 14 2 16 16 ∧
    two_gamma_LD 14 14 4 < 0 ∧
    two_gamma_M 14 2 < 0
equations.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)
equations.variables: γ_{LD}: light-dark interfacial tension; γ_{LM}, γ_{DM}: light-medium and dark-medium surface tensions
equations.role: Classifies Cellular Potts cell aggregates into concentric engulfment sorting, partial lens doublets, checkerboard mixing, and cell dissociation
equations.source_citation: Graner & Glazier (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 69(13):2013-2016 p. 2014; Glazier & Graner (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47(3):2128-2154 Table I

equations.law_name: Cellular Potts Hamiltonian Quadratic Volume Elasticity & Single-Spin Copy Restoring Barrier
equations.lean_code:
def cpm_volume_energy (lam v Vt : Int) : Int :=
  lam * (v - Vt) * (v - Vt)
theorem cpm_volume_elasticity_restoring_identity (lam Vt : Int) :
    cpm_volume_energy lam Vt Vt = 0 ∧
    cpm_delta_vol_gain lam Vt Vt = lam ∧
    cpm_delta_vol_loss lam Vt Vt = lam
equations.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)
equations.variables: H: Cellular Potts Hamiltonian; σ_i: cell spin ID at site i; v_σ: cell volume (area in 2D); V_t: target volume; λ: volume elasticity Lagrange multiplier
equations.role: Maintains finite deformable cell volumes under Metropolis boundary copy updates and establishes the single-pixel lattice pinning barrier ±λ at v = V_t
equations.source_citation: Graner & Glazier (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 69(13):2013-2016 Eq. (1); Glazier & Graner (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47(3):2128-2154 Eq. (1) & Section III.B

equations.law_name: 8-Neighbour Bond-Count Perimeter of a Square Cellular Potts Cell & Compact-Square Target Perimeter P_t
equations.lean_code:
def square_block_perimeter_8nbr (s : Int) : Int :=
  12 * s - 4
theorem cpm_square_block_target_perimeter :
    square_block_perimeter_8nbr 3 = 32 ∧
    square_block_perimeter_8nbr 4 = 44 ∧
    square_block_perimeter_8nbr 5 = 56 ∧
    (∀ s : Int, square_block_perimeter_8nbr (s + 1) - square_block_perimeter_8nbr s = 12)
equations.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)
equations.variables: s: side of the square lattice block; p: 8-neighbour bond-count perimeter (number of (site ∈ σ, 8-neighbour ∉ σ) pairs); P_t: target perimeter
equations.role: Fixes the default target perimeter of the Ouchi et al. (2003) cortical tension term so that lambda_P > 0 leaves the compact 4 × 4 initial cell energetically neutral; the P_t sweep {32, 38, 44, 50, 56} spans the 3 × 3 to 5 × 5 squares
equations.source_citation: Ouchi NB, Glazier JA, Rieu JP, Upadhyaya A, Sawada Y (2003) Physica A 329(3-4):451-458 Eq. (2) (perimeter constraint); perimeter counting convention from Glazier & Graner (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47:2128 Section II (fourth-nearest-neighbour / 8-site interaction range)

equations.law_name: Ouchi et al. (2003) Perimeter / Cortical Tension Elasticity Term & Single-Copy Perimeter Change Parity
equations.formula: H_P = λ_P ∑_{σ>0} (p_σ − P_t)^2;  ΔE_P(p, k) = λ_P k (2 (p − P_t) + k);  Δp_old = 2 n_same − 8, Δp_new = 8 − 2 n_same (even, |Δp| ≤ 8);  ΔE_P(P_t, ±2) = 4 λ_P, ΔE_P(P_t, 8) = 64 λ_P
equations.lean_code:
def cpm_perimeter_energy (lamP p Pt : Int) : Int :=
  lamP * ((p - Pt) * (p - Pt))
def cpm_copy_perimeter_change_old (n : Int) : Int := 2 * n - 8
theorem cpm_perimeter_elasticity_restoring_identity (lamP Pt : Int) :
    cpm_perimeter_energy lamP Pt Pt = 0 ∧
    (∀ n : Int, 0 ≤ n → n ≤ 8 →
      (∃ m : Int, cpm_copy_perimeter_change_old n = 2 * m) ∧
      cpm_copy_perimeter_change_old n = - cpm_copy_perimeter_change_new n ∧
      -8 ≤ cpm_copy_perimeter_change_old n ∧ cpm_copy_perimeter_change_old n ≤ 8) ∧
    cpm_delta_perim lamP Pt Pt 2 = 4 * lamP ∧
    cpm_delta_perim lamP Pt Pt (-2) = 4 * lamP ∧
    cpm_delta_perim lamP Pt Pt 8 = 64 * lamP
equations.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)
equations.variables: λ_P: cortical tension (perimeter elasticity) multiplier; p_σ: cell perimeter in 8-neighbour bonds; P_t: target perimeter; n_same: number of the copied site's 8 neighbours belonging to the leaving/joining cell; k: perimeter change
equations.role: Adds explicit cortical tension to the Graner & Glazier (1992) Hamiltonian; the parity identities are the incremental perimeter bookkeeping used in every Metropolis copy attempt (self-test check 9 verifies zero drift against a full recount), and the 64 λ_P isolated-pixel cost is the energetic barrier against cell fragmentation
equations.source_citation: Ouchi NB, Glazier JA, Rieu JP, Upadhyaya A, Sawada Y (2003) Physica A 329(3-4):451-458 Eq. (2); Farhadifar R et al. (2007) Curr. Biol. 17(24):2095-2104 Eq. (1) (vertex-model perimeter term)

equations.law_name: Cortical Tension Monotonicity Above the Target Perimeter (Effective Line Tension Against Ragged Boundaries)
equations.formula: λ_P ≥ 0 ∧ p ≥ P_t ∧ k ≥ 0 ⇒ E_P(p, P_t) ≤ E_P(p + k, P_t)
equations.lean_code:
theorem cpm_cortical_tension_monotone_above_target
    (lamP p Pt k : Int) (hlam : 0 ≤ lamP) (hp : Pt ≤ p) (hk : 0 ≤ k) :
    cpm_perimeter_energy lamP p Pt ≤ cpm_perimeter_energy lamP (p + k) Pt
equations.math_family: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Extended Large-Q Cellular Potts Model (CPM)
equations.variables: λ_P: cortical tension multiplier; p: current cell perimeter; P_t: target perimeter; k: perimeter increase
equations.role: Proves the perimeter term is an effective cortical line tension: every perimeter increase of an already-over-target cell is energetically non-favourable, which is why RMS(p_σ − P_t) decreases monotonically with λ_P in the C2 sweep (14.05 → 1.06 bonds) and fragmentation drops (0.217 → 0.083)
equations.source_citation: Ouchi NB, Glazier JA, Rieu JP, Upadhyaya A, Sawada Y (2003) Physica A 329(3-4):451-458 Section 2; Glazier & Graner (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47:2128 Section III.B (thermal boundary roughening the term counteracts)

models.name: Grieneisen et al. (2007) Nature & Mähönen et al. (2014) Nature reverse-fountain root tip auxin reflux capacitor solved on a cellular PIN-permeability lattice, with a growing dividing cellular lattice and gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 bending (Friml 2002, Band 2012)
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (primary root apex: vascular stele, pericycle/endodermis, cortex, epidermis/lateral root cap, quiescent center, and columella statocytes)
models.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry

equations.law_name: Grieneisen et al. (2007) Vascular-Epidermal Counter-Current Reflux Conservation Law
equations.formula: d(V_i A_i)/dt = Σ_j [c_ji A_j − c_ij A_i] + σ V_i − μ V_i A_i;  with μ = σ = J_in = escape = 0 every column of the operator sums to zero (Σ_i d(V_i A_i)/dt = 0, J_stele + J_epidermis = 0 across the closed tip)
equations.lean_code:
def stele_reflux_rhs (dJ_s k_lat A_e mu A_s : Int) : Int :=
  -dJ_s + k_lat * A_e - mu * A_s
def epidermis_reflux_rhs (dJ_e k_lat A_e mu : Int) : Int :=
  -dJ_e - k_lat * A_e - mu * A_e
theorem grieneisen_2007_vascular_epidermal_reflux_conservation
    (dJ_s dJ_e k_lat A_s A_e mu J_tip : Int) :
    stele_reflux_rhs dJ_s k_lat A_e mu A_s + epidermis_reflux_rhs dJ_e k_lat A_e mu =
      -(dJ_s + dJ_e) - mu * (A_s + A_e) ∧
    stele_reflux_rhs dJ_s k_lat A_e 0 A_s + epidermis_reflux_rhs (-dJ_s) k_lat A_e 0 = 0 ∧
    cross_section_net_flux J_tip (-J_tip) = 0
equations.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry
equations.variables: A_i: cellular auxin concentration; V_i = l_i w: cell area; c_ij: passive (D·face/dist) plus PIN-permeability (p_ij·face) transport coefficient from cell i to j; σ, μ: biosynthesis and turnover; J_in: shoot vascular influx
equations.role: Proves the pairwise cancellation of internal transfer terms and hence exact mass conservation of the closed reflux lattice; the script checks it numerically as zero column sums (max |Σ| / max |entry| = 0) of the assembled sparse operator plus a steady-state flux budget on the open operator
equations.source_citation: Grieneisen, Xu, Marée, Hogeweg & Scheres (2007) Nature 449(7165):1008-1013 Methods & Fig. 3

equations.law_name: Grieneisen et al. (2007) Quiescent Center (QC) Reflux Capacitor Amplification vs NPA / Lateral-PIN Ablation Collapse Law
equations.formula: A_QC / A_shoot ≫ 1 emerges from v_s, v_e, k_lat, k_col > 0 (solved: 113.6× at z = 52.5 µm);  k_lat = 0 → A_QC drops to 0.18 × WT;  NPA (all p → 3-5 %) → A_QC / A_shoot = 1.10
equations.lean_code:
def qc_two_stage_capacitor (A_shoot v_s v_e k_lat : Int) : Int :=
  A_shoot * (1 + v_s * v_e * k_lat) * (1 + v_s * v_e * k_lat)
theorem grieneisen_2007_qc_capacitor_amplification_vs_collapse
    (A_shoot v_s v_e k_lat : Int)
    (hA : A_shoot > 0) (hvs : v_s > 0) (hve : v_e > 0) (hklat : k_lat > 0) :
    qc_two_stage_capacitor A_shoot v_s v_e k_lat > A_shoot ∧
    qc_two_stage_capacitor A_shoot v_s v_e 0 = A_shoot ∧
    qc_two_stage_capacitor A_shoot 0 0 k_lat = A_shoot
equations.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry
equations.variables: A_QC: emergent stele auxin maximum at the QC/columella boundary; A_shoot: top-row stele concentration; v_s, v_e, k_lat, k_col: PIN permeabilities (µm/s)
equations.role: Qualitative Lean model of the capacitor; the script now produces the amplification, its position and its collapse by solving the operator (Pass 2 hard-coded them)
equations.source_citation: Grieneisen, Xu, Marée, Hogeweg & Scheres (2007) Nature 449(7165):1008-1013 Figs. 1-3

equations.law_name: Mähönen et al. (2014) PLETHORA (PLT1/2) Dosage Gradient & Meristem Boundary Monotonicity Law
equations.formula: l_k dP_k/dt = α H(A_k) l_k − (γ + r_k) l_k P_k + F_{k+1/2} − F_{k−1/2},  H(A) = A²/(K² + A²),  F = D_plt (P_{k+1} − P_k)/d;  z_MZ = top of last row with P ≥ Θ_MZ
equations.lean_code:
def plethora_axial_dosage (alpha_plt G_reflux beta_decay z : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_plt * G_reflux - beta_decay * z
def meristem_boundary_coord (alpha_plt G_reflux Theta_MZ : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_plt * G_reflux - Theta_MZ
theorem mahonen_2014_plethora_meristem_boundary_monotonicity
    (alpha_plt G1 G2 beta_decay z Theta_MZ : Int)
    (h_alpha : alpha_plt > 0) (h_gain : G2 > G1) :
    plethora_axial_dosage alpha_plt G2 beta_decay z >
      plethora_axial_dosage alpha_plt G1 beta_decay z ∧
    meristem_boundary_coord alpha_plt G2 Theta_MZ >
      meristem_boundary_coord alpha_plt G1 Theta_MZ
equations.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry
equations.variables: P_k: PLT dosage of row k; α: synthesis rate (1/h); γ: turnover (1/h); r_k: relative growth (dilution) rate; D_plt: cell-to-cell movement (µm²/h); Θ_MZ, Θ_EZ: zone thresholds
equations.role: Positions the meristematic and elongation zone boundaries from the solved auxin field; emergent WT z_MZ = 240 µm, decapitated 225, pin2 120, k_lat=0 45, QC-ablation 255 (NPA: PLT saturates everywhere — disclosed disagreement)
equations.source_citation: Mähönen et al. (2014) Nature 515(7525):125-129 Figs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Friml et al. (2002) / Kleine-Vehn et al. (2010) Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Columella Efflux Asymmetry Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: p_lower = k_col (1 + g),  p_upper = k_col (1 − g),  p_lower + p_upper = 2 k_col,  p_lower − p_upper = 2 k_col g (monotone in g),  g = g_max sin(φ)·[β < β_tip]
equations.lean_code:
def lower_side_permeability (k_col g : Int) : Int := k_col * (1 + g)
def upper_side_permeability (k_col g : Int) : Int := k_col * (1 - g)
def lateral_efflux_asymmetry (k_col g : Int) : Int :=
  lower_side_permeability k_col g - upper_side_permeability k_col g
theorem friml_2002_gravistimulated_columella_efflux_asymmetry
    (k_col g g1 g2 : Int) (hk : k_col > 0) (hg : g > 0) (hmono : g2 > g1) :
    lower_side_permeability k_col g + upper_side_permeability k_col g = 2 * k_col ∧
    lower_side_permeability k_col g > upper_side_permeability k_col g ∧
    lateral_efflux_asymmetry k_col g = 2 * k_col * g ∧
    lower_side_permeability k_col 0 = upper_side_permeability k_col 0 ∧
    lateral_efflux_asymmetry k_col g2 > lateral_efflux_asymmetry k_col g1
equations.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry
equations.variables: k_col: apolar columella PIN3/4/7 permeability; g ∈ [0, 1]: statocyte relocalisation asymmetry; φ: tip inclination from the gravity vector; β: bending angle; β_tip: Band (2012) tipping point
equations.role: Proves the gravistimulated split conserves columella efflux, strictly favours the lower side for g > 0 and is monotone in g; the solved lattice then yields an EZ lower/upper epidermal auxin ratio of 1.85 at g_max = 0.18 (Spearman ρ = 1.0 over the g sweep) that drives sine-law bending (tipping point reached at 5.55 h vs Band's ≈2 h — disclosed)

equations.law_name: Mähönen et al. (2014) PLETHORA Growth-Dilution Monotonicity Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: P (γ + r) = S  ⇒  r₂ > r₁ ≥ 0 ∧ γ > 0 ∧ P₁, P₂ > 0  ⇒  P₂ < P₁
equations.lean_code:
def plt_dilution_balance (P gamma r : Int) : Int := P * (gamma + r)
theorem mahonen_2014_plethora_growth_dilution_monotone
    (P1 P2 gamma r1 r2 S : Int)
    (_hP1 : P1 > 0) (hP2 : P2 > 0) (hgamma : gamma > 0) (hr1 : r1 ≥ 0) (hr : r2 > r1)
    (h1 : plt_dilution_balance P1 gamma r1 = S) (h2 : plt_dilution_balance P2 gamma r2 = S) :
    P2 < P1
equations.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry
equations.variables: P: PLT dosage; S = α H(A): auxin-induced synthesis; γ: turnover; r: relative growth rate of the cell row (ln2/T_cycle in the meristem, r_ez (1 − l/l_mature) in the elongation zone)
equations.role: Formalises the growth-dilution mechanism used by `solve_plethora_gradient` on the growing lattice: elongating rows dilute PLT faster and exit the meristem, which is what positions the EZ/DZ boundary in `simulate_growing_cellular_lattice`
equations.source_citation: Mähönen et al. (2014) Nature 515(7525):125-129 Figs. 3-4 (growth dilution of PLT proteins)

equations.law_name: Explicit Mitotic Division Length-Conservation Law of the Growing Cellular Lattice (Pass 3)
equations.formula: l ≥ 2 l_birth ∧ l_birth > 0  ⇒  ⌊l/2⌋ + (l − ⌊l/2⌋) = l ∧ ⌊l/2⌋ ≥ l_birth ∧ l − ⌊l/2⌋ ≥ l_birth ∧ n_cells → n_cells + 1
equations.lean_code:
def daughter_a (l : Int) : Int := l / 2
def daughter_b (l : Int) : Int := l - l / 2
theorem mitotic_division_length_conservation
    (l l_birth n_cells : Int) (_hb : l_birth > 0) (hl : l ≥ 2 * l_birth) :
    daughter_a l + daughter_b l = l ∧
    daughter_a l ≥ l_birth ∧
    daughter_b l ≥ l_birth ∧
    (n_cells - 1) + 2 = n_cells + 1
equations.math_family: Solved 2D Cellular PIN1/PIN2/PIN3 Permeability Transport Lattice (Vascular–Epidermal Reverse-Fountain Reflux Capacitor) with Finite-Volume PLETHORA Zonation, Explicit Mitotic Division on a Growing Lattice, and Gravistimulated PIN3/PIN7 Statocyte Efflux Asymmetry
equations.variables: l: meristematic cell row length; l_birth: daughter length at birth (7 µm); n_cells: number of rows in the file
equations.role: Guarantees the division rule of `simulate_growing_cellular_lattice` conserves file length and never creates sub-birth-length daughters; the script's self-test checks the same invariants on the 24 h run (23 divisions, 26 meristem cells, min length ≥ l_birth)
equations.source_citation: Beemster & Baskin (1998) Plant Physiol 116(4):1515-1526 (kinematic cell production); Dello Ioio et al. (2007) Curr Biol 17(8):678-682 (meristem cell number)

models.name: Hamant et al. (2008), Bozorg et al. (2014), Sampathkumar et al. (2014), Uyttewaal et al. (2012), Heisler et al. (2010) & Louveaux et al. (2016) shoot apical meristem shell stress tensor, stress-vs-strain CMT alignment, katanin boundary morphogenesis and PIN1/CMT co-alignment on a growing L1 cellular vertex mesh
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (shoot apical meristem L1 epidermal shell, organ-meristem saddle boundary, cylindrical stem, and epidermal cells)
models.math_family: Finite-Element Pressurized Shell Turgor Stress Tensor, Bozorg Stress-vs-Strain Cue Discrimination, Anisotropic Viscoplastic Lockhart Growth & (Pass 3) Heisler PIN1/CMT Co-Alignment on a Growing L1 Cellular Vertex Mesh

equations.law_name: Hamant et al. (2008) & Bozorg et al. (2014) Saddle-Boundary Stress Anisotropy Amplification & Gaussian Curvature Inversion Law
equations.formula: K = κ_1 κ_2;  Δσ(P_s, κ_1, κ_2) = P_s (κ_1 - κ_2);  Δσ(P_s, κ_0, κ_0) = 0 (dome, K > 0) vs Δσ(P_s, κ_0, -κ_s) = P_s(κ_0 + κ_s) > P_s κ_0 > 0 (saddle crease, K < 0)
equations.lean_code:
def gaussian_curvature (kappa_1 kappa_2 : Int) : Int :=
  kappa_1 * kappa_2
def saddle_stress_anisotropy (P_s kappa_1 kappa_2 : Int) : Int :=
  P_s * (kappa_1 - kappa_2)
theorem hamant_bozorg_saddle_boundary_stress_anisotropy_amplification
    (P_s kappa_0 kappa_s : Int)
    (hP : P_s > 0) (hk0 : kappa_0 > 0) (hks : kappa_s > 0) :
    gaussian_curvature kappa_0 kappa_0 > 0 ∧
    saddle_stress_anisotropy P_s kappa_0 kappa_0 = 0 ∧
    gaussian_curvature kappa_0 (-kappa_s) < 0 ∧
    saddle_stress_anisotropy P_s kappa_0 (-kappa_s) = P_s * kappa_0 + P_s * kappa_s ∧
    saddle_stress_anisotropy P_s kappa_0 (-kappa_s) > P_s * kappa_0
equations.math_family: Finite-Element Pressurized Shell Turgor Stress Tensor, Bozorg Stress-vs-Strain Cue Discrimination, Anisotropic Viscoplastic Lockhart Growth & (Pass 3) Heisler PIN1/CMT Co-Alignment on a Growing L1 Cellular Vertex Mesh
equations.variables: κ_1, κ_2: principal curvatures along and across organ-meristem boundary (μm^-1); K = κ_1 κ_2: Gaussian curvature (μm^-2); P_s: turgor shell stress scale; Δσ: principal tensile stress difference (MPa)
equations.role: Proves that transitioning from the positive-Gaussian-curvature SAM dome (K > 0) to the negative-Gaussian-curvature organ boundary saddle (K < 0) switches tensile stress from isotropic (Δσ = 0) to strongly amplified along the boundary crease axis
equations.source_citation: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 2 & SOM; Bozorg et al. (2014) PLoS Comput. Biol. 10(1):e1003410 Figs. 3-4

equations.law_name: Bozorg et al. (2014) & Hamant et al. (2008) Cylindrical Stem 2:1 Hoop-to-Axial Laplace Stress Switch & Longitudinal Lockhart Elongation Law
equations.formula: σ_θ = P R / h = 2 S_0 = 2 σ_z > σ_z;  ε̇_z - ε̇_θ = C_z σ_z - C_θ σ_θ = (C_z - 2 C_θ) S_0 > 0  for C_z > 2 C_θ
equations.lean_code:
def cylinder_axial_stress (S_0 : Int) : Int := S_0
def cylinder_hoop_stress (S_0 : Int) : Int := 2 * S_0
def lockhart_elongation_rate (compliance sigma : Int) : Int := compliance * sigma
theorem bozorg_cylinder_to_saddle_stress_switch
    (S_0 C_z C_theta : Int)
    (hS : S_0 > 0) (hC : C_z > 2 * C_theta) :
    cylinder_hoop_stress S_0 = 2 * cylinder_axial_stress S_0 ∧
    cylinder_hoop_stress S_0 - cylinder_axial_stress S_0 = S_0 ∧
    cylinder_hoop_stress S_0 > cylinder_axial_stress S_0 ∧
    lockhart_elongation_rate C_z (cylinder_axial_stress S_0) -
      lockhart_elongation_rate C_theta (cylinder_hoop_stress S_0) =
      (C_z - 2 * C_theta) * S_0 ∧
    lockhart_elongation_rate C_z (cylinder_axial_stress S_0) >
      lockhart_elongation_rate C_theta (cylinder_hoop_stress S_0)
equations.math_family: Finite-Element Pressurized Shell Turgor Stress Tensor, Bozorg Stress-vs-Strain Cue Discrimination, Anisotropic Viscoplastic Lockhart Growth & (Pass 3) Heisler PIN1/CMT Co-Alignment on a Growing L1 Cellular Vertex Mesh

theorem uyttewaal_katanin_oryzalin_feedback_gain_reduction
    (E_0 dE Delta_sigma gamma_WT gamma_bot1 : Int)
    (hdE : dE > 0) (hDS : Delta_sigma > 0) (hG : gamma_WT > gamma_bot1) :

equations.formula: χ = V - E + F;  division along σ_1: (V, E, F) → (V + 2, E + 3, F + 1), χ invariant, F + 1 > F;  after n ≥ 0 divisions (V + 2n, E + 3n, F + n) has the same χ;  T1: (V, E, F) unchanged
equations.lean_code:
def euler_characteristic (V E F : Int) : Int := V - E + F
def vertices_after_divisions (V n : Int) : Int := V + 2 * n
def edges_after_divisions (E n : Int) : Int := E + 3 * n
def cells_after_divisions (F n : Int) : Int := F + n
theorem louveaux_vertex_mesh_division_preserves_euler_characteristic
    (V E F n : Int) (hn : n ≥ 0) :
    euler_characteristic (vertices_after_divisions V 1) (edges_after_divisions E 1) (cells_after_divisions F 1) = euler_characteristic V E F ∧
    cells_after_divisions F 1 > F ∧
    euler_characteristic (vertices_after_divisions V n) (edges_after_divisions E n) (cells_after_divisions F n) = euler_characteristic V E F ∧
    cells_after_divisions F n ≥ F ∧
    euler_characteristic V E F = euler_characteristic V E F

equations.law_name: Hannezo et al. (2017) Topological Binary-Tree Balance & Critical Galton-Watson Branching Law
equations.formula: A_final = 1 + N_branch - N_term = 0  =>  N_term = N_branch + 1,  N_total = 2 N_branch + 1,  q_branch = N_branch / (N_branch + N_term) = N_branch / (2 N_branch + 1) -> 1/2 = q_term
equations.lean_code:
def active_tips_remaining (n_branch n_term : Int) : Int := 1 + n_branch - n_term
def total_tree_segments (n_branch n_term : Int) : Int := n_branch + n_term
theorem hannezo_topological_tree_balance_and_critical_branching (n_branch : Int) :
    active_tips_remaining n_branch (n_branch + 1) = 0 ∧
    total_tree_segments n_branch (n_branch + 1) = 2 * n_branch + 1 ∧
    2 * n_branch < total_tree_segments n_branch (n_branch + 1) ∧
    active_tips_remaining 33 34 = 0 ∧
    total_tree_segments 33 34 = 67 := by
  simp [active_tips_remaining, total_tree_segments]; omega
equations.math_family: Stochastic Branching and Annihilating Random Walk (BARW), Critical Galton-Watson Tree Topology & Fisher-KPP Travelling Wavefront
equations.variables: N_branch: number of dichotomous tip bifurcation events (A -> 2A); N_term: number of tip-duct annihilation/termination events (A + I -> I); q_branch: ensemble branching probability
equations.role: Proves that any finite self-terminating binary ductal tree starting from 1 primary stalk satisfies N_term = N_branch + 1, tuning the tree automatically to a critical Galton-Watson process (q_branch -> 1/2) with universal P(S) ~ S^(-3/2) subtree size scaling
equations.source_citation: Hannezo et al. (2017) Cell 171(1):242-255 Eqs. (1)-(3); Scheele et al. (2017) Nature 542:313-317

equations.law_name: Hannezo et al. (2017) Mean-Field BARW Travelling-Wave PDE & Homeostatic Duct Density Law
equations.lean_code:
def active_tip_reaction (kb ka a i : Int) : Int := kb * a - ka * a * (a + i)
def duct_deposition_rate (v0 a : Int) : Int := v0 * a
def per_tip_net_growth (kb ka a i : Int) : Int := kb - ka * (a + i)
theorem hannezo_barw_homeostatic_steady_state (kb ka v0 i_inf : Int) :
    active_tip_reaction kb ka 0 i_inf = 0 ∧
    duct_deposition_rate v0 0 = 0 ∧
    per_tip_net_growth (ka * i_inf) ka 0 i_inf = 0 := by
  simp [active_tip_reaction, duct_deposition_rate, per_tip_net_growth]; omega
equations.math_family: Stochastic Branching and Annihilating Random Walk (BARW), Critical Galton-Watson Tree Topology & Fisher-KPP Travelling Wavefront
equations.variables: a(x,t): active proliferative tip density; i(x,t): differentiated inactive duct density; D: tip effective diffusivity; v_0: tip speed; k_b: Poisson bifurcation rate; k_a: tip-duct annihilation kernel
equations.role: Establishes that an invading pulse of active tips a(x,t) self-extinguishes behind the Fisher-KPP wavefront (a_∞ = 0) while depositing a uniform homeostatic plateau of differentiated ducts i_∞ ∝ k_b / k_a
equations.source_citation: Hannezo et al. (2017) Cell 171(1):242-255 STAR Methods Eqs. (4)-(10)

equations.law_name: Hannezo et al. (2017) & Silberstein & Daniel (1987) Annihilation-Radius Hyper-Branching Density Scaling & Explosion Ablation Law
equations.formula: i_∞(R_a) ∝ k_b / (v_0 R_a)  =>  i_∞(R_a,hypo) < i_∞(R_a,WT) < i_∞(R_a,hyper);  for R_a = 0 (no annihilation): N_active(g) = 2^g -> ∞
equations.lean_code:
def homeostatic_density_scaled (ra_10 : Nat) : Nat := 10000 / ra_10
def unarrested_branch_step (n : Nat) : Nat := 2 * n
def unarrested_gen5 (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  unarrested_branch_step (unarrested_branch_step (unarrested_branch_step (unarrested_branch_step (unarrested_branch_step n))))
theorem hannezo_annihilation_radius_scaling_and_explosion_ablation (n : Nat) :
    homeostatic_density_scaled 70 < homeostatic_density_scaled 35 ∧
    homeostatic_density_scaled 35 < homeostatic_density_scaled 17 ∧
    unarrested_gen5 n = 32 * n ∧ 0 < unarrested_gen5 1

equations.variables: R_a: tip-duct steric/TGF-beta sensing and annihilation radius; g: branching generation; N_active(g): active tip count under R_a = 0 ablation
equations.role: Proves that attenuating TGF-beta signaling (reducing R_a) produces hyper-dense ductal trees while exogenous TGF-beta (increasing R_a) yields sparse hypoplastic trees, whereas complete ablation of annihilation (R_a = 0) destroys self-termination and triggers exponential tip explosion
equations.source_citation: Hannezo et al. (2017) Cell 171(1):242-255 Fig. 4; Silberstein & Daniel (1987) Science 237:291-293

equations.law_name: Anisotropic ECM Nematic Alignment Order Law for 3D BARW in cylindrical fat-pad / spherical mesenchymal geometries (Bordeu et al. 2023)
equations.formula: du/dt = sigma_theta xi_perp + lambda (f.u)(f - (f.u) u);  S = < (3 cos^2 theta - 1)/2 >_length,  S(iso) = 0,  S(parallel) = 1,  S(perp) = -1/2;  R_s(t) = R_s(0)(1 + gamma t) (inflation)
equations.lean_code:
def nematic_order_twice (c : Int) : Int := 3 * c * c - 1
def nematic_torque (lambda_ fu : Int) : Int := lambda_ * fu
theorem hannezo_nematic_ecm_alignment_order (c lambda_ fu : Int) :
    nematic_order_twice 1 = 2 ∧ nematic_order_twice (-1) = 2 ∧ nematic_order_twice 0 = -1 ∧
    -1 ≤ nematic_order_twice c ∧ nematic_order_twice c = nematic_order_twice (-c) ∧
    nematic_order_twice 1 + nematic_order_twice 0 + nematic_order_twice 0 = 0 ∧
    nematic_torque 0 fu = 0 ∧ nematic_torque lambda_ 0 = 0 ∧
    nematic_torque lambda_ (-fu) = - nematic_torque lambda_ fu
equations.math_family: Stochastic Branching and Annihilating Random Walk (BARW), Critical Galton-Watson Tree Topology & Fisher-KPP Travelling Wavefront
equations.variables: u: unit tip direction; f: ECM fiber axis; lambda: nematic alignment strength (1/time); theta: angle between a ductal segment and f; S: length-weighted nematic order parameter; gamma: capsule inflation rate
equations.role: Specifies the anisotropic-ECM torque of the 3D BARW simulator (nematic, not polar: symmetric under u -> -u, zero for isotropic matrix or perpendicular tips) and the order parameter used to quantify fiber alignment of the ductal network; S rises monotonically with lambda and over-alignment (lambda >= 0.4) collapses the tree by alignment-induced sibling annihilation
equations.source_citation: Bordeu I, Chatzeli L, Simons BD (2023) Nat. Commun. 14:3422 (doi:10.1038/s41467-023-39124-x); Hannezo et al. (2017) Cell STAR Methods

equations.law_name: Scheele et al. (2017) Moran Neutral-Drift Martingale for labelled stem cells inside a terminal end bud
equations.lean_code:
def moran_expected_numerator (n k : Int) : Int :=
  (k + 1) * (k * (n - k)) + (k - 1) * (k * (n - k)) + k * (n * n - 2 * (k * (n - k)))
def moran_variance_numerator (n k : Int) : Int := 2 * (k * (n - k))
theorem scheele_moran_neutral_drift_martingale (n k : Int) :
    moran_expected_numerator n k = k * (n * n) ∧
    moran_variance_numerator n 0 = 0 ∧ moran_variance_numerator n n = 0 ∧
    (0 ≤ k → k ≤ n → 0 ≤ moran_variance_numerator n k)
equations.math_family: Stochastic Branching and Annihilating Random Walk (BARW), Critical Galton-Watson Tree Topology & Fisher-KPP Travelling Wavefront
equations.variables: N: equipotent stem cells per TEB; k: labelled cells; k': labelled cells after one Moran birth-death step
equations.role: Proves that neutral drift of a labelled clone inside a TEB conserves the expected labelled fraction while generating clonal variance only in mosaic TEBs; this is the reference (f_bar = f_0) against which the duct-length-weighted labelled fraction of the simulated tree is measured
equations.source_citation: Scheele CLGJ et al. (2017) Nature 542:313-317 (doi:10.1038/nature21060); Moran PAP (1958) Math. Proc. Camb. Phil. Soc. 54:60-71; Klein AM, Simons BD (2011) Development 138:3103-3111

equations.law_name: Label Conservation at a TEB Bifurcation (hypergeometric half-split + doubling)
equations.lean_code:
def daughter_labels (k k1 : Int) : Int × Int := (2 * k1, 2 * (k - k1))
theorem scheele_teb_split_label_conservation (k k1 h : Int) :
    (daughter_labels k k1).1 + (daughter_labels k k1).2 = 2 * k ∧
    2 * (h * k) = (2 * h) * k
equations.math_family: Stochastic Branching and Annihilating Random Walk (BARW), Critical Galton-Watson Tree Topology & Fisher-KPP Travelling Wavefront
equations.variables: k: labelled cells in the parent TEB; k_1: labelled cells in the first half of the split; h = N/2
equations.role: Shows that the A -> 2A bifurcation is label-neutral: the total labelled count doubles with cell number and each daughter is an unbiased copy of the parent, so the martingale of Law 5 extends to the whole BARW tree (clone fate is dictated by the tree's bifurcation/termination statistics, Scheele et al. 2017)
equations.source_citation: Scheele CLGJ et al. (2017) Nature 542:313-317 (doi:10.1038/nature21060)

equations.law_name: Hannezo–Prost–Joanny 3D Epithelial Equilibrium Aspect-Ratio & Squamous-Cuboidal-Columnar Scaling Law
equations.lean_code:
def aspect_stationarity_residual (Ga_Gb c_Gl d0 h0 : Int) : Int :=
  4 * Ga_Gb * d0 - c_Gl * h0
def epithelial_morphology_class (c_Gl four_Ga_Gb : Nat) : Nat :=
  if c_Gl < four_Ga_Gb then 0
  else if c_Gl == four_Ga_Gb then 1
  else 2
theorem hannezo_equilibrium_aspect_ratio_hierarchy (Ga_Gb k : Int) (g base delta : Nat) :
    aspect_stationarity_residual Ga_Gb (4 * Ga_Gb) k k = 0 ∧
    epithelial_morphology_class g (g + base + 1) = 0 ∧
    epithelial_morphology_class (g + 1) (g + 1) = 1 ∧
    epithelial_morphology_class (g + delta + 2) (g + 1) = 2
equations.math_family: 3D Incompressible Vertex / Continuum Epithelial Energy with Apical (Gamma_a), Basal (Gamma_b), and Lateral (Gamma_l) Surface Tensions & Substrate Elastic Foundation
equations.variables: Γ_a, Γ_b: apical and basal actomyosin surface tensions; Γ_l: lateral cell-cell tension; V_0 = A_0 h_0: conserved 3D cell volume; c = 2√(2√3) ≈ 3.7224: hexagonal perimeter factor; h_0/d_0: equilibrium cell aspect ratio
equations.role: Determines the universal equilibrium cell height h_0 and aspect ratio h_0/d_0 continuously spanning squamous (h_0/d_0 < 1), cuboidal (h_0/d_0 ≈ 1), and tall columnar (h_0/d_0 > 1) epithelia
equations.source_citation: Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111(1):27-32 Eqs. (1)-(4); Krajnc & Ziherl (2015) Phys. Rev. E 92:052713 Eqs. (5)-(9)

equations.law_name: Single-Cell Energy Convexity (E''(A^*) > 0) & Elastic Substrate Buckling Wavenumber Stationarity
equations.formula: E''_cell(A^*) = 3 c Γ_l V_0 / (8 (A^*)^(5/2)) > 0,  N_c(q) = κ_eff q^2 + K_sub / q^2  ⇒  κ_eff q_c^4 = K_sub,  λ_c = 2π (κ_eff / K_sub)^(1/4)
equations.lean_code:
def cell_energy_hessian_num (c Gamma_l V_0 : Nat) : Nat :=
  3 * c * Gamma_l * V_0
def buckling_quartic_residual (q kappa_eff K_sub : Int) : Int :=
  kappa_eff * (q * q * q * q) - K_sub
theorem flat_monolayer_convexity_and_buckling_stationarity (c gl v0 : Nat) (q kappa_eff : Int) :
    cell_energy_hessian_num (c + 1) (gl + 1) (v0 + 1) > 0 ∧
    buckling_quartic_residual q kappa_eff (kappa_eff * (q * q * q * q)) = 0
equations.math_family: 3D Incompressible Vertex / Continuum Epithelial Energy with Apical (Gamma_a), Basal (Gamma_b), and Lateral (Gamma_l) Surface Tensions & Substrate Elastic Foundation
equations.variables: E''_cell(A^*): second derivative of single-cell energy at equilibrium area A^*; κ_eff: effective monolayer bending modulus; K_sub: stromal elastic foundation stiffness; λ_c: critical buckling wavelength
equations.role: Guarantees mechanical stability of flat epithelial sheets below the critical homeostatic buckling pressure and selects the characteristic folding wavelength λ_c = 2π(κ_eff / K_sub)^(1/4) above threshold
equations.source_citation: Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111(1):27-32 Eqs. (6)-(11)

equations.law_name: Apico-Basal Differential Tension & Spontaneous Curvature Sign Reversal Law
equations.formula: C_0 ∝ (Γ_a - Γ_b) / (Γ_l h_0),  C_0(Γ_b, Γ_a) = -C_0(Γ_a, Γ_b),  Γ_a > Γ_b ⇒ C_0 > 0 (apical constriction),  Γ_b > Γ_a ⇒ C_0 < 0 (basal constriction)
equations.lean_code:
def spontaneous_curvature_num (Gamma_a Gamma_b : Int) : Int :=
  Gamma_a - Gamma_b
theorem apicobasal_spontaneous_curvature_sign_reversal (Ga Gb : Int) (base dG : Nat) :
    spontaneous_curvature_num Ga Gb = -spontaneous_curvature_num Gb Ga ∧
    spontaneous_curvature_num Ga Ga = 0 ∧
    spontaneous_curvature_num (Int.ofNat (base + dG + 1)) (Int.ofNat base) > 0 ∧
    spontaneous_curvature_num (Int.ofNat base) (Int.ofNat (base + dG + 1)) < 0
equations.math_family: 3D Incompressible Vertex / Continuum Epithelial Energy with Apical (Gamma_a), Basal (Gamma_b), and Lateral (Gamma_l) Surface Tensions & Substrate Elastic Foundation
equations.variables: ΔΓ = Γ_a - Γ_b: apico-basal differential surface tension; C_0: spontaneous monolayer curvature; h_0: equilibrium cell height
equations.role: Explains how apical actomyosin enrichment (Γ_a > Γ_b) vs basal tension enrichment (Γ_b > Γ_a) reverses the polarity of epithelial folds and drives acinar closure when |C_0| exceeds substrate confinement
equations.source_citation: Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111(1):27-32 Eq. (5) & Fig. 2; Krajnc & Ziherl (2015) Phys. Rev. E 92:052713 Eq. (14); Sui et al. (2018) Nat. Commun. 9:4620

equations.law_name: Curved-Tube Surface Ratio & Isometric No-Scutoid Law (Pass 3, 3D polyhedral scutoid mesh)
equations.formula: s = R_b / R_a = (R_a + h_0) / R_a > 1 for h_0 > 0;  scutoid(cell) ⇔ N_apical(cell) ≠ N_basal(cell);  s = 1 ⇒ N_apical = N_basal ∀ cells ⇒ Σ scutoid = 0;  s_crest = 1 + h_0 κ_max
equations.lean_code:
def surface_ratio_numerator (R_a h_0 : Nat) : Nat :=
  R_a + h_0
def scutoid_indicator (apical basal : List Nat) : Nat :=
  if apical == basal then 0 else 1
def scutoid_count (cells : List (List Nat × List Nat)) : Nat :=
  cells.foldr (fun c acc => scutoid_indicator c.1 c.2 + acc) 0
theorem scutoid_count_isometric (nbrs : List (List Nat)) :
    scutoid_count (nbrs.map (fun n => (n, n))) = 0
theorem isometric_projection_has_no_scutoids (nbrs : List (List Nat)) (R_a h_0 : Nat) :
    scutoid_count (nbrs.map (fun n => (n, n))) = 0 ∧
    surface_ratio_numerator R_a (h_0 + 1) > R_a ∧
    surface_ratio_numerator R_a 0 = R_a ∧
    scutoid_indicator [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] = 0 ∧
    scutoid_indicator [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6] [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7] = 1
equations.math_family: 3D Incompressible Vertex / Continuum Epithelial Energy with Apical (Gamma_a), Basal (Gamma_b), and Lateral (Gamma_l) Surface Tensions & Substrate Elastic Foundation
equations.variables: R_a, R_b: apical and basal tube radii; h_0: Hannezo equilibrium cell height (Law 1); s: surface ratio; N_apical, N_basal: Voronoi neighbour sets of a cell on the two surfaces; κ_max: maximal apico-basal curvature of the buckled sheet
equations.role: Couples the Hannezo cell height to the Gómez-Gálvez scutoid mechanism: curvature (tube or fold crest) makes s ≠ 1, the radially projected basal tessellation is anisotropically stretched and apico-basal neighbour intercalations (scutoids) appear; flat sheets (s = 1) have none
equations.source_citation: Gómez-Gálvez et al. (2018) Nat. Commun. 9:2960 Figs. 1-2 (Voronoi tubes, scutoid number vs surface ratio); Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111:27-32 Eq. (4) for h_0

equations.law_name: Trivalent Torus Neighbour Conservation Law (Pass 3, Euler 2E = 6F on apical and basal surfaces)
equations.formula: 3 V = 2 E (trivalent) ∧ V − E + F = 0 (torus) ⇒ 2 E = 6 F ⇒ ⟨n⟩_apical = ⟨n⟩_basal = 6;  Σ_cells n_apical = Σ_cells n_basal
equations.lean_code:
def total_neighbor_count (E : Nat) : Nat :=
  2 * E
theorem trivalent_torus_neighbor_conservation
    (V_a E_a V_b E_b F : Nat)
    (h_triv_a : 3 * V_a = 2 * E_a) (h_euler_a : V_a + F = E_a)
    (h_triv_b : 3 * V_b = 2 * E_b) (h_euler_b : V_b + F = E_b) :
    total_neighbor_count E_a = 6 * F ∧
    total_neighbor_count E_b = 6 * F ∧
    total_neighbor_count E_a = total_neighbor_count E_b
equations.math_family: 3D Incompressible Vertex / Continuum Epithelial Energy with Apical (Gamma_a), Basal (Gamma_b), and Lateral (Gamma_l) Surface Tensions & Substrate Elastic Foundation
equations.variables: V, E, F: vertices, edges, faces (cells) of the doubly periodic Voronoi tessellation on the apical (a) or basal (b) surface; n: neighbour number per cell
equations.role: Guarantees that apico-basal intercalations redistribute but conserve the neighbour budget (mean 6 on both surfaces); checked numerically on every periodic mesh in `self_test` (checks 9) and reported as a MorphoEval measurement
equations.source_citation: Euler characteristic of the torus; Gómez-Gálvez et al. (2018) Nat. Commun. 9:2960 Fig. 3 (apical vs basal neighbour distributions)

models.organism: Galliform chicks — Japanese quail (Coturnix japonica; wild-type, recessive-black and Fawn strains), common pheasant (Phasianus colchicus), helmeted guineafowl (Numida meleagris), red-legged partridge (Alectoris rufa), and wild turkey (Meleagris gallopavo)

equations.law_name: Somite-Specified Dorsoventral Stripe Period Partition & Exogenous Agouti Bead Reciprocity
equations.formula: w_{\text{yellow}} + w_{\text{black}} = \Lambda_{\text{somite}}; \quad w_{\text{black}}(\Lambda, w_y + \Delta_{\text{bead}}) = w_{\text{black}}(\Lambda, w_y) - \Delta_{\text{bead}}
equations.lean_code:
def black_stripe_width (Lambda w_y : Int) : Int := Lambda - w_y
theorem somite_stripe_period_conservation_and_agouti_bead_expansion
    (Lambda w_y delta_bead : Int)
    (hw : 0 ≤ w_y) (hbead : delta_bead > 0) (hcap : w_y + delta_bead ≤ Lambda) :
    w_y + black_stripe_width Lambda w_y = Lambda ∧
    (w_y + delta_bead) + black_stripe_width Lambda (w_y + delta_bead) = Lambda ∧
    w_y + delta_bead > 0 ∧
    black_stripe_width Lambda (w_y + delta_bead) ≥ 0 ∧
    black_stripe_width Lambda (w_y + delta_bead) < black_stripe_width Lambda w_y ∧
    black_stripe_width Lambda (w_y + delta_bead) = black_stripe_width Lambda w_y - delta_bead := by
  unfold black_stripe_width; omega
equations.math_family: Somite-Prepatterned Stripe Spacing
equations.variables: Lambda: somite-specified dorsoventral stripe period (μm); w_y: Agouti-positive yellow pheomelanin stripe width; delta_bead: exogenous Agouti protein bead expansion
equations.role: Proves conservation of the somite-specified dorsoventral stripe period and exact reciprocal narrowing of adjacent black eumelanin bands upon exogenous Agouti bead implantation
equations.source_citation: Haupaix et al. (2018) Science 361(6408):eaar4777 Figs. 1 & 4

equations.law_name: Heterospecific Somite-to-Dermis Chimera Donor Autonomy Law
equations.formula: W_{\text{chimera}} = \alpha_{\text{donor}} w_{\text{donor}} + (1 - \alpha_{\text{donor}}) w_{\text{host}}; \quad w_{\text{donor}} > w_{\text{host}} \implies W_{\text{chimera}} > w_{\text{host}}
equations.lean_code:
def chimera_agouti_width_scaled (alpha_pct w_donor w_host : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_pct * w_donor + (100 - alpha_pct) * w_host
theorem interspecific_somite_graft_donor_autonomy
    (w_donor w_host : Int) (h_diff : w_donor > w_host) :
    chimera_agouti_width_scaled 100 w_donor w_host = 100 * w_donor ∧
    chimera_agouti_width_scaled 94 w_donor w_host > 100 * w_host ∧
    chimera_agouti_width_scaled 94 w_host w_donor < 100 * w_donor := by
  unfold chimera_agouti_width_scaled; omega
equations.math_family: Somite-Prepatterned Stripe Spacing
equations.variables: alpha_pct: percentage donor somite autonomy in chimeric dermis (≈94% in galliform chimeras); w_donor, w_host: donor and host species Agouti stripe widths
equations.role: Proves that heterospecific somite grafting between quail, pheasant, and guineafowl autonomously shifts host dermal Agouti stripe width toward the somite donor species
equations.source_citation: Haupaix et al. (2018) Science 361(6408):eaar4777 Fig. 3

equations.law_name: Agouti-MC1R Threshold Fate Switch & Connexin40 Melanocyte Reaction-Diffusion Instability
equations.formula: F_{\text{pigment}}(A) = \mathbb{I}(A \ge \theta_A); \quad \partial_t u = D_u \nabla^2 u + f(u,v) + \beta_A S_{\text{somite}}(y), \; \partial_t v = D_v \nabla^2 v + g(u,v)
equations.lean_code:
def mc1r_pigment_fate (A theta_A : Nat) : Nat := if A ≥ theta_A then 1 else 0
theorem agouti_mc1r_switch_and_cx40_turing_instability :
    mc1r_pigment_fate 75 50 = 1 ∧ mc1r_pigment_fate 0 50 = 0 ∧
    turing_trace 5 (-7) < 0 ∧ turing_det 5 (-7) (-8) 6 > 0 ∧
    turing_cross_term 5 (-7) 1 < 0 ∧ turing_cross_term 5 (-7) 20 > 0 := by decide
equations.math_family: Somite-Prepatterned Stripe Spacing
equations.variables: A: dermal Agouti concentration; theta_A: MC1R antagonism threshold; u, v: melanocyte gap-junction activator and long-range inhibitor; d_ratio = D_v/D_u
equations.role: Proves that Agouti threshold antagonism switches melanocytes from black eumelanin (0) to yellow pheomelanin (1) while differential diffusivity (d=20 vs d=1) amplifies periodic stripes aligned to the somite prepattern
equations.source_citation: Haupaix et al. (2018) Science 361:eaar4777 Fig. 3; Inaba et al. (2019) PNAS 116:6884-6890 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Lin (2013) Ring-Niche Chevron Geometry on the Opened Feather-Follicle Cylinder
equations.formula: s_{\text{edge}}(\ell) = s_0 + k\,|\ell|, \quad k = \frac{v_z}{r_f\,\omega}; \quad s(\ell) = s(-\ell), \; s(\ell)|_{k=0} = s_0, \; s_0 \le s(\ell), \; k < k' \wedge \ell \ne 0 \implies s_k(\ell) < s_{k'}(\ell)
equations.lean_code:
def chevron_s (s0 k ell : Int) : Int := s0 + k * (Int.natAbs ell : Int)
theorem ring_niche_chevron_geometry (s0 k ell : Int) (hk : 0 ≤ k) :
    chevron_s s0 k ell = chevron_s s0 k (-ell) ∧
    chevron_s s0 0 ell = s0 ∧
    s0 ≤ chevron_s s0 k ell ∧
    (∀ k', k < k' → ell ≠ 0 → chevron_s s0 k ell < chevron_s s0 k' ell) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [chevron_s, Int.natAbs_neg]
  · simp [chevron_s]
  · unfold chevron_s; have h := Int.mul_nonneg hk (Int.natCast_nonneg (Int.natAbs ell)); omega
  · intro k' hk' hell; unfold chevron_s
    have hpos : (0 : Int) < (Int.natAbs ell : Int) := by omega
    have h := Int.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hk' hpos; omega
equations.math_family: Somite-Prepatterned Stripe Spacing
equations.variables: s: proximodistal position from the feather tip (growth-time axis); ell: signed lateral/azimuthal distance from the anterior rachis on the cylinder opened at the posterior new-barb locus; k = v_z/(r_f omega): helical pitch of a pigment switch propagating around the ring niche at angular rate omega while melanocytes rise at v_z
equations.role: Proves that a pigment switch propagating around the Lin (2013) ring niche yields a mirror-symmetric chevron band on the opened follicle whose apex sits on the rachis and whose opening grows monotonically with the helical pitch, degenerating to a transverse bar for a synchronous ring (k = 0)
equations.source_citation: Lin et al. (2013) Science 340(6139):1442-1445 Fig. 1B, Fig. 2B, fig. S9

equations.law_name: Haupaix (2018) Agouti-Dose Yellow-Pulse Duration & Feather-Type Law on the Follicle Niche
equations.formula: A(\tau) = A_i - a + a\cos(2\pi(\tau - \tfrac12)); \quad \text{type} = \mathbb{I}(A_i \ge \theta_A) + \mathbb{I}(A_i - 2a \ge \theta_A) \in \{0: b,\; 1: y,\; 2: \text{fully pheomelanic}\}; \quad \text{duty} = \tfrac{1}{\pi}\arccos\!\big(\tfrac{\theta_A - (A_i - a)}{a}\big)
equations.lean_code:
def mc1r_pigment_fate_int (A theta_A : Int) : Nat := if A ≥ theta_A then 1 else 0
def feather_type (A a theta_A : Int) : Nat :=
  mc1r_pigment_fate_int (A + a) theta_A + mc1r_pigment_fate_int (A - a) theta_A
theorem agouti_pulse_duration_feather_type (A a theta_A : Int) (ha : 0 < a) :
    (A - a ≥ theta_A → feather_type A a theta_A = 2) ∧
    (A + a < theta_A → feather_type A a theta_A = 0) ∧
    (theta_A - a ≤ A ∧ A < theta_A + a → feather_type A a theta_A = 1) ∧
    (∀ A', A ≤ A' → feather_type A a theta_A ≤ feather_type A' a theta_A) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro h; simp only [feather_type, mc1r_pigment_fate_int]; split <;> (try split) <;> omega
  · intro h; simp only [feather_type, mc1r_pigment_fate_int]; split <;> (try split) <;> omega
  · intro h; simp only [feather_type, mc1r_pigment_fate_int]; split <;> (try split) <;> omega
  · intro A' h; simp only [feather_type, mc1r_pigment_fate_int]; repeat (first | omega | split)
equations.math_family: Somite-Prepatterned Stripe Spacing
equations.variables: A_i: dermal agouti dose read by the follicle ring niche from the body-wide field u(x_i, y_i) (Lean A = A_i - a); a: amplitude of the transient yellow-pulse modulation (peak A_i at mid-growth, trough A_i - 2a at tip and base); theta_A: MC1R antagonism threshold; duty: relative yellow band length
