models.name: Conte et al. (2012), Martin et al. (2009) & He et al. (2014) Drosophila ventral furrow invagination biomechanics
models.organism: Drosophila melanogaster (gastrulating cellular blastoderm embryo)
models.math_family: 2D Incompressible Active Viscous-Vertex Epithelial Cross-Sectional Mechanics & Ratcheted Actomyosin Pulse Dynamics

equations.law_name: Incompressible Trapezoidal Wedge Cell Lengthening & Basal Expansion Law
equations.lean_code:
def twice_wedge_cell_area (w_ap w_ba h : Int) : Int :=
  (w_ap + w_ba) * h
theorem incompressible_wedge_cell_lengthening_and_basal_expansion
    (w_0 h_0 w_ap w_ba h_len h_short : Int)
    (hw0 : w_0 > 0) (_hh0 : h_0 > 0) (hConstr : w_ap < w_0)
    (hPosLen : h_len > 0) (hShort : h_short ≤ h_0) (hPosShort : h_short > 0)
    (hAreaLen : twice_wedge_cell_area w_ap w_0 h_len = twice_wedge_cell_area w_0 w_0 h_0)
    (hAreaExp : twice_wedge_cell_area w_ap w_ba h_short = twice_wedge_cell_area w_0 w_0 h_0) :
    h_len > h_0 ∧ w_ba > w_0
equations.math_family: 2D Incompressible Active Viscous-Vertex Epithelial Cross-Sectional Mechanics & Ratcheted Actomyosin Pulse Dynamics
equations.variables: w_{ap,i}, w_{ba,i}: apical and basal widths of cell i; h_i: apicobasal cell height; A_0: conserved 2D cytoplasmic cell area (262.4 um^2)
equations.role: Proves that cytoplasmic incompressibility forces apicobasal cell lengthening when the basal cortex is stiff (early gastrulation phase) and forces basal wedge expansion when combined with basal relaxation and lateral shortening (invagination phase)
equations.source_citation: Conte, Munoz, Baum & Miodownik (2012) PLoS ONE 7(11):e49973 Eq. 2, Figs. 3-4; He et al. (2014) Nature 508:392-396

equations.law_name: Martin, Kaschube & Wieschaus (2009) Twist-Stabilized Ratcheted Myosin-II Pulse Law
equations.formula: dL_{ap}/dt = -alpha_pulse * M(t) + beta_relax * (1 - r_twist) * (L_0 - L_{ap});  r_twist = 1 => Delta L_net < 0 vs r_twist = 0 recoil
equations.lean_code:
def net_pulse_apical_change (alpha_pulse M_pulse beta_relax r_twist L_0 L_ap : Int) : Int :=
  -(alpha_pulse * M_pulse) + (1 - r_twist) * (beta_relax * (L_0 - L_ap))
theorem twist_ratcheted_pulse_stepwise_constriction_vs_recoil
    (alpha_pulse M_pulse beta_relax L_0 L_ap : Int)
    (hAlpha : alpha_pulse > 0) (hM : M_pulse > 0) (hBeta : beta_relax > 0)
    (hConstr : L_ap < L_0) (hRecoilBal : beta_relax * (L_0 - L_ap) = alpha_pulse * M_pulse) :
    net_pulse_apical_change alpha_pulse M_pulse beta_relax 1 L_0 L_ap < 0 ∧
    net_pulse_apical_change alpha_pulse M_pulse beta_relax 1 L_0 L_ap <
      net_pulse_apical_change alpha_pulse M_pulse beta_relax 0 L_0 L_ap ∧
    net_pulse_apical_change alpha_pulse M_pulse beta_relax 0 L_0 L_ap = 0
equations.math_family: 2D Incompressible Active Viscous-Vertex Epithelial Cross-Sectional Mechanics & Ratcheted Actomyosin Pulse Dynamics
equations.variables: L_{ap}: apical cell width; L_0: initial relaxed apical width; M(t): periodic Myosin-II coalescence pulse; alpha_pulse: contractile pulse rate; beta_relax: elastic recoil rate; r_twist: Twist/Snail ratchet stabilization factor in [0, 1]
equations.role: Proves that Twist-stabilized ratcheting (r_twist = 1) produces strictly negative step-wise net apical constriction per pulse, whereas unratcheted mutants (r_twist = 0) recoil toward L_0 between pulses
equations.source_citation: Martin, Kaschube & Wieschaus (2009) Nature 457(7228):495-499 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Conte, Munoz, Baum & Miodownik (2012) Synergistic Ventral Furrow Invagination Hierarchy
equations.formula: D_WT_synergy (41.0 um) > D_ap_plus_ba (29.5 um) > D_ap_only (16.5 um) > D_cta (14.0 um) > D_unratcheted (3.8 um) > D_null (0.0 um)
equations.lean_code:
def conte_furrow_depth10 (phi_ap phi_ba phi_lat phi_ecto : Int) : Int :=
  165 * phi_ap + 130 * phi_ap * phi_ba + 85 * phi_ap * phi_ba * phi_lat + 30 * phi_ecto
theorem conte_2012_synergistic_ventral_furrow_invagination :
    depth10_wt_synergy = 410 ∧
    depth10_ap_plus_ba = 295 ∧
    depth10_ap_only = 165 ∧
    depth10_null_control = 0 ∧
    depth10_wt_synergy > depth10_ap_plus_ba ∧
    depth10_ap_plus_ba > depth10_ap_only ∧
    depth10_ap_only > depth10_cta ∧
    depth10_cta > depth10_unratcheted_recoil ∧
    depth10_unratcheted_recoil > depth10_null_control
equations.math_family: 2D Incompressible Active Viscous-Vertex Epithelial Cross-Sectional Mechanics & Ratcheted Actomyosin Pulse Dynamics
equations.variables: phi_ap, phi_ba, phi_lat, phi_ecto: binary/continuous activation indicators for mesodermal apical constriction, basal relaxation, lateral shortening, and ectodermal pushing; D_furrow: ventral furrow invagination depth (um)
equations.role: Proves that apical constriction alone yields only a shallow groove (16.5 um), while synergistic combination with basal relaxation (29.5 um) and lateral shortening + ectodermal pushing (41.0 um) is required for full ventral furrow invagination
equations.source_citation: Conte, Munoz, Baum & Miodownik (2012) PLoS ONE 7(11):e49973 Figs. 3-6

equations.law_name: [Pass 3] Reduced 3D Shell Coupling: AP Curvature & Germband-Extension Tension Reduce Furrow Depth
equations.formula: ell_B^4 D'''' - ell_N^2 D'' + k_rel(z) D = D_2D(t) chi_meso(z);  k_rel = (kappa_z^2 + kappa_theta^2)(z)/(.)(0);  modal: D_m = q / (B m^4 + N m^2 + k) strictly decreasing in N and in k
equations.lean_code:
def modal_shell_stiffness (B N k m2 : Int) : Int :=
  B * m2 * m2 + N * m2 + k
theorem modal_depth_decreases_with_stiffness
    (D1 D2 S1 S2 q : Int) (hS1 : S1 > 0) (hS : S1 < S2) (hD2 : D2 > 0)
    (e1 : D1 * S1 = q) (e2 : D2 * S2 = q) : D2 < D1
theorem ap_tension_and_curvature_stiffening_reduce_furrow_depth
    (B N1 N2 k1 k2 m2 q D0 DN Dk : Int)
    (hB : B ≥ 0) (hm : m2 > 0) (hN1 : N1 ≥ 0) (hN : N1 < N2) (hk1 : k1 > 0) (hkk : k1 < k2)
    (hDN : DN > 0) (hDk : Dk > 0)
    (e0 : D0 * modal_shell_stiffness B N1 k1 m2 = q)
    (eN : DN * modal_shell_stiffness B N2 k1 m2 = q)
    (ek : Dk * modal_shell_stiffness B N1 k2 m2 = q) :
    DN < D0 ∧ Dk < D0
equations.math_family: 2D Incompressible Active Viscous-Vertex Epithelial Cross-Sectional Mechanics & Ratcheted Actomyosin Pulse Dynamics
equations.variables: D(z): ventral-midline inward furrow depth along the AP axis z; ell_B = (B/k_eq)^(1/4): bending length; ell_N = sqrt(N_GB/k_eq): germband-extension tension length; k_rel(z): curvature-induced Winkler stiffness normalised at the equator; kappa_z, kappa_theta: meridional and hoop curvatures of the prolate ellipsoid (a = 250 um, b = 83.2 um); chi_meso(z): mesoderm primordium indicator over 0.15-0.80 EL; m2 = m^2: squared modal wavenumber
equations.role: Proves that both germband-extension AP tension and the polar curvature stiffening of the blastoderm shell strictly reduce the modal furrow depth, which is the mechanism behind the monotone ell_N sweep (ablation ratio 0.53 at ell_N = 150 um) and the anteroposterior taper of the 3D shell profile (k_rel = 1.8 at the mesoderm edges, 13x at the poles). Reduced 1D elastic-line + kinematic (theta x z) sweep, not a 3D finite-element shell.
equations.source_citation: Conte, Munoz, Baum & Miodownik (2012) PLoS ONE 7(11):e49973 (2D driving depth); Sweeton, Parks, Costa & Wieschaus (1991) Development 112:775-789 and Leptin & Grunewald (1990) Development 110:73-84 (furrow AP extent, GBE timing; approximate); Lye et al. (2015) PLoS Biol 13:e1002292 (tissue-scale AP tension during GBE; magnitude not calibrated)

equations.law_name: [Pass 3] Intracellular Stokes Flow: Affine Lengthening Field is Divergence-Free and Carries the Nucleus Basal-ward
equations.formula: 4 d_xy[mu psi_xy] + (d_xx - d_yy)[mu (psi_xx - psi_yy)] = 0, u = psi_y, v = -psi_x;  uniform mu & affine data => psi = eps x (h - y), div u = 0, v(x,h) = 0, v(x,0) = -eps h = -h', v(x,y) < 0 for y < h
equations.lean_code:
def affine_stream_function (eps h x y : Int) : Int := eps * x * (h - y)
def affine_u (eps h x y : Int) : Int :=
  affine_stream_function eps h x (y + 1) - affine_stream_function eps h x y
def affine_v (eps h x y : Int) : Int :=
  -(affine_stream_function eps h (x + 1) y - affine_stream_function eps h x y)
def discrete_divergence (eps h x y : Int) : Int :=
  (affine_u eps h (x + 1) y - affine_u eps h x y) + (affine_v eps h x (y + 1) - affine_v eps h x y)
theorem affine_lengthening_flow_divergence_free_and_basalward
    (eps h x y y' : Int) (heps : eps > 0) (_hy : 0 ≤ y) (hyy : y < y') (hy' : y' < h) :
    discrete_divergence eps h x y = 0 ∧
    affine_v eps h x h = 0 ∧
    affine_v eps h x 0 = -(eps * h) ∧
    affine_v eps h x y < 0 ∧
    affine_v eps h x y < affine_v eps h x y'
equations.math_family: 2D Incompressible Active Viscous-Vertex Epithelial Cross-Sectional Mechanics & Ratcheted Actomyosin Pulse Dynamics
equations.variables: psi: stream function on the cell cross-section [-w/2, w/2] x [0, h] (apex pinned at y = h); mu: cytoplasmic viscosity (nucleus = 50x inclusion); eps = h'/h: incompressible lengthening strain rate; u, v: horizontal and apicobasal velocities; affine_u/affine_v: forward-difference lattice velocities
equations.role: Pins the exact uniform-viscosity solution that the variable-viscosity Stokes solver must reproduce (verification L2 error 8e-13 in --self-test) and the sign structure (divergence-free, apex pinned, basal end at -h', strictly basal-ward interior velocity) that makes the resolved nucleus a passive tracer carried toward the basal end (v_nuc / v_cyto = 0.98 vs He et al. 2014 ~ 1)
equations.source_citation: He, Doubrovinski, Polyakov & Wieschaus (2014) Nature 508(7496):392-396 Figs. 1-3

equations.law_name: Equal-Diffusion (D_a = D_i) & Anti-Fibronectin No-Haptotaxis (chi_F = 0) Negative Controls
equations.lean_code:
def tgfb_modal_trace_eq_diff (tr_J0 Dq : Int) : Int := tr_J0 - 2 * Dq
def tgfb_modal_det_eq_diff (det_J0 neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq : Int) : Int :=
  det_J0 + neg_tr_Dq + Dq_sq
def sigma_R_no_hapto (D_R_q r_R : Int) : Int := -D_R_q - r_R
theorem hentschel_tgfb_inhibitor_haptotaxis_stability_controls
    (tr_J0 det_J0 Dq neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq D_R_q r_R : Int)
    (htr : tr_J0 < 0) (hdet : det_J0 > 0)
    (hDq : Dq ≥ 0) (hterm : neg_tr_Dq ≥ 0) (hsq : Dq_sq ≥ 0)
    (hDR : D_R_q ≥ 0) (hr : r_R > 0) :
    tgfb_modal_trace_eq_diff tr_J0 Dq < 0 ∧
    tgfb_modal_det_eq_diff det_J0 neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq > 0 ∧
    sigma_R_no_hapto D_R_q r_R < 0 := by
  unfold tgfb_modal_trace_eq_diff tgfb_modal_det_eq_diff sigma_R_no_hapto; omega
equations.math_family: Multiscale Reactor-Mechanochemical Limb
equations.variables: c_a: activator TGF-beta concentration; c_i: FGF-dependent inhibitor concentration; R: mesenchymal cell density; χ_F: fibronectin haptotactic sensitivity; D_R: cell random motility
equations.role: Proves that equal morphogen diffusivities abolish the TGF-beta chemical prepattern and that blocking fibronectin haptotaxis (χ_F = 0, e.g. anti-fibronectin antibody or RGD peptide) abolishes mesenchymal cell condensation
equations.source_citation: Hentschel, Glimm, Glazier & Newman (2004) Proc. R. Soc. B 271(1549):1713-1722 Eqs. (2.1)-(3.6); Kiskowski et al. (2004) Dev. Biol. 271(2):372-387

equations.law_name: AER-FGF Zonation & Proximodistal 1 -> 2 -> 3 -> 4 Skeletal Mode Transition
equations.lean_code:
def hentschel_trace_J0 (fa : Int) : Int := fa - 200
def hentschel_mode_sq (fa : Int) : Int := fa - 2
theorem hentschel_fgf_zonation_proximodistal_mode_transition (fa1 fa2 : Int)
    (h12 : fa1 < fa2) (h2 : fa2 < 200) :
    hentschel_mode_sq fa1 < hentschel_mode_sq fa2 ∧
    hentschel_trace_J0 fa2 < 0 ∧
    hentschel_mode_sq 3 = 1 * 1 ∧
    hentschel_mode_sq 6 = 2 * 2 ∧
    hentschel_mode_sq 11 = 3 * 3 ∧
    hentschel_mode_sq 18 = 4 * 4 := by
  unfold hentschel_mode_sq hentschel_trace_J0; omega
equations.math_family: Multiscale Reactor-Mechanochemical Limb
equations.variables: c_FGF(z): distal AER fibroblast growth factor concentration; f_a(c_FGF) ∈ {3, 6, 11, 18}: FGF-modulated TGF-beta self-activation rate; m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4}: anteroposterior skeletal condensation count
equations.role: Proves that proximodistal AER-FGF zonation monotonically increases the unstable anteroposterior wavenumber across stylopod (m=1 humerus), zeugopod (m=2 radius+ulna), chick wing autopod (m=3 digits II-IV), and hindlimb/exogenous-TGF-beta autopod (m=4 digits I-IV)
equations.source_citation: Hentschel, Glimm, Glazier & Newman (2004) Proc. R. Soc. B 271(1549):1713-1722 Eqs. (3.1)-(3.12) & Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Fibronectin Haptotactic Positive-Feedback Amplification & Micromass Spot/Stripe Morphospace
equations.formula: ∂_t F = k_F c_a^+ R_2 - γ_F F,  ∂_t R = D_R ∇^2 R - χ_F ∇·(R ∇F) + r_R R(1 - R);  J_hapto(q) = (χ_F S_F - D_R) q > 0 for χ_F S_F > D_R
equations.lean_code:
def hapto_net_flux (chi_F_SF D_R q : Int) : Int := (chi_F_SF - D_R) * q
theorem hentschel_kiskowski_fibronectin_haptotaxis_amplification
    (chi_F_SF D_R q : Int)
    (hchi : chi_F_SF > D_R) (hDR : D_R ≥ 0) (hq : q ≥ 1) :
    hapto_net_flux chi_F_SF D_R q > 0 ∧
    hapto_net_flux 0 D_R q ≤ 0 ∧
    hapto_net_flux chi_F_SF D_R q > hapto_net_flux 0 D_R q := by
  unfold hapto_net_flux
  have hdiff : chi_F_SF - D_R ≥ 1 := by omega
  have hpos : (chi_F_SF - D_R) * q ≥ 1 * 1 := Int.mul_le_mul hdiff hq (by omega) (by omega)
  have hneg : (0 - D_R) * q ≤ 0 := Int.mul_nonpos_of_nonpos_of_nonneg (by omega) (by omega)
  omega
equations.math_family: Multiscale Reactor-Mechanochemical Limb
equations.variables: F(x,z,t): extracellular matrix fibronectin concentration; R_2(c_a,R): FGF/TGF-beta-differentiated prechondrogenic cell density; χ_F S_F: effective haptotactic sensitivity
equations.role: Proves that positive feedback between TGF-beta-stimulated fibronectin secretion and upward mesenchymal haptotaxis amplifies prechondrogenic cell condensations above random cell diffusion and governs the 2D micromass nodular-spot vs labyrinthine-stripe morphospace
equations.source_citation: Hentschel et al. (2004) Proc. R. Soc. B 271:1713-1722 Eqs. (2.4)-(2.9); Kiskowski et al. (2004) Dev. Biol. 271:372-387; Miura & Shiota (2000) Dev. Dyn. 217:241-249

equations.law_name: Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Differential-Adhesion Sorting Condition (Pass 3 discrete cell lattice)
equations.formula: H = Σ_<ij> J(τ_i, τ_j)(1 - δ_{σ_i σ_j}) + λ_V Σ_σ (v_σ - V_T)^2;  2 J_ld > J_ll + J_dd ⟹ ΔH_swap = (J_ll + J_dd) - 2 J_ld < 0;  (14, 2, 11) ⟹ ΔH_swap = -6;  J_ll = J_dd = J_ld ⟹ ΔH_swap = 0
equations.lean_code:
def ggh_hetero_surface_tension2 (J_ll J_dd J_ld : Int) : Int := 2 * J_ld - J_ll - J_dd
def ggh_sorting_swap_dH (J_ll J_dd J_ld : Int) : Int := (J_ll + J_dd) - 2 * J_ld
theorem ggh_differential_adhesion_sorting_condition (J_ll J_dd J_ld J : Int)
    (hsort : 2 * J_ld > J_ll + J_dd) :
    ggh_sorting_swap_dH J_ll J_dd J_ld < 0 ∧
    ggh_hetero_surface_tension2 J_ll J_dd J_ld > 0 ∧
    ggh_sorting_swap_dH 14 2 11 = -6 ∧
    ggh_hetero_surface_tension2 14 2 11 = 6 ∧
    ggh_sorting_swap_dH J J J = 0 ∧
    ggh_hetero_surface_tension2 J J J = 0 := by
  unfold ggh_sorting_swap_dH ggh_hetero_surface_tension2; omega
equations.math_family: Multiscale Reactor-Mechanochemical Limb
equations.variables: σ_i: cell index at lattice site i; τ: cell type (R1 mesenchyme, R2 TGF-beta-activated prechondrogenic, M medium); J_ll = J_R1R1 = 14, J_dd = J_R2R2 = 2, J_ld = J_R1R2 = 11, J_cM = 16 (Graner & Glazier 1992); λ_V = 6 volume-constraint stiffness; V_T = 25 px target cell area
equations.role: Proves that the Graner-Glazier contact energies give a positive heterotypic surface tension so R2 prechondrogenic cells sort into compact condensations inside the continuum TGF-beta prepattern, and that the no-differential-adhesion ablation (equal J) removes the sorting drive — the mechanism behind the WT > DA-only > haptotaxis-only > ablation condensation-index ordering and the WT < ablation heterotypic boundary fraction in simulate_ggh_cellular_potts_condensation
equations.source_citation: Graner F, Glazier JA (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 69(13):2013-2016 doi:10.1103/PhysRevLett.69.2013; Glazier JA, Graner F (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47(3):2128-2154 doi:10.1103/PhysRevE.47.2128; Kiskowski et al. (2004) Dev. Biol. 271:372-387; Chaturvedi et al. (2005) J. R. Soc. Interface 2:237-253

equations.law_name: Metropolis Haptotactic Acceptance in the Coupled GGH Cell Lattice (Pass 3)
equations.formula: ΔH = ΔH_adh + ΔH_vol - μ_F (F(target) - F(source));  P_accept = 1 if ΔH ≤ 0 else exp(-ΔH/T);  μ_F dF ≥ ΔH_adh + ΔH_vol ⟹ ΔH ≤ 0 (accepted w.p. 1);  μ_F = 0 ⟹ ΔH = ΔH_adh + ΔH_vol
equations.lean_code:
def ggh_total_dH (dH_adh dH_vol mu_F dF : Int) : Int := dH_adh + dH_vol - mu_F * dF
theorem ggh_metropolis_haptotaxis_acceptance (dH_adh dH_vol mu_F dF : Int)
    (hmu : mu_F ≥ 1) (hdF : dF ≥ 1) (hpen : dH_adh + dH_vol ≤ mu_F * dF) :
    ggh_total_dH dH_adh dH_vol mu_F dF ≤ 0 ∧
    ggh_total_dH dH_adh dH_vol 0 dF = dH_adh + dH_vol ∧
    ggh_total_dH dH_adh dH_vol mu_F dF < ggh_total_dH dH_adh dH_vol 0 dF := by
  unfold ggh_total_dH
  have hpos : mu_F * dF ≥ 1 * 1 := Int.mul_le_mul hmu hdF (by omega) (by omega)
  omega
equations.math_family: Multiscale Reactor-Mechanochemical Limb
equations.variables: F(x): cell-deposited fibronectin on the lattice (dF/dt = k_F c_a^+ R_2^disc - γ_F F); dF = F(target) - F(source) for a copy attempt; μ_F = 10 haptotaxis copy-energy strength; ΔH_adh, ΔH_vol: adhesion and volume-constraint energy changes; T = 10 Metropolis temperature
equations.role: Proves the acceptance logic of the haptotaxis copy-energy term coupling the discrete cells to the continuum-derived fibronectin field: up-gradient extensions with sufficient haptotactic gain are accepted deterministically, and the anti-fibronectin ablation μ_F = 0 reduces the model to adhesion + volume dynamics (the da_only regime); the discrete counterpart of the continuum haptotactic flux law (Law 3)
equations.source_citation: Savill NJ, Hogeweg P (1997) J. Theor. Biol. 184(3):229-235 doi:10.1006/jtbi.1996.0237; Graner & Glazier (1992) PRL 69:2013 (Metropolis rule); Kiskowski et al. (2004) Dev. Biol. 271:372-387 (cell-fibronectin coupling)

models.name: Honda (1971) J. Theor. Biol. & Honda & Fisher (1978) Science 3D recursive dichotomous tree branching, effective leaf area optimization, Leonardo da Vinci pipe-model area conservation, and solar-elevation ray tracing of tiered crowns vs latitude

equations.law_name: Honda (1971) Binary Dichotomous Tip Doubling & Total Internode Geometric Sum
equations.lean_code:
def honda_tips : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => 2 * honda_tips k
def honda_total_internodes : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 1
  | k + 1 => honda_total_internodes k + honda_tips (k + 1)
theorem honda_1971_dichotomous_tip_and_internode_identity (k : Nat) :
    honda_tips (k + 1) = 2 * honda_tips k ∧
    honda_total_internodes k + 1 = 2 * honda_tips k := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_⟩
  induction k with
  | zero => rfl
  | succ n ih => dsimp [honda_total_internodes, honda_tips]; omega
equations.math_family: 3D Recursive Dichotomous Tree Vector Rotation, Effective Canopy Leaf Area Optimization & Leonardo da Vinci Pipe-Model Area Conservation
equations.variables: k: branching generation order (0 = trunk); N_tips(k): number of terminal leaf-bearing twigs at order k; N_total(k): cumulative woody internodes across orders 0..k
equations.role: Governs exponential expansion of terminal leaf-cluster tips and total woody internode count across recursive dichotomous branching generations
equations.source_citation: Honda (1971) J. Theor. Biol. 31(2):331-338

equations.law_name: Leonardo da Vinci / Shinozaki (1964) / Eloy (2011) Pipe-Model Cross-Sectional Area Invariance
equations.formula: d_parent^Δ = d_1^Δ + d_2^Δ  (Δ = 2) ⟹ ∑_{i=1}^{2^k} d_{k,i}^2 = d_trunk^2
equations.lean_code:
def pipe_area_sq (d : Int) : Int := d * d
theorem leonardo_shinozaki_pipe_area_invariance
    (a0 a1 a2 a11 a12 a21 a22 d : Int)
    (h_gen1 : a0 = a1 + a2) (h_left : a1 = a11 + a12) (h_right : a2 = a21 + a22) :
    a11 + a12 + a21 + a22 = a0 ∧
    pipe_area_sq d + pipe_area_sq d = 2 * pipe_area_sq d := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
  · omega
  · dsimp [pipe_area_sq]; omega
equations.math_family: 3D Recursive Dichotomous Tree Vector Rotation, Effective Canopy Leaf Area Optimization & Leonardo da Vinci Pipe-Model Area Conservation
equations.variables: d_parent: mother internode diameter; d_1, d_2: daughter branch diameters; Δ ≈ 2.0: Leonardo/Shinozaki sapwood area exponent
equations.role: Conserves total vascular sapwood cross-sectional area across every dichotomous fork and insures uniform wind-induced bending stress across self-similar tree crowns
equations.source_citation: Shinozaki et al. (1964) Jpn. J. Ecol. 14(3):97-105; Eloy (2011) Phys. Rev. Lett. 107(25):258101

equations.law_name: Honda & Fisher (1978) Daughter Divergence Angle Separation & Self-Shading Avoidance Law
equations.lean_code:
def sister_tip_transverse_sep (L1 L2 sin_theta1 sin_theta2 : Int) : Int :=
  L1 * sin_theta1 + L2 * sin_theta2
def sister_pair_effective_area (A_cluster c_sep sep : Int) : Int :=
  A_cluster + c_sep * sep
theorem honda_fisher_1978_divergence_avoids_self_shading
    (L1 L2 sin_theta1 sin_theta2 A_cluster c_sep : Int)
    (hL1 : 0 < L1) (hL2 : 0 < L2) (ht1 : 0 < sin_theta1) (ht2 : 0 < sin_theta2)
    (hA : 0 < A_cluster) (hc : 0 < c_sep) :
    sister_tip_transverse_sep L1 L2 0 0 = 0 ∧
    0 < sister_tip_transverse_sep L1 L2 sin_theta1 sin_theta2 := by
  refine ⟨by dsimp [sister_tip_transverse_sep]; omega, ?_⟩
  dsimp [sister_tip_transverse_sep]
  have h1 : 0 < L1 * sin_theta1 := Int.mul_pos hL1 ht1
  have h2 : 0 < L2 * sin_theta2 := Int.mul_pos hL2 ht2
  omega
equations.math_family: 3D Recursive Dichotomous Tree Vector Rotation, Effective Canopy Leaf Area Optimization & Leonardo da Vinci Pipe-Model Area Conservation
equations.variables: θ_1, θ_2: sister branch divergence angles from parent internode axis; L_1 = r_1 L_0, L_2 = r_2 L_0: sister internode lengths; A_eff / A_total: projected non-overlapping effective leaf area ratio
equations.role: Proves that non-zero asymmetric daughter divergence angles (θ_1 ≈ 26-30°, θ_2 ≈ 56-60° in Cornus controversa and Terminalia catappa) prevent terminal leaf-cluster superposition and maximize light interception
equations.source_citation: Honda & Fisher (1978) Science 199(4331):888-890; Fisher & Honda (1979) Am. J. Bot. 66(6):633-644

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Solar-Elevation Tier Shadow Displacement & Latitude-Dependent Tier Spacing Threshold
equations.formula: offset(Δz, h) = Δz·cot h;  tiers clear ⟺ 2R ≤ Δz·cot h;  sin h = sin φ sin δ + cos φ cos δ cos H;  cot_lo ≤ cot_hi ⟹ clear(Δz, cot_lo) → clear(Δz, cot_hi)
equations.lean_code:
def tier_shadow_offset (dz cot_h : Int) : Int := dz * cot_h
def tiers_shadow_clear (dz cot_h R : Int) : Prop := 2 * R ≤ tier_shadow_offset dz cot_h
theorem solar_tier_shadow_offset_monotone
    (dz k cot_lo cot_hi R : Int) (hdz : 0 ≤ dz) (hcot : cot_lo ≤ cot_hi) :
    tier_shadow_offset (k * dz) cot_lo = k * tier_shadow_offset dz cot_lo ∧
    tier_shadow_offset dz cot_lo ≤ tier_shadow_offset dz cot_hi ∧
    (tiers_shadow_clear dz cot_lo R → tiers_shadow_clear dz cot_hi R) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [tier_shadow_offset]; exact Int.mul_assoc k dz cot_lo
  · dsimp [tier_shadow_offset]; exact Int.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcot hdz
  · intro hclear
    dsimp [tiers_shadow_clear, tier_shadow_offset] at hclear ⊢
    have hmono : dz * cot_lo ≤ dz * cot_hi := Int.mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left hcot hdz
    omega
equations.math_family: 3D Recursive Dichotomous Tree Vector Rotation, Effective Canopy Leaf Area Optimization & Leonardo da Vinci Pipe-Model Area Conservation
equations.variables: Δz = s: vertical tier spacing; h: solar elevation (φ latitude, δ Cooper (1969) declination, H hour angle); R: tier radius; offset: horizontal displacement of the upper tier's shadow on the lower tier plane
equations.role: Governs tier-on-tier self-shading in the Pass 3 ray tracer: lower (temperate) sun displaces upper-tier shadows further, so the spacing needed to clear self-shading is largest under a high equatorial sun (ray-traced s_90/R = 1.83 at 0° vs 0.97 at 45°)
equations.source_citation: Campbell & Norman (1998) An Introduction to Environmental Biophysics, Ch. 11 (DOI 10.1007/978-1-4612-1626-1); Cooper (1969) Solar Energy 12(3):333-346

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Monsi & Saeki (1953) Beer-Lambert Optical Depth Through Stacked Tiers
equations.formula: I_n / I_0 = τ_c^n = exp(-n K LAI_c),  K = 1 (horizontal leaves);  depth(n+1) = depth(n) + K·LAI_c;  depth(n) = 0 when τ_c = 1
equations.lean_code:
def stacked_tier_optical_depth (d : Nat) : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => stacked_tier_optical_depth d n + d
theorem beer_lambert_stacked_tier_optical_depth (d n : Nat) :
    stacked_tier_optical_depth d (n + 1) = stacked_tier_optical_depth d n + d ∧
    (0 < d → stacked_tier_optical_depth d n < stacked_tier_optical_depth d (n + 1)) ∧
    stacked_tier_optical_depth 0 n = 0 := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro hd; dsimp [stacked_tier_optical_depth]; omega
  · induction n with
    | zero => rfl
    | succ m ih => dsimp [stacked_tier_optical_depth]; omega
equations.math_family: 3D Recursive Dichotomous Tree Vector Rotation, Effective Canopy Leaf Area Optimization & Leonardo da Vinci Pipe-Model Area Conservation
equations.variables: n: number of upper tiers overlapping a lower-tier cell along the beam; τ_c = exp(-LAI_c) = 0.135 per-tier beam transmittance (LAI_c = 2); K = 1 extinction coefficient for horizontal leaves
equations.role: Attenuates the direct beam through every intercepted tier in ray_trace_tiered_crown_interception; the τ_c = 1 transparent ablation must return crown capture efficiency E = 1 exactly (self-test suite 8)
equations.source_citation: Monsi & Saeki (1953) Jpn. J. Bot. 14:22-52 (English translation Ann. Bot. 95(3):549-567, 2005, DOI 10.1093/aob/mci052)

models.name: Hubaud, Regev, Mahadevan & Pourquié (2017) excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo segmentation clock gated by YAP mechanotransduction, with FGF/Wnt clock-and-wavefront arrest and stiffness-LATS-YAP kinetics (Pass 3)
models.organism: Mus musculus (mouse E9.5-E10.5 presomitic mesoderm LuVeLu Lfng-Venus / Hes7 excitable oscillator)
models.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction

equations.law_name: Hubaud et al. (2017) FitzHugh-Nagumo Cubic Fast Nullcline Extrema & Barrier Law
equations.lean_code:
def fhn_cubic_scaled (u : Int) : Int :=
  3 * u - u * u * u
def fhn_cubic_deriv (u : Int) : Int :=
  1 - u * u
theorem hubaud_2017_fhn_cubic_nullcline_extrema :
    fhn_cubic_deriv 1 = 0 ∧
    fhn_cubic_deriv (-1) = 0 ∧
    fhn_cubic_deriv 0 = 1 ∧
    fhn_cubic_scaled 1 - fhn_cubic_scaled (-1) = 4
equations.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction
equations.variables: u: fast activator (Notch / LuVeLu Lfng-Venus / Hes7 activity); v: slow negative-feedback recovery variable; f(u) = u - u^3/3: cubic fast nullcline nonlinearity
equations.role: Defines the N-shaped folded cubic nullcline knees at u = +/- 1 that separate monostable excitable quiescence (|u^*| > 1) from autonomous relaxation oscillations (|u^*| < 1)
equations.source_citation: Hubaud, Regev, Mahadevan & Pourquie (2017) Cell 171(3):668-682 Fig. 3 & STAR Methods

equations.law_name: Hubaud et al. (2017) Supercritical Hopf Stability Boundary vs Quiescent Branch Law
equations.formula: Tr(tau_u * J(u^*)) = 1 - (u^*)^2 - epsilon * b,  |u_H| = sqrt(1 - epsilon * b)
equations.lean_code:
def fhn_jacobian_trace (M eps_b u_sq : Int) : Int :=
  M * (1 - u_sq) - eps_b
theorem hubaud_2017_hopf_vs_quiescent_stability (M eps_b : Int)
    (h_pos : 0 < eps_b) (h_fast_slow : eps_b < M) :
    fhn_jacobian_trace M eps_b 0 > 0 ∧
    fhn_jacobian_trace M eps_b 1 < 0
equations.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction
equations.variables: u^*: nullcline intersection fixed point; epsilon = tau_u / tau_v: fast-slow timescale ratio (0.08); b: slow recovery damping parameter (0.8)
equations.role: Proves that the fixed point is unstable (Tr J > 0, autonomous limit cycle) on the middle branch |u^*| < sqrt(1 - epsilon*b) and stable (Tr J < 0, excitable quiescent) on the outer branches |u^*| >= 1
equations.source_citation: Hubaud, Regev, Mahadevan & Pourquie (2017) Cell 171(3):668-682 Figs. 3-4 & STAR Methods

equations.law_name: Hubaud et al. (2017) YAP Mechanotransduction Excitability Gating & Latrunculin A Rescue Law
equations.formula: I_eff(Y_nuc, J_Dll1) = I_basal + J_Dll1 - gamma_YAP * Y_nuc,  Delta I_eff = gamma_YAP * Delta Y_nuc
equations.lean_code:
def yap_effective_current (I_basal J_Dll1 gamma_YAP Y_nuc : Int) : Int :=
  I_basal + J_Dll1 - gamma_YAP * Y_nuc
theorem hubaud_2017_latrunculin_yap_inhibition_rescue
    (I_basal J_Dll1 gamma_YAP Y_high delta_Y : Int) :
    yap_effective_current I_basal J_Dll1 gamma_YAP (Y_high - delta_Y) -
      yap_effective_current I_basal J_Dll1 gamma_YAP Y_high =
      gamma_YAP * delta_Y
equations.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction
equations.variables: I_eff: net excitability current; Y_nuc: nuclear YAP translocation fraction [0, 1]; J_Dll1: Notch-Dll1 intercellular coupling input; gamma_YAP: YAP excitability threshold gain
equations.role: Proves that inhibiting nuclear YAP (Latrunculin A, Y-27632 Rockout, soft substrate, Yap1 KO) raises I_eff across the Hopf threshold to ignite autonomous Hes7/Lfng oscillations, whereas Yap5SA locks quiescence
equations.source_citation: Hubaud, Regev, Mahadevan & Pourquie (2017) Cell 171(3):668-682 Figs. 4-6

equations.law_name: Cooke & Zeeman (1976) Clock-and-Wavefront Somite Spacing Law
equations.formula: x_wf(t) = x_wf0 + v_wf * t,  x_wf(t0 + (n+1) T) - x_wf(t0 + n T) = v_wf * T
equations.lean_code:
def wavefront_position (x_wf0 v_wf t : Int) : Int :=
  x_wf0 + v_wf * t
theorem hubaud_2017_clock_wavefront_somite_spacing (x_wf0 v_wf t0 T n : Int) :
    wavefront_position x_wf0 v_wf (t0 + (n + 1) * T) -
      wavefront_position x_wf0 v_wf (t0 + n * T) = v_wf * T
equations.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction
equations.variables: x_wf: anteroposterior position of the determination front; v_wf: axis-elongation / wavefront regression speed (um/min); T: segmentation-clock period (min); n: clock cycle index
equations.role: Proves that successive arrests of the excitable clock at the regressing FGF/Wnt determination front freeze the phase exactly S = v_wf T apart, the spacing of the Mesp2-like somite stripes measured in simulate_ap_wavefront_arrest and the slope of the v_wf sweep

equations.law_name: Dubrulle et al. (2001) FGF/Wnt-Gated Wavefront Arrest Criterion
equations.formula: F(x,t) = min(1, exp(-(x_tb(t) - x)/lambda_F)),  g(F) = F^h/(F_thr^h + F^h),  I_eff = I_post - gamma_F (g_max - g);  arrested <=> gamma_F (g_max - g) > I_post - I_H
equations.lean_code:
def fgf_gated_current (I_post gamma_F g_max g : Int) : Int :=
  I_post - gamma_F * (g_max - g)
theorem hubaud_2017_fgf_wavefront_arrest_criterion
    (I_post gamma_F g_max g I_H x_tb0 v_wf t dt d : Int) :
    (fgf_gated_current I_post gamma_F g_max g < I_H ↔
      I_post - I_H < gamma_F * (g_max - g)) ∧
    ((wavefront_position x_tb0 v_wf (t + dt) - d) -
      (wavefront_position x_tb0 v_wf t - d) = v_wf * dt)
equations.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction
equations.variables: F: Fgf8/Wnt3a signal (posterior-high exponential, decay length lambda_F); g(F): Hill gate; gamma_F: FGF/Wnt excitability gain; I_post: tail-bud excitability current; I_H: lower Hopf current; d: fixed decay distance from tail bud to front
equations.role: Defines the determination front as the locus where FGF/Wnt loss exceeds the Hopf margin (wavefront_gate_threshold, g_crit) and proves that the front regresses at v_wf regardless of lambda_F, so lambda_F sets PSM length but not somite spacing (lambda_F sweep in evaluate_wavefront_speed_sweep)

equations.law_name: Dupont et al. (2011) / Wada et al. (2011) YAP Mechanotransduction Nuclear-Fraction Monotonicity Law
equations.formula: T(E,A) = [E^hE/(E50^hE + E^hE)] [A/(A50 + A)] rho_actin c_ROCK,  L(T) = 1/(1 + (T/T_L)^m),  Y_n = r_n/(1 + r_n + r_p),  r_n = r0 (1 + alpha_T T),  r_p = kappa_LATS L(T)
equations.lean_code:
def yap_nuclear_denominator (r_n r_p : Int) : Int :=
  1 + r_n + r_p
theorem hubaud_2017_yap_mechanotransduction_monotonicity
    (r_n1 r_n2 r_n r_p r_p1 r_p2 : Int)
    (h_rp : 0 ≤ r_p) (h_lt : r_n1 < r_n2) (h_rn : 0 < r_n) (h_p : r_p1 < r_p2) :
    r_n1 * yap_nuclear_denominator r_n2 r_p < r_n2 * yap_nuclear_denominator r_n1 r_p ∧
    r_n * yap_nuclear_denominator r_n r_p1 < r_n * yap_nuclear_denominator r_n r_p2
equations.math_family: Excitable FitzHugh-Nagumo Somite Clock Gated by YAP Mechanotransduction
equations.variables: T: F-actin/stress-fibre tension index in [0,1] from substrate stiffness E_sub (kPa), spreading area A_cell (um^2), F-actin content rho_actin (Latrunculin A) and ROCK contractility c_ROCK (Y-27632); L(T): LATS1/2 activity; r_n: tension-driven nuclear import/export ratio; r_p: LATS phosphorylation/dephosphorylation ratio; Y_n: nuclear YAP fraction feeding Law 3
equations.role: Proves (cross-multiplied, division-free) that the steady-state nuclear YAP fraction rises with tension-driven import and falls with LATS phosphorylation, so softer substrates, smaller spreading area, Latrunculin A and Y-27632 all lower Y_nuc toward Y_crit and ignite the clock (calibrate_yap_mechanotransduction, evaluate_substrate_stiffness_sweep, simulate_latrunculin_yap_kinetics)
equations.source_citation: Dupont et al. (2011) Nature 474(7350):179-183, DOI 10.1038/nature10137; Wada et al. (2011) Development 138(18):3907-3914, DOI 10.1242/dev.070987; Hubaud et al. (2017) Cell 171:668-682 Figs. 4-6

models.name: Bentley, Gerhardt & Bates (2008) PLoS Comput. Biol., Hellström et al. (2007) Nature & Jakobsson et al. (2010) Nat. Cell Biol. VEGF-VEGFR2-Dll4-Notch1 tip/stalk salt-and-pepper lateral inhibition and angiogenic sprouting, coupled to lumenized Poiseuille flow, wall-shear pruning and arteriovenous specification (Pass 3)
models.organism: Homo sapiens / Mus musculus (Retinal & embryonic sprouting vascular endothelium)
models.math_family: Bentley–Gerhardt–Bates Coupled Endothelial ODE Network Driving Period-2 Salt-and-Pepper Tip-Cell vs Stalk-Cell Alternation & DAPT Hypersprouting Transition

equations.law_name: Bentley, Gerhardt & Bates (2008) & Collier et al. (1996) Two-Cell Trans-Notch Mutual Inhibition Symmetry Breaking (Brillouin k = π Mode)
equations.formula: dD_i/dt = g(V_i^*) - γ_D D_i,  dN_i/dt = h(D_⟨j⟩) - γ_N N_i,  Δ_antisym = g_D g_N - γ_D γ_N > 0 (k = π unstable),  Δ_sym = -g_D g_N - γ_D γ_N < 0 (k = 0 damped)
equations.lean_code:
def antisymmetric_tip_stalk_mode (D1 D2 : Int) : Int := D1 - D2
def trans_notch_antisym_margin (g_D g_N gamma_D gamma_N : Int) : Int := g_D * g_N - gamma_D * gamma_N
def trans_notch_sym_margin (g_D g_N gamma_D gamma_N : Int) : Int := -(g_D * g_N) - gamma_D * gamma_N
theorem bentley_trans_notch_symmetry_breaking_instability
    (g_D g_N gamma_D gamma_N D1 D2 : Int)
    (h_gain : gamma_D * gamma_N < g_D * g_N)
    (h_decay_pos : 0 < gamma_D * gamma_N) :
    0 < trans_notch_antisym_margin g_D g_N gamma_D gamma_N ∧
    trans_notch_sym_margin g_D g_N gamma_D gamma_N < 0 ∧
    antisymmetric_tip_stalk_mode D1 D2 + antisymmetric_tip_stalk_mode D2 D1 = 0
equations.math_family: Bentley–Gerhardt–Bates Coupled Endothelial ODE Network Driving Period-2 Salt-and-Pepper Tip-Cell vs Stalk-Cell Alternation & DAPT Hypersprouting Transition
equations.variables: D_i: endothelial Dll4 ligand level; N_i: active Notch1 intracellular domain level; g_D, g_N: linearized trans-inhibition feedback gains; γ_D, γ_N: degradation rates
equations.role: Proves that when cross-cellular Dll4-Notch1 gain g_D g_N exceeds intrinsic decay γ_D γ_N, the alternating Brillouin-zone k = π mode grows exponentially while the uniform k = 0 mode is damped, generating salt-and-pepper Tip-Stalk alternation
equations.source_citation: Bentley, Gerhardt & Bates (2008) PLoS Comput. Biol. 4(3):e1000052; Collier et al. (1996) J. Theor. Biol. 183(4):429-446

equations.law_name: Hellström et al. (2007) DAPT / Dll4-Null Notch Blockade All-Tip Hypersprouting Collapse Law
equations.formula: V_i = V_max M_tot^p / (M_tot^p + N_i^p),  N_i = 0  =>  V_i = V_max ∀ i  =>  V_1 - V_2 = 0  =>  M_stalk = M - M_tip = 0 (100% tip hypersprouting)
equations.lean_code:
def vegfr2_notch_hill_residual (V_i V_max M_p N_p : Int) : Int := V_i * (M_p + N_p) - V_max * M_p
def vessel_stalk_cell_count (M M_tip : Int) : Int := M - M_tip
theorem hellstrom_dapt_notch_blockade_all_tip_hypersprouting
    (V_max M_p M : Int) :
    vegfr2_notch_hill_residual V_max V_max M_p 0 = 0 ∧
    antisymmetric_tip_stalk_mode V_max V_max = 0 ∧
    vessel_stalk_cell_count M M = 0
equations.math_family: Bentley–Gerhardt–Bates Coupled Endothelial ODE Network Driving Period-2 Salt-and-Pepper Tip-Cell vs Stalk-Cell Alternation & DAPT Hypersprouting Transition
equations.variables: V_i: VEGFR2 receptor expression; V_max: unrepressed maximal VEGFR2 transcription; M_tot: Notch1 half-repression threshold; N_i: active Notch1 signaling; M: vessel endothelial cell count
equations.role: Proves that pharmacological γ-secretase Notch blockade (DAPT, k_t = 0 => N_i = 0) or Dll4 loss abolishes VEGFR2 repression across all endothelial cells, eliminating tip-stalk contrast and collapsing stalk cells to zero (100% all-tip hypersprouting)
equations.source_citation: Hellström et al. (2007) Nature 445(7129):776-780; Bentley, Gerhardt & Bates (2008) PLoS Comput. Biol. 4(3):e1000052

equations.law_name: Chappell et al. (2009) & Jakobsson et al. (2010) VEGFR1 (sFlt1) Decoy-Receptor Sequestration Window Shift Law
equations.formula: VEGF_eff = VEGF_raw - α_F F_flt1 < V_osc  when  VEGF_raw - V_osc < α_F F_flt1
equations.lean_code:
def flt1_sequestered_vegf (VEGF_raw alpha_F F_flt1 : Int) : Int := VEGF_raw - alpha_F * F_flt1
def salt_and_pepper_window_margin (V_osc VEGF_eff : Int) : Int := V_osc - VEGF_eff
theorem chappell_flt1_decoy_sequestration_window_rescue
    (VEGF_raw V_osc alpha_F F_flt1 : Int)
    (h_overload : V_osc ≤ VEGF_raw)
    (h_decoy : VEGF_raw - V_osc < alpha_F * F_flt1) :
    flt1_sequestered_vegf VEGF_raw alpha_F F_flt1 < VEGF_raw ∧
    0 < salt_and_pepper_window_margin V_osc (flt1_sequestered_vegf VEGF_raw alpha_F F_flt1)
equations.math_family: Bentley–Gerhardt–Bates Coupled Endothelial ODE Network Driving Period-2 Salt-and-Pepper Tip-Cell vs Stalk-Cell Alternation & DAPT Hypersprouting Transition
equations.variables: VEGF_raw: extracellular unsequestered VEGF-A concentration; VEGF_eff: bioavailable pericellular VEGF-A; F_flt1: soluble VEGFR1 (sFlt1) decoy concentration; α_F: decoy binding affinity; V_osc: synchronous oscillation threshold

equations.law_name: Pries, Secomb & Gaehtgens (1998) Lumenized Poiseuille/Kirchhoff Plexus with Pressure-Dependent Wall-Shear Set Point and Emergent Murray (1926) Cube Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: G_e = π r_e^4 / (8 μ L_e),  Σ_e G_e (P_u - P_v) = 0 ∀ internal nodes,  τ_e = 4 μ |Q_e| / (π r_e^3),  dr_e/dt = k_a r_e [log10((τ_e+τ_0)/(τ*(P_e)+τ_0)) + k_m log10(1 + Q_ref/|Q_e|) - k_s],  τ*(P) = 0.1(100 - 86 e^{-5000 (log10 log10 P)^5.4}) Pa;  uniform τ* + Kirchhoff  =>  r_p^3 = r_1^3 + r_2^3
equations.lean_code:
def poiseuille_flow_at_uniform_shear (c r : Int) : Int := c * (r * r * r)
def murray_cube_law_residual (r_p r_1 r_2 : Int) : Int := r_p * r_p * r_p - r_1 * r_1 * r_1 - r_2 * r_2 * r_2
theorem murray_cube_law_from_uniform_wall_shear
    (c r_p r_1 r_2 : Int)
    (h_shear_pos : c ≠ 0)
    (h_kirchhoff : poiseuille_flow_at_uniform_shear c r_p =
      poiseuille_flow_at_uniform_shear c r_1 + poiseuille_flow_at_uniform_shear c r_2) :
    murray_cube_law_residual r_p r_1 r_2 = 0
equations.math_family: Bentley–Gerhardt–Bates Coupled Endothelial ODE Network Driving Period-2 Salt-and-Pepper Tip-Cell vs Stalk-Cell Alternation & DAPT Hypersprouting Transition
equations.variables: r_e, L_e: lumen radius and length of segment e; μ: blood apparent viscosity (3.5 mPa s); G_e: Hagen-Poiseuille conductance; P_u: nodal pressure; Q_e: volumetric flow; τ_e: wall shear stress; τ*(P): Pries pressure-dependent set point; k_a, k_m, k_s: adaptation, metabolic and shrinkage gains; c = π τ*/(4 μ)
equations.role: Proves that when every perfused segment at a bifurcation has adapted to the same wall-shear set point (Q_e = c r_e^3) and Kirchhoff mass conservation holds, the lumen radii obey Murray's cube law exactly; the script therefore reports the fitted bifurcation exponent k as an EMERGENT diagnostic of the remodelled plexus (WT k ≈ 3.5, reference 3) rather than as a parameter
equations.source_citation: Pries AR, Secomb TW, Gaehtgens P (1998) Am. J. Physiol. 275(2):H349-H360; Pries, Secomb & Gaehtgens (1995) Circ. Res. 77(5):1017-1023; Murray CD (1926) PNAS 12(3):207-214

equations.law_name: Chen et al. (2012) / Franco et al. (2015) Flow-Stealing Pruning Cascade and Lawson et al. (2001) Notch-Gated Arteriovenous Specification (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Q_1 = G_1 ΔP / (1 + R_s (G_1 + G_2))  <  G_1 ΔP / (1 + R_s G_1) = Q_1^pruned  (cross-multiplied: G_1 ΔP (1 + R_s G_1) < G_1 ΔP (1 + R_s (G_1 + G_2)));  prune e when r_e < r_min = 1.3 μm;  AV_e = σ(ν_Notch [g_P p̂_e + g_τ log10((τ_e+τ_0)/(τ_ref+τ_0))]),  ν_Notch = k_t / k_t,WT
equations.lean_code:
def survivor_flow_cross_term (G_1 dP R_s G_other : Int) : Int := G_1 * dP * (1 + R_s * (G_1 + G_other))
theorem franco_pruning_flow_stealing_cascade
    (G_1 G_2 R_s dP : Int)
    (h_G1 : 0 < G_1) (h_G2 : 0 < G_2) (h_Rs : 0 < R_s) (h_dP : 0 < dP) :
    survivor_flow_cross_term G_1 dP R_s 0 < survivor_flow_cross_term G_1 dP R_s G_2 ∧
    survivor_flow_cross_term G_1 dP R_s 0 = G_1 * dP * (1 + R_s * G_1)
equations.math_family: Bentley–Gerhardt–Bates Coupled Endothelial ODE Network Driving Period-2 Salt-and-Pepper Tip-Cell vs Stalk-Cell Alternation & DAPT Hypersprouting Transition
equations.variables: G_1, G_2: conductances of two parallel capillary rungs; R_s: series feeding-arteriole/draining-venule resistance; ΔP: arteriolar-venular pressure drop; r_min: minimum red-cell-perfusable lumen radius; AV_e: arterial (ephrinB2, →1) vs venous (EphB4, →0) identity; p̂_e: local pressure rank relative to the rung midpoint; ν_Notch: Dll4/Notch1 transduction gain
equations.role: Proves that pruning a neighbouring rung strictly increases the surviving rung's flow (and hence Poiseuille wall shear), making shear-driven regression a self-reinforcing cascade; the script couples this to a Notch-gated hemodynamic readout so that DAPT (ν_Notch = 0) leaves the pressure/shear field intact but abolishes arteriovenous marker segregation (index 0.5, AV shunting), while perfusion arrest removes both
equations.source_citation: Chen Q, et al. (2012) PLoS Biol. 10(8):e1001374; Franco CA, et al. (2015) PLoS Biol. 13(4):e1002125; Lawson ND, et al. (2001) Development 128(19):3675-3683; le Noble F, et al. (2004) Development 131(2):361-375; Wang HU, Chen ZF, Anderson DJ (1998) Cell 93(5):741-753

models.name: Jönsson et al. (2006) & Smith et al. (2006) up-the-gradient PIN1 polarization with explicit PIN1 trafficking kinetics, quasi-3D subepidermal canalization, and polar auxin transport for shoot apical meristem phyllotaxis
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (shoot apical meristem L1 epidermis & subepidermal provascular strand); Aeonium tabuliforme (spiral rosette specimen)
models.math_family: Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Turing-Like Phyllotactic Spacing

equations.law_name: Jönsson et al. (2006) & Smith et al. (2006) Up-the-Gradient Boltzmann PIN1 Allocation Law
equations.formula: P_ij = P_i exp(c_1 a_j) / ∑_{k∈N(i)} exp(c_1 a_k);  ∑_{j∈N(i)} P_ij = P_i;  a_j > a_k ⇒ P_ij > P_ik
equations.lean_code:
def pin1_alloc_scaled (P_i w_j : Int) : Int := P_i * w_j
def pin1_partition_sum3 (w1 w2 w3 : Int) : Int := w1 + w2 + w3
theorem jonsson_2006_up_gradient_pin1_allocation (P_i w1 w2 w3 w_j w_k : Int)
    (hP : P_i > 0) (hw : w_j > w_k) :
    pin1_alloc_scaled P_i w1 + pin1_alloc_scaled P_i w2 + pin1_alloc_scaled P_i w3 =
      P_i * pin1_partition_sum3 w1 w2 w3 ∧
    pin1_alloc_scaled P_i w_j > pin1_alloc_scaled P_i w_k
equations.math_family: Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Turing-Like Phyllotactic Spacing
equations.variables: P_i: total PIN1 pool in L1 cell i; P_ij: PIN1 allocated to anticlinal wall i→j; a_j: auxin concentration in neighbor cell j; c_1: up-the-gradient feedback exponent; w_j = exp(c_1 a_j): Boltzmann weight
equations.role: Directs cellular PIN1 efflux carriers preferentially toward neighboring cells with higher auxin concentration while conserving each cell's total PIN1 pool

equations.law_name: Jönsson et al. (2006) Intercellular Active Polar + Diffusive Auxin Flux Conservation Law
equations.formula: da_i/dt = ρ_0 - μ a_i + ∑_{j∈N(i)} J_{i←j},  J_{i←j} = T(P_ji a_j - P_ij a_i) + D(a_j - a_i),  J_{i←j} + J_{j←i} = 0
equations.lean_code:
def intercellular_auxin_flux (T D P_ij P_ji a_i a_j : Int) : Int :=
  T * (P_ji * a_j - P_ij * a_i) + D * (a_j - a_i)
theorem jonsson_2006_intercellular_flux_conservation (T D P_ij P_ji P0 a_i a_j a0 : Int) :
    intercellular_auxin_flux T D P_ij P_ji a_i a_j +
      intercellular_auxin_flux T D P_ji P_ij a_j a_i = 0 ∧
    intercellular_auxin_flux T D P0 P0 a0 a0 = 0
equations.math_family: Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Turing-Like Phyllotactic Spacing
equations.variables: a_i: auxin concentration in cell i; T: active PIN1 polar transport rate; D: passive apoplastic/plasmodesmatal diffusion rate; ρ_0: basal auxin synthesis rate; μ: auxin turnover rate
equations.role: Guarantees exact pairwise intercellular auxin mass conservation across every shared cell wall and equilibrium stationarity at homogeneous state a_0 = ρ_0 / μ
equations.source_citation: Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS 103(5):1633-1638 Eqs. 1-3

equations.law_name: Jönsson et al. (2006) Up-the-Gradient Turing-Like Instability & NPA Pin-Formed Collapse Law
equations.formula: Γ_mode = T P_i (c_1 a_0 - 1) - z D > 0  ⇔  D_eff < 0;  T = 0 (NPA / pin1) ⇒ Γ_mode = -z D < 0
equations.lean_code:
def effective_diffusion_scaled (z_D T P_i c1_a0 : Int) : Int :=
  z_D - T * P_i * (c1_a0 - 1)
def mode_instability_gain (z_D T P_i c1_a0 : Int) : Int :=
  T * P_i * (c1_a0 - 1) - z_D
theorem jonsson_2006_up_gradient_instability_and_npa_collapse (z_D T P_i c1_a0 : Int)
    (h_instab : T * P_i * (c1_a0 - 1) > z_D)
    (h_diff : z_D > 0) :
    effective_diffusion_scaled z_D T P_i c1_a0 < 0 ∧
    mode_instability_gain z_D T P_i c1_a0 > 0 ∧
    mode_instability_gain z_D 0 P_i c1_a0 < 0
equations.math_family: Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Turing-Like Phyllotactic Spacing
equations.variables: c_1 a_0: dimensionless PIN1 polarization feedback product; z: cellular coordination number; D_eff: effective linearized diffusion coefficient; Γ_mode: spatial perturbation growth gain
equations.role: Establishes the bifurcation threshold where up-the-gradient active transport overcomes passive diffusion to form periodic auxin convergence maxima separated by λ_c, and proves that blocking polar transport (T = 0 in NPA or pin1 mutant) abolishes instability to yield a pin-formed apex
equations.source_citation: Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS 103(5):1633-1638 pp. 1635-1636; Reinhardt et al. (2003) Nature 426:255-260

equations.law_name: Jönsson et al. (2006) Explicit PIN1 Exocytosis / Endocytosis Trafficking Kinetics & Quasi-Steady-State Allocation Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: dP_ij/dt = k_exo f(a_j) P_cyt,i − k_endo P_ij,  P_cyt,i + ∑_j P_ij = P_tot;  P*_ij = k_exo f_j P_tot / Z_i,  P*_cyt = k_endo P_tot / Z_i,  Z_i = k_endo + k_exo ∑_k f_k;  k_endo P*_ij = k_exo f_j P*_cyt;  f_j > f_k ⇒ P*_ij > P*_ik;  k_exo = 0 (BFA) ⇒ P*_ij = 0
equations.lean_code:
def pin1_membrane_qss_num (k_exo f_j P_tot : Int) : Int := k_exo * f_j * P_tot
def pin1_cytosol_qss_num (k_endo P_tot : Int) : Int := k_endo * P_tot
def pin1_trafficking_partition (k_exo k_endo f1 f2 f3 : Int) : Int := k_endo + k_exo * (f1 + f2 + f3)
theorem jonsson_2006_pin1_trafficking_qss (k_exo k_endo f1 f2 f3 f_j f_k P_tot : Int)
    (hk : k_exo > 0) (hP : P_tot > 0) (hf : f_j > f_k) :
    pin1_cytosol_qss_num k_endo P_tot + pin1_membrane_qss_num k_exo f1 P_tot +
        pin1_membrane_qss_num k_exo f2 P_tot + pin1_membrane_qss_num k_exo f3 P_tot =
      P_tot * pin1_trafficking_partition k_exo k_endo f1 f2 f3 ∧
    k_endo * pin1_membrane_qss_num k_exo f_j P_tot =
      k_exo * f_j * pin1_cytosol_qss_num k_endo P_tot ∧
    pin1_membrane_qss_num k_exo f_j P_tot > pin1_membrane_qss_num k_exo f_k P_tot ∧
    pin1_membrane_qss_num 0 f_j P_tot = 0
equations.math_family: Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Turing-Like Phyllotactic Spacing
equations.variables: P_cyt,i: cytosolic/endosomal PIN1 pool of cell i; P_ij: plasma-membrane PIN1 on wall i→j; k_exo: exocytosis rate per unit targeting weight; k_endo: endocytosis rate; f(a_j) = exp(c_1 (a_j − a_0)): up-the-gradient exocytosis targeting; Z_i: cleared partition denominator
equations.role: Replaces the instantaneous Boltzmann allocation by explicit membrane cycling with a finite trafficking time 1/k_endo; its fixed point conserves membrane + cytosolic PIN1, retains up-the-gradient polarity, reduces to Law 1 as k_endo/(k_exo ∑ f) → 0, and predicts complete PIN1 internalisation under a brefeldin A exocytosis block
equations.source_citation: Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS 103(5):1633-1638 (PIN1 cycling kinetics and quasi-steady state); Geldner et al. (2001) Nature 413:425-428 (BFA); Paciorek et al. (2005) Nature 435:1251-1256 (auxin-inhibited endocytosis)

equations.law_name: Mitchison (1980/1981) With-the-Flux Canalization Winner-Take-All Law (subepidermal provascular strand; Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def flux_feedback_quadratic (J : Int) : Int := J * J
theorem mitchison_1980_canalization_winner_take_all (J1 J2 alpha : Int)
    (h2 : J2 ≥ 0) (h : J1 > J2) (ha : alpha > 0) :
    flux_feedback_quadratic J1 - flux_feedback_quadratic J2 = (J1 - J2) * (J1 + J2) ∧
    flux_feedback_quadratic J1 > flux_feedback_quadratic J2 ∧
    alpha * (flux_feedback_quadratic J1 - flux_feedback_quadratic J2) > 0
equations.math_family: Up-the-Gradient Auxin-PIN1 Polarized Transport & Turing-Like Phyllotactic Spacing
equations.variables: J_1, J_2: net auxin efflux through two competing walls of a subepidermal cell; Φ: with-the-flux exocytosis targeting (quadratic case of Φ = J^n/(K^n + J^n)); α: feedback gain (k_exo P_cyt)
equations.role: Shows that a superlinear flux feedback amplifies any flux asymmetry between competing walls, so a symmetric split is linearly unstable and auxin efflux canalizes into a single-file provascular strand connecting the L1 convergence point to the existing vasculature (Bayer et al. 2009 integration)
equations.source_citation: Mitchison GJ (1980) Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 207:79-109; Mitchison GJ (1981) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. B 295:461-471; Feugier et al. (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236:366-375; Bayer et al. (2009) Genes Dev. 23:373-384

models.name: Van Essen (1997), Hilgetag & Barbas (2006) & Mota & Herculano-Houzel (2015) cortico-cortical axonal tension and cortical folding
models.organism: Primate & mammalian cerebral cortex and white-matter tracts (Homo sapiens, Macaca mulatta, Pan troglodytes, Tursiops truncatus, Felis catus, Mus musculus)
models.math_family: Viscoelastic Cortico-Cortical Axonal Tension Mechanics, Laminar Volume Conservation & Universal Gyrification Scaling

equations.law_name: Van Essen (1997) Cortico-Cortical Axonal Tension & Chord-vs-Arc Gyral Wiring Economy
equations.formula: F_axon = sum_{i<j} k_a C_{ij} (||x_i - x_j|| - L_{0,ij})_+ + E_bend(κ);  ΔV_wire = C_{ij} (d_arc - d_chord) > 0 for C_strong > C_weak
equations.lean_code:
def wiring_volume_saving (C d_arc d_chord : Int) : Int :=
  C * d_arc - C * d_chord
theorem van_essen_gyral_wiring_economy (C_strong C_weak d_chord delta : Int) :
    wiring_volume_saving C_strong d_chord d_chord = 0 ∧
    wiring_volume_saving C_strong (d_chord + delta) d_chord -
      wiring_volume_saving C_weak (d_chord + delta) d_chord =
      (C_strong - C_weak) * delta
equations.math_family: Viscoelastic Cortico-Cortical Axonal Tension Mechanics, Laminar Volume Conservation & Universal Gyrification Scaling
equations.variables: C_{ij}: cortico-cortical axonal connectivity density; d_arc: unfolded geodesic surface arc distance (mm); d_chord: 3D Euclidean trans-gyral chord distance (mm); k_a: axonal spring constant
equations.role: Establishes that viscoelastic tension along dense cortico-cortical white-matter tracts pulls strongly connected areas together across outward gyral crowns to minimize 3D wiring volume while weakly connected zones fold inward as sulcal fundi
equations.source_citation: Van Essen (1997) Nature 385:313-318 Fig. 1-3; Toro & Burnod (2005) Cerebral Cortex 15:1900-1913; Karbowski (2001) Phys. Rev. Lett. 86:3674

equations.law_name: Hilgetag & Barbas (2006) Isometric Laminar Volume Conservation & Gyral-vs-Sulcal Thickness Dichotomy
equations.formula: V_col = A_surf * h = A_0 * h_0  ⇒  h_gyrus = h_0 / λ_{t,gyrus} > h_wall = h_0 > h_fundus = h_0 / λ_{t,fundus}
equations.lean_code:
def laminar_volume_residual (A_surf h A_ref h_ref : Int) : Int :=
  A_surf * h - A_ref * h_ref
theorem hilgetag_barbas_laminar_thickness_dichotomy (A_0 h_0 k m d : Int) :
    laminar_volume_residual (k * A_0) (m * h_0) (m * A_0) (k * h_0) = 0 ∧
    (k + d) * h_0 - k * h_0 = d * h_0
equations.math_family: Viscoelastic Cortico-Cortical Axonal Tension Mechanics, Laminar Volume Conservation & Universal Gyrification Scaling
equations.variables: V_col: cortical column volume; A_surf: local tangential surface area; h: radial cortical thickness (mm); λ_t: tangential strain factor (λ_{t,gyrus} = 0.78 < 1 < λ_{t,fundus} = 1.26)
equations.role: Proves that isometric volume conservation under gyral tangential compression and sulcal tangential stretching produces systematically thicker gyral crowns and thinner sulcal fundi (h_gyrus / h_fundus ≈ 1.62)
equations.source_citation: Hilgetag & Barbas (2006) PLoS Comput. Biol. 2(3):e22 Eq. 1-4 & Fig. 2-6

equations.law_name: Mota & Herculano-Houzel (2015) Universal Mammalian Cortical Folding Power Law
equations.lean_code:
def mota_herculano_houzel_residual (A_T_pow4 h_pow2 k_pow4 A_E_pow5 : Int) : Int :=
  A_T_pow4 * h_pow2 - k_pow4 * A_E_pow5
def gyrification_area_excess (A_T A_E : Int) : Int :=
  A_T - A_E
theorem mota_herculano_houzel_universal_scaling (A_E h_pow2 k_pow4 : Int) :
    gyrification_area_excess A_E A_E = 0 ∧
    mota_herculano_houzel_residual (k_pow4 * A_E) h_pow2 k_pow4 (A_E * h_pow2) = 0 ∧
    mota_herculano_houzel_residual (16 * k_pow4 * A_E) h_pow2 k_pow4 (16 * A_E * h_pow2) = 0
equations.math_family: Viscoelastic Cortico-Cortical Axonal Tension Mechanics, Laminar Volume Conservation & Universal Gyrification Scaling
equations.variables: A_T: total pial cortical surface area (mm^2); A_E: exposed convex-hull surface area (mm^2); h: mean cortical gray-matter thickness (mm); k: dimensionless axonal-tension folding constant; GI: 3D gyrification index
equations.role: Unifies mammalian cortical folding across 12 species spanning lissencephalic rodents to gyrencephalic primates and cetaceans with universal log-log slope α = 5/4 = 1.25
equations.source_citation: Mota & Herculano-Houzel (2015) Science 349(6243):74-77 Eq. 3-5 & Fig. 2-3

measurements.name: 12-species mammalian universal folding scaling exponent alpha (Mota & Herculano-Houzel 2015)
measurements.method: OLS slope of log10(A_T * sqrt(h)) vs log10(A_E) across 12 mammalian species (SE ± 0.0047, r=0.9999, p=1.38e-20)
measurements.reference_source: Mota & Herculano-Houzel (2015) Science 349(6243):74-77 Eq. 3-5 & Fig. 2 (alpha = 5/4 = 1.25)

measurements.name: 12-species mammalian 3D Gyrification Index correlation (Mota & Herculano-Houzel 2015)
measurements.method: Linear correlation of predicted GI = k * h^(-1/2) * A_E^(1/4) vs observed 3D GI across 12 mammalian species (p=1.36e-12, RMSE=0.0761)
measurements.reference_source: Mota & Herculano-Houzel (2015) Science 349(6243):74-77 Fig. 2-3

models.name: Kondo & Asai (1995) Pomacanthus reaction-diffusion stripe insertion & Y-branch unzipping
models.organism: Pomacanthus semicirculatus & Pomacanthus imperator (marine angelfish)
models.math_family: Growing-Domain Reaction-Diffusion

equations.law_name: Kondo & Asai (1995) Piecewise-Linear Saturating Activator-Inhibitor Steady State & Uniform Stability
equations.formula: F(A^*, I^*) = min(F_max, max(0, c_1 A^* + c_2 I^* + c_3)) = g_A A^*,  G(A^*, I^*) = min(G_max, max(0, c_4 A^* + c_5)) = g_I I^*;  tr J = f_A + g'_I < 0 ∧ det J = f_A g'_I - f_I g'_A > 0
equations.lean_code:
def clip_rate (S_max raw : Int) : Int := min S_max (max 0 raw)
def kondo_trace (f_A g_I_prime D_A D_I q : Int) : Int := (f_A + g_I_prime) - (D_A + D_I) * q
def kondo_det (f_A f_I g_A_prime g_I_prime D_A D_I q : Int) : Int :=
  (D_A * D_I) * (q * q) - (D_I * f_A + D_A * g_I_prime) * q + (f_A * g_I_prime - f_I * g_A_prime)
theorem kondo_asai_1995_piecewise_gm_steady_state_and_uniform_stability (D_A D_I : Int) :
    clip_rate 200 (80 * 3 + (-80) * 5 / 2 + 50) = 90 ∧
    clip_rate 500 (100 * 3 - 150) = 150 ∧
    kondo_trace 50 (-60) D_A D_I 0 = -10 ∧
    kondo_det 50 (-80) 100 (-60) D_A D_I 0 = 5000 := by
  unfold clip_rate kondo_trace kondo_det; refine ⟨by decide, by decide, by omega, by omega⟩
equations.math_family: Growing-Domain Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: A, I: activator and inhibitor concentrations; c_1..c_5: linear synthesis coefficients; g_A, g_I: decay rates; F_max, G_max: upper saturation ceilings; (A^*, I^*) = (3.0, 2.5): interior homogeneous steady state
equations.role: Proves that the interior equilibrium (A^*, I^*) = (3.0, 2.5) lies strictly inside the unsaturated linear window (0 < F^* = 0.09 < 0.20, 0 < G^* = 0.15 < 0.50) and is asymptotically stable to uniform perturbations (tr J = -0.01 < 0, det J = 0.005 > 0)
equations.source_citation: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376(6543):765-768 Fig. 1 legend; Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) Kybernetik 12(1):30-39

equations.law_name: Kondo & Asai (1995) Turing Wave Instability Threshold (D_I / D_A > d_c)
equations.lean_code:
theorem kondo_asai_1995_turing_wave_instability_and_subcritical_stability :
    kondo_det 50 (-80) 100 (-60) 7 100 3 = -2440 ∧
    kondo_det 50 (-80) 100 (-60) 7 50 3 = 1910 ∧
    kondo_det 50 (-80) 100 (-60) 7 7 3 = 5651 := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Growing-Domain Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: D_A = 0.007, D_I = 0.10: activator and inhibitor diffusivities; d = D_I / D_A = 14.29: diffusivity ratio; d_c = 10.26: critical Turing ratio; k_c^2 = 3.2714: critical squared wavenumber; λ_c = 2π / k_c = 3.4739: intrinsic stripe wavelength
equations.role: Proves that the canonical Kondo-Asai diffusivity ratio d = 100/7 ≈ 14.29 exceeds d_c ≈ 10.26 and drives det M(q) = -2440 < 0 at q = 3, whereas subcritical inhibitor diffusion (D_I = 0.050, d = 7.14 < d_c) keeps det M(q) > 0
equations.source_citation: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376(6543):765-768 Fig. 1

equations.law_name: Kondo & Asai (1995) P. semicirculatus Mid-Trough Doubling Cascade vs P. imperator Y-Branch Unzipping
equations.formula: L(t) = s L_0 (s ∈ {1,2,4,8}) ⟹ N_semicirculatus(s) = 3 s ∈ {3,6,12,24} (λ(s) = λ_c);  N_imperator(N_0, u) = N_0 + u
equations.lean_code:
def semicirculatus_stripes (N_0 s : Nat) : Nat := N_0 * s
def imperator_unzipped_stripes (N_0 unzipped_branches : Nat) : Nat := N_0 + unzipped_branches
theorem kondo_asai_1995_semicirculatus_insertion_vs_imperator_unzipping :
    semicirculatus_stripes 3 1 = 3 ∧
    semicirculatus_stripes 3 2 = 6 ∧
    semicirculatus_stripes 3 4 = 12 ∧
    semicirculatus_stripes 3 8 = 24 ∧
    imperator_unzipped_stripes 3 1 = 4 := by
  unfold semicirculatus_stripes imperator_unzipped_stripes; omega
equations.math_family: Growing-Domain Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: s = L(t)/L_0: ontogenetic body-length doubling scale (2 → 4 → 8 → 16 cm); N_0 = 3: initial juvenile stripe count; u: number of horizontally unzipped 2D Y-junction branch points
equations.role: Formalizes the species-specific wavelength-homeostasis laws in Pomacanthus: simultaneous 1D mid-trough secondary stripe insertion (3 → 6 → 12 → 24) in P. semicirculatus versus 2D horizontal Y-branch dislocation unzipping (+1 stripe per branch) in P. imperator
equations.source_citation: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376(6543):765-768 Figs. 1-4; Crampin, Gaffney & Maini (1999) Bull. Math. Biol. 61(6):1093-1120

equations.law_name: Kondo & Asai (1995) Curvilinear C-Shaped Mid-Trough Inhibitor Threshold Partition for Concentric Arc Insertion (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Lap_phys = R^-2 [∂²_ρ + ρ^-1 ∂_ρ + ρ^-2 ∂²_θ] on ρ ∈ [ρ_in, 1], θ ∈ [-Θ, Θ], R(t) = R_0 s(t);  F_trough(I) = min(F_max, max(0, c_2 I + c_3)) = 0 ⟺ I ≥ I_thr = c_3/|c_2| = 0.625;  I_1 ≤ I_2 ⟹ F_trough(I_2) ≤ F_trough(I_1);  N_arcs(s) = N_0 s (3 → 6);  π(R_in + kλ) < π(R_in + (k+1)λ)
equations.lean_code:
def trough_synthesis (I : Int) : Int := clip_rate 200 ((-80) * I / 1000 + 50)
def concentric_arcs (N_0 s : Nat) : Nat := N_0 * s
def arc_length_pi (R_in lam k : Nat) : Nat := R_in + lam * k
theorem kondo_asai_1995_curvilinear_mid_trough_threshold_partition :
    trough_synthesis 2500 = 0 ∧ trough_synthesis 625 = 0 ∧
    trough_synthesis 600 = 2 ∧ trough_synthesis 0 = 50 ∧
    (∀ I : Int, 625 ≤ I → trough_synthesis I = 0) ∧
    (∀ I₁ I₂ : Int, I₁ ≤ I₂ → trough_synthesis I₂ ≤ trough_synthesis I₁) ∧
    concentric_arcs 3 2 = 6 ∧
    (∀ R_in lam k : Nat, 0 < lam → arc_length_pi R_in lam k < arc_length_pi R_in lam (k + 1)) := by
  refine ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_, by decide, ?_⟩ <;> ...  -- omega / Nat.add_lt_add_left
equations.math_family: Growing-Domain Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: ρ = r/R(t): scaled radius on the posterior-centred C-shaped sector; θ: polar angle; s = R(t)/R_0: radial growth scale; I_mid: mid-trough inhibitor minimum along the central radial transect; I_thr = c_3/|c_2| = 0.625: zero-activator insertion threshold (625 in 10^3-scaled Int units); N_0 = 3: equilibrated concentric arcs
equations.role: Proves the threshold partition that drives de novo concentric arc insertion in the curvilinear solver: in an activator-depleted trough the piecewise-linear synthesis is silent for I ≥ 0.625 and active below it (antitone in I), so arcs insert exactly when the inhibitor minimum between stretched arcs crosses the threshold; concentric arc number doubles with radial span while arc length grows strictly with arc index (the polar (1/ρ)∂_ρ term shifts phase, not count)
equations.source_citation: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376(6543):765-768 Fig. 1d-f; Crampin, Gaffney & Maini (1999) Bull. Math. Biol. 61(6):1093-1120

equations.law_name: Discrete Iridophore/Melanophore Agent Fate Partition Coupled to the Kondo-Asai Activator Field with Bounded Feedback (Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def cell_fate (A A_thr : Int) : Int := if A_thr ≤ A then 1 else 0
def coupled_c3 (c3 kappa_A fate : Int) : Int := c3 + kappa_A * fate
def coupled_c5 (c5 kappa_I fate : Int) : Int := c5 + kappa_I * (1 - fate)
theorem kondo_asai_1995_pigment_agent_fate_partition_and_bounded_feedback :
    (∀ A₁ A₂ A_thr : Int, A₁ ≤ A₂ → cell_fate A₁ A_thr ≤ cell_fate A₂ A_thr) ∧
    (∀ A A_thr : Int, cell_fate A A_thr = 0 ∨ cell_fate A A_thr = 1) ∧
    cell_fate 3000 3000 = 1 ∧ cell_fate 0 3000 = 0 ∧
    (∀ c3 kappa_A A A_thr : Int, 0 ≤ kappa_A → c3 ≤ coupled_c3 c3 kappa_A (cell_fate A A_thr) ∧ coupled_c3 c3 kappa_A (cell_fate A A_thr) ≤ c3 + kappa_A) ∧
    (∀ c5 kappa_I A A_thr : Int, 0 ≤ kappa_I → c5 ≤ coupled_c5 c5 kappa_I (cell_fate A A_thr) ∧ coupled_c5 c5 kappa_I (cell_fate A A_thr) ≤ c5 + kappa_I) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> ...  -- split <;> omega
equations.math_family: Growing-Domain Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: A: local macroscopic activator read by a discrete pigment cell; A_thr = A^* = 3.0 (3000 in 10^3-scaled Int units): fate threshold; fate = 1 iridophore/light-stripe cell, 0 melanophore/dark-interstripe cell; κ_A, κ_I: agent-to-field feedback strengths added to the basal synthesis rates c_3, c_5
equations.role: Formalizes the hybrid continuum-agent coupling: the deterministic fate partition is monotone and binary (so iridophores occupy activator peaks and melanophores the troughs), and the agent feedback perturbs the Kondo-Asai source terms within bounded intervals, preserving the Jacobian sign structure; the stochastic contact rules (short-range exclusion, long-range support) in the script are abstracted from Nakamasu et al. (2009)
equations.source_citation: Nakamasu, Takahashi, Kanbe & Kondo (2009) PNAS 106(21):8429-8434; Bullara & De Decker (2015) Nat. Commun. 6:6971; Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376(6543):765-768

measurements.method: IMEX sparse-LU polar-sector solver (rho in [0.25, 1], theta in [-100, 100] deg, 48x96) equilibrated at 3 arcs (radial spacing 3.4369 = lambda_c +/- 1.06%, angular coherence 1.0000) then grown exponentially to s = 2.6; first mid-trough arc insertion at s = 2.1825, arc counts on 5 transects = [6, 6, 6, 6, 6]
measurements.reference_source: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376(6543):765-768 Figs. 1-2 (3 -> 6 mid-trough doubling) transferred to the concentric C-shaped juvenile P. semicirculatus geometry; Lean theorem kondo_asai_1995_curvilinear_mid_trough_threshold_partition (concentric_arcs 3 2 = 6)

models.name: Kriegman et al. (2020, 2021) Xenobot evolutionary biomechanics & kinematic self-replication
models.organism: Xenopus laevis (African clawed frog blastula ectoderm & cardiac progenitor biobots)
models.math_family: Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuated Continuum Mechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication

equations.law_name: Kriegman et al. (2020) Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuation & Passive Ectoderm Volume Invariance Law
equations.formula: L_{ij}(t) = L_{ij,0}(1 + ε_act a_{ij} sin(ω t + φ_{ij}));   a_{ij}=0 ⟹ L_{ij}(t)=L_{ij,0};   L_{ij}(+s)+L_{ij}(-s)=2L_{ij,0}
equations.lean_code:
def voxel_rest_length (L0 a eps s : Int) : Int :=
  L0 + a * eps * s
theorem voxel_actuation_invariance_and_cycle_symmetry (L0 a eps s : Int) :
    voxel_rest_length L0 0 eps s = L0 ∧
    voxel_rest_length L0 a 0 s = L0 ∧
    voxel_rest_length L0 1 eps s + voxel_rest_length L0 1 eps (-s) = 2 * L0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [voxel_rest_length]
  · simp [voxel_rest_length]
  · simp [voxel_rest_length, Int.mul_neg]
    omega
equations.math_family: Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuated Continuum Mechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication
equations.variables: L_{ij,0}: rest spring length between adjacent voxels; a_{ij} in {0,1}: tissue type (0 = passive ectoderm, 1 = contractile cardiac progenitor); epsilon_act = 0.18: volumetric contraction strain; f_act = 1.5 Hz: cardiac contraction frequency
equations.role: Governs rhythmic volumetric actuation of contractile cardiac voxels while enforcing strict rest-volume invariance in passive animal-cap ectoderm voxels
equations.source_citation: Kriegman, Blackiston, Levin & Bongard (2020) PNAS 117(4):1853-1859 SI Appendix S1; Cheney et al. (2013) GECCO pp. 167-174

equations.law_name: Ventral-Concavity Asymmetric Substrate Ratchet & Dorsal Inversion Collapse Law
equations.formula: Δx_stride(μ_ant, μ_post, e) = (μ_ant - μ_post) e;   μ_ant = μ_post ⟹ Δx_stride = 0;   Δx_stride(μ_post, μ_ant, e) = -Δx_stride(μ_ant, μ_post, e)
equations.lean_code:
def xenobot_stride (mu_ant mu_post e : Int) : Int :=
  (mu_ant - mu_post) * e
theorem ventral_ratchet_and_dorsal_inversion_collapse (mu mu_ant mu_post e : Int) :
    xenobot_stride mu mu e = 0 ∧
    xenobot_stride mu_post mu_ant e = -xenobot_stride mu_ant mu_post e ∧
    xenobot_stride 65 18 4 = 188 ∧
    xenobot_stride 25 25 4 = 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide⟩
  · simp [xenobot_stride]
  · simp [xenobot_stride, Int.sub_mul]
    omega
equations.math_family: Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuated Continuum Mechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication
equations.variables: mu_ant = 0.65: anterior ventral leg substrate friction; mu_post = 0.18: posterior ventral leg substrate friction; e: cyclic ventral cardiac contraction stroke
equations.role: Proves that ventral-concavity bipedal leg asymmetry rectifies zero-mean cardiac oscillations into net forward locomotion, whereas 180-deg dorsal inversion equalizes contact friction and collapses net propulsion
equations.source_citation: Kriegman, Blackiston, Levin & Bongard (2020) PNAS 117(4):1853-1859 Figs. 1-3

equations.law_name: AFPO Phase-Robustness Transferability & Pac-Man Kinematic Self-Replication Law
equations.formula: T_sim2real(F_det, F_rob) = I(F_det ≥ F_min ∧ F_rob ≥ F_rob_min);   N_daughters(θ_mouth) = floor(η_sweep(θ_mouth) v_orbit ρ_free / N_thresh)
equations.lean_code:
def afpo_transferable (F_det F_rob F_det_min F_rob_min : Nat) : Bool :=
  (F_det ≥ F_det_min) && (F_rob ≥ F_rob_min)
def kinematic_daughter_generations (eta_mouth v_orbit rho_free N_thresh : Nat) : Nat :=
  (eta_mouth * v_orbit * rho_free) / N_thresh
theorem afpo_transferability_and_pacman_replication :
    afpo_transferable 195 140 120 100 = true ∧
    afpo_transferable 185 32 120 100 = false ∧
    afpo_transferable 12 10 120 100 = false ∧
    kinematic_daughter_generations 18 3 4 55 = 3 ∧
    kinematic_daughter_generations 6 3 4 55 = 1 := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuated Continuum Mechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication
equations.variables: F_det: synchronous cardiac phase displacement (body lengths); F_rob: phase-randomized cardiomyocyte displacement; eta_mouth(theta_mouth): C-shaped Pac-Man concavity sweeping efficiency; N_thresh = 55: critical stem-cell pile size for self-sustaining daughter spheroid compaction
equations.role: Formalizes the Kriegman et al. (2020) phase-randomization sim-to-real transferability filter and the Kriegman et al. (2021) C-shaped Pac-Man kinematic self-replication advantage over spherical morphologies
equations.source_citation: Kriegman et al. (2020) PNAS 117:1853-1859 Fig. 2; Kriegman et al. (2021) PNAS 118:e2112672118 Figs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Regularised-Stokeslet Force-Free Cancellation & Squirmer Mobility Superposition Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Σ_k c f_k = c Σ_k f_k = 0 for a force-free body;   U(β) = U0 + β U1,  U(β₁+β₂) = U(β₁) + β₂ U1
equations.lean_code:
def stokeslet_constant_part (c f1 f2 f3 : Int) : Int :=
  c * f1 + c * f2 + c * f3
def squirmer_velocity (U0 U1 beta : Int) : Int :=
  U0 + beta * U1
theorem stokeslet_force_free_cancellation_and_mobility_superposition
    (c f1 f2 f3 U0 U1 b1 b2 : Int) (hff : f1 + f2 + f3 = 0) :
    stokeslet_constant_part c f1 f2 f3 = 0 ∧
    squirmer_velocity U0 U1 0 = U0 ∧
    squirmer_velocity U0 U1 1 = U0 + U1 ∧
    squirmer_velocity U0 U1 (b1 + b2) = squirmer_velocity U0 U1 b1 + b2 * U1 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · unfold stokeslet_constant_part
    rw [← Int.mul_add, ← Int.mul_add, hff, Int.mul_zero]
  · simp [squirmer_velocity]
  · simp [squirmer_velocity]
  · simp [squirmer_velocity, Int.add_mul]
    omega
equations.math_family: Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuated Continuum Mechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication
equations.variables: f_k: regularised Stokeslet strengths on the parent boundary; c: the common scalar part of the 2D kernel (-(1/2) constant and far-field -ln r); U0, U1: rigid velocity at zero and unit left/right ciliary turn bias; beta: turn bias
equations.role: Guarantees that the force-free squirmer flow has no net-Stokeslet (log) far field and that the mobility is affine in the turn bias, which is how the orbit radius is fitted and the precessing orbit is driven without re-solving the boundary integral
equations.source_citation: Cortez (2001) SIAM J. Sci. Comput. 23:1204-1225 (regularised Stokeslets); Blake (1971) J. Fluid Mech. 46:199-208 (squirmer); Kriegman et al. (2021) PNAS 118:e2112672118

equations.law_name: 3D Voxel Lattice Stokes-Drag Dissipation & Passive-Spring Rest Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: P_drag = γ v·v ≥ 0 for γ ≥ 0;   P_drag(γ=0) = 0;   a_ij = 0 ⟹ L_ij(t) = L_ij,0
equations.lean_code:
def drag_power (gamma v : Int) : Int :=
  gamma * (v * v)
theorem int_mul_self_nonneg (v : Int) : 0 ≤ v * v := by
  rcases Int.le_total 0 v with h | h
  · exact Int.mul_nonneg h h
  · have h' : 0 ≤ -v := Int.neg_nonneg_of_nonpos h
    have hm := Int.mul_nonneg h' h'
    rwa [Int.neg_mul_neg] at hm
theorem lattice_drag_dissipation_nonneg_and_passive_spring_rest
    (gamma v L0 eps s : Int) (hg : 0 ≤ gamma) :
    0 ≤ drag_power gamma v ∧
    drag_power 0 v = 0 ∧
    voxel_rest_length L0 0 eps s = L0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · exact Int.mul_nonneg hg (int_mul_self_nonneg v)
  · simp [drag_power]
  · simp [voxel_rest_length]
equations.math_family: Voxel Spring-Lattice Actuated Continuum Mechanics, Age-Fitness Pareto Optimization (AFPO), & Kinematic Self-Replication
equations.variables: gamma: per-node Stokes drag coefficient (non-dimensional, default 2.0); v: node velocity; L_ij,0: spring rest length; a_ij: fraction of cardiac voxels adjoining the spring (0 for passive-only springs)
equations.role: Explains the monotone fitness decrease with Stokes drag (gamma in {0,1,2,4,8}) and the zero locomotion of the passive_only_control body in the 8x8x7 lattice
equations.source_citation: Kriegman, Blackiston, Levin & Bongard (2020) PNAS 117(4):1853-1859 SI Appendix S1 (VoxCAD 8x8x7 workspace); Hiller & Lipson (2014) Soft Robotics 1:88-101 (VoxCAD dynamics)
