models.name: Lauschke, Tsiairis, François & Aulehla (2013) scale-invariant phase-gradient encoding in ex vivo monolayer presomitic mesoderm (mPSM)
models.organism: Mus musculus (mouse E10.5 tailbud LuVeLu Lfng-Venus monolayer presomitic mesoderm)
models.math_family: Scale-Invariant Kinematic Phase-Gradient Encoding (Ex Vivo Monolayer PSM)

equations.law_name: Lauschke et al. (2013) Proportional Segment Scaling Law under Invariant Phase Span
equations.formula: S_n = alpha * R(t_n),  where Delta_phi_total = phi(0, t) - phi(R(t), t) = Phi_0 = 2*pi
equations.lean_code:
def scaled_segment_width (alpha R : Nat) : Nat :=
  alpha * R
theorem lauschke_2013_proportional_segment_scaling (alpha k R R1 R2 : Nat) :
    scaled_segment_width alpha (k * R) = k * scaled_segment_width alpha R ∧
    scaled_segment_width alpha (R1 + R2) =
      scaled_segment_width alpha R1 + scaled_segment_width alpha R2
equations.math_family: Scale-Invariant Kinematic Phase-Gradient Encoding (Ex Vivo Monolayer PSM)
equations.variables: S_n: newly specified concentric segment width at cycle n (um); R(t_n): residual unsegmented mPSM radius (um); alpha: dimensionless proportional scaling slope (0.11)
equations.role: Establishes linear scale-invariance of embryonic segment size with residual tissue radius via a constant 2*pi total phase span across the active mPSM
equations.source_citation: Lauschke, Tsiairis, Francois & Aulehla (2013) Nature 493(7430):101-105 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Lauschke et al. (2013) Geometric Residual mPSM Radius Progression & Conservation Law
equations.formula: R(t_{n+1}) = R(t_n) - S_n = (1 - alpha) * R(t_n) = R_0 * (1 - alpha)^n
equations.math_family: Scale-Invariant Kinematic Phase-Gradient Encoding (Ex Vivo Monolayer PSM)
equations.variables: R_n: residual mPSM radius at cycle n (um); R_0: initial mPSM explant radius (um); S_n: n-th concentric segment width (um)
equations.role: Governs the inward periphery-to-center geometric contraction of the active mPSM domain and exact radial conservation across successive segmentation cycles
equations.source_citation: Lauschke, Tsiairis, Francois & Aulehla (2013) Nature 493(7430):101-105 Figs. 1-3

equations.law_name: Lauschke et al. (2013) Radial Notch Phase-Wave Velocity Scaling Law
equations.formula: v_wave(t) = lambda(t) / T_osc = (2*pi / Phi_0) * (R(t) / T_osc)
equations.lean_code:
def phase_wave_kinematic_residual (v_wave T_osc lambda_ratio R : Int) : Int :=
  v_wave * T_osc - lambda_ratio * R
theorem lauschke_2013_phase_wave_velocity_scaling (lambda_ratio T_osc c : Int) :
    phase_wave_kinematic_residual (lambda_ratio * c) T_osc lambda_ratio (T_osc * c) = 0
equations.math_family: Scale-Invariant Kinematic Phase-Gradient Encoding (Ex Vivo Monolayer PSM)
equations.variables: v_wave(t): radial LuVeLu Notch phase-wave propagation speed (um/min); lambda(t): effective radial phase wavelength (um); T_osc: central pacemaker clock period (140 min)
equations.role: Explains why LuVeLu Notch oscillation waves propagate faster in larger mPSM explants and decelerate as R(t) shrinks while maintaining a 2*pi phase span
equations.source_citation: Lauschke, Tsiairis, Francois & Aulehla (2013) Nature 493(7430):101-105 Fig. 4

equations.law_name: FGF/Wnt Source-Sink Signalling Gradient Scale Covariance (shrinking gradient on the active mPSM)
equations.formula: D W'' - k W = 0, W(0) = W_0, W(R) = 0  =>  W = W_0 sinh((R - r)/l_k)/sinh(R/l_k);  l_k >> R: W = W_0 (1 - r/R), l_half = R/2;  W(k R, k r) = k W(R, r) (scaled units)
equations.lean_code:
def source_sink_gradient (W0 R r : Int) : Int :=
  W0 * (R - r)
theorem lauschke_2013_fgf_wnt_gradient_scale_covariance (W0 k R r : Int) :
    source_sink_gradient W0 (k * R) (k * r) = k * source_sink_gradient W0 R r
equations.math_family: Scale-Invariant Kinematic Phase-Gradient Encoding (Ex Vivo Monolayer PSM)
equations.variables: W(r,t): FGF/Wnt signalling level (W_0 at the central source, 0 at the peripheral determination-front sink); l_k = sqrt(D/k): diffusion-decay length (um); l_half: half-maximum length of the gradient (um)
equations.role: Supplies the shrinking FGF/Wnt gradient of Lauschke et al. (2013) Fig. 4 whose length scales with the residual mPSM radius and drives wavelength adaptation; the fixed-length exponential gradient (Dubrulle & Pourquie 2004) is the mechanistic non-scaling control
equations.source_citation: Lauschke, Tsiairis, Francois & Aulehla (2013) Nature 493(7430):101-105 Fig. 4; Aulehla et al. (2008) Nat Cell Biol 10:186-193; Dubrulle & Pourquie (2004) Nature 427:419-422

equations.law_name: Dynamic Notch Phase-Wave Wavelength Adaptation to the FGF/Wnt Gradient Length
equations.formula: d lambda/dt = -(lambda - c_lambda l_half(t))/tau_lambda;  Phi(t) = 2 pi R(t)/lambda(t);  phi(r,t) = omega_0 t - Phi(t) (r/R(t))^p;  S_n = R(t_n)[1 - (1 - delta_phi_seg/Phi(t_n))^(1/p)], delta_phi_seg = Phi_0[1 - (1 - alpha)^p];  discrete error step M e_{n+1} = (M - h) e_n
equations.lean_code:
def wavelength_adaptation_error_step (M h e : Int) : Int :=
  (M - h) * e
theorem lauschke_2013_wavelength_adaptation_contraction (M h e : Int)
    (h0 : 0 ≤ h) (hM : h ≤ M) :
    Int.natAbs (wavelength_adaptation_error_step M h e) ≤ Int.natAbs (M * e)
equations.math_family: Scale-Invariant Kinematic Phase-Gradient Encoding (Ex Vivo Monolayer PSM)
equations.variables: lambda(t): Notch phase-wave wavelength (um); tau_lambda: adaptation time (35 min default, inf = frozen ablation); Phi(t): dynamic total phase span (rad); delta_phi_seg: peripheral gating window (0.9144 rad); alpha = S_n/R(t_n): emergent scaling ratio
equations.role: Closes the Pass 2 remediation item: the 2*pi phase span and alpha = 0.11 are recovered dynamically from the shrinking FGF/Wnt gradient (mean Phi = 6.125 rad, alpha_8 = 0.1103 at tau_lambda = T_osc/4) and lost when adaptation is frozen (alpha_8 = 0.560) or the gradient has fixed length (constant 39.5 um segments)
equations.source_citation: Lauschke, Tsiairis, Francois & Aulehla (2013) Nature 493(7430):101-105 Fig. 4; Beaupeux & Francois (2016) Phys Biol 13:036009

equations.law_name: Kuramoto-Sakaguchi Reaggregate Lattice & Target-Wave Pacemaker Dispersion (Tsiairis & Aulehla 2016)
equations.formula: d theta_i/dt = omega_i + (K/n_i) sum_j [sin(theta_j - theta_i - a) + sin a], omega_i = omega_0 (1 + eta xi_i);  continuum: theta_t = omega + D lap theta + beta |grad theta|^2, D = K cos(a) d^2/4, beta = K sin(a) d^2/4;  pacemaker excess Delta omega = beta k^2 (monotone in k)
equations.lean_code:
def target_wave_frequency_excess (beta k : Nat) : Nat :=
  beta * k * k

equations.law_name: Lewis (2003) Her1/Her7 Autoinhibitory Delay-Loop Invariance & Protein Translation Balance
equations.formula: dp(t)/dt = a * m(t - T_p) - b * p(t),  dm(t)/dt = k / (1 + (p(t - T_m) / p_0)^n) - c * m(t),  T_tot = T_m + T_p
equations.lean_code:
def lewis_protein_dde_residual (a m_delayed b p : Int) : Int :=
  a * m_delayed - b * p
def lewis_total_loop_delay (T_m T_p : Int) : Int :=
  T_m + T_p
theorem lewis_2003_protein_steady_state_and_delay_invariance (a b q T_m T_p delta : Int) :
    lewis_protein_dde_residual a (b * q) b (a * q) = 0 ∧
    lewis_total_loop_delay (T_m + delta) (T_p - delta) = lewis_total_loop_delay T_m T_p
equations.math_family: Time-Delayed Transcriptional Oscillator & DeltaC-Notch Phase Coupling (Somitogenesis)
equations.variables: m(t): her1/her7 mRNA molecules per cell; p(t): Her1/Her7 repressor protein molecules per cell; T_m: transcriptional delay (min); T_p: translational delay (min)
equations.role: Establishes the intracellular delayed negative feedback loop of the zebrafish segmentation clock and proves that stability and period depend only on the sum T_tot = T_m + T_p
equations.source_citation: Lewis (2003) Current Biology 13(16):1398-1408 Eqs. 1-2 & Appendix

equations.law_name: Lewis (2003) Delay-Driven Oscillation Period & Hopf Bifurcation Law
equations.formula: T_osc = 2 * (T_m + T_p + tau_m + tau_p)  for  T_m + T_p > T_crit
equations.lean_code:
def lewis_oscillation_period (T_m T_p tau_m tau_p : Nat) : Nat :=
  2 * (T_m + T_p + tau_m + tau_p)
theorem lewis_2003_oscillation_period_delay_sensitivity (T_m T_p tau_m tau_p delta_Tm : Nat) :
    lewis_oscillation_period (T_m + delta_Tm) T_p tau_m tau_p =
      lewis_oscillation_period T_m T_p tau_m tau_p + 2 * delta_Tm
equations.math_family: Time-Delayed Transcriptional Oscillator & DeltaC-Notch Phase Coupling (Somitogenesis)
equations.variables: T_osc: segmentation clock oscillation period (min); T_crit: Hopf bifurcation critical delay threshold (7.54 min computed); tau_m, tau_p: mRNA and protein half-life relaxation times (min)
equations.role: Predicts the ~30 min zebrafish somite clock period from transcriptional/translational delays plus macromolecular half-lives and explains period shifts under intron deletion or Notch delay changes
equations.source_citation: Lewis (2003) Current Biology 13(16):1398-1408 Box 1 & Figs. 2-3; Giudicelli et al. (2007) PLoS Biology 5:e150

equations.law_name: Lewis (2003) DeltaC-Notch Intercellular Synchronization vs bea/des/aei Mutant Desynchronization Law
equations.formula: Delta_phi_next = (1 - kappa) * Delta_phi + delta_omega;  R_sync = |1/N * sum_j exp(i * theta_j)|
equations.lean_code:
def notch_phase_difference_step (kappa Delta_phi delta_omega : Int) : Int :=
  (1 - kappa) * Delta_phi + delta_omega
theorem lewis_2003_notch_coupling_synchronization_contraction (Delta_phi delta_omega : Int) :
    notch_phase_difference_step 1 Delta_phi 0 = 0 ∧
    notch_phase_difference_step 0 Delta_phi delta_omega = Delta_phi + delta_omega
equations.math_family: Time-Delayed Transcriptional Oscillator & DeltaC-Notch Phase Coupling (Somitogenesis)
equations.variables: kappa: intercellular DeltaC-Notch phase-coupling strength; Delta_phi: phase difference between adjacent PSM cells; R_sync: Kuramoto tissue synchronization order parameter
equations.role: Explains how intercellular DeltaC-Notch signaling maintains phase synchrony (R_sync > 0.95) against molecular copy-number noise in wild-type PSM, whereas Notch mutants (bea, des, aei; kappa=0) form 5-7 normal anterior somites before desynchronizing into salt-and-pepper defects
equations.source_citation: Lewis (2003) Current Biology 13(16):1398-1408 Figs. 5-6; Herrgen et al. (2010) Current Biology 20:1244-1253

equations.law_name: Lewis (2003) 2D Multicellular DDE Lattice: Notch-Gated her Transcription with Delayed DeltaC Translation & NICD Cleavage (Pass 3)
equations.formula: dN_i/dt = k_N * Dbar_i(t - T_N) / (K_D + Dbar_i(t - T_N)) - b_N * N_i;  G_N(N) = (1 - eps_N) + eps_N * N^h / (N_0^h + N^h);  Dbar_i = (D_up + D_down + D_left + D_right) / 4;  dD_i/dt = a_D * d_i(t - T_pD) - b_D * D_i
equations.lean_code:
def notch_transcription_gate (eps_N s : Int) : Int :=
  (1 - eps_N) + eps_N * s
theorem lewis_2003_notch_gate_mutant_independence (s : Int) :
    notch_transcription_gate 0 s = 1 ∧ notch_transcription_gate 1 s = s
def deltac_neighbour_mean (D_up D_down D_left D_right : Nat) : Nat :=
  (D_up + D_down + D_left + D_right) / 4
theorem deltac_lattice_uniform_neighbour_mean_fixed_point (D : Nat) :
    deltac_neighbour_mean D D D D = D
equations.math_family: Time-Delayed Transcriptional Oscillator & DeltaC-Notch Phase Coupling (Somitogenesis)
equations.variables: N_i: NICD molecules in cell i; Dbar_i: mean DeltaC protein of the 4 von Neumann neighbours; T_N: Notch binding/gamma-secretase cleavage/nuclear-entry delay (min); T_pD: DeltaC translation+trafficking delay (min); eps_N: Notch-dependent fraction of her transcription (0 in bea/des/aei); K_D, N_0, h: NICD occupancy constants
equations.role: Extends the 1D phase chain to an explicit 8 x 24 multicellular DDE sheet in which DeltaC protein is translated with delay, cleaved Notch (NICD) gates her1/her7 transcription, and eps_N = 0 reproduces the bea/des/aei loss of coupling (5-7 coherent anterior cycles before salt-and-pepper desynchronisation); a uniform DeltaC field is a fixed point of the coupling
equations.source_citation: Lewis (2003) Current Biology 13(16):1398-1408 Figs. 5-6 (coupled-cell DDEs); Herrgen et al. (2010) Current Biology 20:1244-1253 (coupling delay sets collective period)

equations.law_name: Schroter et al. (2012) Her1/Her7/Hes6 Dimer DNA-Binding Truth Table on the AP Hes6 Gradient (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Rep_i = sum_{(A,B)} B_AB * [A:B]_i / K_AB,  [A:B] = A * B;  B_11 = B_76 = 1, B_17 = B_16 = B_77 = B_66 = 0;  Hes6_i = H_ant + (H_post - H_ant) * x_i / (n_cols - 1);  (w + v) T7 <= w T7 + v T1 <= (w + v) T1
equations.lean_code:
def schroter_dimer_repression (B11 B76 B17 B16 B77 B66 p1 p7 h6 : Nat) : Nat :=
  B11 * (p1 * p1) + B76 * (p7 * h6) + B17 * (p1 * p7) + B16 * (p1 * h6) + B77 * (p7 * p7) + B66 * (h6 * h6)
theorem schroter_2012_dimer_truth_table_repression (p1 p7 h6 : Nat) :
    schroter_dimer_repression 1 1 0 0 0 0 p1 p7 h6 = p1 * p1 + p7 * h6 ∧
    schroter_dimer_repression 1 1 0 0 0 0 p1 p7 0 = p1 * p1
def hes6_weighted_loop_delay (w v T7 T1 : Nat) : Nat :=
  w * T7 + v * T1
theorem schroter_2012_hes6_gradient_period_interpolation (w v T7 T1 : Nat) (h : T7 ≤ T1) :
    (w + v) * T7 ≤ hes6_weighted_loop_delay w v T7 T1 ∧
    hes6_weighted_loop_delay w v T7 T1 ≤ (w + v) * T1
equations.math_family: Time-Delayed Transcriptional Oscillator & DeltaC-Notch Phase Coupling (Somitogenesis)
equations.variables: p1, p7: Her1, Her7 protein molecules; h6: non-oscillating Hes6 protein (posterior-high AP gradient); B_AB: DNA-binding truth table bit; K_11, K_76: dimer dissociation constants (reduced parameters); T7, T1: her7 (fast) and her1 (slow) loop delays; w, v: Hes6-dependent repression weights
equations.role: Couples the anterior-to-posterior phase gradient to the dimer composition: Hes6-high posterior cells are repressed through the short-delay Her7:Hes6 loop (faster), Hes6-low anterior cells through the Her1 homodimer loop (slower), hes6-null tissue is AP-uniform at the her1-only period; the lattice AP period gradient is bracketed by the pure-branch periods
equations.source_citation: Schroter et al. (2012) PLoS Biology 10(7):e1001364 Figs. 2-3 (dimerization and DNA binding), Figs. 5-7 (hes6 gradient, genetic interactions); Giudicelli et al. (2007) PLoS Biology 5:e150 (kinematic waves)

equations.law_name: Incompatible Saddle Target Curvature Tensor & Gauss's Theorema Egregium Incompatibility Law

def saddle_target_gaussian_curvature (kappa0 : Int) : Int :=

    saddle_target_trace kappa0 = 0 ∧

    narrow_helicoid_torsion kappa0 1 = kappa0 ∧

    freund_scaled_crack_speed cR gamma gamma = 0 ∧

def released_elastic_energy (e_init e_final : Int) : Int :=

    (e_final ≤ e_init → 0 ≤ released_elastic_energy e_init e_final) ∧
    (0 ≤ eta → 0 ≤ dU1 → 0 ≤ catapult_kinetic_energy eta dU1) ∧
    (eta ≤ 1 → 0 ≤ dU1 → catapult_kinetic_energy eta dU1 ≤ dU1) ∧
    released_elastic_energy 0 0 = 0 ∧

equations.law_name: Hexagonal Skin-Scale First-Nearest-Neighbor Partition & Labyrinthine Symmetry
equations.lean_code:
def hex_black_neighbors (n_g : Nat) : Nat := 6 - n_g
theorem hex_scale_neighbor_partition_and_symmetry (n_g : Nat) (h : n_g ≤ 6) :
    n_g + hex_black_neighbors n_g = 6 ∧
    (n_g = hex_black_neighbors n_g ↔ n_g = 3) := by
  unfold hex_black_neighbors; omega
equations.math_family: Scale-Level Cellular Automaton vs PDE
equations.variables: n_g: number of green first-nearest-neighbor scales; n_b: number of black first-nearest-neighbor scales on the 6-regular hexagonal skin lattice
equations.role: Establishes the exact 6-neighbor conservation law on hexagonal lizard skin scales and proves n_g = n_b = 3 is the unique symmetric labyrinthine chain degree
equations.source_citation: Manukyan et al. (2017) Nature 544(7649):173-179 Fig. 3d-f

equations.law_name: Scale-Border Thickness Reduction Inter-Scale Flux Attenuation (D_border = P D_interior ≪ D_interior)
equations.formula: J_border = P · D_interior · ∇u;   0 < P < 1 ⟹ 0 < J_border < J_continuum,   P = 0 ⟹ J_border = 0
equations.lean_code:
def interscale_border_flux (P_pct flux_unit : Int) : Int :=
  P_pct * flux_unit
theorem border_diffusivity_reduction_quenches_interscale_flux
    (P_pct flux_unit : Int)
    (hP_lo : P_pct ≥ 1) (hP_hi : P_pct ≤ 99) (hF : flux_unit ≥ 1) :
    interscale_border_flux 0 flux_unit = 0 ∧
    interscale_border_flux 17 flux_unit > 0 ∧
    interscale_border_flux 17 flux_unit < interscale_border_flux 100 flux_unit ∧
    P_pct < 100 := by
  unfold interscale_border_flux; omega
equations.math_family: Scale-Level Cellular Automaton vs PDE
equations.variables: P = h_border / h_interior: scale-border thickness reduction factor (P ≈ 0.17 in Timon lepidus); D_interior: intra-scale morphogen diffusivity; ∇u: inter-scale morphogen difference
equations.role: Proves that thinning skin at scale borders attenuates inter-scale diffusive flux relative to intra-scale homogenization, discretizing continuous Turing PDEs into monochromatic scale states
equations.source_citation: Manukyan et al. (2017) Nature 544(7649):173-179 Fig. 4 & Methods Eqs. (1)-(8); Fofonjka & Milinkovitch (2021) Nat. Commun. 12:2433

equations.role: Proves that n_g = 3 is a simultaneous fixed point for both green and black scales while overcrowded green clusters (n_g ≥ 4) flip to black and isolated black pockets (n_g ≤ 1) flip to green

equations.law_name: Thin-Film Depth Average of a Skin Column (3D voxel skin volume → 2D depth-averaged reduction)
equations.formula: ū = (1/h) Σ_z u;   u(z) ≡ c ⟹ ū = (h·c)/h = c;   h_border ≤ h_interior ⟹ h_border·c ≤ h_interior·c
equations.lean_code:
def column_mass (h c : Nat) : Nat := h * c
def depth_average (h m : Nat) : Nat := m / h
theorem thin_film_depth_average_recovers_uniform_column
    (h_interior h_border c : Nat) (hpos : 0 < h_interior) (hle : h_border ≤ h_interior) :
    depth_average h_interior (column_mass h_interior c) = c ∧
    column_mass h_border c ≤ column_mass h_interior c := by
  unfold depth_average column_mass
  exact ⟨Nat.mul_div_cancel_left c hpos, Nat.mul_le_mul_right c hle⟩
equations.math_family: Scale-Level Cellular Automaton vs PDE
equations.variables: h: skin column height in voxels (h_interior = 12, h_border = P·h_interior); c: voxel concentration; ū: depth-averaged concentration used by the 2D reduction d ū/dt = F(ū) + (1/h)∇·(h D ∇ū)
equations.role: Justifies replacing the 3D voxel field by its depth average wherever the field is vertically uniform (thin-film regime h ≪ λ_c) and gives the border column its reduced capacity h(x) in the depth-averaged equation
equations.source_citation: Fofonjka & Milinkovitch (2021) Nat. Commun. 12:2433 (3D skin-scale reaction-diffusion); thin-film / lubrication reduction of diffusion in a domain of varying thickness

equations.law_name: Finite-Volume Face Conductance Between Skin Columns Equals Shared Face Area (min(h_i, h_j)·D)
equations.formula: C_ij = min(h_i, h_j)·D;   C_int,border·h_interior = C_int,int·h_border  (ratio = h_border/h_interior ∀ D);   h_border = 0 ⟹ C = 0;   h_border < h_interior ∧ D > 0 ⟹ C_int,border < C_int,int
equations.lean_code:
def face_conductance (h_i h_j D : Nat) : Nat := min h_i h_j * D
theorem voxel_face_conductance_ratio_equals_thickness_ratio
    (h_interior h_border D : Nat) (hlt : h_border < h_interior) (hD : 0 < D) :
    face_conductance h_interior h_border D = h_border * D ∧
    face_conductance h_interior h_interior D = h_interior * D ∧
    face_conductance h_interior h_border D * h_interior =
      face_conductance h_interior h_interior D * h_border ∧
    face_conductance h_interior 0 D = 0 ∧
    face_conductance h_interior h_border D < face_conductance h_interior h_interior D := by
  unfold face_conductance
  have hmin : min h_interior h_border = h_border := Nat.min_eq_right (Nat.le_of_lt hlt)
  have hself : min h_interior h_interior = h_interior := Nat.min_self h_interior
  have hzero : min h_interior 0 = 0 := Nat.min_eq_right (Nat.zero_le h_interior)
  rw [hmin, hself, hzero]
  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, ?_, by simp, Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hlt hD⟩
  ac_rfl
equations.math_family: Scale-Level Cellular Automaton vs PDE
equations.variables: h_i, h_j: heights (voxels) of two laterally adjacent skin columns; D: morphogen diffusivity; C_ij: depth-integrated conductance of their shared vertical face (number of skin-skin voxel pairs × D)
equations.role: Proves that in the voxel skin volume all inter-scale flux passes through the thinned border with conductance reduced exactly by the thickness ratio P = h_border/h_interior, that P = 0 insulates scales, and that the 2D reduction's face conductance min(h_i, h_j)·D is the exact depth integral of the 3D face
equations.source_citation: Manukyan et al. (2017) Nature 544(7649):173-179 Fig. 4 (P = h_border/h_interior ≈ 0.17); Fofonjka & Milinkovitch (2021) Nat. Commun. 12:2433

models.name: Morris (2012), Mooi & David (1998/2008), Lovén (1874), Duboc et al. (2005), Luo & Su (2012) & Meinhardt (2008) echinoderm bilateral-to-pentaradial hydrocoel ring symmetry breaking with Ocular Plate Rule test growth
models.organism: Strongylocentrotus purpuratus & Tripneustes gratilla (Echinoidea crown-group echinoderms)
models.math_family: Circular-Ring Activator-Inhibitor Mode m=5 Selection (k_m = m / R_ring), Lovén's Law (II, IV, I, III, V) Ocular/Ambulacral Ordering, Duboc Nodal Left-Right Rudiment Multiplicity, Ocular Plate Rule Biserial Plate Addition (Pass 3) & Continuous Nodal/BMP2-4 Hill Dose-Response (Pass 3)

equations.law_name: Circular Hydrocoel Ring Laplacian Eigenvalue & Pentaradial Mode m^* = 5 Selection Law
equations.formula: - (1 / R_ring^2) d^2(cos(m theta))/dtheta^2 = (m^2 / R_ring^2) cos(m theta),   m^* = argmax_m sigma(m / R_ring) = 5 (Delta_theta = 72 deg) when 2*pi R_ring / lambda_c in (4.5, 5.5)
equations.lean_code:
def ring_laplacian_eigen_num (m : Nat) : Nat := m * m
def hydrocoel_angular_period_deg (m : Nat) : Nat := 360 / m
theorem hydrocoel_ring_pentaradial_mode5_selection :
    ring_laplacian_eigen_num 5 = 25 ∧
    hydrocoel_angular_period_deg 5 = 72 ∧
    5 * hydrocoel_angular_period_deg 5 = 360 ∧
    hydrocoel_turing_growth_score 5 50 > hydrocoel_turing_growth_score 4 50 ∧
    hydrocoel_turing_growth_score 5 50 > hydrocoel_turing_growth_score 6 50 := by decide
equations.math_family: Circular-Ring Activator-Inhibitor Mode m=5 Selection (k_m = m / R_ring), Lovén's Law (II, IV, I, III, V) Ocular/Ambulacral Ordering, Duboc Nodal Left-Right Rudiment Multiplicity, Ocular Plate Rule Biserial Plate Addition (Pass 3) & Continuous Nodal/BMP2-4 Hill Dose-Response (Pass 3)
equations.variables: m in {3, 4, 5, 6, 7}: azimuthal harmonic mode on closed hydrocoel ring; R_ring: hydrocoel ring radius (um); lambda_c: Turing critical wavelength (um); Delta_theta = 360 deg / m: inter-ambulacral angular spacing
equations.role: Governs spontaneous symmetry breaking of the closed circular left hydrocoel ring into 5 primary podia lobes spaced at 72 deg, while explaining 4-rayed (90 deg) and 6-rayed (60 deg) teratological variants under ring-radius perturbations
equations.source_citation: Meinhardt (2008) Curr. Top. Dev. Biol. 81:1-63; Morris (2012) Evol. Dev. 14(4):313-326

equations.law_name: Lovén's Law (1874) & Morris (2012) Hydrocoel Crescent Initiation Ordering (II, IV, I, III, V)
equations.formula: Initiation rank r in {1..5} -> Ray (II, IV, I, III, V) = (C, A, D, B, E);   Peristomial biserial dominance: (Ib, IIb, IIIa, IVa, Va) = (ba, ba, ab, ab, ab)
equations.lean_code:
def loven_initiation_rank_to_ray : Nat → Nat
  | 1 => 2 | 2 => 4 | 3 => 1 | 4 => 3 | 5 => 5 | _ => 0
theorem loven_law_crescent_ordering_and_asymmetric_biserial_rule :
    loven_initiation_rank_to_ray 1 = 2 ∧
    loven_initiation_rank_to_ray 5 = 5 ∧
    (loven_b_column_enlarged 1 + loven_b_column_enlarged 2 +
     loven_b_column_enlarged 3 + loven_b_column_enlarged 4 +
     loven_b_column_enlarged 5) = 2 := by decide
equations.math_family: Circular-Ring Activator-Inhibitor Mode m=5 Selection (k_m = m / R_ring), Lovén's Law (II, IV, I, III, V) Ocular/Ambulacral Ordering, Duboc Nodal Left-Right Rudiment Multiplicity, Ocular Plate Rule Biserial Plate Addition (Pass 3) & Continuous Nodal/BMP2-4 Hill Dose-Response (Pass 3)
equations.variables: r in {1..5}: developmental initiation rank during crescent-to-ring closure; I..V: Lovén ambulacral ray indices; (a, b): counter-clockwise half-ambulacral plate columns
equations.role: Explains how progressive anterior-to-posterior activation along the closing bilateral hydrocoel crescent generates Lovén's invariant asymmetric biserial peristomial plate law across Echinoidea
equations.source_citation: Lovén (1874) K. Sven. Vetensk.-Akad. Handl. 11(7):1-91; Mooi & David (1998) Am. Zool. 38:965-974; Morris (2012) Evol. Dev. 14:313-326

equations.law_name: Duboc et al. (2005) Right-Sided Nodal Signaling & Bilateral Twin-Rudiment Multiplicity Law
equations.formula: N_rings = I(Nodal_L = 0) + I(Nodal_R = 0),   N_podia = 5 * N_rings in {5 (WT: Nodal_R = 1), 10 (Nodal LOF: Nodal_L = Nodal_R = 0, twin 2x5 rudiments), 0 (Nodal GOF: Nodal_L = Nodal_R = 1)}
equations.lean_code:
def active_hydrocoel_rings (nodal_left nodal_right : Nat) : Nat :=
  (if nodal_left == 0 then 1 else 0) + (if nodal_right == 0 then 1 else 0)
def total_primary_podia (m_ring nodal_left nodal_right : Nat) : Nat :=
  m_ring * active_hydrocoel_rings nodal_left nodal_right
theorem duboc_nodal_left_right_rudiment_multiplicity :
    total_primary_podia 5 0 1 = 5 ∧
    total_primary_podia 5 0 0 = 10 ∧
    total_primary_podia 5 1 1 = 0 := by decide
equations.math_family: Circular-Ring Activator-Inhibitor Mode m=5 Selection (k_m = m / R_ring), Lovén's Law (II, IV, I, III, V) Ocular/Ambulacral Ordering, Duboc Nodal Left-Right Rudiment Multiplicity, Ocular Plate Rule Biserial Plate Addition (Pass 3) & Continuous Nodal/BMP2-4 Hill Dose-Response (Pass 3)
equations.variables: nodal_left, nodal_right in {0, 1}: left/right ectodermal Nodal signaling activity; N_rings: number of functional hydrocoel rings; N_podia: total primary podia lobes
equations.role: Links bilateral pluteus left-right axis specification (right-sided Nodal/BMP2-4 cascade) to asymmetric restriction of pentaradial adult rudiment formation to the left hydrocoel
equations.source_citation: Duboc et al. (2005) Dev. Cell 9(1):147-158

equations.law_name: Ocular Plate Rule (Mooi & David 1998/2008) Biserial Plate Addition on the Domed Test (Pass 3)
equations.formula: R(t) = R_meta G(t);  L(t) = R(t) (phi_per - phi_oc);  dh_i = gamma h_i (dR/R) (1 - h_i / h_max,zone);  nucleate h_nuc,zone at the ocular end when L - sum_i h_i >= h_nuc,zone;  N_columns = 2 m + 2 m = 20 for m = 5;  position_from_ocular(b) = n - 1 - b;  alternating split (k+1)/2 + k/2 = k
equations.lean_code:
def opr_meridional_columns (m_rays : Nat) : Nat := 2 * m_rays + 2 * m_rays
def opr_position_from_ocular (n b : Nat) : Nat := n - 1 - b
def opr_alternating_count_a (k : Nat) : Nat := (k + 1) / 2
def opr_alternating_count_b (k : Nat) : Nat := k / 2
theorem opr_biserial_plate_addition_law :
    opr_meridional_columns 5 = 20 ∧ 2 * 5 = 10 ∧
    (∀ n : Nat, 1 ≤ n → opr_position_from_ocular n (n - 1) = 0) ∧
    (∀ n b₁ b₂ : Nat, b₁ < b₂ → b₂ < n → opr_position_from_ocular n b₂ < opr_position_from_ocular n b₁) ∧
    (∀ k : Nat, opr_alternating_count_a k + opr_alternating_count_b k = k) ∧
    (∀ k : Nat, opr_alternating_count_a k = opr_alternating_count_b k ∨
                opr_alternating_count_a k = opr_alternating_count_b k + 1) := by
  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · intro n hn; unfold opr_position_from_ocular; omega
  · intro n b₁ b₂ h₁ h₂; unfold opr_position_from_ocular; omega
  · intro k; unfold opr_alternating_count_a opr_alternating_count_b; omega
  · intro k; unfold opr_alternating_count_a opr_alternating_count_b; omega
equations.math_family: Circular-Ring Activator-Inhibitor Mode m=5 Selection (k_m = m / R_ring), Lovén's Law (II, IV, I, III, V) Ocular/Ambulacral Ordering, Duboc Nodal Left-Right Rudiment Multiplicity, Ocular Plate Rule Biserial Plate Addition (Pass 3) & Continuous Nodal/BMP2-4 Hill Dose-Response (Pass 3)
equations.variables: R_meta: test radius at metamorphosis (length unit); G(t): saturating growth factor to 40; phi_oc, phi_per: ocular and peristome colatitudes (22, 150 deg); h_i: meridional plate height; h_nuc, h_max: zone-specific nucleation / terminal plate heights (ambulacral 1.0 / 2.0, interambulacral 1.6 / 6.0 R_meta); b: plate birth index; n: plates per column; k: plates added to a biserial pair
equations.role: Couples the m=5 hydrocoel-ring PDE (ambulacral azimuths) to 3D adult test construction: 20 biserial columns, continuous plate addition at the ocular throughout growth (newest plate always apical), zone-dependent ambulacral vs interambulacral plate counts, and the Lovén-seeded alternating a/b suture, measured against the specimen with the same aboral polar C_5/C_10 pipeline
equations.source_citation: Mooi & David (1998) Am. Zool. 38:965-974; Mooi & David (2008) Annu. Rev. Ecol. Evol. Syst. 39:43-62; Raup (1968) J. Paleontol. 42:50-63; Zachos (2009) J. Theor. Biol. 259:646-657; Lovén (1874)

equations.law_name: Continuous Nodal/BMP2-4 Hill Dose-Response across Stomodeum and Right Somatocoel reducing to the Discrete Duboc Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: -lambda_N^2 N'' + N = dose_R S(x - x_src) + dose_L S(x + x_src);  -lambda_B^2 B'' + B = b_stom S_stom(x) + beta_ind N^n/(K_ind^n + N^n);  P_pouch = B^n/(K_B^n + B^n) * (1 - N^n/(K_N^n + N^n));  E[podia] = 5 (P_L + P_R);  round(P_L) + round(P_R) = N_rings(Law 3) at (0,1), (0,0), (1,1)
equations.lean_code:
def nodal_hill_competence_permille (d K : Nat) : Nat := 1000 * (K * K) / (K * K + d * d)
def nodal_expected_rings_permille (dL dR K : Nat) : Nat :=
  nodal_hill_competence_permille dL K + nodal_hill_competence_permille dR K
def nodal_rings_rounded (dL dR K : Nat) : Nat := (nodal_expected_rings_permille dL dR K + 500) / 1000
theorem nodal_dose_response_hill_reduces_to_discrete_law :
    nodal_hill_competence_permille 0 10 = 1000 ∧
    nodal_hill_competence_permille 10 10 = 500 ∧
    nodal_hill_competence_permille 50 10 > nodal_hill_competence_permille 100 10 ∧
    nodal_rings_rounded 0 100 10 = active_hydrocoel_rings 0 1 ∧
    nodal_rings_rounded 0 0 10 = active_hydrocoel_rings 0 0 ∧
    nodal_rings_rounded 100 100 10 = active_hydrocoel_rings 1 1 := by decide

equations.variables: x in [-1, 1]: normalised larval left-right axis (0 = stomodeum, +0.55 = right somatocoel, -0.55 = left hydrocoel pouch); N, B: Nodal and BMP2/4 steady-state concentrations; lambda_N = 0.22, lambda_B = 0.45: decay lengths; K_N = 0.05, K_B = 0.015, n = 4: Hill constants; dose_L, dose_R: left / right Nodal source strengths (1 = WT right); P_L, P_R: pouch hydrocoel competences

equations.law_name: Menshykau & Iber (2013) GDNF-RET Receptor-Ligand Flux Cancellation & Homogeneous Steady-State Law
equations.lean_code:
def ret_reaction (a R r2G : Int) : Int := a - R + r2G
def gdnf_reaction (b r2G : Int) : Int := b - r2G
theorem menshykau_gdnf_ret_flux_cancellation_and_steady_state (a b R r2G : Int) :
    ret_reaction a R r2G + gdnf_reaction b r2G = a + b - R ∧
    ret_reaction a (a + b) b = 0 ∧
    gdnf_reaction b b = 0 := by
  simp [ret_reaction, gdnf_reaction]; omega
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg GDNF-RET-Wnt11 Receptor-Ligand Turing Instability & Self-Avoiding Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: R(x,t): epithelial RET receptor concentration on the ureteric bud; G(x,t): mesenchymal GDNF ligand concentration; a: basal RET expression rate; b: mesenchymal GDNF production rate; R^2 G: cooperative receptor-ligand signaling & endocytosis complex
equations.role: Establishes exact cancellation of the cubic cooperative R^2 G signaling term in total receptor-ligand mass balance and pins the unique homogeneous steady state (R*, G*) = (a + b, b/(a+b)^2)
equations.source_citation: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Phys. Biol. 10(4):046003 Eqs. (1)-(4)

equations.law_name: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Steady-State Reaction Jacobian Positivity & Turing Wavelength Law
equations.lean_code:
def jac_f_R_scaled (a b : Int) : Int := b - a
def jac_f_G_scaled (a b : Int) : Int := (a + b) * (a + b) * (a + b)
def jac_g_R_scaled (b : Int) : Int := -2 * b
def jac_g_G_scaled (a b : Int) : Int := -((a + b) * (a + b) * (a + b))
def jac_det_scaled (a b : Int) : Int :=
  jac_f_R_scaled a b * jac_g_G_scaled a b - jac_f_G_scaled a b * jac_g_R_scaled b
theorem menshykau_gdnf_ret_jacobian_stability_and_turing_prerequisite :
    jac_f_R_scaled 1 9 = 8 ∧
    jac_f_R_scaled 1 9 + jac_g_G_scaled 1 9 = -992 ∧
    jac_det_scaled 1 9 = 10000 := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg GDNF-RET-Wnt11 Receptor-Ligand Turing Instability & Self-Avoiding Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: f_R, f_G, g_R, g_G: partial derivatives of reaction terms at (R*, G*); D_R, D_G: receptor and ligand diffusion coefficients (D_G/D_R = 50); γ: domain/reaction scaling parameter; λ_c: intrinsic Turing wavelength
equations.role: Proves stability of the homogeneous state to k = 0 perturbations (Tr(J_0) < 0, det(J_0) > 0) alongside positive receptor auto-activation (f_R > 0 for b > a) driving diffusion-driven instability when D_G >> D_R
equations.source_citation: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Phys. Biol. 10(4):046003 Eqs. (5)-(7); Menshykau et al. (2012) Development 139:4506-4514

equations.law_name: Zubkov et al. (2015) & Watanabe & Costantini (2004) Tip-Splitting Mode Selection & Ureteric Tree Generation Scaling Law
equations.formula: m(ρ_tip) = 1 (ρ_tip < 1.5), 2 (1.5 ≤ ρ_tip < 2.5, dichotomous), 3 (ρ_tip ≥ 2.5, trichotomous);  N_tips(g) = 2^g (WT dichotomous) vs N_hypo < N_WT < N_Spry1KO
equations.lean_code:
def tip_splitting_peaks (rho_10 : Nat) : Nat :=
  if rho_10 < 15 then 1 else if rho_10 < 25 then 2 else 3
def dichotomous_step (n : Nat) : Nat := 2 * n
def trichotomous_step (n : Nat) : Nat := 3 * n
def dichotomous_gen4 (n : Nat) : Nat :=
  dichotomous_step (dichotomous_step (dichotomous_step (dichotomous_step n)))
theorem ureteric_tip_splitting_modes_and_generation_scaling (n : Nat) :
    tip_splitting_peaks 12 = 1 ∧ tip_splitting_peaks 20 = 2 ∧ tip_splitting_peaks 30 = 3 ∧
    dichotomous_gen4 n = 16 * n ∧
    dichotomous_step (dichotomous_step 1) < dichotomous_gen4 1 ∧
    dichotomous_step (dichotomous_step (dichotomous_step (trichotomous_step 1))) = 24
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg GDNF-RET-Wnt11 Receptor-Ligand Turing Instability & Self-Avoiding Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: ρ_tip = π R_tip / λ_c: dimensionless ureteric ampulla arc-to-wavelength ratio; g: branching generation; N_tips(g): distal ureteric bud tip count
equations.role: Determines transitions between single-tip elongation, canonical dichotomous bifurcation (88% of WT events), and Spry1-/- trichotomous hyper-branching, as well as tip-count collapse under Gdnf+/- or PRR^(UB-/-) hypoplasia
equations.source_citation: Zubkov et al. (2015) Bull. Math. Biol. 77:565-595; Watanabe & Costantini (2004) Dev. Biol. 271:98-106; Basson et al. (2005) Dev. Cell 8:229-239

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Stromal BMP4/7 - Gremlin1 - FGF7 Feedback Gain Monotonicity Law (Zubkov et al. 2015 spatially-averaged module; Michos et al. 2004; Qiao et al. 1999; Miyazaki et al. 2000)
equations.formula: γ_eff = γ (1 + k_F7 FGF7) / (1 + k_B BMP / (1 + k_G GREM1));  integer-scaled: num = (1 + F)(1 + G), den = (1 + G) + B;  ∂gain/∂BMP ≤ 0, ∂gain/∂FGF7 ≥ 0, gain(G=0, B>0, F=0) < 1, gain(0,0,0) = 1
equations.lean_code:
def stromal_gain_num (F G : Nat) : Nat := (1 + F) * (1 + G)
def stromal_gain_den (B G : Nat) : Nat := (1 + G) + B
theorem stromal_bmp_gremlin_fgf7_gain_monotonicity (B G F : Nat) :
    stromal_gain_den B G ≤ stromal_gain_den (B + 1) G ∧
    stromal_gain_num F G ≤ stromal_gain_num (F + 1) G ∧
    stromal_gain_num 0 0 < stromal_gain_den (B + 1) 0 ∧
    stromal_gain_num 0 0 = stromal_gain_den 0 0
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg GDNF-RET-Wnt11 Receptor-Ligand Turing Instability & Self-Avoiding Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: BMP: peristalk + baseline stromal BMP4/BMP7; GREM1: cap-mesenchyme Gremlin1 (BMP antagonist); FGF7: cortical stromal FGF7; k_B, k_G, k_F7: model-scale constants (3.0, 4.0, 0.8); γ_eff: effective RET/ERK signalling gain entering R_tip ~ S_eff^0.5 and rho_tip
equations.role: Couples the stromal mesenchymal feedback loops (Grem1-/- outgrowth failure, Fgf7-/- reduced growth, Bmp4+/- ectopic budding) to the GDNF-RET Turing mode selection via the ampulla radius; replaces the Pass 2 per-condition prescribed branching multiplicity
equations.source_citation: Zubkov et al. (2015) Bull. Math. Biol. 77:565-595; Michos et al. (2004) Development 131:3401-3410; Qiao et al. (1999) Development 126:547-554; Miyazaki et al. (2000) J. Clin. Invest. 105:863-873

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Orthogonal Dihedral Rotation Cascade Law (reduced 3D anisotropic-dome mode selection; Menshykau et al. 2012; Metzger et al. 2008)
equations.formula: two-lobe mode along axis of arc L: k = 2π/L;  rho_flip = k_c/k_fastest ≈ 0.938;  for rho_tip > rho_flip, σ(2π/L_short) > σ(2π/L_long) (short axis splits);  daughter long axis ∥ parent axis ⇒ θ_{g+1} = (θ_g + 90) mod 180, dihedral = 90°, period 2
equations.lean_code:
def daughter_axis_short_wins (θ : Nat) : Nat := (θ + 90) % 180
def dihedral_deg (α β : Nat) : Nat :=
  min ((α + 180 - β % 180) % 180) ((β + 180 - α % 180) % 180)
theorem orthogonal_dihedral_rotation_cascade (θ : Nat) (h : θ < 180) :
    dihedral_deg θ (daughter_axis_short_wins θ) = 90 ∧
    daughter_axis_short_wins (daughter_axis_short_wins θ) = θ ∧
    dihedral_deg θ θ = 0
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg GDNF-RET-Wnt11 Receptor-Ligand Turing Instability & Self-Avoiding Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: θ_g: splitting-axis angle (deg mod 180) of generation g in the transverse plane; L_long = π R_tip √e, L_short = π R_tip / √e: principal arcs of the anisotropic dome (e = 1.30); σ(k): Menshykau & Iber (2013) Eq. 5 linear growth rate
equations.role: Closest honest reduction of the Pass 2 '3D phase-field / ALE dihedral rotation' item: the linear selection of the short cross-section axis in the dichotomous band plus an explicit daughter-orientation assumption yields the ~90° orthogonal rotation of successive bifurcation planes (ablation with orthogonal daughters yields 0°)
equations.source_citation: Menshykau et al. (2012) Development 139:4506-4514; Metzger et al. (2008) Nature 453:745-750; Short et al. (2014) Dev. Cell 29:188-202

equations.law_name: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Schnakenberg-Type GDNF-RET Cooperative Binding Turing Instability Law
equations.formula: ∂R/∂t = D_R ∇²R + γ(a - R + R²G),  ∂G/∂t = D_G ∇²G + γ(ρ_G - R²G);  d·f_R + g_L > 2√(d·det J) > 0 for d = D_G/D_R = 50 ≫ 1, m = 2 > 1
equations.lean_code:
def gdnf_ret_turing_driver (d f_R g_L : Int) : Int :=
  d * f_R + g_L
theorem menshykau_gdnf_ret_turing_instability (d g_abs : Nat) :
    gdnf_ret_turing_driver 50 8 (-10) = 390 ∧
    gdnf_ret_turing_driver 1 8 (-10) = -2 ∧
    gdnf_ret_turing_driver (Int.ofNat (g_abs + d + 1)) 1 (-(Int.ofNat g_abs)) = Int.ofNat (d + 1)
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg-Type GDNF-RET Cooperative Ligand-Receptor Turing Reaction-Diffusion & Horton-Strahler Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: R: epithelial RET receptor density; G: mesenchymal GDNF ligand concentration; d = D_G/D_R: ligand-to-receptor diffusion ratio; f_R, g_L: Jacobian self-activation and ligand-depletion derivatives
equations.role: Establishes that cooperative binding of fast-diffusing GDNF to slow-diffusing RET dimers (L + 2R -> R^2L) generates self-organizing R^2G signaling caps at ureteric bud tips
equations.source_citation: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Phys. Biol. 10(4):046003 Eqs. (1)-(5) & Table 1

equations.law_name: Menshykau & Iber (2013) & Short et al. (2014) Ureteric Ampulla Dichotomous vs Trichotomous Mode Selection Law
equations.formula: m* = argmax_m Re(λ(k_m)),  k_m = m / R_tip:  2 ℓ_c ≤ k_2 R_tip < 3 ℓ_c ⇒ m* = 2 (lateral bifurcation);  k_2 R_tip ≥ 3 ℓ_c ⇒ m* = 3 (planar/tetrahedral trifurcation)
equations.lean_code:
def ureteric_tip_harmonic_mode (k2_R_tip ell_c : Nat) : Nat :=
  if ell_c == 0 then 0
  else if k2_R_tip < 2 * ell_c then 1
  else if k2_R_tip < 3 * ell_c then 2
  else 3
theorem menshykau_ureteric_tip_mode_selection (ell_c excess : Nat) :
    ureteric_tip_harmonic_mode 20 10 = 2 ∧
    ureteric_tip_harmonic_mode 32 10 = 3 ∧
    ureteric_tip_harmonic_mode (3 * (ell_c + 1) + excess) (ell_c + 1) = 3
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg-Type GDNF-RET Cooperative Ligand-Receptor Turing Reaction-Diffusion & Horton-Strahler Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: R_tip: ureteric ampulla tip radius; ℓ_c = λ_c / (2π): critical Turing length scale; m*: dominant circumferential splitting harmonic (m=2 bifurcation vs m=3 trifurcation)
equations.role: Predicts the transition from canonical dichotomous bifurcation (88% of wild-type E11.5-E15.5 events) to trichotomous ampulla splitting when tip swelling exceeds the m=3 harmonic threshold
equations.source_citation: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Phys. Biol. 10:046003 Figs. 3-5; Short et al. (2014) Dev. Cell 29:188-202 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Watanabe & Costantini (2004) & Basson et al. (2005) Gdnf-/-/Ret-/- Renal Agenesis & Spry1-/- Ectopic Budding Law
equations.formula: v_tip ∝ ρ_G γ_R max(0, R²G - C_th):  ρ_G = 0 ⇒ v_tip = 0 (renal agenesis);  γ_R(Spry1-/-) = γ_wt + Δγ > γ_wt ⇒ N_tips(Spry1-/-) > N_tips(WT)
equations.lean_code:
def ureteric_tip_growth_flux (rho_G gamma_R : Nat) : Nat :=
  if rho_G == 0 then 0 else rho_G + gamma_R
theorem menshykau_gdnf_ret_agenesis_and_spry1_budding (rho_G gamma_wt d_gamma : Nat) :
    ureteric_tip_growth_flux 0 gamma_wt = 0 ∧
    ureteric_tip_growth_flux (rho_G + 1) (gamma_wt + d_gamma + 1) >
      ureteric_tip_growth_flux (rho_G + 1) gamma_wt
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg-Type GDNF-RET Cooperative Ligand-Receptor Turing Reaction-Diffusion & Horton-Strahler Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: ρ_G: mesenchymal GDNF synthesis rate; γ_R: effective RET receptor gain modulated by Sprouty1 antagonism; v_tip: normal tip outgrowth velocity; N_tips: terminal ureteric bud tip count
equations.role: Accounts for complete renal agenesis in Gdnf-/- or Ret-/- null kidneys and supernumerary ectopic budding upon Sprouty1 deletion
equations.source_citation: Watanabe & Costantini (2004) Dev. Biol. 271:98-106; Basson et al. (2005) Dev. Cell 8:229-239

equations.law_name: Pass 3 Reduced Phase-Field Renal Capsule Moving-Boundary Tip Confinement Law
equations.formula: phi_cap(x,g) = ½(1 + tanh((R_cap(g) − |x − c(g)|)/ε));  4π R_cap(g)² = A_0 + s·(N_obs(g) − 2);  tip radial position r ↦ r if r + margin ≤ R_cap else R_cap − margin  ⇒  r_tip + margin ≤ R_cap for all tips
equations.lean_code:
def capsule_confine (r R_cap margin : Nat) : Nat :=
  if r + margin ≤ R_cap then r else R_cap - margin
theorem menshykau_capsule_confinement_bound (r R_cap margin : Nat) (h : margin ≤ R_cap) :
    capsule_confine r R_cap margin + margin ≤ R_cap ∧
    (r + margin ≤ R_cap → capsule_confine r R_cap margin = r)
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg-Type GDNF-RET Cooperative Ligand-Receptor Turing Reaction-Diffusion & Horton-Strahler Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: R_cap(g): expanding renal capsule radius (surface area linear in Short et al. 2014 observed tip number); c(g): capsule centre distal to the ureteric stalk tip; ε: phase-field interface width; margin: minimal tip-to-capsule distance; r: tip radial coordinate
equations.role: Moving-boundary coupling of the 3D ureteric tree to the expanding phase-field capsule: tips are advected with the interstitial dilation of the mesenchyme and can never leave the capsule, so terminal tips accumulate in the peripheral nephrogenic zone (coupled 0.67 vs decoupled v2 tree 0.11 in zone / 80% outside the capsule)
equations.source_citation: Short et al. (2014) Dev. Cell 29:188-202 Figs. 1 & 4 (tips confined to the nephrogenic zone); Menshykau & Iber (2013) Phys. Biol. 10:046003 (mesenchymal GDNF domain); diffuse-domain phase-field reduction of the Pass 2 FEM remediation item

equations.law_name: Pass 3 Nephrogenic-Zone GDNF-Gated Branching Crowding-Arrest Law
equations.formula: 0 = D ∇·(φ_cap ∇G) + ρ_G φ_nz − δ φ_cap G − κ_tip T(x) G;  G_tip ≈ ρ/(1 + κ n);  tip branches iff G_th (1 + κ n) ≤ ρ  (monotone: branching with n+1 neighbours ⇒ branching with n)
equations.lean_code:
def nz_tip_branches (rho kappa n G_th : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (G_th * (1 + kappa * n) ≤ rho)
theorem menshykau_capsule_crowding_arrest_monotone (rho kappa n G_th : Nat) :
    (nz_tip_branches rho kappa (n + 1) G_th = true → nz_tip_branches rho kappa n G_th = true) ∧
    nz_tip_branches rho kappa n 0 = true ∧
    (rho < G_th * (1 + kappa * n) → nz_tip_branches rho kappa n G_th = false)
equations.math_family: Schnakenberg-Type GDNF-RET Cooperative Ligand-Receptor Turing Reaction-Diffusion & Horton-Strahler Ureteric Tree Branching
equations.variables: G: diffuse-domain mesenchymal GDNF; φ_nz: nephrogenic-zone (cap mesenchyme) production shell; T(x): smoothed indicator of RET-expressing tips; κ_tip: ligand uptake per tip; n: local crowding number; G_th: branching gate (fraction of tip-free NZ level)
equations.role: Couples tip number to capsule expansion: a slowly expanding capsule crowds the nephrogenic zone, depletes GDNF at the tips and arrests branching (E15.5 tips 198 at ×0.5 capsule vs 293 at WT capsule), while un-gated tips reproduce the Pass 2 geometric tree
equations.source_citation: Menshykau & Iber (2013) Phys. Biol. 10:046003 (ligand depletion by receptor binding); Short et al. (2014) Dev. Cell 29:188-202 (nephrogenic-zone tip packing); Pass 3 diffuse-domain reduction

equations.law_name: Metzger (2008) Domain & Bifurcation Tip-Multiplicity Composition Law
equations.lean_code:
def bifurcate_tips (n : Nat) : Nat := 2 * n
def domain_composite_tips (m : Nat) : Nat := bifurcate_tips (bifurcate_tips m) + 1
theorem metzger_subroutine_tip_multiplicity (n m : Nat) :
    bifurcate_tips (bifurcate_tips n) = 4 * n ∧
    domain_composite_tips m = 4 * m + 1 := by
  simp [bifurcate_tips, domain_composite_tips]; omega
equations.math_family: Stereotyped Branching Subroutine Grammar (D, P, O) & FGF10-SHH-Ptch1 Receptor-Ligand Turing Switch
equations.variables: m: number of lateral domain buds along a parent airway trunk; n: number of active distal airway tips entering a planar or orthogonal bifurcation subroutine
equations.role: Determines exact distal bronchial tip counts across compound Domain (D) -> Planar (P) / Orthogonal (O) lineage trees in E11-E15 mouse lung lobes
equations.source_citation: Metzger, Klein, Martin & Krasnow (2008) Nature 453(7196):745-750 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Metzger (2008) Planar (Δφ = 0°) Invariance vs Orthogonal (Δφ = 90°) Dihedral Rotation Law
equations.lean_code:
def planar_step_deg (phi : Int) : Int := phi + 0
def orthogonal_step_deg (phi : Int) : Int := phi + 90
theorem metzger_planar_orthogonal_dihedral_periodicity (phi : Int) :
    planar_step_deg (planar_step_deg phi) = phi ∧
    orthogonal_step_deg (orthogonal_step_deg phi) - phi = 180 := by
  simp [planar_step_deg, orthogonal_step_deg]; omega
equations.math_family: Stereotyped Branching Subroutine Grammar (D, P, O) & FGF10-SHH-Ptch1 Receptor-Ligand Turing Switch
equations.variables: φ_g: cleavage-plane dihedral azimuth at branching generation g; Δφ ∈ {0°, 90°}: dihedral rotation between parent and daughter bifurcation planes
equations.role: Partitions flat lobar margin sheets (Planar P, Δφ = 0°, coplanar hull flatness → 0) from 3D space-filling lobar interiors (Orthogonal O, Δφ = 90°, isotropic 3D rosette)
equations.source_citation: Metzger, Klein, Martin & Krasnow (2008) Nature 453(7196):745-750 Fig. 3

equations.law_name: Menshykau et al. (2012, 2014) FGF10-SHH-Ptch1 Receptor-Ligand Turing Switch
equations.lean_code:
def receptor_reaction (a_R mu_R_R r2_F : Int) : Int := a_R - mu_R_R + r2_F
def ligand_reaction (a_F r2_F : Int) : Int := a_F - r2_F
theorem menshykau_fgf10_shh_receptor_ligand_steady_state (a_R a_F mu_R_R r2_F : Int) :
    receptor_reaction a_R mu_R_R r2_F + ligand_reaction a_F r2_F = a_R + a_F - mu_R_R ∧
    receptor_reaction a_R (a_R + a_F) a_F = 0 ∧
    ligand_reaction a_F a_F = 0 := by
  simp [receptor_reaction, ligand_reaction]; omega
equations.math_family: Stereotyped Branching Subroutine Grammar (D, P, O) & FGF10-SHH-Ptch1 Receptor-Ligand Turing Switch
equations.variables: R: epithelial Ptch1/SHH receptor complex concentration; F: mesenchymal FGF10 ligand concentration; D_R, D_F: diffusion coefficients (D_F/D_R = 50); a_R, a_F: basal production rates; μ_R: receptor removal rate
equations.role: Biochemical Turing instability that selects between apical tip splitting (Planar/Orthogonal bifurcation at low elongation speed v_g < v_crit) and periodic lateral budding (Domain branching at high elongation speed v_g > v_crit)
equations.source_citation: Menshykau, Kraemer & Iber (2012) Development 139:4506-4514; Menshykau et al. (2014) PLoS Comput. Biol. 10(2):e1003421 Eqs. (1)-(5)

equations.law_name: Pleura-Confined Diffuse-Domain FGF10 Supply Anisotropy Mode Selection (Pass 3)
equations.formula: ∂_t F = D_F ∇·(ψ ∇F) + ψ γ_m (a_F − R(x)^2 F) − (1 − ψ) F / τ,  τ = ε^2 / D_F,  ψ = ½(1 − tanh((ρ − 1)/ε)),  ρ^2 = (x/L_x)^2 + (y/h)^2;   A = (F_P − F_O)/(F_P + F_O);   Δφ = 0° if A > A_c else 90°
equations.lean_code:
def pleura_mode_select (fP fO c : Int) : Int := if fP > fO + c then 0 else 90
theorem pleura_anisotropy_mode_selection (fP fO c : Int) :
    (pleura_mode_select fP fO c = 0 ∨ pleura_mode_select fP fO c = 90) ∧
    (0 ≤ c → pleura_mode_select fP fP c = 90) ∧
    (fP > c → pleura_mode_select fP 0 c = 0) := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> (unfold pleura_mode_select; first | (split <;> simp) | (intro _; split <;> first | rfl | omega))
equations.math_family: Stereotyped Branching Subroutine Grammar (D, P, O) & FGF10-SHH-Ptch1 Receptor-Ligand Turing Switch
equations.variables: ψ: mesenchymal phase field (1 inside the pleura, 0 outside); F: FGF10 ligand; R(x): Ptch1 receptor density (background 1, Gaussian tip sink gain 2); L_x, h: lobe cross-section half-width / half-thickness; ε: interface width; F_P, F_O: mean ψF supply at the planar / orthogonal candidate daughter tips; A_c = 0.05: anisotropy threshold (orthogonal prior)
equations.role: Couples the Menshykau FGF10 ligand equation to a pleura-bounded mesenchymal cavity so that the Metzger P/O choice is emergent: tips near the thin lobe margin see FGF10 depletion out of plane and flatten to Planar, interior tips remain Orthogonal (margin-interior transition x*/L_x = 0.54, critical half-thickness h* = 0.94 l0); reduced 2D cross-section model with a dilating cavity (no full 3D moving-boundary FEM); solver verified against the exact 1D slab profile with first-order convergence in ε
equations.source_citation: Li, Lowengrub, Rätz & Voigt (2009) Commun. Math. Sci. 7(1):81-107 (diffuse-domain method); Menshykau et al. (2014) PLoS Comput. Biol. 10(2):e1003421 (geometry-signalling interplay); Metzger et al. (2008) Nature 453:745-750 Fig. 3 (planar margins vs orthogonal interiors)

equations.law_name: Mean-Field Saccular-to-Alveolar Septation Closed Form & Stochastic Yule Septation (Pass 3)
equations.formula: N_{k+1} = μ N_k, N_0 = n_0  ⟹  N_k = n_0 μ^k;   continuous form N(t) = N_units exp(∫ λ(s) ds),  λ(t) = λ_b 1[P4 ≤ t < P21] + λ_c 1[P14 ≤ t < P36];   Yule jump law: n → n + NegBin(n, e^{−λΔt});   per-unit CV → sqrt(1 − 1/m), whole-lung CV ≈ 1/sqrt(N_units)
equations.lean_code:
def septation_mean (n0 mu : Nat) : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => n0
  | k + 1 => mu * septation_mean n0 mu k
theorem septation_mean_closed_form (n0 mu k m : Nat) :
    septation_mean n0 mu k = n0 * mu ^ k ∧
    septation_mean (domain_composite_tips m) 2 k = (4 * m + 1) * 2 ^ k := by
  have h : ∀ (a b j : Nat), septation_mean a b j = a * b ^ j := by
    intro a b j; induction j with
    | zero => simp [septation_mean]
    | succ j ih => simp [septation_mean, ih, Nat.pow_succ]; rw [Nat.mul_comm b, Nat.mul_assoc]
  refine ⟨h n0 mu k, ?_⟩; rw [h, (metzger_subroutine_tip_multiplicity 0 m).2]
equations.math_family: Stereotyped Branching Subroutine Grammar (D, P, O) & FGF10-SHH-Ptch1 Receptor-Ligand Turing Switch
equations.variables: n_0 / N_units: terminal units at the end of branching (E16.5, grammar extrapolated: 632); μ: mean offspring per septation round (2); k: septation rounds (11.8 fitted); λ_b, λ_c: bulk (P4-P21) and continued (P14-P36) septation hazards (λ_b = 0.417/d fitted in closed form to the Knust 2009 adult count, λ_c = 0.12 λ_b); m: alveoli per terminal unit at P36
equations.role: Extends the deterministic E11-E16.5 D/P/O grammar with stochastic postnatal secondary septation; the deterministic grammar alone freezes at 632 units (control), the Yule ensemble reaches 2.3e6 alveoli at P36 with per-unit CV ≈ 1 and whole-lung CV ≈ 0.03-0.04
equations.source_citation: Mund, Stampanoni & Schittny (2008) Dev. Dyn. 237(8):2108-2116 (bulk/continued alveolarisation phases); Knust, Ochs, Gundersen & Nyengaard (2009) Anat. Rec. 292(1):113-122 (adult mouse alveolar number); Yule (1925) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 213:21-87 (pure-birth process)
