models.name: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) & Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) ocular dominance column development & plasticity, with Pass 3 orientation coupling and curved V1 sheet
models.organism: Macaca mulatta / Felis catus primary visual cortex (V1 Layer IVC)
models.math_family: Correlation-Based Hebbian Ocular Dominance Columns & Critical-Period Plasticity

equations.law_name: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Sum/Difference Synaptic Mode Decoupling & Subtractive Normalization Conservation Law
equations.formula: dS_Sigma/dt = d(S^L + S^R)/dt = 0;   dS_Delta/dt = (A * I * (C^{LL} - C^{LR})) * S_Delta - gamma * S_Delta
equations.lean_code:
def raw_rate_L (S_L S_R C_LL C_LR : Int) : Int :=
  C_LL * S_L + C_LR * S_R
def raw_rate_R (S_L S_R C_LL C_LR : Int) : Int :=
  C_LR * S_L + C_LL * S_R
def norm_rate_2L (S_L S_R C_LL C_LR : Int) : Int :=
  2 * raw_rate_L S_L S_R C_LL C_LR - (raw_rate_L S_L S_R C_LL C_LR + raw_rate_R S_L S_R C_LL C_LR)
def norm_rate_2R (S_L S_R C_LL C_LR : Int) : Int :=
  2 * raw_rate_R S_L S_R C_LL C_LR - (raw_rate_L S_L S_R C_LL C_LR + raw_rate_R S_L S_R C_LL C_LR)
def sum_mode_rate_2 (S_L S_R C_LL C_LR : Int) : Int :=
  norm_rate_2L S_L S_R C_LL C_LR + norm_rate_2R S_L S_R C_LL C_LR
def diff_mode_rate (C_Delta S_Delta : Int) : Int :=
  C_Delta * S_Delta
theorem miller_sum_difference_decoupling (S_L S_R C_LL C_LR C_Delta S_Delta : Int)
    (h_cd : C_Delta > 0) (h_sd : S_Delta > 0) :
    sum_mode_rate_2 S_L S_R C_LL C_LR = 0 ∧
    norm_rate_2L 10 4 8 2 = 36 ∧
    norm_rate_2R 10 4 8 2 = -36 ∧
    norm_rate_2L 10 4 8 2 - norm_rate_2R 10 4 8 2 = 2 * (8 - 2) * (10 - 4) ∧
    diff_mode_rate C_Delta S_Delta > 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [sum_mode_rate_2, norm_rate_2L, norm_rate_2R]
    omega
  · dsimp [diff_mode_rate]
    exact Int.mul_pos h_cd h_sd
equations.math_family: Correlation-Based Hebbian Ocular Dominance Columns & Critical-Period Plasticity
equations.variables: S_L, S_R: left-eye and right-eye geniculocortical synaptic densities in V1 Layer IVC; S_Sigma = S_L + S_R: conserved total synaptic density; S_Delta = S_L - S_R: ocular dominance difference mode; C_LL, C_LR: within-eye and between-eye LGN activity correlations; C_Delta = C_LL - C_LR: difference correlation
equations.role: Proves that subtractive homeostatic normalization identically conserves total cortical synaptic weight (dS_Sigma/dt = 0) while decoupling the ocular dominance difference mode S_Delta = S_L - S_R so that positive difference correlation C_Delta = C_LL - C_LR > 0 strictly amplifies eye-specific segregation
equations.source_citation: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Science 245(4918):605-615 Eqs. 1-6

equations.law_name: Swindale (1980) & Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Mexican-Hat Band-Pass Peak Wavenumber & Characteristic Column Wavelength Law
equations.formula: k_c^2 = 2 * ln(kappa_I * sigma_I^2 / sigma_E^2) / (sigma_I^2 - sigma_E^2) > 0;   lambda_c = 2 * pi / k_c = 2 * w_col approx 800 um
equations.lean_code:
def mexican_hat_denom (sigma_E_sq sigma_I_sq : Int) : Int :=
  sigma_I_sq - sigma_E_sq
def full_cycle_wavelength (w_col : Int) : Int :=
  2 * w_col
theorem swindale_miller_bandpass_wavelength (sigma_E_sq sigma_I_sq w_1 w_2 : Int)
    (h_range : sigma_E_sq < sigma_I_sq) (h_w : w_1 < w_2) :
    mexican_hat_denom sigma_E_sq sigma_I_sq > 0 ∧
    mexican_hat_denom (109 * 109) (218 * 218) = 35643 ∧
    (3 * (218 * 218)) / (4 * (109 * 109)) = 3 ∧
    full_cycle_wavelength 400 = 800 ∧
    full_cycle_wavelength w_1 < full_cycle_wavelength w_2 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [mexican_hat_denom]
    omega
  · dsimp [full_cycle_wavelength]
    omega
equations.math_family: Correlation-Based Hebbian Ocular Dominance Columns & Critical-Period Plasticity
equations.variables: sigma_E, sigma_I: intracortical excitatory and inhibitory lateral interaction ranges (109 um, 218 um); kappa_I: relative inhibitory amplitude (0.75); k_c: fastest-growing Fourier wavenumber; lambda_c = 2 * w_col: full-cycle ocular dominance band wavelength (800 um for 400 um single-eye column width)
equations.role: Proves positivity of the Mexican-hat Fourier band-pass denominator sigma_I^2 - sigma_E^2 > 0 and inhibitory moment ratio kappa_I * sigma_I^2 / sigma_E^2 = 3 > 1, selecting the characteristic macaque V1 Layer IVC stripe wavelength lambda_c ~ 800 um (400 um per single-eye column)
equations.source_citation: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Science 245:605-615; Swindale (1980) Proc. R. Soc. B 208:243-264; Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 278:377-409

equations.law_name: Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) Monocular Deprivation Territory Shift vs Stryker & Harris (1986) Bilateral TTX Blockade Law
equations.formula: f_L(Delta_MD) = 0.5 - Delta_MD < 0.5 < f_R(Delta_MD) = 0.5 + Delta_MD, f_L + f_R = 1;   C_Delta = 0 ==> omega(k) = -gamma < 0
equations.lean_code:
def deprived_eye_pct (delta_md : Int) : Int :=
  50 - delta_md
def open_eye_pct (delta_md : Int) : Int :=
  50 + delta_md
def dispersion_omega (C_Delta AK_hat gamma : Int) : Int :=
  C_Delta * AK_hat - gamma
theorem hubel_wiesel_md_and_ttx_blockade (delta_md AK_hat gamma : Int)
    (h_md : delta_md > 0) (h_gamma : gamma > 0) :
    deprived_eye_pct 0 = 50 ∧
    open_eye_pct 0 = 50 ∧
    deprived_eye_pct delta_md < 50 ∧
    open_eye_pct delta_md > 50 ∧
    open_eye_pct delta_md - deprived_eye_pct delta_md = 2 * delta_md ∧
    deprived_eye_pct delta_md + open_eye_pct delta_md = 100 ∧
    deprived_eye_pct 26 = 24 ∧
    open_eye_pct 26 = 76 ∧
    dispersion_omega 0 AK_hat gamma < 0 := by
  refine ⟨by decide, by decide, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [deprived_eye_pct]
    omega
  · dsimp [open_eye_pct]
    omega
  · dsimp [open_eye_pct, deprived_eye_pct]
    omega
  · dsimp [deprived_eye_pct, open_eye_pct]
    omega
  · dsimp [dispersion_omega]
    omega
equations.math_family: Correlation-Based Hebbian Ocular Dominance Columns & Critical-Period Plasticity
equations.variables: delta_md > 0: monocular deprivation competitive shift (percentage points); deprived_eye_pct, open_eye_pct: Layer IVC cortical territory percentages occupied by deprived and open eyes; dispersion_omega(C_Delta, AK_hat, gamma): Fourier growth rate under bilateral TTX blockade (C_Delta = 0)
equations.role: Proves that critical-period monocular deprivation shifts cortical territory away from 50/50 symmetry (shrinking deprived-eye stripes to 24% and expanding open-eye columns to 76% while conserving total area 100%), whereas bilateral TTX blockade (C_Delta = 0) makes omega(k) = -gamma < 0 for all wavenumbers and prevents column segregation
equations.source_citation: Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 278(961):377-409; Stryker & Harris (1986) J. Neurosci. 6(8):2117-2133

equations.law_name: Swindale (1992) & Obermayer & Blasdel (1993) Orthogonal Iso-Orientation / Ocular Dominance Border Coupling Quadratic Form (Pass 3)
equations.formula: dz/dt = A*(I_z*z)*C_Delta - gamma*z - |z|^2 z + div(D_c * w * n n^T grad z) - beta_blob * S_Delta^2 * z,  n = grad S_Delta/|grad S_Delta|;   v^T (g g^T) v = (g . v)^2 >= 0, = 0 iff grad theta _|_ grad S_Delta
equations.lean_code:
def dot2 (g1 g2 v1 v2 : Int) : Int :=
  g1 * v1 + g2 * v2
def coupling_form (g1 g2 v1 v2 : Int) : Int :=
  dot2 g1 g2 v1 v2 * dot2 g1 g2 v1 v2
theorem orthogonal_coupling_quadratic_form (g1 g2 v1 v2 : Int)
    (h_orth : g1 * v1 + g2 * v2 = 0) :
    coupling_form g1 g2 v1 v2 = 0 ∧
    (∀ a b c d : Int, coupling_form a b c d ≥ 0) ∧
    coupling_form 3 4 (-4) 3 = 0 ∧
    coupling_form 3 4 3 4 = 625 ∧
    coupling_form 3 4 3 4 > coupling_form 3 4 (-4) 3 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [coupling_form, dot2]
    rw [h_orth]
    rfl
  · intro a b c d
    dsimp [coupling_form]
    rcases Int.le_total 0 (dot2 a b c d) with h | h
    · exact Int.mul_nonneg h h
    · exact Int.mul_nonneg_of_nonpos_of_nonpos h h
equations.math_family: Correlation-Based Hebbian Ocular Dominance Columns & Critical-Period Plasticity
equations.variables: z = r exp(2 i theta): complex orientation preference field (r selectivity, theta preferred orientation); g = grad S_Delta: ocular dominance gradient (normal to OD borders); v = grad z: orientation gradient; D_c = 4500 um^2: anisotropic coupling diffusivity; w = |g|^2/(|g|^2 + eps^2): border weight; beta_blob = 0.6: selectivity suppression at OD column centres
equations.role: Proves the Pass 3 anisotropic coupling tensor n n^T is positive semidefinite (its quadratic form (g . v)^2 is non-negative), so the coupling is a stable gradient flow whose energy vanishes exactly when the orientation gradient is orthogonal to the OD gradient, i.e. when iso-orientation contours cross OD borders at right angles; the script measures the resulting intersection angle (coupled ~67 deg vs uncoupled ablation ~42 deg, random baseline 45 deg), pinwheel density and CO-blob-like low-selectivity patches at OD column centres
equations.source_citation: Swindale (1992) Biol. Cybern. 66(3):217-230; Obermayer & Blasdel (1993) J. Neurosci. 13(10):4114-4129; Horton & Hubel (1981) Nature 292:762-764; Kaschube et al. (2010) Science 330:1113-1116

equations.law_name: Curved Riemannian V1 Sheet Chart Projection Compression of the Intrinsic Stripe Period (Pass 3)
equations.formula: g_ij = delta_ij + h_i h_j;  Delta_g f = (1/sqrt g) d_i(sqrt g g^{ij} d_j f);  I * S = H_{sigma_E^2/2} S - kappa_I H_{sigma_I^2/2} S;   lambda_chart^2 (1 + slope^2) = lambda^2  ==>  lambda_chart^2 <= lambda^2
equations.lean_code:
def chart_metric (slope_sq : Int) : Int :=
  1 + slope_sq
def intrinsic_period_sq (lambda_chart_sq slope_sq : Int) : Int :=
  lambda_chart_sq * chart_metric slope_sq
theorem curved_chart_projection_compression (lambda_chart_sq slope_sq : Int)
    (h_slope : slope_sq ≥ 0) (h_pos : lambda_chart_sq ≥ 0) :
    lambda_chart_sq ≤ intrinsic_period_sq lambda_chart_sq slope_sq ∧
    intrinsic_period_sq lambda_chart_sq 0 = lambda_chart_sq ∧
    intrinsic_period_sq (400 * 400) 3 = 800 * 800 ∧
    chart_metric slope_sq ≥ 1 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [intrinsic_period_sq, chart_metric]
    have h_prod : lambda_chart_sq * slope_sq ≥ 0 := Int.mul_nonneg h_pos h_slope
    have h_expand : lambda_chart_sq * (1 + slope_sq) = lambda_chart_sq + lambda_chart_sq * slope_sq := by
      rw [Int.mul_add, Int.mul_one]
    rw [h_expand]
    omega
  · dsimp [intrinsic_period_sq, chart_metric]
    omega
  · dsimp [chart_metric]
    omega
equations.math_family: Correlation-Based Hebbian Ocular Dominance Columns & Critical-Period Plasticity
equations.variables: h(u,v): cortical height field over the 6.4 mm chart (operculum dome amplitude 1000 um / width 2000 um, calcarine groove depth 1600 um / width 500 um); g_ij: induced metric, sqrt g <= 2.44; H_t: Laplace-Beltrami heat kernel (Gaussian of width sigma == heat flow for time sigma^2/2); lambda: intrinsic stripe period (~800 um); lambda_chart: period seen in the flat chart; slope^2 = h'^2 along the chart direction
equations.role: Proves that on the curved V1 sheet the intrinsic stripe period selected by the Mexican-hat band-pass is invariant while its chart projection is compressed by 1/sqrt(1 + slope^2) (equality only in the flat limit); the script realises the Mexican hat as a difference of Laplace-Beltrami heat kernels with zero-flux elliptical perimeter and measures intrinsic lambda_g ratio (calcarine wall / flat) ~1.07, chart ratio ~0.72, and OD border / perimeter intersection angle ~70 deg (LeVay et al. 1985)
equations.source_citation: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Science 245:605-615; LeVay, Connolly, Houde & Van Essen (1985) J. Neurosci. 5(2):486-501

measurements.name: Normal binocular 2D FFT characteristic ocular dominance stripe wavelength lambda_emp
measurements.method: Power-weighted dominant 2D FFT wavelength 2*pi / k_dom of normal binocular S_Delta(x,y) on 6400x6400 um V1 sheet
measurements.reference_source: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Science 245:605-615; Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 278:377-409 (Lean 4 swindale_miller_bandpass_wavelength)

measurements.name: Normal binocular left-eye cortical territory fraction f_L
measurements.method: Fraction of V1 Layer IVC grid points with S_Delta(x,y) > 0 under symmetric binocular input (C_Delta = 0.80, b_MD = 0)
measurements.reference_source: Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 278:377-409; Swindale (1980) Proc. R. Soc. B 208:243-264

measurements.name: Hubel-Wiesel critical-period monocular deprivation (MD) deprived-eye territory fraction f_L
measurements.method: Fraction of V1 Layer IVC occupied by deprived Left-eye stripes (S_Delta > 0) under monocular lid suture (b_MD = -0.36)
measurements.reference_source: Hubel, Wiesel & LeVay (1977) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 278:377-409 Figs. 14-22 (Lean 4 hubel_wiesel_md_and_ttx_blockade)

measurements.name: Strabismus interocular decorrelation broadened stripe wavelength lambda_strab
measurements.method: 2D FFT dominant wavelength under strabismic interocular decorrelation (C_Delta = 1.25, sigma_I = 244 um)
measurements.reference_source: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Science 245:605-615; Lowel (1994) J. Neurosci. 14:7451-7468 (broadened strabismic columns)

measurements.name: Intracortical inhibition range sigma_I vs simulated column wavelength Pearson correlation r
measurements.method: Linear correlation between analytical Mexican-hat wavelength lambda_c(sigma_I) and 2D FFT simulated wavelength across 6-point sigma_I sweep (170-290 um)
measurements.reference_source: Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) Science 245:605-615 Fig. 4 (linear scaling of column width with lateral interaction range)

measurements.name: Tangential ODC specimen CV stripe territory fraction f_L and branchpoint count
measurements.method: Automated CV median thresholding, 2D Hanning FFT radial spectrum, and medial-ridge branchpoint extraction on odc_tangential_pattern_specimen.png
measurements.reference_source: Tangential V1 ODC stripe pattern (Wikimedia Commons File:ODCsim.png, CC BY-SA 3.0) & Macaca mulatta V1 Nissl section (CC0)

measurements.name: Coupled iso-orientation contour / OD border mean intersection angle phi
measurements.method: Mean angle between grad S_Delta and grad theta (theta = arg z / 2, wrap-free gradient Im(conj z grad z)/(2|z|^2)) over OD border cells |S_Delta| < 0.1 max, coupled run (D_c = 4500 um^2, beta_blob = 0.6); uncoupled ablation reported in note
measurements.reference_source: Obermayer & Blasdel (1993) J. Neurosci. 13:4114-4129 (iso-orientation contours cross OD borders at steep, near-orthogonal angles; random-direction baseline 45 deg); Swindale (1992) Biol. Cybern. 66:217-230 coupling model

measurements.name: Coupled orientation map pinwheel density per orientation hypercolumn Lambda^2
measurements.method: Count of +-1 winding-number plaquettes of arg z times Lambda^2 / L^2, Lambda = power-weighted FFT wavelength of Re z
measurements.reference_source: Kaschube et al. (2010) Science 330:1113-1116 (pinwheel density ~ pi per hypercolumn in primates/carnivores); model value NOT fitted

measurements.name: Fraction of low-selectivity (CO-blob-like) patches located in OD column centres
measurements.method: Local minima of smoothed selectivity r = |z| (7x7 window, lowest 30th percentile) classified as column-centre if |S_Delta| > median |S_Delta|; random baseline 0.5
measurements.reference_source: Horton & Hubel (1981) Nature 292:762-764; Obermayer & Blasdel (1993) J. Neurosci. 13:4114-4129 (CO blobs / low-selectivity zones centred on OD columns)

measurements.name: Curved V1 sheet intrinsic (metric) stripe wavelength ratio calcarine wall / flat control
measurements.method: lambda_g = 2 pi / sqrt(<g^{ij} d_i S d_j S> / <S^2>) (sqrt g-weighted) in the steep calcarine wall band (sqrt g > 1.4) of the curved Laplace-Beltrami heat-kernel run divided by the same estimator on the flat torus control; naive chart (Euclidean) estimator ratio given in note
measurements.reference_source: Lean 4 curved_chart_projection_compression (intrinsic period invariant; chart period compressed by 1/sqrt(1 + slope^2)); Miller, Keller & Stryker (1989) lambda_c = 800 um

measurements.name: OD border / V1 perimeter intersection angle on the curved masked sheet
measurements.method: |grad S_Delta|-weighted mean angle between grad S_Delta and the perimeter normal over boundary cells (zero-flux boundary); 90 deg means OD borders meet the perimeter orthogonally, random baseline 45 deg
measurements.reference_source: LeVay, Connolly, Houde & Van Essen (1985) J. Neurosci. 5:486-501 (ocular dominance stripes meet the V1/V2 border approximately at right angles)

models.name: Hamant et al. (2008) & Heisler et al. (2010) pressurized SAM shell stress tensor, cortical microtubule alignment, PIN1-auxin phyllotactic mechanics, and (Pass 3) 3D multi-layered L1/L2/L3 Voronoi cell mesh with dynamic division planes
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (shoot apical meristem L1 epidermis, L2/L3 corpus & floral primordia)
models.math_family: Pressurized Thin-Shell Principal Stress Tensor, Nematic Microtubule Feedback & Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Auxin Transport

equations.law_name: Hamant et al. (2008) Pressurized Shell Principal Stress & 2:1 Cylinder Anisotropy Law
equations.formula: σ_θθ^dome = σ_mm^dome = PR/(2t) (A_σ = 0);  σ_θθ^cyl = PR/t = 2 σ_zz^cyl (A_σ = 1/3);  κ_m σ_m + κ_θ σ_θ = P/t
equations.lean_code:
def sphere_hoop_stress_2t (P R : Int) : Int := P * R
def sphere_meridional_stress_2t (P R : Int) : Int := P * R
def cylinder_hoop_stress_2t (P R : Int) : Int := 2 * (P * R)
def cylinder_axial_stress_2t (P R : Int) : Int := P * R
theorem hamant_2008_pressurized_shell_anisotropy (P R : Int) :
    sphere_hoop_stress_2t P R - sphere_meridional_stress_2t P R = 0 ∧
    cylinder_hoop_stress_2t P R = 2 * cylinder_axial_stress_2t P R ∧
    3 * (cylinder_hoop_stress_2t P R - cylinder_axial_stress_2t P R) =
      cylinder_hoop_stress_2t P R + cylinder_axial_stress_2t P R
equations.math_family: Pressurized Thin-Shell Principal Stress Tensor, Nematic Microtubule Feedback & Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Auxin Transport
equations.variables: P: turgor pressure (MPa); R: shell curvature radius (um); t: L1 outer epidermal wall thickness (um); σ_θθ, σ_mm: circumferential and meridional principal tensile stresses (MPa); A_σ = (σ_1 - σ_2)/(σ_1 + σ_2): stress anisotropy
equations.role: Predicts isotropic tensile stress on the spherical SAM dome (driving hyper-dynamic isotropic microtubules), 2:1 circumferential hoop stress on cylindrical flanks, and amplified 5:1 crease stress at negative-Gaussian-curvature primordium boundaries
equations.source_citation: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322(5908):1650-1655 Figs. 1-2 & SOM Text S1

equations.law_name: Kirsch / Hamant et al. (2008) Laser Ablation Wound Rim Hoop-Stress Doubling Law
equations.lean_code:
def kirsch_radial_scaled (sig_inf r_sq a0_sq : Int) : Int :=
  sig_inf * (r_sq - a0_sq)
def kirsch_hoop_scaled (sig_inf r_sq a0_sq : Int) : Int :=
  sig_inf * (r_sq + a0_sq)
theorem hamant_2008_ablation_rim_hoop_doubling (sig_inf r_sq a0_sq : Int) :
    kirsch_radial_scaled sig_inf a0_sq a0_sq = 0 ∧
    kirsch_hoop_scaled sig_inf a0_sq a0_sq = 2 * (sig_inf * a0_sq) ∧
    kirsch_radial_scaled sig_inf r_sq a0_sq + kirsch_hoop_scaled sig_inf r_sq a0_sq =
      2 * (sig_inf * r_sq)
equations.math_family: Pressurized Thin-Shell Principal Stress Tensor, Nematic Microtubule Feedback & Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Auxin Transport
equations.variables: σ_∞: far-field isotropic dome membrane tension (MPa); a_0: laser ablation wound radius (um); r: radial distance from wound center (um)
equations.role: Explains why single-cell or patch laser ablation in the L1 epidermis zeroes radial tension and doubles circumferential tension at the wound rim, reorienting both CMTs and PIN1 circumferentially around the ablation site
equations.source_citation: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 3; Heisler et al. (2010) PLoS Biol. 8:e1000516 Fig. 4

equations.law_name: Heisler et al. (2010) & Jonsson et al. (2006) Stress- & Auxin-Coupled PIN1 Active Transport Conservation Law
equations.formula: P_ij = P_tot exp(b_a a_j + b_σ |n_ij · e_1,i|^2) / Z_i;  J_{i←j} = T_PIN (P_ji a_j - P_ij a_i),  J_{i←j} + J_{j←i} = 0
equations.lean_code:
def pin1_active_flux (T_pin P_ij P_ji a_i a_j : Int) : Int :=
  T_pin * (P_ji * a_j - P_ij * a_i)
theorem heisler_2010_pin1_flux_conservation (T_pin P_ij P_ji P_sym a_i a_j a : Int) :
    pin1_active_flux T_pin P_ij P_ji a_i a_j + pin1_active_flux T_pin P_ji P_ij a_j a_i = 0 ∧
    pin1_active_flux T_pin P_sym P_sym a a = 0
equations.math_family: Pressurized Thin-Shell Principal Stress Tensor, Nematic Microtubule Feedback & Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Auxin Transport
equations.variables: a_i: auxin concentration in L1 cell i; P_ij: PIN1 efflux carrier allocated to membrane i→j; e_1,i: maximal principal tensile stress eigenvector; T_PIN: active polar transport coefficient
equations.role: Couples PIN1 membrane allocation to both neighbor auxin concentration and cell-wall tensile stress orientation, generating golden-angle (137.5 deg) phyllotactic auxin maxima and synchronous PIN1/CMT reorientation
equations.source_citation: Heisler et al. (2010) PLoS Biol. 8(10):e1000516 Figs. 1-4; Jonsson et al. (2006) PNAS 103:1633-1638 Eqs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Hamant et al. (2008) / Kutschera & Niklas (2007) Multi-layered L1/L2/L3 Pressurized Shell Load-Sharing Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: N_j = k_j ε (compatible in-plane strain ε across glued layers);  Σ_j N_j = (k_1 + k_2 + k_3) ε;  N_1 / Σ N = k_1 / Σ k;  2 Σ N = P R (Laplace-Young recovered as the aggregate)
equations.lean_code:
def layer_membrane_tension (k eps : Int) : Int :=
  k * eps
theorem hamant_2008_multilayer_shell_load_sharing (k1 k2 k3 eps P R : Int)
    (h_laplace : 2 * ((k1 + k2 + k3) * eps) = P * R) :
    layer_membrane_tension k1 eps + layer_membrane_tension k2 eps + layer_membrane_tension k3 eps
      = (k1 + k2 + k3) * eps ∧
    layer_membrane_tension k1 eps * (k1 + k2 + k3) = k1 * ((k1 + k2 + k3) * eps) ∧
    2 * (layer_membrane_tension k1 eps + layer_membrane_tension k2 eps + layer_membrane_tension k3 eps)
      = P * R
equations.math_family: Pressurized Thin-Shell Principal Stress Tensor, Nematic Microtubule Feedback & Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Auxin Transport
equations.variables: k_j: in-plane wall stiffness of layer j (L1 epidermis, L2 sub-epidermis, L3 corpus; k_1 = 5 k_inner); ε: common in-plane membrane strain; N_j: in-plane tension carried by layer j; P: turgor pressure; R: dome radius
equations.role: Predicts that the stiff outer L1 wall carries the stiffness share k_1/Σk of the total turgor-driven shell tension (5/7 for the k_L1/k_inner = 5 assumption); checked numerically against the per-layer virial tension sums of the 3D Voronoi mesh (0.714 vs 0.714) and across the stiffness-ratio sweep
equations.source_citation: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 SOM Text S1 (thick L1 outer wall); Kutschera & Niklas (2007) J. Plant Physiol. 164:1395-1409 (epidermal-growth-control theory)

equations.law_name: Louveaux et al. (2016) Tension-Aligned Anticlinal Division Plane & Sachs Volume Bookkeeping Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: n_div = n_s × e_1  ⇒  n_div · n_s = 0 (anticlinal: new wall contains the surface normal) and n_div · e_1 = 0 (new wall contains the maximal-tension direction);  V_1 + V_2 = V_mother, V_1 = V_2 ⇒ 2 V_1 = V_mother
equations.lean_code:
def cross_x (a2 a3 b2 b3 : Int) : Int := a2 * b3 - a3 * b2
def cross_y (a1 a3 b1 b3 : Int) : Int := a3 * b1 - a1 * b3
def cross_z (a1 a2 b1 b2 : Int) : Int := a1 * b2 - a2 * b1
def dot3 (x1 x2 x3 y1 y2 y3 : Int) : Int := x1 * y1 + x2 * y2 + x3 * y3
theorem louveaux_2016_anticlinal_tension_division_plane
    (n1 n2 n3 e1 e2 e3 V1 V2 Vm : Int)
    (h_sum : V1 + V2 = Vm) (h_sym : V1 = V2) :
    dot3 (cross_x n2 n3 e2 e3) (cross_y n1 n3 e1 e3) (cross_z n1 n2 e1 e2) n1 n2 n3 = 0 ∧
    dot3 (cross_x n2 n3 e2 e3) (cross_y n1 n3 e1 e3) (cross_z n1 n2 e1 e2) e1 e2 e3 = 0 ∧
    2 * V1 = Vm
equations.math_family: Pressurized Thin-Shell Principal Stress Tensor, Nematic Microtubule Feedback & Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Auxin Transport
equations.variables: n_s: outward surface normal of the L1/L2 cell; e_1: in-plane maximal-tension eigenvector of the cell tension tensor (tissue virial + cell-autonomous turgor term); n_div: normal of the new cell wall; V_1, V_2, V_mother: daughter and mother cell volumes
equations.role: Defines the mechanical (Louveaux 2016) division rule used for L1/L2 cells of the 3D mesh: the new anticlinal wall is placed along maximal tension; the Gibbs rule of Besson & Dumais (2011, β = 20.6) is the geometric alternative. Benchmarked against the 65-77 % shortest-plane and 81 % symmetric-division statistics of the shoot apex (the tension rule reaches only 0.38 shortest-plane, reported as a FAILED comparison)
equations.source_citation: Louveaux et al. (2016) PNAS 113(30):E4294-E4303; Besson & Dumais (2011) PNAS 108:6294-6299; Reddy et al. (2004) Development 131:4225-4237

measurements.name: cylindrical_flank_hoop_to_axial_stress_ratio
measurements.method: Doubly-curved thin-shell Laplace-Young equilibrium (anisotropy A_sigma = 0.3333 vs exact 1/3, SD = 0.0001)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 1 (sigma_theta / sigma_z = 2.0 on cylindrical stem flank)

measurements.name: primordium_saddle_crease_stress_anisotropy
measurements.method: Negative-Gaussian-curvature (K = -0.00036 um^-2) boundary crease shell balance (sigma_theta = 145.0 MPa vs sigma_m = 29.0 MPa)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 1-2 (5:1 hoop-to-meridional crease stress ratio => A_sigma = 2/3)

measurements.name: four_zone_cmt_nematic_order_pearson_r
measurements.method: Pearson correlation across 4 SAM curvature zones (r = 0.9921, p = 7.88e-03, RMSE = 0.0523 ± 0.0042)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Figs. 1-2 regional CMT nematic order S_CMT in {0.18, 0.54, 0.72, 0.86}

measurements.name: l1_pin1_cmt_coaligned_30deg_fraction
measurements.method: 168-cell coupled Auxin-PIN1-CMT ODE on the paraboloidal SAM dome with the base stress field from the 3D L1/L2/L3 mesh (p = 4.46e-41 Binomial test vs uniform null 0.3333; Pass 2 analytic-field ablation gives 0.8491). CAVEAT: the fraction is dominated by the imposed 15.5% PIN1-switching subpopulation and 0.165 rad jitter (not an emergent ODE output)
measurements.reference_source: Heisler et al. (2010) PLoS Biology 8(10):e1000516 Fig. 1-2 (84.5% of L1 cells aligned within +-30 deg)

measurements.name: l1_pin1_cmt_circular_correlation
measurements.method: Mean axial nematic cosine <cos(2*(theta_CMT - theta_PIN1))> across polarized L1 cells (SE = 0.021)
measurements.reference_source: Heisler et al. (2010) PLoS Biology 8(10):e1000516 Fig. 2 axial circular correlation between PIN1 and CMTs

measurements.name: phyllotactic_divergence_angle_mean
measurements.method: Successive azimuthal angles between auxin convergence maxima P1..P5 (mean = 137.06 ± 5.07 deg SD)
measurements.reference_source: Jonsson et al. (2006) PNAS 103:1633-1638 & Mirabet et al. (2012) PLoS Comput. Biol. 8:e1002389 golden divergence angle 137.5078 deg

measurements.name: laser_ablation_rim_circumferential_fraction
measurements.method: Kirsch wound-rim hoop-stress doubling (sigma_theta/sigma_inf = 2.0000) driving CMT+PIN1 reorientation at t = 6.0 h (vs pre-ablation control 0.34)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 3 & Heisler et al. (2010) Fig. 4 (post-ablation circumferential alignment 0.91 vs 0.34 pre-ablation baseline)

measurements.name: oryzalin_depolymerization_control_nematic_order
measurements.method: Negative perturbation control k_sigma = 0, dE_fiber = 0 (wall stiffness ratio E_par/E_perp = 1.0000 vs WT crease 4.7069)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 2 (20 ug/mL oryzalin CMT depolymerization abolishes nematic order S -> 0.04 and anisotropic stiffening)

measurements.name: specimen_sam_dome_calibrated_radius
measurements.method: Parabolic L1 contour fit on segmented Toluidine-Blue Arabidopsis SAM section (R_px = 81.3 px, N = 539 nuclei, NN spacing CV = 0.2602). CAVEAT: the 50.0 um value is the calibration target itself (R_px is scaled to 50 um), so this is an identity, not a measurement
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 & File:Arabidopsis round SAM.jpg (Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 4.0)

measurements.name: multilayer_mesh_flank_l1_hoop_alignment_fraction
measurements.method: Fraction of interior L1 cells with r >= 30 um whose in-plane virial tension e_1 (same-sheet wall springs, 526-cell 4-sheet Voronoi mesh at quasi-static equilibrium, relative residual 0.145, mean L1 strain 0.0447) lies within 30 deg of the circumferential direction
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 1 & SOM Text S1: axisymmetric membrane theory puts the maximal principal tension e_1 circumferentially everywhere on the dome flank (CMTs circumferential on the flank)

measurements.name: multilayer_mesh_l1_anisotropy_vs_membrane_law_rmse
measurements.method: RMSE between the radial-bin L1 in-plane tension anisotropy of the 3D mesh (bin-mean tensors, 6 bins 0-46 um: [0.098 0.05 0.029 0.048 0.036 0.086]) and the membrane law ([0.003 0.025 0.06 0.101 0.139 0.172]); Pearson r = -0.107 (p = 0.84). FAILED comparison: the cell-centre mesh reproduces the hoop DIRECTION but not the radial growth of the anisotropy MAGNITUDE (apex bin shows a sunflower-lattice artefact)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) SOM thin-shell balance on the paraboloid z = -r^2/(2R): A_sigma(r) = (1-q)/(3-q), q = kappa_m/kappa_theta (0 at the apex, 0.20 at r = R)

measurements.name: multilayer_mesh_dome_centre_anisotropy
measurements.method: Anisotropy of the bin-mean in-plane L1 tension tensor over interior L1 cells with r <= 15 um in the 3D mesh (nonzero value is a lattice-irregularity artefact of the sunflower centre, not a physical prediction)
measurements.reference_source: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322:1650-1655 Fig. 1: isotropic tension (sigma_theta = sigma_m) on the spherical apical dome

measurements.name: multilayer_mesh_l1_tension_load_share
measurements.method: Sum of tensile in-plane (same-sheet) wall-spring tensions in L1 divided by the sum over L1 + L2 + L3 (shares [0.714 0.127 0.103 0.056]); stiffness-ratio sweep k_L1/k_inner in {1, 2, 5, 10} reported in Panel H
measurements.reference_source: Lean Law 4 (hamant_2008_multilayer_shell_load_sharing): compatible-strain layer stack predicts N_1/N_total = k_1/(k_1 + k_2 + k_3) = 5/7 for the k_L1/k_inner = 5 assumption (Hamant 2008 SOM thick L1 outer wall; Kutschera & Niklas 2007). MODEL-INTERNAL reference, not a measured specimen value

measurements.name: l1_l2_tension_rule_shortest_plane_fraction
measurements.method: Fraction of the 164 L1/L2 divisions under the tension rule (plane normal n_s x e_1 of tissue virial + cell-autonomous turgor tension) whose anticlinal wall length is within 5% of the shortest of 12 candidate anticlinal planes through the centroid; two-sided binomial p = 5.38e-18 vs 0.71. Gibbs-rule ablation (Besson-Dumais 2011, beta = 20.6): 0.7205 (n = 161). FAILED comparison for the tension rule: the tissue-level hoop tension overrides cell shape in this mesh
measurements.reference_source: Louveaux et al. (2016) PNAS 113:E4294-E4303: 65-77% of all observed division planes at the Arabidopsis shoot apex are the shortest (Besson-Dumais class 1) plane (midpoint 0.71)

measurements.name: l1_l2_symmetric_division_fraction
measurements.method: Fraction of L1/L2 divisions whose smaller daughter polyhedron occupies 40-50% of the two daughters' summed Voronoi volume one step after cytokinesis (Sachs/Lean Law 5 bookkeeping; summed daughter volume / mother volume = 1.292, a Voronoi re-tessellation artefact)
measurements.reference_source: Louveaux et al. (2016) PNAS 113:E4294 Fig. S2E: 81% of 829 shoot-apex divisions have the smaller daughter at 40-50% of the mother's area

measurements.name: l1_l2_anticlinal_new_wall_fraction

models.name: Mitchison (1980, 1981) & Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) with-the-flux auxin canalization: exponent bifurcation, growing hex-lamina canalization (solved), Sachs wound bypass (solved + prescribed), hand-drawn Feugier venation templates, and cleared-leaf specimen segmentation
models.organism: Pisum sativum & Arabidopsis thaliana (dicot leaf lamina & stem vascular strands)
models.math_family: With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization & PIN1 Carrier-Allocated Venation Topology

equations.law_name: Mitchison (1980) Linear vs Quadratic Flux-Canalization Symmetry Breaking Law
equations.formula: dD_ij/dt = α |φ_ij|^p + β - γ D_ij;  D_2 dD_1/dt - D_1 dD_2/dt = β(D_2 - D_1) (p=1, diffuse)  vs  (D_1 - D_2)(α (ΔS)^2 D_1 D_2 - β) (p=2, winner-take-all canalization)
equations.lean_code:
def linear_canalization_rhs (alpha beta gamma dS D : Int) : Int :=
  alpha * (D * dS) + beta - gamma * D
def quadratic_canalization_rhs (alpha beta gamma dS D : Int) : Int :=
  alpha * (D * dS) * (D * dS) + beta - gamma * D
theorem mitchison_1980_quadratic_vs_linear_symmetry_breaking
    (alpha beta gamma dS D1 D2 : Int) :
    D2 * linear_canalization_rhs alpha beta gamma dS D1 -
      D1 * linear_canalization_rhs alpha beta gamma dS D2 = beta * (D2 - D1) ∧
    D2 * quadratic_canalization_rhs alpha beta gamma dS D1 -
      D1 * quadratic_canalization_rhs alpha beta gamma dS D2 =
      (D1 - D2) * (alpha * dS * dS * D1 * D2 - beta)
equations.math_family: With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization & PIN1 Carrier-Allocated Venation Topology
equations.variables: D_ij: intercellular auxin diffusivity across cell wall (i,j); φ_ij = D_ij(S_i - S_j): auxin flux; p: feedback exponent (p<=1 diffuse sheet, p=2 single-cell strand); α: flux reinforcement gain; β: basal diffusivity synthesis; γ: carrier degradation rate
equations.role: Proves why linear feedback (p <= 1) damps conductivity perturbations back to a broad diffuse sheet whereas quadratic feedback (p = 2) triggers supercritical pitchfork winner-take-all symmetry breaking into 1-cell-wide vascular strands
equations.source_citation: Mitchison (1980) Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 207(1166):79-109 Eqs. 2-6 & Fig. 1

equations.law_name: Mitchison (1980) Canalized Vein Auxin Concentration Drainage Law (S_vein < S_parenchyma)
equations.formula: D^*(φ) = (α φ^2 + β)/γ,  S(φ) = φ / D^*(φ)  ⇒  S_par - S_vein = (φ_vein - φ_par)(α φ_vein φ_par - β) / (γ D_vein D_par) > 0
equations.lean_code:
def steady_conductivity_scaled (alpha beta phi : Int) : Int :=
  alpha * phi * phi + beta
def drainage_conc_diff_scaled (alpha beta phi_vein phi_par : Int) : Int :=
  phi_par * steady_conductivity_scaled alpha beta phi_vein -
    phi_vein * steady_conductivity_scaled alpha beta phi_par
theorem mitchison_1980_vein_concentration_drainage (alpha beta phi_vein phi_par : Int) :
    drainage_conc_diff_scaled alpha beta phi_vein phi_par =
      (phi_vein - phi_par) * (alpha * phi_vein * phi_par - beta)
equations.math_family: With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization & PIN1 Carrier-Allocated Venation Topology
equations.variables: S_vein, S_par: steady-state auxin concentration inside the canalized vascular strand vs surrounding parenchyma; φ_vein, φ_par: axial auxin flux in vein vs parenchyma
equations.role: Proves that quadratic flux-driven conductivity growth drops the auxin concentration inside a canalizing vein below that of surrounding parenchyma (S_vein < S_par), turning the differentiating vein into a lateral drainage sink that recruits tributaries and bypasses stem wounds (Sachs 1981)
equations.source_citation: Mitchison (1980) Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 207:79-109 Fig. 2 & pp. 83-87; Sachs (1981) Adv. Bot. Res. 9:151-262

equations.law_name: Mitchison (1981) & Feugier et al. (2005) Polar Carrier-Allocated Intercellular Flux Conservation Law
equations.formula: φ_{i→j} = P_ij S_i - P_ji S_j + D_0(S_i - S_j),  φ_{i→j} + φ_{j→i} = 0;  dP_ij/dt = F(φ_{i→j}, P_cell) - γ P_ij
equations.lean_code:
def polar_canalization_flux (P_ij P_ji D0 S_i S_j : Int) : Int :=
  P_ij * S_i - P_ji * S_j + D0 * (S_i - S_j)
theorem feugier_2005_polar_flux_conservation (P_ij P_ji D0 S_i S_j S : Int) :
    polar_canalization_flux P_ij P_ji D0 S_i S_j +
      polar_canalization_flux P_ji P_ij D0 S_j S_i = 0 ∧
    polar_canalization_flux P_ij P_ji D0 S S = (P_ij - P_ji) * S
equations.math_family: With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization & PIN1 Carrier-Allocated Venation Topology
equations.variables: P_ij: directed PIN1 efflux carrier permeability on membrane face i→j; S_i: cytoplasmic auxin concentration in cell i; D_0: apoplastic passive diffusivity; β_1 = E - V + C: venation graph cycle rank (areole loop count)
equations.role: Guarantees exact pairwise intercellular auxin conservation while enabling polar transport against concentration gradients and governing the Feugier et al. (2005) topological transition between open hierarchical venation trees (β_1 = 0) and closed-areole venation loops (β_1 > 0)
equations.source_citation: Mitchison (1981) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 295:461-471 Eqs. 1-5; Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236:366-375 Eqs. 1-9 & Figs. 3-7

equations.law_name: Mitchison (1980) Saturating Flux-Feedback Canalization on a Growing Lamina — Boundedness & Monotonicity Law (Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def saturating_feedback_num (alpha phi phis : Int) : Int :=
  alpha * (phi * phi) * (phis * phis)
def saturating_feedback_den (phi phis : Int) : Int :=
  phis * phis + phi * phi
theorem saturating_canalization_feedback_bounded (alpha phi phis : Int) (h : 0 ≤ alpha) :
    saturating_feedback_num alpha phi phis ≤ alpha * (phis * phis) * saturating_feedback_den phi phis
theorem saturating_canalization_feedback_monotone (phi1 phi2 phis : Int)
    (h0 : 0 ≤ phi1) (h12 : phi1 ≤ phi2) :
    phi1 * phi1 * saturating_feedback_den phi2 phis ≤ phi2 * phi2 * saturating_feedback_den phi1 phis
equations.math_family: With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization & PIN1 Carrier-Allocated Venation Topology
equations.variables: φ_ij = D_ij (S_i - S_j): wall flux on the hexagonal cell lattice; φ_s: soft-saturation flux (1.0 = 100 cells' production); α, β, γ as in Law 1; the lamina grows by cell division (4x cells per stage) so the midrib flux grows 4x per stage
equations.role: Guarantees that the flux feedback stays bounded (F ≤ α φ_s^2) as total lamina production grows with cell number, while preserving the Law 1 winner-take-all ordering (more flux => at least as much reinforcement), which is why a hierarchy of strand orders can be solved across three growth stages without a hard conductance cap turning strands into sheets
equations.source_citation: Mitchison (1980) Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 207:79-109 Eqs. 2-3 (feedback form); saturation after Feugier, Mochizuki & Iwasa (2005) J. Theor. Biol. 236:366-375 (saturating carrier response)

equations.law_name: Sachs (1981) Irreversible Vascular Differentiation Monotonicity Law (Pass 3 ablation)
equations.formula: d_{t+1} = d_t ∨ [D_ij(t) > D_diff];  d_t = true ⇒ d_{t+1} = true (differentiated wall set is non-decreasing)
equations.lean_code:
def differentiation_update (d : Bool) (exceeds : Bool) : Bool :=
  d || exceeds
theorem irreversible_differentiation_monotone (d exceeds : Bool) (h : d = true) :
    differentiation_update d exceeds = true
equations.math_family: With-the-Flux Auxin Canalization & PIN1 Carrier-Allocated Venation Topology
equations.variables: d_t: differentiated flag of a cell wall; D_diff = 3 β/γ: differentiation threshold
equations.role: Formalises the optional irreversibility rule used as an ablation in the growing-lamina solver; the solver shows that irreversibility alone does not close loops (β_1 = 0 in both variants), carrying loop closure forward as an open remediation item
equations.source_citation: Sachs (1981) Adv. Bot. Res. 9:151-262 (irreversible vascular differentiation); Feugier & Iwasa (2006) J. Theor. Biol. 243:235-244

models.name: Moulton, Goriely & Chirat (2015) & Chirat et al. (2013) hierarchical mollusc aperture spine folding and fractal frond serration
models.organism: Murex pecten (Venus comb murex) & Chicoreus ramosus (ramose murex / Muricidae)
models.math_family: Kirchhoff-Clebsch Elastica on Unilateral Foundation & Hierarchical Multi-Stage Mantle Spine Buckling

equations.law_name: Moulton, Goriely & Chirat (2015) Multi-Generational Fractal Fronding Wavenumber Cascade
equations.lean_code:
def frond_wavenumber_residual (E_h3 k4 K_s : Int) : Int :=
  E_h3 * k4 - 3 * K_s
def frond_cascade_gap (h_coarse h_fine : Int) : Int :=
  h_coarse * h_coarse * h_coarse - h_fine * h_fine * h_fine
theorem moulton_secondary_frond_cascade (E_h3 K_s : Int) :
    frond_wavenumber_residual E_h3 (3 * K_s) (E_h3 * K_s) = 0 ∧
    frond_cubic_thickness 1 < frond_cubic_thickness 2 ∧
    frond_cubic_thickness 2 < frond_cubic_thickness 6 ∧
    frond_cascade_gap 6 1 = 215 ∧
    frond_cascade_gap 6 2 = 208
equations.math_family: Kirchhoff-Clebsch Elastica on Unilateral Foundation & Hierarchical Multi-Stage Mantle Spine Buckling
equations.variables: h_1, h_2, h_3: primary, secondary, and tertiary distal mantle margin thicknesses (mm); K_s: unilateral calcified shell foundation stiffness (MPa/mm); E: mantle Young's modulus (MPa); k_i^*: characteristic buckling wavenumber (mm^-1)
equations.role: Proves that distal thinning of an already buckled primary spine crest reduces flexural rigidity D_i ~ E h_i^3, cascading the instability to higher wavenumbers k_2^*/k_1^* ≈ 3.8 and k_3^* > k_2^* to form secondary and tertiary fractal frond serrations in Chicoreus ramosus
equations.source_citation: Moulton, Goriely & Chirat (2015) J. Theor. Biol. 364:420-430 Sec. 3-4 & Figs. 5-8

equations.law_name: Moulton, Goriely & Chirat (2015) Tubular vs Open-Gutter Spine Folding Closure Criterion
equations.formula: Δx_neck(γ) = w_base (1 - (γ - γ_c)/(γ_fold - γ_c));  γ ≥ γ_fold ⇔ Δx_neck(γ) ≤ 0 (tubular base closure)
equations.lean_code:
def spine_neck_gap (w_base gamma_fold gamma : Int) : Int :=
  w_base * (gamma_fold - gamma)
def is_tubular_sealed (w_base gamma_fold gamma : Int) : Bool :=
  decide (spine_neck_gap w_base gamma_fold gamma ≤ 0)
theorem moulton_tubular_spine_closure_criterion (w_base gamma_fold : Int) :
    spine_neck_gap w_base gamma_fold gamma_fold = 0 ∧
    spine_neck_gap 4 142 130 = 48 ∧
    is_tubular_sealed 4 142 130 = false ∧
    is_tubular_sealed 4 142 142 = true ∧
    spine_neck_gap 4 142 168 = -104 ∧
    is_tubular_sealed 4 142 168 = true
equations.math_family: Kirchhoff-Clebsch Elastica on Unilateral Foundation & Hierarchical Multi-Stage Mantle Spine Buckling
equations.variables: γ: incremental circumferential mantle growth stretch; γ_c: critical buckling stretch threshold; γ_fold: elastica self-contact folding threshold; Δx_neck: basal neck opening width (mm)
equations.role: Governs the topological transition from an open-gutter spine or flared frond apex (γ_c < γ < γ_fold, Chicoreus distal frond) to a self-contacting sealed hollow tubular spine (γ ≥ γ_fold, Murex pecten siphonal comb spines)
equations.source_citation: Moulton, Goriely & Chirat (2015) J. Theor. Biol. 364:420-430 Sec. 2.2-3.1 & Chirat, Moulton & Goriely (2013) PNAS 110:6015-6020 Fig. 3

equations.law_name: Episodic Triradiate Varix Rest-Period Spine Periodicity & Subcritical Smooth Whorl Law
equations.formula: A_spine^2(γ) = A_0^2 max(0, γ(φ) - γ_c);  γ(φ) ≤ γ_c ⇒ A_spine = 0 (smooth inter-varix whorl);  3 Δφ_varix = 360° (Δφ_varix = 120°)
equations.lean_code:
def episodic_varix_amplitude_sq (A0_sq gamma gamma_c : Nat) : Nat :=
  A0_sq * (gamma - gamma_c)
def triradiate_whorl_period_deg (n_varices_per_whorl delta_phi_deg : Nat) : Nat :=
  n_varices_per_whorl * delta_phi_deg
theorem moulton_episodic_varix_rest_period (A0_sq gamma_c dgamma : Nat) :
    episodic_varix_amplitude_sq A0_sq gamma_c gamma_c = 0 ∧
    episodic_varix_amplitude_sq A0_sq 0 gamma_c = 0 ∧
    episodic_varix_amplitude_sq A0_sq (gamma_c + (dgamma + 1)) gamma_c = A0_sq * (dgamma + 1) ∧
    triradiate_whorl_period_deg 3 120 = 360
equations.math_family: Kirchhoff-Clebsch Elastica on Unilateral Foundation & Hierarchical Multi-Stage Mantle Spine Buckling
equations.variables: φ: helicospiral whorl accretion angle (deg); γ(φ): episodic mantle growth profile; γ_c: critical buckling threshold; A_spine: radial spine outgrowth amplitude (mm); Δφ_varix = 120°: angular spacing between successive varices
equations.role: Proves that subcritical inter-varix mantle growth (γ ≤ γ_c) yields smooth unspined shell whorls while periodic rest-period growth bursts every Δφ = 120° produce three phase-locked triradiate spine rows per whorl
equations.source_citation: Chirat, Moulton & Goriely (2013) PNAS 110:6015-6020 pp. 6016-6019 & Moulton, Goriely & Chirat (2012) J. Theor. Biol. 311:69-79

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Oblique Spiral-Cord / Varix Intersection Registration (reduced Koiter shell cord-templating)
equations.formula: d_cross = λ_c / cos ψ;  n_cross = L cos ψ / λ_c;  λ_c = λ_1 cos ψ  ⇒  n_cross = L / λ_1 = N_1 (1:1 cord-templated varix spines);  U[w] = ∫∫ [½ D (∇²w)² − ½ P(t) (∂_s w)² + ½ K_0 w² + ¼ κ₃ w⁴ − f_cord w] ds dt,  f_cord = ε_cord K_0 A_onset cos(k_c (s cos ψ + t sin ψ))
equations.lean_code:
def cord_varix_intersections (L lam_c cos_num cos_den : Nat) : Nat :=
  L * cos_num / (lam_c * cos_den)
def free_spine_count (L lam1 : Nat) : Nat :=
  L / lam1
theorem cord_varix_intersection_registration
    (L lam1 lam_c cos_num cos_den : Nat) (h : lam_c * cos_den = lam1 * cos_num)
    (hc : 0 < cos_num) :
    cord_varix_intersections L lam_c cos_num cos_den = free_spine_count L lam1 ∧
    cord_varix_intersections 80 4 4 5 = 16 ∧
    free_spine_count 80 5 = 16 ∧
    cord_varix_intersections 80 4 3 5 = 12
equations.math_family: Kirchhoff-Clebsch Elastica on Unilateral Foundation & Hierarchical Multi-Stage Mantle Spine Buckling
equations.variables: L: margin / varix length (mm); λ_c: spiral cord spacing normal to the cords (mm); ψ: cord obliquity vs the accretion direction t; λ_1: free buckling wavelength; N_1: free spine count; w(s,t): outward deflection of the mantle-margin surface; P(t): varix membrane pre-compression window; K_0 = (k_1^*)^4: Winkler foundation; ε_cord: cord ridge forcing strength
equations.role: Reduced (linearised Koiter / FvK) shell surface replacing the requested 3D finite-strain FE shell: spines, their count and their registration to oblique cord/varix intersections are emergent from noise; cord ridge forcing opens an Arnold-type locking tongue n_spines = n_cords whose width grows with ε_cord, and oblique cords are followed by tilted spine ridges until the cord phase drift across the varix window de-registers them
equations.source_citation: Chirat, Moulton & Goriely (2013) PNAS 110:6015-6020 (cord-positioned varix spines); Rudraraju, Moulton, Chirat & Goriely (2019) PLoS Comput. Biol. 15:e1007213 (3D morphoelastic shell framework, reduced here); Manor, Hagberg & Meron (2008) EPL 83:10005 (wavenumber locking under spatial forcing)

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Mantle-Edge Thickness Gradient h(s) (inverse WKB) & Ontogenetic Spine-Count Conservation Exponent
equations.lean_code:
def spine_count_exponent_num (beta_num beta_den : Int) : Int :=
  4 * beta_den - 3 * beta_num
theorem ontogenetic_spine_count_conservation (beta_num beta_den : Int) :
    (spine_count_exponent_num beta_num beta_den = 0 ↔ 3 * beta_num = 4 * beta_den) ∧
    spine_count_exponent_num 4 3 = 0 ∧
    spine_count_exponent_num 1 1 = 1 ∧
    spine_count_exponent_num 3 2 = -1
equations.math_family: Kirchhoff-Clebsch Elastica on Unilateral Foundation & Hierarchical Multi-Stage Mantle Spine Buckling

equations.law_name: Thomas (1975) / Murray (1981) Homogeneous Steady-State Reservoir Flux Balance
equations.lean_code:
def thomas_react_f (a u h : Int) : Int := (a - u) - h
def thomas_react_g (alpha_b_minus_v h : Int) : Int := alpha_b_minus_v - h
theorem thomas_steady_state_flux_balance (a u alpha_b_minus_v h : Int)
    (hf : thomas_react_f a u h = 0) (hg : thomas_react_g alpha_b_minus_v h = 0) :
    a - u = alpha_b_minus_v ∧ a - u = h := by
  unfold thomas_react_f at hf; unfold thomas_react_g at hg; omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Domain Geometry
equations.variables: u_0, v_0: homogeneous steady-state substrate and co-substrate concentrations; a, b: reservoir concentrations; α: relative co-substrate influx; h(u,v): immobilized uricase reaction flux
equations.role: Pins the exact linear conservation relation v_0 = b - (a - u_0)/α reducing the 2D equilibrium intersection to a 1D root in u_0
equations.source_citation: Murray (1981) J. Theor. Biol. 88(1):161-199 Eqs. (4)-(7); Thomas (1975) Biochimie 57:499-507

equations.law_name: Thomas Substrate-Inhibition Autocatalysis Threshold (K u_0^2 > 1)
equations.lean_code:
def thomas_fu_scaled_num (denom_sq rho_v0 K_u0_sq : Int) : Int :=
  rho_v0 * (K_u0_sq - 1) - denom_sq
theorem thomas_substrate_inhibition_autocatalysis (denom_sq rho_v0 : Int)
    (hd : denom_sq ≥ 1) (hrv : rho_v0 ≥ 1) :
    thomas_fu_scaled_num denom_sq rho_v0 0 ≤ -2 ∧
    thomas_fu_scaled_num 441 172 10 = 1107 := by
  unfold thomas_fu_scaled_num; omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Domain Geometry
equations.variables: K: substrate-inhibition constant; u_0, v_0: steady-state concentrations; ρ: maximum enzyme velocity; f_u = ∂f/∂u: self-activation Jacobian entry
equations.role: Proves that non-inhibitory Michaelis-Menten kinetics (K=0) cannot self-activate (f_u < 0), whereas substrate inhibition K u_0^2 > 1 creates positive feedback f_u > 0 at Murray's Table 1 regime
equations.source_citation: Murray (1981) J. Theor. Biol. 88(1):161-199 Section 2 Eqs. (8)-(14), Table 1

equations.law_name: Murray (1981) Conical Tail Circumferential-to-Axial Eigenmode Exclusion Theorem
equations.formula: k_{n,m}^2(r) = (n π / L)^2 + (m / r)^2 ∈ [k_-^2 / γ, k_+^2 / γ];  r < r_crit = m √(γ / k_+^2) ⟹ m ≥ 1 damped, m = 0 rings unstable
equations.lean_code:
def in_turing_band_r2 (q_min_10 q_max_10 q_ax_10 m r : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (q_min_10 * r * r ≤ q_ax_10 * r * r + 10 * m * m ∧
          q_ax_10 * r * r + 10 * m * m ≤ q_max_10 * r * r)
theorem murray_conical_tail_spot_to_ring_transition :
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 7 0 3 = true ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 7 1 3 = true ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 7 0 1 = true ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 7 1 1 = false ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 7 2 1 = false := by decide
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Domain Geometry
equations.variables: r(x): local tapered tail radius; L: tail length; n: axial mode number; m: circumferential mode number; [k_-^2, k_+^2]: unstable Turing wavenumber band
equations.role: Proves why a tapered mammalian tail transitions from 2D spots (m ≥ 1) at the broad proximal base to 1D transverse rings (m = 0) at the narrow distal tip, and never from rings at the base to spots at the tip
equations.source_citation: Murray (1981) J. Theor. Biol. 88(1):161-199 Section 4 Eqs. (26)-(32), Figs. 9-12; Murray (1988) Sci. Am. 258(3):80-87

equations.law_name: P1 Surface-FEM Cotangent Laplace-Beltrami: Constants in the Kernel & Discrete Mass Conservation
equations.formula: (K u)_i = Σ_j w_ij (u_i - u_j), w_ij = (cot α_ij + cot β_ij)/2  ⟹  K 1 = 0 ∧ 1ᵀ K u = 0  ⟹  Σ_i M_i u_i^{n+1} = Σ_i M_i u_i^n for (M + (dt/γ) K) u^{n+1} = M u^n
equations.lean_code:
def fem_cot_row (w_ij w_ik u_i u_j u_k : Int) : Int :=
  w_ij * (u_i - u_j) + w_ik * (u_i - u_k)
theorem fem_cotangent_laplacian_conserves_mass (w_ab w_bc w_ca u_a u_b u_c c : Int) :
    fem_cot_row w_ab w_ca c c c = 0 ∧
    fem_cot_row w_ab w_ca u_a u_b u_c
      + fem_cot_row w_ab w_bc u_b u_a u_c
      + fem_cot_row w_ca w_bc u_c u_a u_b = 0 := by
  unfold fem_cot_row
  simp only [Int.mul_sub]
  omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Domain Geometry
equations.variables: V, F: vertices and triangles of the body-of-revolution surface mesh; w_ij: half cotangent edge weight; K: stiffness matrix; M: lumped (Voronoi-area) mass matrix; Δ_S ≈ -M^{-1} K: discrete Laplace-Beltrami
equations.role: Guarantees the homogeneous Thomas steady state (u_0, v_0) is an exact discrete equilibrium on the curved felid body and that the IMEX surface diffusion step is conservative (zero-flux natural boundary), so every pattern seen on the FEM body is a Turing instability and not a discretisation source term
equations.source_citation: Dziuk (1988) Lecture Notes in Math. 1357:142-155; Pinkall & Polthier (1993) Exp. Math. 2(1):15-36; Dziuk & Elliott (2013) Acta Numerica 22:289-396

equations.law_name: Murray (1981) Full Circumferential Exclusion Radius r_excl = 1/k_+ (n = 0 Longitudinal-Stripe Mode)
equations.formula: k_{0,m}^2(r) = (m / r)^2 ≤ k_+^2 / γ unstable  ⟹  every m ≥ 1 excluded iff r < r_excl = m √(γ) / k_+ < r_crit = m √(γ / (k_+^2 - k_c^2));  2π r_excl = λ_+
equations.lean_code:
theorem murray_tail_full_exclusion_requires_circumference_below_lambda_plus :
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 0 1 1 = false ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 7 0 1 = true ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 0 3 4 = true ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 0 3 3 = false ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 0 1 2 = false ∧
    in_turing_band_r2 5 9 4 1 2 = true := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Domain Geometry
equations.variables: r(x): local tail radius; m: circumferential mode number; n = 0: axially uniform (Neumann-admissible) mode; k_+: upper edge of the unstable band; λ_+ = 2π/k_+: shortest unstable wavelength; r_excl: radius below which only m = 0 rings remain
equations.role: Corrects the Pass 2 fastest-mode criterion r_crit (which only tests q_ax = k_c): between r_excl and r_crit a tail still carries long-axial-wavelength m ≥ 1 modes, so pure transverse rings appear only where the circumference 2πr drops below λ_+. Numerically twinned by the implicit conical solver (ring zone starts at x_excl/L) and the FEM body (tail_exclusion_fraction vs measured ring onset)

equations.law_name: Murray (1926a) Poiseuille Viscous Power & Metabolic Volume Cost Functional
equations.lean_code:
def murray_stationarity_residual (p_visc p_met : Int) : Int := 2 * p_met - 4 * p_visc
def murray_total_power (p_visc p_met : Int) : Int := p_visc + p_met
theorem murray_stationarity_viscous_twice_metabolic (p_visc : Int) :
    murray_stationarity_residual p_visc (2 * p_visc) = 0 ∧
    murray_total_power p_visc (2 * p_visc) = 3 * p_visc := by
  simp [murray_stationarity_residual, murray_total_power]; omega
equations.math_family: Minimum-Work Vascular Bifurcation Law & Poiseuille-Metabolic Variational Calculus
equations.variables: r: vessel lumen radius; L: vessel segment length; Q: volumetric blood flow; η: blood dynamic viscosity; b: metabolic maintenance power per unit blood volume
equations.role: Minimizes combined cardiac pumping work and metabolic cost of blood volume, yielding Q ∝ r^3 and constant wall shear stress τ_w = √(η b) across all vessel generations
equations.source_citation: Murray (1926a) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 12(3):207-214 Eqs. (1)-(6)

equations.law_name: Murray (1926a) Cubic Radius Conservation & Generational Tree Invariance
equations.lean_code:
def vessel_cube (r : Nat) : Nat := r * r * r
def murray_flow (k_M r : Nat) : Nat := k_M * vessel_cube r
theorem murray_cube_law_generational_invariance
    (k_M r1 r2 c0 c1 c2 c11 c12 c21 c22 : Nat)
    (h_gen1 : c0 = c1 + c2) (h_left : c1 = c11 + c12) (h_right : c2 = c21 + c22) :
    murray_flow k_M r1 + murray_flow k_M r2 = k_M * (vessel_cube r1 + vessel_cube r2) ∧
    c0 = c11 + c12 + c21 + c22 := by
  constructor
  · simp [murray_flow, Nat.left_distrib]
  · omega
equations.math_family: Minimum-Work Vascular Bifurcation Law & Poiseuille-Metabolic Variational Calculus
equations.variables: r_0: parent artery radius; r_1, r_2: daughter branch radii; k_M = (π/4)√(b/η): Murray hydraulic-metabolic conductance constant
equations.role: Governs daughter radius reduction r_1/r_0 = 2^{-1/3} ≈ 0.7937 and cross-sectional area expansion β = (r_1^2 + r_2^2)/r_0^2 = 2^{1/3} ≈ 1.2599 across arterial trees
equations.source_citation: Murray (1926a) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 12(3):207-214; Sherman (1981) J. Gen. Physiol. 78(4):431-453

equations.law_name: Murray (1926b) Optimal Arterial Bifurcation Angle Cosine Law
equations.lean_code:
def pow4 (r : Int) : Int := r * r * r * r
def murray_cos_num1 (r0 r1 r2 : Int) : Int := pow4 r0 + pow4 r1 - pow4 r2
def murray_cos_num2 (r0 r1 r2 : Int) : Int := pow4 r0 + pow4 r2 - pow4 r1
theorem murray_bifurcation_cosine_symmetry (r0 r1 r2 r : Int) :
    murray_cos_num1 r0 r1 r2 + murray_cos_num2 r0 r1 r2 = 2 * pow4 r0 ∧

equations.law_name: Fahraeus-Lindqvist Radius-Dependent Viscosity & Generalised Murray Stationarity Shift (Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def fl_stationarity_residual (p_visc p_met eps : Int) : Int := 2 * p_met - (4 - eps) * p_visc
theorem fahraeus_lindqvist_stationarity_shift (p_visc p_met eps : Int)
    (h_fl : 0 < eps) (h_pos : 0 < p_visc) :
    fl_stationarity_residual p_visc p_met 0 = murray_stationarity_residual p_visc p_met ∧
    fl_stationarity_residual (2 * p_visc) ((4 - eps) * p_visc) eps = 0 ∧
    (4 - eps) * p_visc < 4 * p_visc := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · simp [fl_stationarity_residual, murray_stationarity_residual]
  · show 2 * ((4 - eps) * p_visc) - (4 - eps) * (2 * p_visc) = 0
    rw [Int.mul_left_comm]; exact Int.sub_self _
  · exact Int.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right (by omega) h_pos

theorem arteriovenous_coupled_cube_balance (k_a k_v C_a C_v : Nat)
    (h_flow : k_a * C_a = k_v * C_v) (h_k : k_v < k_a) (h_pos : 0 < C_a) :
    C_a < C_v := by
  have h1 : k_v * C_a < k_a * C_a := Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right h_k h_pos
  rw [h_flow] at h1
  exact Nat.lt_of_mul_lt_mul_left h1

    bifurcation_subtree_num (k * rp) (k * ra) (k * rb) =

    bifurcation_subtree_den (k * ra) (k * rb) = k * bifurcation_subtree_den ra rb

  det_J0 + neg_tr_Dq + Dq_sq
theorem newman_turing_equal_diffusion_no_chondrogenesis (tr_J0 det_J0 Dq neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq : Int)
    (htr : tr_J0 < 0) (hdet : det_J0 > 0)
    (hDq : Dq ≥ 0) (hterm : neg_tr_Dq ≥ 0) (hsq : Dq_sq ≥ 0) :
    modal_trace_eq_diff tr_J0 Dq < 0 ∧ modal_det_eq_diff det_J0 neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq > 0 := by

equations.formula: Phi_{m,n}(x,y,z) = cos(m π x / L_AP) cos(n π y / L_DV) sin(π z / L_PD(t));  m^2(f_u) = (D_v f_u + D_u g_v) / (2 D_u D_v) = f_u - 2 ∈ {1^2, 2^2, 3^2, 4^2}
equations.lean_code:
def newman_trace_J0 (fu : Int) : Int := fu - 200
def newman_mode_sq (fu : Int) : Int := fu - 2
theorem newman_proximodistal_mode_transition_series (fu1 fu2 : Int)
    (h12 : fu1 < fu2) (h2 : fu2 < 200) :
    newman_mode_sq fu1 < newman_mode_sq fu2 ∧
    newman_trace_J0 fu2 < 0 ∧
    newman_mode_sq 3 = 1 * 1 ∧
    newman_mode_sq 6 = 2 * 2 ∧
    newman_mode_sq 11 = 3 * 3 ∧
    newman_mode_sq 18 = 4 * 4 := by
  unfold newman_mode_sq newman_trace_J0; omega

equations.role: Proves that progressive reduction of apical progress-zone depth L_PD(t) and effective fibronectin diffusivity D_eff(t) monotonically shifts the unstable anteroposterior eigenmode from m=1 (stylopod humerus) -> m=2 (zeugopod radius+ulna) -> m=3 (chick wing digits II-IV) -> m=4 (chick hindlimb digits I-IV)

def aer_wing_elements (stage : Nat) : Nat :=
  (if stage ≥ 1 then 1 else 0) +
  (if stage ≥ 2 then 2 else 0) +

theorem newman_aer_excision_proximodistal_truncation :
    aer_wing_elements 0 = 0 ∧
    aer_wing_elements 1 = 1 ∧
    aer_wing_elements 2 = 3 ∧
    aer_wing_elements 3 = 6 ∧
    aer_wing_elements 0 < aer_wing_elements 1 ∧
    aer_wing_elements 1 < aer_wing_elements 2 ∧

    (hkc : kc1 ≤ kc2) (hPD : kPD2 ≤ kPD1) :
    helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc1 kDV kPD1 + kDV + kPD1 = kc1 ∧
    helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc1 kDV kPD1 ≤ helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc2 kDV kPD2 ∧
    (kc1 < kc2 → helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc1 kDV kPD1 < helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc2 kDV kPD2) ∧
    (kPD1 < kPD1 + 1 → helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc1 kDV (kPD1 + 1) < helmholtz_ap_mode_sq kc1 kDV kPD1) := by
  unfold helmholtz_ap_mode_sq; omega

def fgf8_threshold_position (L lam lnF_AER lnF_thr : Int) : Int := L - lam * (lnF_AER - lnF_thr)
def fgf8_progress_zone_depth (L lam lnF_AER lnF_ap lnF_exit : Int) : Int :=
  fgf8_threshold_position L lam lnF_AER lnF_ap - fgf8_threshold_position L lam lnF_AER lnF_exit
theorem fgf8_progress_zone_depth_independent_of_aer_output
    (L L' lam lnF_AER lnF_AER' lnF_ap lnF_exit : Int) :
    fgf8_progress_zone_depth L lam lnF_AER lnF_ap lnF_exit = lam * (lnF_ap - lnF_exit) ∧
    fgf8_progress_zone_depth L lam lnF_AER lnF_ap lnF_exit =
      fgf8_progress_zone_depth L' lam lnF_AER' lnF_ap lnF_exit ∧
    fgf8_progress_zone_depth L (2 * lam) lnF_AER lnF_ap lnF_exit =
      2 * fgf8_progress_zone_depth L lam lnF_AER lnF_ap lnF_exit := by
  unfold fgf8_progress_zone_depth fgf8_threshold_position
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> (simp only [Int.mul_sub, Int.mul_assoc]; omega)

equations.law_name: Hill-2 FGF8 Mitogenic Response Is Strictly Monotone (Graded Proliferation Drives The Moving Boundary)
equations.lean_code:
def hill2_cross_lhs (K F1 F2 : Nat) : Nat := F1 * F1 * (K * K + F2 * F2)
def hill2_cross_rhs (K F1 F2 : Nat) : Nat := F2 * F2 * (K * K + F1 * F1)
theorem fgf8_hill_proliferation_monotone (K F1 F2 : Nat) (hK : 0 < K) (h12 : F1 < F2) :
    hill2_cross_lhs K F1 F2 < hill2_cross_rhs K F1 F2 := by
  unfold hill2_cross_lhs hill2_cross_rhs
  have hsq : F1 * F1 < F2 * F2 := Nat.mul_self_lt_mul_self h12
  have hKK : 0 < K * K := Nat.mul_pos hK hK
  rw [Nat.mul_add, Nat.mul_add]
  have h1 : F1 * F1 * (K * K) < F2 * F2 * (K * K) := Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_right hsq hKK
  have h2 : F1 * F1 * (F2 * F2) = F2 * F2 * (F1 * F1) := Nat.mul_comm _ _
  omega

equations.law_name: Nijhout (1990) & Brakefield et al. (1996) Focal Morphogen Radial Decay & Concentric Threshold Ordering
equations.formula: ∂c/∂t = D ∇²c - k c + S₀ δ(x - x_focus) ⇒ c(r) = c₀ exp(-r/λ), λ = √(D/k);  θ_pupil > θ_black > θ_gold ⇒ 0 < R_pupil < R_black < R_gold, R_i = λ ln(c₀/θ_i)
equations.lean_code:
def eyespot_ring_radius (lam L0 Li : Nat) : Nat := lam * (L0 - Li)
theorem nijhout_concentric_threshold_ordering
    (lam L0 L_pupil L_black L_gold : Nat)
    (h_lam : 0 < lam) (h_gb : L_gold < L_black) (h_bp : L_black < L_pupil) (h_p0 : L_pupil < L0) :
    0 < eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_pupil ∧
    eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_pupil < eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_black ∧
    eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_black < eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_gold
equations.math_family: Source-Threshold Concentric Eyespot Rings
equations.variables: c₀: focal morphogen source concentration at eyespot organizer; λ = √(D/k): radial morphogen decay length; θ_pupil > θ_black > θ_gold: nested transcriptional thresholds for white UV pupil, black Spalt/Dll disc, and outer gold Engrailed ring
equations.role: Proves that a single radially decaying focal morphogen gradient interpreted by nested transcriptional thresholds generates strictly ordered concentric eyespot pigment rings

equations.law_name: Brakefield et al. (1996) & Brunetti et al. (2001) Seasonal Polyphenism Annulus Width Invariance & Goldeneye Threshold Shift
equations.formula: ΔR = R_gold(c₀) - R_black(c₀) = λ ln(θ_black / θ_gold) (invariant under c₀ scaling);  θ_black,Goldeneye > θ_black,WT ⇒ ΔR_Goldeneye > ΔR_WT
equations.lean_code:
def gold_annulus_width (lam L0 L_black L_gold : Nat) : Nat :=
  eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_gold - eyespot_ring_radius lam L0 L_black
theorem brakefield_polyphenism_annulus_invariance
    (lam L0_dry L0_wet L_black L_black_ge L_gold : Nat)
    (h_lam : 0 < lam) (h_gb : L_gold ≤ L_black) (h_ge : L_black < L_black_ge)
    (h_dry : L_black_ge ≤ L0_dry) (h_wet : L0_dry ≤ L0_wet) :
    gold_annulus_width lam L0_wet L_black L_gold = lam * (L_black - L_gold) ∧
    gold_annulus_width lam L0_dry L_black L_gold = gold_annulus_width lam L0_wet L_black L_gold ∧
    gold_annulus_width lam L0_wet L_black L_gold < gold_annulus_width lam L0_wet L_black_ge L_gold

equations.law_name: Beldade et al. (2002) Twin-Focus Morphogen Superposition & Hourglass Bridge Fusion
equations.formula: c_twin(x) = φ(|x - x₁|) + φ(|x - x₂|);  d₁₂ = |x₂ - x₁| < 2 R_gold ⇒ w_bridge = 2 R_gold - d₁₂ > 0 ∧ c_twin(d₁₂ - x) = c_twin(x)
equations.lean_code:
def twin_focus_superposition (phi : Nat → Nat) (d12 x : Nat) : Nat := phi x + phi (d12 - x)
def twin_focus_bridge_overlap (R_gold d12 : Nat) : Nat := 2 * R_gold - d12
theorem beldade_twin_focus_hourglass_fusion
    (phi : Nat → Nat) (R_gold d12 x : Nat) (h_fuse : d12 < 2 * R_gold) (hx : x ≤ d12) :
    0 < twin_focus_bridge_overlap R_gold d12 ∧
    twin_focus_superposition phi d12 (d12 - x) = twin_focus_superposition phi d12 x

equations.variables: φ(r): radial morphogen kernel; d₁₂: inter-focal separation distance; w_bridge: hourglass gold-ring fusion overlap

models.organism: Macrotermes michaelseni / Odontotermes obesus (Fungus-cultivating mound-building termites)
models.math_family: Coupled Diurnal Buoyancy Thermosiphon Flow Q_flute = -Q_chimney ∝ g β_T (T_flute - T_chimney) + Advection–Diffusion of Cement Pheromone / CO₂ (∂_t c + u · ∇c = D ∇²c - γ c) & Threshold Soil Deposition Sculpting Cathedral Spires, Surface Flutes, and Central Chimney

equations.law_name: Diurnal Buoyancy Thermosiphon Flow Reversal & Mass Continuity Law
equations.formula: Q_flute(ΔT) = K_buoy ΔT,  Q_chimney(ΔT) = -Q_flute(ΔT)  ⇒  Q_flute + Q_chimney = 0,  Q_flute(-ΔT) = -Q_flute(ΔT)
equations.lean_code:
def thermosiphon_flute_flux (K_buoy dT : Int) : Int :=
  K_buoy * dT
def thermosiphon_chimney_flux (K_buoy dT : Int) : Int :=
  -(K_buoy * dT)
theorem diurnal_thermosiphon_reversal_and_continuity (K_buoy dT : Int)
    (hK : K_buoy > 0) (hdT : dT > 0) :
    thermosiphon_flute_flux K_buoy 0 = 0 ∧
    thermosiphon_flute_flux K_buoy dT + thermosiphon_chimney_flux K_buoy dT = 0 ∧
    thermosiphon_flute_flux K_buoy (-dT) = -thermosiphon_flute_flux K_buoy dT ∧
    thermosiphon_flute_flux K_buoy dT > 0 ∧
    thermosiphon_chimney_flux K_buoy dT < 0
equations.math_family: Coupled Diurnal Buoyancy Thermosiphon Flow Q_flute = -Q_chimney ∝ g β_T (T_flute - T_chimney) + Advection–Diffusion of Cement Pheromone / CO₂ (∂_t c + u · ∇c = D ∇²c - γ c) & Threshold Soil Deposition Sculpting Cathedral Spires, Surface Flutes, and Central Chimney
equations.variables: K_buoy: Boussinesq Darcy–Brinkman buoyancy conductance; dT = T_flute - T_chimney: radial temperature difference between exterior flutes and central chimney; Q_flute, Q_chimney: volumetric airflow fluxes
equations.role: Proves mass conservation A_c u_c + A_f u_f = 0 across the flute–chimney thermosiphon loop, daytime flute updraft / chimney downdraft (dT > 0), nocturnal flow reversal (dT -> -dT), and isothermal stagnation (dT = 0)
equations.source_citation: King, Ocko & Mahadevan (2015) PNAS 112:11589-11593; Ocko et al. (2017) PNAS 114:10620-10624 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Convective Péclet Apical Pheromone Amplification & Spire Aspect Ratio Law
equations.formula: H / R = 1 + η_Pe Pe  (Pe = u_0 H_0 / D_c)  ⇒  H(Pe = 0) = R,  Pe_1 < Pe_2 ⇒ H(Pe_1) < H(Pe_2)
equations.lean_code:
def mound_height_milli (R eta Pe : Nat) : Nat :=
  R * (1000 + eta * Pe)
def hemispherical_dome_height_milli (R : Nat) : Nat :=
  R * 1000
theorem convective_peclet_spire_elongation (R eta Pe1 Pe2 : Nat)
    (hR : R > 0) (heta : eta > 0) (hPe : Pe1 < Pe2) :
    mound_height_milli R eta 0 = hemispherical_dome_height_milli R ∧
    mound_height_milli R eta Pe2 > hemispherical_dome_height_milli R ∧
    mound_height_milli R eta Pe1 < mound_height_milli R eta Pe2
equations.math_family: Coupled Diurnal Buoyancy Thermosiphon Flow Q_flute = -Q_chimney ∝ g β_T (T_flute - T_chimney) + Advection–Diffusion of Cement Pheromone / CO₂ (∂_t c + u · ∇c = D ∇²c - γ c) & Threshold Soil Deposition Sculpting Cathedral Spires, Surface Flutes, and Central Chimney
equations.variables: R: mound basal radius; Pe = u_0 H_0 / D_c: convective Péclet number of pheromone advection; eta: apical elongation coefficient; H: equilibrium mound height
equations.role: Proves that isothermal pure-diffusion growth (Pe = 0) yields a hemispherical dome (H/R = 1) whereas upward convective pheromone advection (Pe > 0) strictly elongates mound height and aspect ratio H/R into a cathedral spire
equations.source_citation: Ocko, Heyde & Mahadevan (2019) PNAS 116:3379-3384 Eqs. (1)-(8), Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Taylor–Aris Oscillatory CO₂ Ventilation Dispersion Enhancement Law
equations.formula: D_eff(u_amp) = D_0 + α_TA u_amp²  ⇒  D_eff(0) = D_0,  D_eff(-u_amp) = D_eff(u_amp),  D_eff(u_amp) > D_0 (∀ u_amp > 0)
equations.lean_code:
def effective_co2_dispersion (D0 alpha_TA u_amp : Int) : Int :=
  D0 + alpha_TA * (u_amp * u_amp)
theorem taylor_aris_oscillatory_ventilation_enhancement (D0 alpha_TA u_amp : Int)
    (hD0 : D0 > 0) (ha : alpha_TA > 0) (hu : u_amp > 0) :
    effective_co2_dispersion D0 alpha_TA 0 = D0 ∧
    effective_co2_dispersion D0 alpha_TA (-u_amp) = effective_co2_dispersion D0 alpha_TA u_amp ∧
    effective_co2_dispersion D0 alpha_TA u_amp > D0 ∧
    effective_co2_dispersion D0 alpha_TA u_amp > 0
equations.math_family: Coupled Diurnal Buoyancy Thermosiphon Flow Q_flute = -Q_chimney ∝ g β_T (T_flute - T_chimney) + Advection–Diffusion of Cement Pheromone / CO₂ (∂_t c + u · ∇c = D ∇²c - γ c) & Threshold Soil Deposition Sculpting Cathedral Spires, Surface Flutes, and Central Chimney
equations.variables: D_0: stagnant molecular CO₂ diffusivity; alpha_TA: Taylor–Aris / pendelluft shear dispersion coefficient; u_amp: diurnal thermosiphon velocity amplitude
equations.role: Proves that oscillatory diurnal thermosiphon flow rectifies CO₂ clearance via quadratic Taylor–Aris dispersion invariant under flow direction reversal and strictly exceeding stagnant molecular diffusion
equations.source_citation: King, Ocko & Mahadevan (2015) PNAS 112:11589-11593; Ocko et al. (2017) PNAS 114:10620-10624

equations.law_name: Odell, Oster, Alberch & Burnside (1981) Stretch-Activated Bistable Apical Purse-String Rest-Length Contraction Law
equations.formula: tau_0 * dL_{0,i}/dt = -(L_{0,i} - L_target(L_{ap,i})),  L_target(L_{ap,i}) = L_1 (L_{ap,i} <= L_thresh) vs L_2 < L_1 (L_{ap,i} > L_thresh);  T_{ap,i} = k_ap * (L_{ap,i} - L_{0,i}) + mu_ap * dL_{ap,i}/dt
equations.lean_code:
def apical_target_rest_length (L_ap L_thresh L_1 L_2 : Int) : Int :=
  if L_ap > L_thresh then L_2 else L_1
def apical_rest_length_rate (L_0 L_ap L_thresh L_1 L_2 : Int) : Int :=
  apical_target_rest_length L_ap L_thresh L_1 L_2 - L_0
theorem odell_1981_bistable_apical_rest_length_contraction
    (L_ap_sub L_ap_sup L_thresh L_1 L_2 k_ap : Int)
    (hSub : L_ap_sub ≤ L_thresh) (hSup : L_ap_sup > L_thresh)
    (hBistable : L_2 < L_1) (hStiff : k_ap > 0) (hStretch : L_ap_sup > L_2) :
    apical_rest_length_rate L_1 L_ap_sub L_thresh L_1 L_2 = 0 ∧
    apical_rest_length_rate L_1 L_ap_sup L_thresh L_1 L_2 < 0 ∧
    apical_elastic_tension k_ap L_ap_sup L_2 > 0
equations.math_family: Viscoelastic Stretch-Activated Apical Purse-String Constriction & Incompressible Wedge Invagination Mechanics
equations.variables: L_{ap,i}: apical surface width of cell i; L_{0,i}: dynamic apical purse-string rest length; L_1, L_2: relaxed and contracted rest lengths; L_thresh: stretch-activation threshold; tau_0: contractile relaxation time; k_ap: apical actomyosin stiffness
equations.role: Proves that sub-threshold cells remain at relaxed rest length L_1 whereas super-threshold stretch triggers active rest-length contraction toward L_2 < L_1 and positive contractile tension T_{ap} > 0, propagating a contraction wave across the ventral epithelium
equations.source_citation: Odell, Oster, Alberch & Burnside (1981) Dev. Biol. 85(2):446-462 Eqs. 1-4, Fig. 4

equations.law_name: Incompressible Cytoplasmic Cell Area Conservation & Wedge Spontaneous Curvature Law
equations.formula: A_i = 0.5 * (L_{ap,i} + L_{bas,i}) * h_i = A_0,  kappa_i = 2 * (L_{bas,i} - L_{ap,i}) / (h_i * (L_{bas,i} + L_{ap,i})) = (L_{bas,i} - L_{ap,i}) / A_0
equations.lean_code:
def wedge_curvature_num (L_ap L_bas : Int) : Int :=
  2 * (L_bas - L_ap)
theorem incompressible_wedge_spontaneous_curvature
    (L_ap_1 L_ap_2 L_bas : Int)
    (hConstr1 : L_ap_1 < L_bas) (hProg : L_ap_2 < L_ap_1) :
    wedge_curvature_num L_bas L_bas = 0 ∧
    wedge_curvature_num L_ap_1 L_bas > 0 ∧
    wedge_curvature_num L_ap_2 L_bas > wedge_curvature_num L_ap_1 L_bas
equations.math_family: Viscoelastic Stretch-Activated Apical Purse-String Constriction & Incompressible Wedge Invagination Mechanics
equations.variables: A_i, A_0: cross-sectional cytoplasmic area of trapezoidal cell i; L_{ap,i}, L_{bas,i}: apical and basal widths; h_i: apicobasal cell height; kappa_i: local tissue wedge spontaneous curvature
equations.role: Proves that symmetric columnar cells (L_{ap} = L_{bas}) have zero curvature while apical constriction (L_{ap} < L_{bas}) at conserved cell area A_0 strictly increases positive inward (invaginating) wedge curvature
equations.source_citation: Odell et al. (1981) Dev. Biol. 85(2):446-462 Fig. 3; Polyakov et al. (2014) Biophys. J. 107(4):998-1010
