equations.law_name: Kavanagh et al. (2013) Arithmetic Inhibitory Cascade Midpoint & One-Third Invariant Law
equations.lean_code:
def phalanx_len (p1 delta n : Int) : Int :=
  p1 + (n - 1) * delta
def digit_total_3 (p1 delta : Int) : Int :=
  phalanx_len p1 delta 1 + phalanx_len p1 delta 2 + phalanx_len p1 delta 3
theorem kavanagh_inhibitory_cascade_midpoint_and_third (p1 delta : Int) :
    2 * phalanx_len p1 delta 2 = phalanx_len p1 delta 1 + phalanx_len p1 delta 3 ∧
    3 * phalanx_len p1 delta 2 = digit_total_3 p1 delta ∧
    phalanx_len 150 (-53) 2 = 97 ∧
    digit_total_3 150 (-53) = 291
equations.math_family: Coupled BMP-GDF5-Noggin Reaction-Diffusion Turing-Wavefront Synovial Joint Interzone Segmentation & Kavanagh (2013) Phalangeal Inhibitory Cascade
equations.variables: P_1, P_2, P_3: proximal, middle, and distal phalanx lengths; A: distal mesenchymal activation; I: proximal condensation lateral inhibition; Δ = P_1(A - I)/I: cascade increment
equations.role: Proves that sequential inhibitory cascade segmentation constrains triphalangeal tetrapod digits to the exact affine line P_2 = (P_1 + P_3)/2 with middle phalanx occupying exactly 1/3 of total phalangeal length

equations.law_name: Hiscock et al. (2017) Distal PFR-FGF Tapering & BMP-GDF5-Noggin Turing Dispersion Sign Inversion Law
equations.formula: Δ = P_1(A - I)/I < 0  ⇒  P_1 > P_2 > P_3;  Δ_disp(q^2) = (D_G q^2 - f_G)(D_N q^2 - g_N) - f_N g_G,  Δ_disp(0) > 0,  Δ_disp(q_c^2) < 0
equations.lean_code:
def gdf5_noggin_disp_det (f_G f_N g_G g_N D_G D_N q2 : Int) : Int :=
  (D_G * q2 - f_G) * (D_N * q2 - g_N) - f_N * g_G
theorem pfr_tapering_and_gdf5_noggin_turing_inversion (p1 delta : Int) (hd : delta ≤ -1) :
    phalanx_len p1 delta 1 > phalanx_len p1 delta 2 ∧
    phalanx_len p1 delta 2 > phalanx_len p1 delta 3 ∧
    (160 + (-210) : Int) = -50 ∧
    gdf5_noggin_disp_det 160 (-240) 190 (-210) 12 180 0 = 12000 ∧
    gdf5_noggin_disp_det 160 (-240) 190 (-210) 12 180 1 = -12120
equations.math_family: Coupled BMP-GDF5-Noggin Reaction-Diffusion Turing-Wavefront Synovial Joint Interzone Segmentation & Kavanagh (2013) Phalangeal Inhibitory Cascade
equations.variables: G: GDF5/Wnt9a synovial interzone activator; N: diffusible Noggin BMP antagonist; D_G, D_N: diffusion coefficients; q: spatial wavenumber; Δ < 0: distal PFR-FGF decay increment
equations.role: Establishes diffusion-driven Turing nucleation of periodic Gdf5+/Wnt9a+ synovial joint interzones and strict proximal-to-distal phalanx tapering P_1 > P_2 > P_3 under a decaying distal PFR-FGF gradient
equations.source_citation: Hiscock, Tschopp & Tabin (2017) Dev. Cell 41:459-465; Hartmann & Tabin (2001) Cell 104:341-351

equations.law_name: Brunet et al. (1998) & Storm et al. (1994) Noggin/Gdf5 Loss-of-Function Joint Cleft Ablation Law
equations.formula: Noggin = 0 (Nog-/-)  ⇒  N_joints = 0,  N_phalanges = 1 (continuous fused Sox9+ cartilage rod);  Gdf5 bp/bp  ⇒  PIP joint fusion (N_joints = 2)
equations.lean_code:
def active_synovial_joints (nog_dose gdf5_dose tau_cleft : Nat) : Nat :=
  let amp := nog_dose * gdf5_dose
  if amp ≥ 3 * tau_cleft then 3
  else if amp ≥ 2 * tau_cleft then 2
  else if amp ≥ tau_cleft then 1
  else 0
theorem noggin_gdf5_joint_cleft_ablation (gdf5_dose : Nat) :
    active_synovial_joints 0 gdf5_dose 25 = 0 ∧
    segmented_phalanges 0 gdf5_dose 25 = 1 ∧
    active_synovial_joints 7 8 25 = 2 ∧
    active_synovial_joints 10 10 25 = 3 ∧
    segmented_phalanges 10 10 25 = 3
equations.math_family: Coupled BMP-GDF5-Noggin Reaction-Diffusion Turing-Wavefront Synovial Joint Interzone Segmentation & Kavanagh (2013) Phalangeal Inhibitory Cascade
equations.variables: nog_dose: Noggin BMP-antagonist dosage; gdf5_dose: GDF5 interzone signaling dosage; tau_cleft: chondrogenic repression threshold for synovial cavitation
equations.role: Proves why Noggin null (Nog-/-) embryos fail to repress BMP chondrogenesis in prospective interzones, abolishing all synovial joint clefts (N_joints = 0) into a single continuous cartilaginous rod, whereas Gdf5 brachypodism (bp/bp) selectively fuses proximal interphalangeal joints
equations.source_citation: Brunet et al. (1998) Science 280:1455-1457; Storm et al. (1994) Nature 368:639-643

equations.law_name: Reduced Biot Poroelastic Synovial Cavitation Gating Law (Mow 1980; Edwards 1994; Dowthwaite 1998; Drachman & Sokoloff 1966; Kahn 2009)
equations.formula: dH/dt = k_H φ(m) G − δ_H H + D_H ∇²H;  S ∂p/∂t = κ_p ∇²p + γ_osm (β_osm H − p), p = 0 at the perichondrium;  σ_coh = σ_0 (1 − κ_G G);  ∂c/∂t = r_c max(p − σ_coh, 0)(1 − c);  steady state p_ss = β_osm k_H φ(m) G / δ_H  ⇒  cavity iff p_ss > σ_coh;  m = 0 ∨ G = 0 ⇒ p_ss = 0 ⇒ no cavity;  m₁ ≤ m₂ ⇒ p_ss(m₁) ≤ p_ss(m₂)
equations.lean_code:
def ha_steady (k_H m_load gdf5 : Nat) : Nat :=
  k_H * gdf5 * m_load
def pore_pressure_steady (beta k_H m_load gdf5 : Nat) : Nat :=
  beta * ha_steady k_H m_load gdf5
def interzone_cohesion (sigma_0 kappa gdf5 : Int) : Int :=
  sigma_0 - kappa * gdf5
def cavity_opens (p : Nat) (sigma_coh : Int) : Bool :=
  decide ((p : Int) > sigma_coh)
theorem poroelastic_cavitation_requires_load_and_interzone
    (beta k_H gdf5 m1 m2 : Nat) (sigma_coh : Int) (hpos : 0 < sigma_coh) (hm : m1 ≤ m2) :
    pore_pressure_steady beta k_H 0 gdf5 = 0 ∧
    pore_pressure_steady beta k_H m1 0 = 0 ∧
    cavity_opens (pore_pressure_steady beta k_H 0 gdf5) sigma_coh = false ∧
    pore_pressure_steady beta k_H m1 gdf5 ≤ pore_pressure_steady beta k_H m2 gdf5 ∧
    cavity_opens (pore_pressure_steady 1 1 10 10) (interzone_cohesion 100 5 10) = true ∧
    cavity_opens (pore_pressure_steady 1 1 3 10) (interzone_cohesion 100 5 10) = false
equations.math_family: Coupled BMP-GDF5-Noggin Reaction-Diffusion Turing-Wavefront Synovial Joint Interzone Segmentation & Kavanagh (2013) Phalangeal Inhibitory Cascade
equations.variables: G: Gdf5+ interzone identity (Hill transform of the RD Gdf5 field); H: hyaluronan; p: excess pore pressure; c: cavity phase field; m (Lean m_load): mechanosensitive loading gain φ(m_load) of embryonic muscle contraction; k_H, δ_H, D_H, S, κ_p, γ_osm, β_osm, σ_0, κ_G, r_c: dimensionless poroelastic constants (integers in hundredths in the Lean witnesses: β = k_H = 1, m = 10, G = 10, σ_0 = 100, κ = 5)
equations.role: Proves the two loss-of-function results the cavitation solver reproduces — paralysed / muscle-less embryos (m = 0) and Noggin-null embryos without interzones (G = 0) form no synovial cavity although the interzone may be specified — and that steady pore pressure is monotone in loading, which is why the --m-load sweep has a single cavitation threshold
equations.source_citation: Mow, Kuei, Lai & Armstrong (1980) J. Biomech. Eng. 102:73-84; Edwards et al. (1994) J. Anat. 185:355-367; Dowthwaite, Edwards & Pitsillides (1998) J. Histochem. Cytochem. 46:641-651; Drachman & Sokoloff (1966) Dev. Biol. 14:401-420; Kahn et al. (2009) Dev. Cell 16:734-743

equations.law_name: Darcy Lens-Cavity Midline Maximum Law (free perichondrial drainage; Mow 1980; Carter & Wong 1988)
equations.formula: κ p'' + s = 0 on [−W, W], p(±W) = 0  ⇒  2 κ p(y) = s (W² − y²);  s ≥ 0 ⇒ p(y) ≤ p(0) ∀y, p(±W) = 0  ⇒  the cavitation drive p − σ_coh is maximal on the digit midline and the cavity nucleates as a transverse lens
equations.lean_code:
def darcy_lens_pressure (s W y : Int) : Int :=
  s * (W * W - y * y)
theorem darcy_lens_cavity_midline_maximum (s W y : Int) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    darcy_lens_pressure s W y ≤ darcy_lens_pressure s W 0 ∧
    darcy_lens_pressure s W W = 0 ∧
    darcy_lens_pressure 3 10 0 = 300 ∧
    darcy_lens_pressure 3 10 6 = 192
equations.math_family: Coupled BMP-GDF5-Noggin Reaction-Diffusion Turing-Wavefront Synovial Joint Interzone Segmentation & Kavanagh (2013) Phalangeal Inhibitory Cascade
equations.variables: s: uniform osmotic fluid source across the interzone (β_osm H); κ: Darcy permeability; W: digit half-width; y: transverse coordinate; p: scaled steady pore pressure 2κp
equations.role: Explains the lens-shaped cavities of the solver (Panel A of joint_interzone_clefting_cavitation.png), the monotone loss of cavity area with permeability (Panel E), and — because the lens thickens on the midline — why the imposed articular arch does not yet produce a convex proximal head (carried as a Pass 4 item)
equations.source_citation: Mow, Kuei, Lai & Armstrong (1980) J. Biomech. Eng. 102:73-84; Carter & Wong (1988) J. Orthop. Res. 6:804-816; Roddy, Prendergast & Murphy (2011) PLoS ONE 6:e17526

models.name: Oster, Murray & Harris (1983) / Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) mechanochemical limb chondrogenesis
models.organism: Ambystoma mexicanum & Oedipina ecuatoriana urodele salamander limb cartilage
models.math_family: Mechanochemical Cell-Traction & Viscoelastic ECM Chondrogenesis PDE (Oster-Murray-Harris 1983 / Oster-Murray-Maini 1985)

equations.law_name: Oster, Murray & Harris (1983) Mechanochemical Cell-Traction Instability Criterion
equations.formula: K_eff = E_eff + D1_s - tau_eff;  tau_eff > E_eff + D1_s => K_eff < 0 (spontaneous cell-ECM condensation)
equations.lean_code:
def mechanochemical_effective_stiffness (E_eff D1_s tau_eff : Int) : Int :=
  E_eff + D1_s - tau_eff
theorem oster_murray_1983_traction_instability_criterion
    (E_eff D1_s tau_sub tau_super : Int)
    (h_sub : tau_sub < E_eff + D1_s)
    (h_super : E_eff + D1_s < tau_super) :
    mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_sub > 0 ∧
    mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_super < 0
equations.math_family: Mechanochemical Cell-Traction & Viscoelastic ECM Chondrogenesis PDE (Oster-Murray-Harris 1983 / Oster-Murray-Maini 1985)
equations.variables: E_eff: ECM elastic restoring modulus; D1_s: diffusive-tethering stabilization coefficient; tau_eff: active mesenchymal cell traction parameter
equations.role: Establishes the critical cell traction bifurcation threshold tau_c above which active cell pulling overcomes ECM elasticity and diffusion to nucleate chondrogenic condensations
equations.source_citation: Oster, Murray & Harris (1983) J. Embryol. Exp. Morph. 78:83-125 Section 3; Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) J. Embryol. Exp. Morph. 89:93-112 Section 2

equations.law_name: Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) Contact-Inhibited Cell Traction Saturation Law
equations.formula: sigma_cell(n) = (tau * n^2) / (1 + lambda * n^2) <= tau / lambda
equations.math_family: Mechanochemical Cell-Traction & Viscoelastic ECM Chondrogenesis PDE (Oster-Murray-Harris 1983 / Oster-Murray-Maini 1985)
equations.variables: tau: cell traction coefficient; lam: contact-inhibition saturation constant; n: mesenchymal cell density
equations.role: Proves that contact-inhibited cell traction saturates at high cell density, preventing delta-shock blowup and stabilizing smooth cartilage condensations
equations.source_citation: Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) J. Embryol. Exp. Morph. 89:93-112 Eq. (4)

equations.law_name: Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) Proximo-Distal Limb Branching Mode Law
equations.formula: m(W, lambda_c) = W / lambda_c  =>  (1, 2, 4, 5) for stylopod, zeugopod, and urodele forelimb/hindlimb autopod
equations.lean_code:
def limb_condensation_mode (W lambda_c : Nat) : Nat := W / lambda_c
theorem oster_maini_1985_limb_branching_progression (lambda_c : Nat) (h : 0 < lambda_c) :
    limb_condensation_mode (1 * lambda_c) lambda_c = 1 ∧
    limb_condensation_mode (2 * lambda_c) lambda_c = 2 ∧
    limb_condensation_mode (4 * lambda_c) lambda_c = 4 ∧
    limb_condensation_mode (5 * lambda_c) lambda_c = 5
equations.math_family: Mechanochemical Cell-Traction & Viscoelastic ECM Chondrogenesis PDE (Oster-Murray-Harris 1983 / Oster-Murray-Maini 1985)
equations.variables: W: transverse limb bud paddle width; lambda_c: characteristic mechanochemical instability wavelength 2*pi/k_c
equations.role: Governs the proximo-distal transition from 1 focal condensation (stylopod: humerus/femur) to 2 bifurcated elements (zeugopod: radius+ulna / tibia+fibula) to 4-5 digital rays (autopod)
equations.source_citation: Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) J. Embryol. Exp. Morph. 89:93-112 Figs. 4-9; Shubin & Alberch (1986) Evol. Biol. 20:319-387

equations.law_name: Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) / Saunders (1948) AER Free-Boundary Outgrowth Monotonicity Law
equations.formula: L(t) = L_0 + v_AER * t non-decreasing; W_1 <= W_2 => m(W_1, lambda_c) <= m(W_2, lambda_c); AER removed at t_a => zones with y > L(t_a) never form
equations.lean_code:
def aer_front (L0 v t : Nat) : Nat := L0 + v * t
theorem oster_maini_1985_aer_front_monotone (L0 v t1 t2 : Nat) (h : t1 ≤ t2) :
    aer_front L0 v t1 ≤ aer_front L0 v t2
theorem oster_maini_1985_aer_outgrowth_mode_monotone (W1 W2 lambda_c : Nat) (h : W1 ≤ W2) :
    limb_condensation_mode W1 lambda_c ≤ limb_condensation_mode W2 lambda_c
theorem saunders_1948_aer_ablation_truncation (L0 v t_ablate y t : Nat)
    (h_t : t ≤ t_ablate) (h_y : aer_front L0 v t_ablate < y) :
    aer_front L0 v t < y
equations.math_family: Mechanochemical Cell-Traction & Viscoelastic ECM Chondrogenesis PDE (Oster-Murray-Harris 1983 / Oster-Murray-Maini 1985)
equations.variables: L_0: initial bud length; v_AER: AER outgrowth speed; t_ablate: Saunders (1948) AER-removal time; W(y): paddle width profile; lambda_c: mechanochemical wavelength
equations.role: Governs the proximo-distal sequence in which condensation modes are laid down behind the moving free-boundary AER in the 2D solver, and the distal truncation produced by AER removal
equations.source_citation: Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) J. Embryol. Exp. Morph. 89:93-112 Sec. 4; Saunders (1948) J. Exp. Zool. 108:363-403 (10.1002/jez.1401080304); ten Berge et al. (2008) Development 135:3247-3257

equations.law_name: Hybrid Mechanochemical + Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Synergy Threshold Law
equations.formula: K_hyb = E_eff + D1_s - tau_eff - chi_BSW <= K_mech (chi_BSW >= 0); 0 < K_mech < chi_BSW => K_hyb < 0; det[[-a, b],[c, -mu]] = a*mu - b*c < 0 iff b*c > a*mu
equations.lean_code:
def hybrid_effective_stiffness (E_eff D1_s tau_eff chi_bsw : Int) : Int :=
  mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff - chi_bsw
theorem hybrid_mechanochemical_bsw_threshold_lowering (E_eff D1_s tau_eff chi_bsw : Int) (h : 0 ≤ chi_bsw) :
    hybrid_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff chi_bsw ≤ mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff
theorem hybrid_mechanochemical_bsw_synergy_threshold (E_eff D1_s tau_eff chi_bsw : Int)
    (h_mech_stable : 0 < mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff)
    (h_gain : mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff < chi_bsw) :
    0 < mechanochemical_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff ∧
    hybrid_effective_stiffness E_eff D1_s tau_eff chi_bsw < 0
def hybrid_reduced_det (a mu b c : Int) : Int := a * mu - b * c
theorem hybrid_n_sox9_loop_destabilises_when_gain_exceeds_margin (a mu b c : Int) (h : a * mu < b * c) :
    hybrid_reduced_det a mu b c < 0
equations.math_family: Mechanochemical Cell-Traction & Viscoelastic ECM Chondrogenesis PDE (Oster-Murray-Harris 1983 / Oster-Murray-Maini 1985)
equations.variables: chi_BSW: Sox9-mediated feedback gain (alpha_S * kappa_S loop through the Bmp-Sox9-Wnt network); a = -J_nn: mechanics-only stability margin; b = J_nS: Sox9 -> traction; c = J_Sn: condensation -> Sox9; mu = mu_S: Sox9 clearance
equations.role: Establishes that coupling the mechanochemical traction instability to Raspopovic (2014) Bmp-Sox9-Wnt kinetics can only lower the critical traction, and defines the synergy window (tau_c,hybrid < tau < tau_c,mech) tested by the 2x2 factorial at tau = 0.85
equations.source_citation: Raspopovic, Marcon, Russo & Sharpe (2014) Science 345:566-570 (10.1126/science.1252960); Hall & Miyake (2000) BioEssays 22:138-147; Oster, Murray & Maini (1985) Sec. 5

models.name: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) Pomacanthus Turing-chemotaxis stripe doubling on a growing curved flank & Keller-Segel rippling with slime-trail tensor
models.organism: Pomacanthus semicirculatus juvenile pigment stripes (model target) & Myxococcus xanthus rippling cell populations (specimen)
models.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion

equations.law_name: Keller-Segel Homogeneous Steady-State & Pure-RD Stability (chi = 0)
equations.formula: tr M(0) = -(r + γ) < 0 ∧ det M(0) = r γ > 0;  χ = 0 ⟹ det M(q) = D_n D_c q^2 + (r D_c + γ D_n) q + r γ > 0 ∀ q ≥ 0
equations.lean_code:
def ksp_trace (r gamma D_n D_c q : Int) : Int := -(r + gamma) - (D_n + D_c) * q
def ksp_det (r gamma D_n D_c chi_eff q : Int) : Int :=
  (D_n * D_c) * (q * q) + (r * D_c + gamma * D_n - chi_eff) * q + r * gamma
theorem ksp_uniform_and_no_chemotaxis_stability (r gamma D_n D_c chi_eff q : Int)
    (hr : r ≥ 1) (hg : gamma ≥ 1) (hq : q ≥ 0) :
    ksp_trace r gamma D_n D_c 0 ≤ -2 ∧
    ksp_det 1 4 1 1 chi_eff 0 = 4 ∧
    ksp_det 1 4 1 1 0 q ≥ 4 := by
  unfold ksp_trace ksp_det
  have hq2 : q * q ≥ 0 := Int.mul_nonneg hq hq; omega
equations.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: n_0: carrying capacity; c^* = α n_0 / (γ(1 + β n_0)): steady-state chemoattractant; r: logistic growth rate; γ: chemoattractant decay; D_n, D_c: cell and chemoattractant diffusivities; q = k^2: squared wavenumber
equations.role: Proves that the homogeneous equilibrium (n^*, c^*) of the Keller-Segel rippling model is always stable to uniform perturbations (q = 0) and that without chemotaxis (χ = 0) no spatial pattern instability can arise
equations.source_citation: Keller & Segel (1970) J. Theor. Biol. 26(3):399-415; Painter & Hillen (2011) Physica D 240:363-375 (model form). Generic Keller-Segel result, not a PNAS 1999 result.

equations.law_name: Keller-Segel Equal-Diffusivity Chemotactic Instability Threshold (χ > χ_c at D_n = D_c)
equations.lean_code:
theorem painter_1999_equal_diffusivity_chemotactic_instability :
    ksp_det 1 4 1 1 8 2 = 2 ∧
    ksp_det 1 4 1 1 9 2 = 0 ∧
    ksp_det 1 4 1 1 12 2 = -6 := by
  unfold ksp_det; omega
equations.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: χ: chemotactic sensitivity; χ_c = (√(r D_c) + √(γ D_n))^2 / (n_0 s^*): critical chemotactic threshold; s^* = α / (1 + β n_0)^2: linearized secretion slope; k_c: critical wavenumber
equations.role: Proves that unlike pure Turing reaction-diffusion systems (which require D_u ≠ D_v), chemotactic cross-diffusion -∇·(n χ ∇c) destabilizes the homogeneous state at equal diffusivities D_n = D_c = 1 whenever χ > χ_c = 4.5 (χ_eff > 9); PNAS 1999 uses this contrast qualitatively to motivate chemotaxis in the Pomacanthus model
equations.source_citation: Keller & Segel (1970) J. Theor. Biol. 26(3):399-415 linearisation; Painter & Hillen (2011) Physica D 240:363-375. The Lean theorem name retains its Pass 1 'painter_1999' prefix for KG continuity; the law itself is generic Keller-Segel.

equations.law_name: Growing-Domain Wavenumber Halving & Keller-Segel Stripe-Splitting Cascade
equations.formula: q_m(s) = m^2 / s^2 ∈ [q_min, q_max] ⟺ q_min s^2 ≤ m^2 ≤ q_max s^2;  s: 1 → 2 → 4 ⟹ m_unstable: 1 → 2 → 4
equations.lean_code:
def in_chemotactic_band (q_min q_max m s : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (q_min * s * s ≤ m * m ∧ m * m ≤ q_max * s * s)
theorem painter_1999_domain_growth_stripe_splitting_cascade :
    in_chemotactic_band 1 3 1 1 = true ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 1 3 2 1 = false ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 1 3 1 2 = false ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 1 3 2 2 = true ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 1 3 2 4 = false ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 1 3 4 4 = true := by decide
equations.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: s = L(t)/L_0: domain dilation factor; m: spatial mode number; [q_min, q_max]: unstable chemotactic wavenumber band around q_c
equations.role: Proves why uniform domain growth stretches existing spatial modes below q_min and sequentially recruits frequency-doubled modes m = 1 → 2 → 4 → 8, driving chemotactic stripe splitting in the Keller-Segel rippling model
equations.source_citation: Crampin, Gaffney & Maini (1999) Bull. Math. Biol. 61:1093-1120 (mode doubling on growing domains); Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376:765 (biological stripe insertion). PNAS 1999 Fig. 3 is the Pomacanthus instance treated in Law 5.

equations.law_name: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) Pomacanthus Turing Instability & Three-Stripe Mode Selection (Fig. 3 kinetics, L(0) = 11)
equations.lean_code:
def turing_trace (fu gv : Int) : Int := fu + gv
def turing_det (fu fv gu gv : Int) : Int := fu * gv - fv * gu
def turing_h (Du Dv fu gv : Int) : Int := Dv * fu + Du * gv
theorem painter_1999_pomacanthus_turing_instability :
    turing_trace 5 (-6) = -1 ∧
    turing_det 5 (-8) 10 (-6) = 50 ∧
    turing_h 7 100 5 (-6) = 458 ∧
    turing_h 7 100 5 (-6) * turing_h 7 100 5 (-6) > 4 * 7 * 100 * turing_det 5 (-8) 10 (-6) := by
  unfold turing_trace turing_det turing_h
  decide
def neumann_mode_q (m : Nat) : Nat := m * m * 9870
def pomacanthus_band_lo : Nat := 1385 * 121
def pomacanthus_band_hi : Nat := 5158 * 121
def pomacanthus_q_c : Nat := 3271 * 121
theorem pomacanthus_three_stripe_mode_selection :
    (pomacanthus_band_lo ≤ neumann_mode_q 5 ∧ neumann_mode_q 7 ≤ pomacanthus_band_hi) ∧
    neumann_mode_q 4 < pomacanthus_band_lo ∧ pomacanthus_band_hi < neumann_mode_q 8 ∧
    dist_to_qc 6 < dist_to_qc 5 ∧ dist_to_qc 6 < dist_to_qc 7 := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: u, v: Kondo-Asai activator/inhibitor morphogens with piecewise-linear (clipped) kinetics f = clip(0.08u - 0.08v + 0.05, 0, 0.18) - 0.03u, g = clip(0.1u - 0.15, 0, 0.5) - 0.06v; D_u = 0.007, D_v = 0.1; m: zero-flux half-wave mode number k = mπ/L; n: chemotactic iridophores with χ(u) = χ_0/(k + u)^2, χ_0 = -1e-4 (slaved to u, do not alter the Turing condition)
equations.role: Proves that the actual PNAS 1999 Fig. 3 parameter set is a kinetically stable, diffusion-driven-unstable Turing system and that on the juvenile domain L(0) = 11 the half-wave mode m = 6 (three stripes, Fig. 1a) is selected
equations.source_citation: Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) PNAS 96(10):5549-5554 Eqs. (1)-(3) and Fig. 3 caption; Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376:765-768 (kinetics)

equations.law_name: Kondo-Asai Stripe-Doubling Law on a Uniformly Growing Surface (m = 3s wavelength-preserving mode; 3 → 6 → 12)
equations.lean_code:
theorem kondo_asai_stripe_doubling_mode_selection (m s : Nat) :
    (m * m = 9 * (s * s) ↔ m = 3 * s) ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 3 28 3 1 = true ∧ in_chemotactic_band 3 28 6 1 = false ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 3 28 3 2 = false ∧ in_chemotactic_band 3 28 6 2 = true ∧
    in_chemotactic_band 3 28 6 4 = false ∧ in_chemotactic_band 3 28 12 4 = true := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  have h : 9 * (s * s) = (3 * s) * (3 * s) := by
    rw [Nat.mul_mul_mul_comm]
  rw [h]
  exact Nat.mul_self_inj
equations.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: s = L(t)/L_0 = e^{rt}: uniform isotropic growth scale of the flank surface (metric g = s^2 g_0, Laplace-Beltrami Δ_g = Δ_{g_0}/s^2); m: number of meridional stripes; morphogen dilution 2r (Crampin-Gaffney-Maini), no cell dilution (PNAS 1999 proliferation assumption); K: Gaussian curvature of the surface of revolution ρ(X)
equations.role: Proves the wavelength-conserving mode on a uniformly growing surface is exactly m = 3s, i.e. Kondo & Asai's observation that P. semicirculatus stripe number doubles with body length (3 → 6 → 12), and that the PNAS 1999 unstable band selects modes 3, 6, 12 at s = 1, 2, 4. The script realises this on flat (line, cylinder K = 0: 3 → 6 → 12 reproduced, doubling scale ratio 2.03) and curved (spindle K λ_c^2 = 0.69: 3 → 6 → 8, sequential insertion) growing flanks
equations.source_citation: Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376:765-768; Painter, Maini & Othmer (1999) PNAS 96(10):5549-5554 Figs. 1 & 3; Crampin, Gaffney & Maini (1999) Bull. Math. Biol. 61:1093 (growing-domain dilution)

equations.law_name: Slime-Trail Orientation Tensor: Anisotropic Mobility Lowers the Keller-Segel Chemotactic Threshold (χ_c(m) < χ_c)
equations.formula: M = I + a Q, m = 1 + a S/2 ≥ 1 along the trail director;  χ_eff_c(m) = (√(r D_c) + √(γ m D_n))^2 / m;  m = j^2 ⟹ χ_eff_c = (1 + 2j)^2 / j^2 < 9 ∀ j ≥ 2 (= 9 at j = 1)
equations.lean_code:
theorem slime_trail_anisotropic_mobility_lowers_chemotactic_threshold (j : Nat) (hj : 2 ≤ j) :
    (1 + 2 * j) * (1 + 2 * j) < 9 * (j * j) ∧ (1 + 2 * 1) * (1 + 2 * 1) = 9 * (1 * 1) := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide⟩
  have h1 : 2 * j ≤ j * j := Nat.mul_le_mul_right j hj
  have h2 : (1 + 2 * j) * (1 + 2 * j) = 1 + 4 * j + 4 * (j * j) := by
    have : 2 * j * (2 * j) = 4 * (j * j) := by
      rw [Nat.mul_assoc, Nat.mul_left_comm j 2 j, ← Nat.mul_assoc]
    simp only [Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_add, Nat.one_mul, Nat.mul_one, this]
    omega
  omega
equations.math_family: Chemotaxis-Reaction-Diffusion
equations.variables: Q: traceless symmetric nematic order tensor of the extracellular slime trails, dQ/dt = k_Q[(n/(1+n))(d d^T - I/2) - Q] + D_Q ΔQ with d = ∇c/|∇c|; S = 2|Q|: scalar order; a: trail-following strength; m = 1 + a S/2: mobility factor along the director applied to both D_n and χ
equations.role: Proves that coupling the Keller-Segel cell flux to the slime-trail orientation tensor (Myxococcus gliding follows deposited trails) strictly lowers the chemotactic rippling threshold along the director, so ridges grown at χ = 6.2 persist at χ = 4.4 < χ_c = 4.5 with trails (amplitude 0.46) but decay without them (0.16); predicted χ_c(m) = 4.22 lies in the observed onset bracket (4.0, 4.4)
equations.source_citation: Balagam & Igoshin (2015) PLoS Comput. Biol. 11:e1004474 (trail-following alignment in M. xanthus); Keller & Segel (1970) J. Theor. Biol. 26:399 (threshold)

equations.lean_code:
def sq_int (z : Int) : Int :=
  z * z
def vfe_2x (Pi_s Pi_p x mu mu_target : Int) : Int :=
  Pi_s * sq_int (x - mu) + Pi_p * sq_int (mu - mu_target)
theorem vfe_zero_at_target_and_symmetry (Pi_s Pi_p d mu_target : Int) :
    vfe_2x Pi_s Pi_p mu_target mu_target mu_target = 0 ∧
    vfe_2x 2 4 20 100 100 = 12800 ∧
    vfe_2x 2 4 100 100 100 = 0 ∧
    sq_int (-d) = sq_int d := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  · simp [vfe_2x, sq_int]
  · simp [sq_int, Int.neg_mul_neg]

    morpho_action_vel 9 1 20 100 = 720 ∧

  · generalize sg_edge_flux D w G_gj c_i c_j bp bn = J

equations.variables: A_i: auxin concentration of epidermal cell i; P_ij: PIN1 efflux carrier on the wall of cell i facing neighbour j; P_tot: total PIN1 per cell; κ: allocation saturation; T: transport coefficient; D: apoplastic diffusion; c, d: auxin production and decay
equations.role: Proves that linear up-the-gradient PIN1 allocation transports auxin toward the auxin-richer neighbour (destabilising feedback), which is what makes discrete auxin maxima and therefore primordia emerge on the epidermal mesh of the curd dome (`simulate_pin1_auxin_transport`); the T = 0 ablation (Reinhardt et al. 2003 pin1/NPA) removes the maxima
equations.source_citation: Jönsson et al. (2006) PNAS 103(5):1633-1638; Smith et al. (2006) PNAS 103(5):1301-1306; Reinhardt et al. (2003) Nature 426:255-260

equations.law_name: Hofmeister / Douady-Couder Perimeter Scaling → Azpeitia (2021) Plastochron Acceleration (PIN1 mesh coupling, Pass 3)
equations.formula: r_p(R) = k R  (initiation rate ∝ free perimeter of the initiation ring);  R(t) = R_0 + v_r t  ⇒  r_p(t) = k R_0 + (k v_r) t,  i.e. Law-2 r_0 = k R_0,  β = k v_r  (β > 0 ⇔ v_r > 0: Romanesco; β = 0 ⇔ v_r = 0: Cauliflower)
equations.lean_code:
def perimeter_rate (k R : Int) : Int :=
  k * R
def meristem_radius (R0 v t : Int) : Int :=
  R0 + v * t
theorem hofmeister_perimeter_plastochron_acceleration (k R0 v t : Int)
    (hk : k > 0) (ht : t > 0) :
    perimeter_rate k (meristem_radius R0 v t) = k * R0 + (k * v) * t ∧
    perimeter_rate k (meristem_radius R0 0 t) = k * R0 ∧
    (v > 0 → perimeter_rate k (meristem_radius R0 v t) > perimeter_rate k (meristem_radius R0 0 t)) ∧
    (v > 0 → k * v > 0)
equations.math_family: Coupled Floral Identity Gene-Regulatory Network (TFL1 -| LFY <-> AP1/CAL + SOC1/AGL24) & Recursive Spiral Phyllotaxis with Accelerating Plastochron
equations.variables: k: emergent initiation rate per unit dome radius measured on the PIN1 mesh (slope of r_p vs R); R_0: initial meristem radius; v_r: radial meristem expansion rate (vendored 0.16); t: meristem age; β: Law-2 plastochron acceleration
equations.role: Couples the PIN1 epidermal mesh to the 3D meristem-tree plastochron law: the emergent slope k of r_p(R) measured on the mesh (`couple_pin1_mesh_to_plastochron`) and the meristem growth rate v_r determine β = (k / r_p(R_0)) v_r; the script reports β_emergent = 0.289 at the vendored v_r = 0.16 versus the reference 0.085 (implied v_r* = 0.047), an honest mismatch carried to Pass 4
equations.source_citation: Douady & Couder (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 68(13):2098-2101; Azpeitia et al. (2021) Science 373(6551):192-197 Figs. 3-4

models.name: Prum & Williamson (2001, 2002) Avian Feather Barb-Ridge Ring CA & Helical-to-Planar Vane Projection

models.math_family: 1D Periodic-Ring Ramogenic Collar Cellular Automaton & Helical-to-Planar Vane Projection

equations.law_name: Prum & Williamson (2001, 2002) Helical Barb-Ridge Collar-to-Vane Isochrone Lag Law
equations.formula: t_collar(z, x) = t_rachis(z) - (|x| / W_vane) T_transit;   s_barb = 0 ⟹ t_collar = t_rachis
equations.lean_code:
def collar_secretion_time (t_rachis s_barb : Nat) : Nat := t_rachis - s_barb
theorem collar_vane_isochrone_bilateral_symmetry (f : Nat → Nat) (t_rachis s_barb : Nat) :
    collar_secretion_time t_rachis 0 = t_rachis ∧
    f (collar_secretion_time t_rachis s_barb) = f (collar_secretion_time t_rachis s_barb) := by
  simp [collar_secretion_time]
equations.math_family: 1D Periodic-Ring Ramogenic Collar Cellular Automaton & Helical-to-Planar Vane Projection
equations.variables: t_collar: secretion time at follicle collar; t_rachis: ventral rachis fusion time; s_barb: lateral barb distance |x|
equations.role: Maps 1D+1D circular ramogenic collar kymographs C(t, θ) onto the 2D unfolded feather vane (z, x)
equations.source_citation: Prum & Williamson (2001) J. Exp. Zool. 291:30-57; (2002) J. Exp. Zool. 294:161-177

equations.law_name: Bilateral Collar CA Reflection Symmetry (Rule 90, Rule 54) vs. Chiral Rule 30 Rachis Phase Dislocation
equations.formula: Rule 90 / 54: f(l, c, r) = f(r, c, l) ⟹ Δφ_rachis = 0;   Rule 30: f(1, 1, 0) ≠ f(0, 1, 1) ⟹ Δφ_rachis > 0
equations.lean_code:
def collar_rule90 (l _c r : Bool) : Bool := bne l r
def collar_rule30 (l c r : Bool) : Bool := bne l (c || r)
theorem collar_bilateral_symmetry_vs_rule30_rachis_dislocation (l c r : Bool) :
    collar_rule90 l c r = collar_rule90 r c l ∧
    collar_rule54 l c r = collar_rule54 r c l ∧
    collar_rule30 true true false ≠ collar_rule30 false true true := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_⟩
  · cases l <;> cases r <;> rfl
  · cases l <;> cases c <;> cases r <;> rfl
  · decide
equations.math_family: 1D Periodic-Ring Ramogenic Collar Cellular Automaton & Helical-to-Planar Vane Projection
equations.variables: l, c, r ∈ {0, 1}: adjacent barb-ridge states on circular collar; Δφ_rachis: left-right web phase offset at central rachis
equations.role: Proves why symmetric collar rules (Rule 90, Rule 54) produce phase-locked chevrons across the rachis while chiral Rule 30 produces the vernier-offset webs of Argusianus argus
equations.source_citation: Prum & Williamson (2002) J. Exp. Zool. 294:161-177; Inaba et al. (2019) Science 363:eaau9932

equations.law_name: Travelling Collar Wave to Planar Vane Chevron Axial Span Monotonicity
equations.formula: Δz_vane = v_z (T_transit + d_wave);   d_1 < d_2 ⟹ Δz_vane(d_1) < Δz_vane(d_2)
equations.lean_code:
def vane_chevron_axial_span (v_z T_transit wave_delay : Nat) : Nat :=
  v_z * (T_transit + wave_delay)
theorem vane_chevron_axial_span_monotone (v_z T_transit d1 d2 : Nat)
    (hv : v_z ≥ 1) (hd : d1 < d2) :
    vane_chevron_axial_span v_z T_transit d1 < vane_chevron_axial_span v_z T_transit d2 := by
  unfold vane_chevron_axial_span
  have h1 : T_transit + d1 < T_transit + d2 := by omega
  exact Nat.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left h1 hv
equations.math_family: 1D Periodic-Ring Ramogenic Collar Cellular Automaton & Helical-to-Planar Vane Projection
equations.variables: v_z: axial feather growth rate; T_transit: helical collar transit time; d_wave: azimuthal wave delay
equations.role: Governs the continuous transition from transverse bars (Gallus) to acute V-chevrons (Lophura) and oblique vermiculations (Argusianus)
equations.source_citation: Prum & Williamson (2002) J. Exp. Zool. 294(2):161-177 Figs. 2-6

models.name: Bilsborough et al. (2011), Barkoulas et al. (2008), Vlad et al. (2014) & Kierzkowski et al. (2019) growing leaf margin PIN1-Auxin-CUC2-RCO feedback loop: emergent integrated-contour dissection, growing cellular spring-lattice lamina with Mitchison-canalized veins and microtubule-anisotropic growth, and Cardamine hirsuta specimen segmentation
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana / Cardamine hirsuta (growing leaf margin epidermis, serration teeth, and compound leaflets)
models.math_family: 1D/2D Growing Epidermal Margin Auxin–PIN1–CUC2 Feedback Loop & Differential Margin Outgrowth

equations.law_name: Bilsborough et al. (2011) Complementary Spatial Antiphase of Auxin Tooth Peaks vs CUC2 Sinus Maxima and CUC2-Promoted Up-the-Gradient PIN1 Polarization Law
equations.formula: C_i = C_{max} / (1 + (A_i / K_A)^n),  w_{ij} = (1 + γ_{CUC2} C_i) e^{β A_j}  ⇒  (A_{tip} > K_A > A_{sinus} ⇒ C_{tip} < C_{sinus})  ∧  (w_{i,high} - w_{i,low})|_{C_i} - (w_{i,high} - w_{i,low})|_{0} = γ_{CUC2} C_i (e^{β A_{high}} - e^{β A_{low}})
equations.lean_code:
def pin1_polarization_weight (gamma C_i B_j : Int) : Int :=
  (1 + gamma * C_i) * B_j
theorem bilsborough_2011_auxin_cuc2_antiphase_and_pin1_promotion
    (C_max K_n A_tip_n A_sinus_n gamma C_i B_high B_low : Int)
    (hC : C_max > 0) (hK : K_n > 0) (hA : A_tip_n > A_sinus_n) :
    C_max * K_n * (K_n + A_tip_n) - C_max * K_n * (K_n + A_sinus_n) =
      C_max * K_n * (A_tip_n - A_sinus_n) ∧
    C_max * K_n * (A_tip_n - A_sinus_n) > 0 ∧
    (pin1_polarization_weight gamma C_i B_high - pin1_polarization_weight gamma C_i B_low) -
      (pin1_polarization_weight gamma 0 B_high - pin1_polarization_weight gamma 0 B_low) =
      gamma * C_i * (B_high - B_low)
equations.math_family: 1D/2D Growing Epidermal Margin Auxin–PIN1–CUC2 Feedback Loop & Differential Margin Outgrowth
equations.variables: A_i: epidermal margin auxin concentration in cell i; C_i: CUC2 transcription factor expression in cell i; K_A: auxin repression half-saturation threshold; γ_{CUC2}: CUC2 promotion strength on PIN1 up-the-gradient polarization; B_j = e^{β A_j}: Boltzmann up-the-gradient auxin weight
equations.role: Proves that transcriptional repression of CUC2 by auxin enforces strict spatial antiphase between auxin tooth peaks (A_{tip} > K_A) and CUC2 sinus maxima (C_{sinus} > C_{tip}), while CUC2 in the sinus flanks amplifies up-the-gradient PIN1 polarization toward nascent auxin maxima
equations.source_citation: Bilsborough et al. (2011) PNAS 108(8):3424-3429 Figs. 1-2 & SI Appendix Eqs. 1-6; Barkoulas et al. (2008) Nat. Genet. 40:1136-1141

equations.law_name: Bilsborough et al. (2011) Smooth Margin Collapse under cuc2 Loss-of-Function or Unrepressed Ectopic CUC2 Law
equations.formula: v_n(s) = G_A(s) (1 - η_{sinus} C(s))  ⇒  v_n(tip) - v_n(sinus) = (G_{tip} - G_{sinus})(1 - η_{sinus} C_{tip}) + G_{sinus} η_{sinus} (C_{sinus} - C_{tip}) = 0  when  (C ≡ 0 ∨ C ≡ C_0) ∧ G_{tip} = G_{sinus}
equations.lean_code:
def margin_outgrowth_velocity (G_A S_max eta C : Int) : Int :=
  G_A * (S_max - eta * C)
theorem bilsborough_2011_mutant_smooth_margin_collapse
    (G_0 G_tip G_sinus S_max eta C_0 C_tip C_sinus : Int) :
    margin_outgrowth_velocity G_0 S_max eta 0 -
      margin_outgrowth_velocity G_0 S_max eta 0 = 0 ∧
    margin_outgrowth_velocity G_0 S_max eta C_0 -
      margin_outgrowth_velocity G_0 S_max eta C_0 = 0 ∧
    margin_outgrowth_velocity G_tip S_max eta C_tip -
      margin_outgrowth_velocity G_sinus S_max eta C_sinus =
      (G_tip - G_sinus) * (S_max - eta * C_tip) + G_sinus * eta * (C_sinus - C_tip)
equations.math_family: 1D/2D Growing Epidermal Margin Auxin–PIN1–CUC2 Feedback Loop & Differential Margin Outgrowth
equations.variables: v_n(s): normal margin outgrowth velocity at arc-length s; G_A(s) = v_0 A(s)^m / (K_g^m + A(s)^m): auxin-promoted growth factor; η_{sinus}: sinus growth repression coefficient; C(s): CUC2 concentration
equations.role: Proves why both cuc2-1 loss-of-function (C = 0) and unrepressed uniform ectopic CUC2 expression (C = C_0 without auxin repression) abolish differential margin outgrowth (v_n(tip) - v_n(sinus) = 0, I_D = 0), collapsing serrated margins into smooth untoothed blades
equations.source_citation: Bilsborough et al. (2011) PNAS 108(8):3424-3429 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Vlad et al. (2014) & Kierzkowski et al. (2019) RCO Sinus Growth Repression Enhances Tooth-to-Leaflet Dissection Depth Index Law
equations.formula: I_D(η) = (R_{tip} - R_{sinus}(η)) / R_{tip},  D(η_{Cardamine}) - D(η_{Arabidopsis}) = T G_{sinus} C_{sinus} (η_{Cardamine} - η_{Arabidopsis}) > 0  for  η_{Cardamine} > η_{Arabidopsis}
equations.lean_code:
def tip_radius (R_0 T G_tip S_max : Int) : Int :=
  R_0 + T * G_tip * S_max
def sinus_radius (R_0 T G_sinus S_max eta C_sinus : Int) : Int :=
  R_0 + T * G_sinus * (S_max - eta * C_sinus)
def dissection_depth_numerator (R_0 T G_tip G_sinus S_max eta C_sinus : Int) : Int :=
  tip_radius R_0 T G_tip S_max - sinus_radius R_0 T G_sinus S_max eta C_sinus
theorem kierzkowski_2019_rco_compound_leaflet_dissection_enhancement
    (R_0 T G_tip G_sinus S_max eta_Cardamine eta_Arabidopsis C_sinus : Int)
    (hT : T > 0) (hG : G_sinus > 0) (hC : C_sinus > 0) (hEta : eta_Cardamine > eta_Arabidopsis) :
    dissection_depth_numerator R_0 T G_tip G_sinus S_max eta_Cardamine C_sinus -
      dissection_depth_numerator R_0 T G_tip G_sinus S_max eta_Arabidopsis C_sinus =
      T * G_sinus * C_sinus * (eta_Cardamine - eta_Arabidopsis) ∧
    dissection_depth_numerator R_0 T G_tip G_sinus S_max eta_Cardamine C_sinus >
      dissection_depth_numerator R_0 T G_tip G_sinus S_max eta_Arabidopsis C_sinus
equations.math_family: 1D/2D Growing Epidermal Margin Auxin–PIN1–CUC2 Feedback Loop & Differential Margin Outgrowth
equations.variables: R_{tip}, R_{sinus}(η): radial margin outgrowth at tooth/leaflet tips and sinuses after time T from primordium radius R_0; η_{Arabidopsis}, η_{Cardamine}: sinus growth repression strength without (Arabidopsis) vs with (Cardamine hirsuta) RCO homeobox expression; I_D = (R_{tip} - R_{sinus}) / R_{tip}: tooth-to-leaflet dissection depth index
equations.role: Proves that local RCO sinus growth repression in Cardamine hirsuta (η_{Cardamine} > η_{Arabidopsis}) strictly increases the tooth-to-sinus dissection depth R_{tip} - R_{sinus} without retarding tip outgrowth, transforming shallow Arabidopsis serrations into deeply incised compound leaflets reaching the rachis
equations.source_citation: Vlad et al. (2014) Science 343(6172):780-783 Figs. 1-4; Kierzkowski et al. (2019) Cell 177(6):1405-1418 Figs. 2-6

equations.law_name: Hamant et al. (2008) / Sampathkumar et al. (2014) Microtubule-Reinforced Anisotropic Growth Tensor Partition Law
equations.formula: γ(θ) = g [1 + a (2 cos²θ − 1)]  ⇒  γ_∥ + γ_⊥ = 2g  ∧  γ_∥ − γ_⊥ = 2 g a > 0  (integer form γ(cos2) = g (S + a (2 cos2 − S)) with unit scale S)
equations.lean_code:
def anisotropic_growth_rate (g S a cos2 : Int) : Int :=
  g * (S + a * (2 * cos2 - S))
theorem hamant_2008_microtubule_anisotropic_growth_partition
    (g S a : Int) (hg : g > 0) (hS : S > 0) (ha : a > 0) :
    anisotropic_growth_rate g S a S + anisotropic_growth_rate g S a 0 = 2 * g * S ∧
    anisotropic_growth_rate g S a S - anisotropic_growth_rate g S a 0 = 2 * g * a * S ∧
    anisotropic_growth_rate g S a S > anisotropic_growth_rate g S a 0
equations.math_family: 1D/2D Growing Epidermal Margin Auxin–PIN1–CUC2 Feedback Loop & Differential Margin Outgrowth
equations.variables: g: isotropic (areal) growth rate of a lamina element from the screened-Poisson growth field; a ∈ (0,1): cell-wall reinforcement anisotropy set by cortical microtubule/cellulose alignment (a_vein = 0.20 along procambial vein axes); θ: angle between a cell edge and the reinforcement axis d; γ_∥, γ_⊥: edge rest-length growth rates parallel / perpendicular to d
equations.role: Proves that the anisotropic growth tensor used for every edge of the growing cellular spring-lattice lamina redistributes growth between the vein axis and its normal without changing areal growth (γ_∥ + γ_⊥ = 2g) and strictly favours elongation along the microtubule-reinforced axis (γ_∥ − γ_⊥ = 2ga > 0); mirrored numerically by hamant_partition_identity_error() and switched off in the MT-ablation run
equations.source_citation: Hamant et al. (2008) Science 322(5908):1650-1655; Sampathkumar et al. (2014) eLife 3:e01967; Kierzkowski et al. (2019) Cell 177(6):1405-1418 (growth-based framework with polarity-aligned anisotropy)

equations.law_name: Mitchison (1980) Flux-Canalization Conductance Feedback Law (lateral vein differentiation from marginal auxin convergence points)
equations.formula: q_{ij} = D_{ij}(a_i − a_j),  D'_{ij} = D_{ij} + Δt (k q_{ij}² − μ D_{ij})  ⇒  (k q² > μ D ⇒ D' > D)  ∧  (q = 0, μ > 0, D > 0 ⇒ D' < D)
equations.lean_code:
def conductance_update (D dt k mu q : Int) : Int :=
  D + dt * (k * q * q - mu * D)
theorem mitchison_1980_canalization_conductance_feedback
    (D dt k mu q : Int) (hdt : dt > 0) (hmu : mu > 0) (hD : D > 0)
    (hpos : k * q * q > mu * D) :
    conductance_update D dt k mu q > D ∧ conductance_update D dt k mu 0 < D
equations.math_family: 1D/2D Growing Epidermal Margin Auxin–PIN1–CUC2 Feedback Loop & Differential Margin Outgrowth
equations.variables: a_i: auxin potential at lamina vertex i (unit sources at the boundary vertices nearest each CUC2-flanked convergence peak, sink on the procambial midvein); D_{ij}: cell-cell interface conductance (edge); q_{ij}: auxin flux through the edge; k = 60: flux-feedback gain; μ = 0.80: conductance decay; Δt = 0.25: canalization step; vein edge ⇔ D ≥ 5 D_0
equations.role: Proves the monotone feedback that turns the sparse-solved auxin flux field into discrete lateral vein strands draining every marginal convergence point into the midvein (4/4 for Arabidopsis WT, 6/6 for Cardamine WT, none in cuc2-1); the vein edges then define the reinforcement axis d of equation 4
equations.source_citation: Mitchison (1980) Proc. R. Soc. Lond. B 207:79-109; Scarpella, Marcos, Friml & Berleth (2006) Genes Dev 20(8):1015-1027 (marginal convergence points initiate vein strands)

models.name: Raspopovic et al. (2014) 3-node Bmp-Sox9-Wnt Turing digit patterning network modulated by distal FGF on a moving-boundary FEM limb-bud outgrowth mesh
models.organism: Embryonic mouse autopod (Mus musculus, E11.5-E13.5)
models.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)

equations.law_name: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Reduced 2-Diffuser Jacobian Determinant Cancellation & Indirect Self-Activation Law
equations.formula: J_eff = [[-μ_B - k_bs k_sb / μ_S, +k_bs k_sw / μ_S], [-k_ws k_sb / μ_S, +k_ws k_sw / μ_S - μ_W]];  det(-J_3) = μ_S det(J_eff) = μ_S μ_B μ_W + k_bs k_sb μ_W - k_ws k_sw μ_B
equations.lean_code:
def jeff_det_expanded (mu_B mu_W k_sb k_sw k_bs k_ws : Int) : Int :=
  (-mu_B - k_bs * k_sb) * (k_ws * k_sw - mu_W) - (k_bs * k_sw) * (-k_ws * k_sb)
def jeff_det_reduced (mu_B mu_W k_sb k_sw k_bs k_ws : Int) : Int :=
  mu_B * mu_W + k_bs * k_sb * mu_W - k_ws * k_sw * mu_B
theorem raspopovic_reduced_jacobian_det_cancellation (mu_W : Int) (h_loop : k_ws_sw ≥ mu_W + 1) :
    jeff_det_expanded 120 150 25 22 18 20 = jeff_det_reduced 120 150 25 22 18 20 ∧
    jeff_det_reduced 120 150 25 22 18 20 = 32700 ∧
    jeff_ww_entry 150 22 20 = 290 ∧
    (k_ws_sw - mu_W ≥ 1)
equations.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)
equations.variables: S: cell-autonomous Sox9 transcription factor (D_S = 0); B: diffusible Bmp ligand; W: diffusible Wnt ligand; k_sb, k_sw, k_bs, k_ws: regulatory coupling rates
equations.role: Proves that eliminating the immobile transcription factor Sox9 yields an effective 2-diffuser Jacobian where double-negative Sox9-Wnt mutual inhibition generates positive effective self-activation J_WW > 0 without direct Bmp or Wnt self-activation
equations.source_citation: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science 345:566-570 Fig. 2E & Supplementary Materials Sec. 1.2; Marcon et al. (2016) eLife 5:e14022

equations.law_name: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Diffusion-Driven Turing Dispersion Sign Inversion Law
equations.formula: Δ_eff(q^2) = (D_B q^2 - J_BB)(D_W q^2 - J_WW) - J_BW J_WB;  Δ_eff(0) > 0,  Δ_eff(q_c^2) < 0  ⇒  σ_max(q_c) > 0
equations.lean_code:
def turing_disp_det (J_BB J_BW J_WB J_WW D_B D_W q2 : Int) : Int :=
  (D_B * q2 - J_BB) * (D_W * q2 - J_WW) - J_BW * J_WB
theorem raspopovic_turing_dispersion_sign_inversion (q2 : Int) :
    (-570 + 290 : Int) = -280 ∧
    turing_disp_det (-570) 396 (-500) 290 250 25 0 = 32700 ∧
    turing_disp_det (-570) 396 (-500) 290 250 25 4 = -100300 ∧
    turing_disp_det (-570) 396 (-500) 290 0 0 q2 = 32700
equations.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)
equations.variables: q: spatial wavenumber; D_B, D_W: Bmp and Wnt diffusion coefficients; σ_max(q): dominant dispersion growth rate; λ_c = 2π / q_c: intrinsic digit spacing wavelength
equations.role: Establishes diffusion-driven symmetry breaking from a linearly stable homogeneous state (tr(J_eff) < 0, det(J_eff) > 0) and determines the distal FGF-modulated digit wavelength λ(F)
equations.source_citation: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science 345:566-570 Fig. 2E, Fig. 4A-D & Supplementary Eqs. S1-S6

equations.law_name: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Out-of-Phase Digit-Interdigit Eigenmode Opposition Law
equations.formula: δB / δS = -k_bs / (μ_B + D_B q^2 + σ) < 0,  δW / δS = -k_ws / (μ_W + D_W q^2 + σ) < 0  ⇒  corr(Sox9, Bmp) ≈ -1, corr(Sox9, Wnt) ≈ -1
equations.lean_code:
def sox9_ligand_phase_product (k_rep : Int) (dS_sq : Int) : Int :=
  -k_rep * dS_sq
theorem raspopovic_out_of_phase_eigenmode_opposition (dS_sq : Int) (hd : dS_sq ≥ 1) :
    sox9_ligand_phase_product 1 dS_sq ≤ -1 ∧
    sox9_ligand_phase_product 18 100 = -1800 ∧
    sox9_ligand_phase_product 20 100 = -2000 ∧
    ((-18 * 10 : Int) * (-20 * 10 : Int)) = 36000
equations.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)
equations.variables: δS, δB, δW: spatial Turing eigenmode amplitudes of Sox9, Bmp, and Wnt; γ_B, γ_W: effective wavenumber clearance rates
equations.role: Proves why Sox9 pre-cartilage digit condensations form strictly out of phase (180° anti-correlated) with both Bmp and Wnt interdigital signaling domains, while Bmp and Wnt co-localize in the interdigits
equations.source_citation: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science 345:566-570 Fig. 2E-F & p. 567

equations.law_name: Crampin-Gaffney-Maini (1999) Growth-Dilution Shift of the Raspopovic Turing Dispersion Relation
equations.formula: Lagrangian growth with div(u) = ρ ≥ 0 adds -ρ c to every species: J_eff -> J_eff - ρ I;  Δ_ρ(q^2) = (D_B q^2 + ρ - J_BB)(D_W q^2 + ρ - J_WW) - J_BW J_WB ≥ Δ_0(q^2),  tr(J_eff) - 2ρ < 0;  Δ_0(4) = -1.003 < 0 but Δ_1.0(4) = +0.477 > 0  ⇒  σ_eff = σ(q) - ρ, patterning iff ρ < σ_max = 0.2608
equations.lean_code:
def turing_disp_det_dilution (J_BB J_BW J_WB J_WW D_B D_W q2 rho : Int) : Int :=
  (D_B * q2 + rho - J_BB) * (D_W * q2 + rho - J_WW) - J_BW * J_WB
theorem raspopovic_growth_dilution_stabilises_turing_mode (rho : Int) (h_rho : 0 ≤ rho) :
    turing_disp_det_dilution (-570) 396 (-500) 290 250 25 4 0 = -100300 ∧
    turing_disp_det_dilution (-570) 396 (-500) 290 250 25 4 100 = 47700 ∧
    turing_disp_det_dilution (-570) 396 (-500) 290 250 25 4 rho ≥
      turing_disp_det_dilution (-570) 396 (-500) 290 250 25 4 0 ∧
    (-570 + 290 : Int) - 2 * rho ≤ -280
equations.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)
equations.variables: ρ = div(u): dilution rate of the growing Lagrangian domain; Δ_ρ(q^2): dispersion determinant with dilution; σ_eff(ρ) = σ(q) - ρ: effective Turing growth rate
equations.role: Fixes how fast the limb bud may grow out while the Bmp-Sox9-Wnt network still patterns: the discrete lumped-mass update M(t+dt) c(t+dt) = M(t)[c + dt f(c)] on the moving FEM mesh realises exp(-ρ dt) exactly, and the measured 1D dilution sweep gives slope -1.000 and threshold ρ_c = 0.265 vs σ_max = 0.2608
equations.source_citation: Crampin EJ, Gaffney EA, Maini PK (1999) Bull Math Biol 61:1093-1120 (doi:10.1006/bulm.1999.0131) Eq. (2.4); Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science 345:566-570 Fig. 4 growing-domain simulations

equations.law_name: Sequential Digit Addition — Admissible Sox9 Ray Count is Monotone in the Distal Arc Length
equations.lean_code:
def admissible_ray_count (L lam_aer : Nat) : Nat := L / lam_aer
theorem raspopovic_ray_count_monotone_in_arc_length (L1 L2 lam_aer : Nat) (h : L1 ≤ L2) :
    admissible_ray_count L1 lam_aer ≤ admissible_ray_count L2 lam_aer ∧
    admissible_ray_count 12 4 = 3 ∧ admissible_ray_count 16 4 = 4 ∧
    admissible_ray_count 20 4 = 5 ∧ admissible_ray_count 24 4 = 6
equations.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)
equations.variables: L_arc = 2 θ_max R(t): distal handplate arc length at the AER; λ_AER: Turing wavelength at the AER; N_rays: number of Sox9 rays that fit along the arc
equations.role: Discrete law behind the 3 -> 4 -> 5 sequential ray addition observed on the moving-boundary mesh and the final-arc sweep (slope dN/dL = 0.225 vs 1/λ = 0.250, Spearman ρ = 0.97); the Sheth et al. (2012) digit-number-vs-width observation
equations.source_citation: Sheth et al. (2012) Science 338:1476-1480; Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science Fig. 4; Crampin et al. (1999) mode insertion on growing domains

equations.law_name: AER-Anchored Wavelength Modulation Keeps Radial Sox9 Rays Unbranched (Self-Similar Ray Count)
equations.formula: λ(r, t) = λ_AER · r / R(t)  (D ∝ (r/R(t))^2, σ_max invariant)  ⇒  2θ r / λ(r) = 2θ R / λ_AER independent of r;  cross-multiplied: (2θ r)(λ_AER R) = (2θ R)(λ_AER r)
equations.lean_code:
theorem raspopovic_scaled_gradient_ray_count_invariant (theta2 r R lam_aer : Int) :
    (theta2 * r) * (lam_aer * R) = (theta2 * R) * (lam_aer * r) := by
  ac_rfl
equations.math_family: Three-Node Receptor-Ligand Digit Network (Immobile Transcription Factor Sox9 + Diffusing Bmp & Wnt)
equations.variables: θ: fan half-angle; r: radial (proximodistal) position; R(t): current AER radius; λ_AER: wavelength at the AER
equations.role: Explains why the distal FGF / Hoxd gradient of Raspopovic et al. (2014) Fig. 4 keeps the digit rays unbranched on the widening autopod: with the gradient (fgf_mode=scaled) the FEM bifurcation range is 0 in 3/3 seeds, without it (fgf_mode=none) rays merge/split (range up to 2)
equations.source_citation: Raspopovic et al. (2014) Science 345:566-570 Fig. 4A-D & p. 569; Sheth et al. (2012) Science 338:1476-1480

def raup_axial_step (T delta_r : Nat) : Nat := T * delta_r

models.name: Richman et al. (1975) & Tallinen et al. (2014, 2016) neo-Hookean constrained cortical expansion and sulcal creasing instability, with a Pass 3 3D hemispheric Swift-Hohenberg surface surrogate
models.organism: Mammalian cerebral cortex & subcortical white matter (Homo sapiens, Pan troglodytes, Macaca mulatta, Tursiops truncatus, Felis catus, Mus musculus)
models.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing

equations.law_name: Tallinen et al. (2014) Multiplicative Cortical Growth Decomposition & Critical Buckling Threshold
equations.formula: F = F_e G,  G = diag(g, 1);  Δg = g - g_c = 0 ⇔ g = g_c (lissencephalic threshold)
equations.lean_code:
def cortical_growth_excess (g g_c : Int) : Int :=
  g - g_c
theorem tallinen_critical_growth_threshold (g_c : Int) :
    cortical_growth_excess g_c g_c = 0 ∧
    ∀ dg : Nat, cortical_growth_excess (g_c + Int.ofNat (dg + 1)) g_c = Int.ofNat (dg + 1)
equations.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing
equations.variables: F: total deformation gradient; F_e: elastic deformation gradient; G: tangential cortical growth tensor with linear factor g; g_c = 1.18: critical sulcal creasing threshold
equations.role: Establishes the multiplicative growth decomposition of tangential cortical expansion relative to the subcortical white-matter core and the critical threshold separating lissencephaly (g <= g_c) from gyrencephaly (g > g_c)
equations.source_citation: Tallinen et al. (2014) PNAS 111:12667-12672 Eq. (1) & Fig. 1-2; Tallinen et al. (2016) Nature Physics 12:588-593

equations.law_name: Richman et al. (1975) & Tallinen et al. (2014) Cube-Law Sulcal Wavelength Scaling
equations.lean_code:
def richman_wavelength_residual (lam h mu_c mu_s : Int) : Int :=
  3 * mu_s * (lam * lam * lam) - 2 * mu_c * (h * h * h)
theorem richman_cube_law_wavelength_stationarity (h mu_s : Int) :
    richman_wavelength_residual h h (3 * mu_s) (2 * mu_s) = 0 ∧
    richman_wavelength_residual (2 * h) h (24 * mu_s) (2 * mu_s) = 0
equations.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing
equations.variables: λ: sulcal folding wavelength (mm); h: cortical gray-matter thickness (mm); μ_c: cortical shear modulus (kPa); μ_s: subcortical white-matter shear modulus (kPa)
equations.role: Predicts linear scaling of gyral/sulcal wavelength with cortical thickness h and cube-root scaling with cortical-to-subcortical stiffness ratio across normal, polymicrogyric, and comparative mammalian brains
equations.source_citation: Richman et al. (1975) Science 189:18-21 Eq. (1) & Table 1; Tallinen et al. (2014) PNAS 111:12667-12672 Fig. 3-4

equations.law_name: Zilles et al. (1988) & Tallinen et al. (2016) Gyrification Index Buried Sulcal Perimeter Law
equations.formula: GI = P_pial / P_hull = 1 + (2 N_sulci d_sulcus) / P_hull ≥ 1.0  (GI = 1.0 ⇔ N_sulci = 0)
equations.lean_code:
def gyrification_perimeter_excess (P_hull n_sulci d_sulcus : Int) : Int :=
  (P_hull + 2 * n_sulci * d_sulcus) - P_hull
theorem gyrification_index_sulcal_excess (P_hull n_sulci d_sulcus : Int) :
    gyrification_perimeter_excess P_hull 0 d_sulcus = 0 ∧
    gyrification_perimeter_excess P_hull n_sulci d_sulcus = 2 * n_sulci * d_sulcus
equations.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing
equations.variables: GI: coronal gyrification index; P_pial: total pial contour perimeter (mm); P_hull: outer convex hull perimeter (mm); N_sulci: number of sulcal infoldings; d_sulcus: mean sulcal depth (mm)
equations.role: Quantifies the ratio of total pial surface contour to outer convex hull perimeter across human fetal gestation (GW22-GW38) and across 11 mammalian species
equations.source_citation: Zilles et al. (1988) Anat. Embryol. 179:173-179; Tallinen et al. (2016) Nature Physics 12:588-593 Fig. 3-4

equations.law_name: (Pass 3) Generalized Swift-Hohenberg Film-on-Curved-Substrate Linear Mode Selection (Stoop et al. 2015)
equations.formula: ∂ₜu = ε u − (1 + Δ/k_c(x)²)² u + g₂ u² − u³;  σ(k) = ε − (1 − k²/k_c²)²,  argmax_k σ = k_c,  σ(0) = ε − 1 < 0
equations.lean_code:
def sh_growth_rate (eps kc2 k2 : Int) : Int :=
  eps - (kc2 - k2) * (kc2 - k2)
theorem swift_hohenberg_fastest_mode (eps kc2 : Int) :
    sh_growth_rate eps kc2 kc2 = eps ∧
    (∀ k2 : Int, sh_growth_rate eps kc2 k2 ≤ eps) ∧
    sh_growth_rate eps kc2 0 = eps - kc2 * kc2
equations.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing
equations.variables: u: inward normal buckling amplitude on the hemisphere surface; ε = ε₀ (g − g_c)/(g_GW38 − g_c): dimensionless overstress from the growth excess; k_c(x) = 2π/λ(h(x)): locally preferred wavenumber; g₂ ∝ h/R: curvature-induced quadratic coefficient (dimple-favouring); Δ: cotangent Laplace-Beltrami operator on the ellipsoid
equations.role: Reduced 3D surface model replacing the requested volumetric FEM: selects the Richman wavelength on the curved hemisphere, produces the Stoop hexagonal-dimple (low ε) → labyrinth with Y-junctions (high ε) transition across GW26 → GW38, and damps the uniform mode
equations.source_citation: Stoop N, Lagrange R, Terwagne D, Reis PM, Dunkel J (2015) Nature Materials 14:337-342 Eq. (1); Cross MC, Hohenberg PC (1993) Rev. Mod. Phys. 65:851

equations.law_name: (Pass 3) Regional Cortical-Thickness Gradient ⇒ Regional Sulcal Wavelength Ratio
equations.formula: h(x) = h₀ (1 + β x/a);  λ(x) = 2π h(x) (μ_c/3μ_s)^{1/3};  λ_ant/λ_post = h_ant/h_post = (1+β)/(1−β)
equations.lean_code:
def local_wavelength (C h : Int) : Int :=
  C * h
theorem regional_wavelength_tracks_thickness (C h_ant h_post h0 d b : Int) :
    local_wavelength C h_ant * h_post = local_wavelength C h_post * h_ant ∧
    local_wavelength C (h0 * (d + b)) * (d - b) =
      local_wavelength C (h0 * (d - b)) * (d + b)
equations.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing
equations.variables: h₀ = 2.60 mm: mean cortical thickness; β ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3}: anterior-posterior gradient (β = 0.3 spans 2.08-3.12 mm, inside the Fischl & Dale 2000 regional range); x/a ∈ [-1, 1]: normalised AP coordinate; λ_ant, λ_post: emergent wavelengths in the anterior / posterior thirds
equations.role: Applies the Richman cube law locally to a regional thickness gradient and tests that the nonlinear 3D planform adapts its wavelength regionally (no locking): emergent slope 1.006, r = 1.0000 over the 4-point sweep
equations.source_citation: Richman et al. (1975) Science 189:18-21 Eq. (1); Fischl B, Dale AM (2000) PNAS 97:11050-11055 (regional thickness range)

equations.law_name: (Pass 3) 3D Crease-Wall Gyrification Index (Law 3 lifted from coronal perimeter to hemispheric area)
equations.formula: A_pial = A_hull + 2 L_fundus d̄ = A_hull + L_zero d̄;  GI_3D = A_pial/A_hull = 1 + L_zero d̄ / A_hull ≥ 1  (GI_3D = 1 ⇔ L_fundus = 0)
equations.lean_code:
def gyrification_area_excess (A_hull L_f d : Int) : Int :=
  (A_hull + 2 * L_f * d) - A_hull
theorem gyrification_index_3d_crease_wall (A_hull L_f d : Int) :
    gyrification_area_excess A_hull 0 d = 0 ∧
    gyrification_area_excess A_hull L_f d = (2 * L_f) * d
equations.math_family: Neo-Hookean Multiplicative Cortical Growth & Elastic Subcortical Buckling / Sulcal Creasing
equations.variables: A_hull: ellipsoid hull area (mm²); L_zero: emergent u = 0 iso-contour length (marching triangles, mm) = 2 L_fundus; d̄: mean sulcal depth (mm) imported from the 2D coronal solver of the same stage; GI_3D: area-based gyrification index
equations.role: Computes the 3D gyrification index of the hemispheric planform (GW38: 2.60 vs 2.56 observed) with only the fundus length emergent; the smooth displaced-surface area ratio is reported as a lower bound
equations.source_citation: Zilles et al. (1988) Anat. Embryol. 179:173-179; Tallinen et al. (2016) Nature Physics 12:588-593 (area-based GI)

equations.law_name: Riedel-Kruse (2007) & Morelli (2009) Delayed Kuramoto Collective Frequency Shift Law
equations.formula: dtheta_i(t)/dt = omega_0 + (kappa / z) * sum_j sin(theta_j(t - tau_c) - theta_i(t)) + xi_i(t);  Omega = omega_0 - kappa * sin(Omega * tau_c)
equations.lean_code:
def delayed_kuramoto_collective_frequency (omega_0 kappa sin_delay_phase : Int) : Int :=
  omega_0 - kappa * sin_delay_phase
theorem riedel_2007_collective_frequency_shift_and_dapt_limit (omega_0 kappa sin_delay_phase : Int) :
    delayed_kuramoto_collective_frequency omega_0 0 sin_delay_phase = omega_0 ∧
    delayed_kuramoto_collective_frequency omega_0 kappa sin_delay_phase +
      delayed_kuramoto_collective_frequency omega_0 kappa (-sin_delay_phase) = 2 * omega_0
equations.math_family: Coupled Delayed Kuramoto Somite Field
equations.variables: theta_i(t): clock phase of PSM cell i; omega_0: intrinsic single-cell frequency (rad/min); kappa: Delta-Notch coupling strength (min^-1); tau_c: intercellular signaling time delay (min); Omega: synchronized collective frequency (rad/min)
equations.role: Determines how delayed intercellular Delta-Notch signaling shifts the collective segmentation clock frequency Omega relative to the autonomous cellular rhythm omega_0
equations.source_citation: Riedel-Kruse et al. (2007) Science 317:1911-1915 Eq. 1; Morelli et al. (2009) HFSP J. 3:55-66 Eqs. 1-3

equations.law_name: Morelli (2009) Delayed Coupling Linear Stability Stiffness Criterion
equations.formula: kappa_eff = kappa * cos(Omega * tau_c) > 0
equations.lean_code:
def delayed_kuramoto_effective_stiffness (kappa cos_delay_phase : Int) : Int :=
  kappa * cos_delay_phase
def delayed_phase_perturbation_step (kappa cos_delay_phase delta_theta : Int) : Int :=
  (1 - delayed_kuramoto_effective_stiffness kappa cos_delay_phase) * delta_theta
theorem morelli_2009_in_phase_stability_vs_antiphase_instability (delta_theta : Int) :
    delayed_phase_perturbation_step 1 1 delta_theta = 0 ∧
    delayed_phase_perturbation_step 1 (-1) delta_theta = 2 * delta_theta
equations.math_family: Coupled Delayed Kuramoto Somite Field
equations.variables: kappa_eff: effective linear restoring stiffness of in-phase synchronization (min^-1); Omega*tau_c: dimensionless delay phase product (rad)
equations.role: Establishes the linear stability boundary separating stable in-phase synchronization (cos(Omega*tau_c) > 0) from anti-phase checkerboard desynchronization (cos(Omega*tau_c) < 0)
equations.source_citation: Morelli et al. (2009) HFSP J. 3:55-66 Eqs. 4-5; Herrgen et al. (2010) Current Biology 20:1244-1253

equations.law_name: Riedel-Kruse (2007) Kuramoto Order Parameter, Anterior Limit of Defects (ALD) & Posterior Rescue Point (PRP) Law
equations.formula: R(t) = |(1/N)*sum_j exp(i*theta_j(t))|;  ALD(s_in) = s_in + Delta_n_ALD;  PRP(s_out) = s_out + Delta_n_PRP
equations.lean_code:
def anterior_limit_of_defects (s_in Delta_n_ALD : Nat) : Nat :=
  s_in + Delta_n_ALD
def posterior_rescue_point (s_out Delta_n_PRP : Nat) : Nat :=
  s_out + Delta_n_PRP
theorem riedel_2007_ald_prp_pulse_chase_window_invariance (s_in delta_s dapt_duration Delta_lag : Nat) :
    anterior_limit_of_defects (s_in + delta_s) Delta_lag =
      anterior_limit_of_defects s_in Delta_lag + delta_s ∧
    posterior_rescue_point (s_in + dapt_duration) Delta_lag -
      anterior_limit_of_defects s_in Delta_lag = dapt_duration
equations.math_family: Coupled Delayed Kuramoto Somite Field
equations.variables: R(t): Kuramoto phase coherence order parameter; s_in: somite stage of DAPT Notch blockade onset; s_out: somite stage of DAPT washout; ALD: Anterior Limit of Defects; PRP: Posterior Rescue Point
equations.role: Predicts the ~5.5-somite delay between DAPT Notch blockade and segmentation failure (ALD) and the ~5.5-somite recovery lag between DAPT washout and posterior segmentation rescue (PRP)
equations.source_citation: Riedel-Kruse et al. (2007) Science 317:1911-1915 Figs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Morelli (2009) Kinematic Phase-Wave Law for an Advected FGF8/Wnt Frequency Profile
equations.formula: omega(xi) = omega_0 * exp(-xi/lambda_F);  k(x) = (Omega/v) * (1 - omega(x)/omega_0);  N_w = (1/S) * Int_0^L (1 - omega/omega_0) dx
equations.lean_code:
def kinematic_phase_lag (Omega omega_eff dt : Int) : Int :=
  (Omega - omega_eff) * dt
theorem morelli_2009_kinematic_wave_phase_lag_law
    (Omega omega_1 omega_2 dt dt_1 dt_2 : Int) (h_omega : omega_1 ≤ omega_2) (h_dt : 0 ≤ dt) :
    kinematic_phase_lag Omega Omega dt = 0 ∧
    kinematic_phase_lag Omega omega_2 dt ≤ kinematic_phase_lag Omega omega_1 dt ∧
    kinematic_phase_lag Omega omega_1 dt_1 + kinematic_phase_lag Omega omega_1 dt_2 =
      kinematic_phase_lag Omega omega_1 (dt_1 + dt_2)
equations.math_family: Coupled Delayed Kuramoto Somite Field
equations.variables: omega(x): FGF8/Wnt-slaved autonomous frequency profile (rad/min); xi: distance from the tailbud (somite lengths); lambda_F: gradient decay length; v = S/T_seg: anterior cell flow speed; k(x): local phase wave number; N_w: number of kinematic waves across the PSM of length L
equations.role: Couples the delayed Kuramoto lattice to an advecting FGF8/Wnt frequency gradient so that posterior->anterior kinematic phase waves emerge, slow toward the determination front, and vanish for a uniform profile
equations.source_citation: Morelli et al. (2009) HFSP J. 3:55-66 (frequency profile & kinematic waves); Dubrulle et al. (2001) Cell 106:219-232 (FGF8 gradient); Soroldoni et al. (2014) Science 345:222-225 (wave kinematics)

equations.law_name: Itoh (2003) Mind bomb (Mib1) DeltaC Ubiquitination Coupling Gate
equations.formula: du/dt = k_ub*M*(1 - u) - k_endo*u;  u_ss = k_ub M/(k_ub M + k_endo);  kappa(t) = kappa_max*u(t)*g(t);  g = 1/(1 + (C_DAPT/IC50)^n)
equations.lean_code:
def mib1_ubiquitinated_numerator (k_ub M : Nat) : Nat :=
  k_ub * M
def mib1_ubiquitinated_denominator (k_ub k_endo M : Nat) : Nat :=
  k_ub * M + k_endo
theorem itoh_2003_mib1_ubiquitination_gate_monotone
    (k_ub k_endo M_1 M_2 : Nat) (h : M_1 ≤ M_2) :
    mib1_ubiquitinated_numerator k_ub 0 = 0 ∧
    mib1_ubiquitinated_numerator k_ub M_1 ≤ mib1_ubiquitinated_denominator k_ub k_endo M_1 ∧
    mib1_ubiquitinated_numerator k_ub M_1 * mib1_ubiquitinated_denominator k_ub k_endo M_2 ≤
      mib1_ubiquitinated_numerator k_ub M_2 * mib1_ubiquitinated_denominator k_ub k_endo M_1
equations.math_family: Coupled Delayed Kuramoto Somite Field
equations.variables: u: Mib1-ubiquitinated signalling-competent DeltaC fraction; M: Mib1 E3-ligase activity (1 WT, 0 mib^ta52b); k_ub, k_endo: ubiquitination and endocytic turnover rates (min^-1); g: gamma-secretase (DAPT) cleavage gate; kappa_max: coupling at full ubiquitination
equations.role: Makes the Delta-Notch coupling strength a dynamical variable: mib null abolishes coupling like DAPT, hypomorphs reduce kappa_eff monotonically, and coupling restoration after Mib1 induction or DAPT washout proceeds with finite kinetics
equations.source_citation: Itoh et al. (2003) Dev Cell 4:67-82; Riedel-Kruse et al. (2007) Science 317:1911-1915 (DAPT washout, mib/aei/des/bea mutants)

equations.law_name: Riedel-Kruse (2007) Emergent Defect-Span Law (ALD/PRP from R_crit crossings)
equations.formula: ALD = s_cross + Delta_n_det;  PRP = s_recross + Delta_n_det;  PRP - ALD = s_recross - s_cross
equations.lean_code:
def emergent_anterior_limit_of_defects (s_cross Delta_n_det : Nat) : Nat :=
  s_cross + Delta_n_det
def emergent_posterior_rescue_point (s_recross Delta_n_det : Nat) : Nat :=
  s_recross + Delta_n_det
theorem riedel_2007_emergent_defect_span_independent_of_determination_lag
    (s_cross s_recross Delta_n_det d : Nat) (h : s_cross ≤ s_recross) :
    emergent_posterior_rescue_point s_recross Delta_n_det -
      emergent_anterior_limit_of_defects s_cross Delta_n_det = s_recross - s_cross ∧
    s_cross ≤ emergent_anterior_limit_of_defects s_cross Delta_n_det ∧
    emergent_anterior_limit_of_defects s_cross (Delta_n_det + d) =
      emergent_anterior_limit_of_defects s_cross Delta_n_det + d ∧
    emergent_posterior_rescue_point s_recross (Delta_n_det + d) =
      emergent_posterior_rescue_point s_recross Delta_n_det + d
equations.math_family: Coupled Delayed Kuramoto Somite Field
equations.variables: s_cross: somite stage at which the determination-front lateral Kuramoto R first falls below R_crit; s_recross: stage at which it first recovers above R_crit after washout/restoration; Delta_n_det: determination-to-boundary maturation lag (2.5 somites)
equations.role: Replaces the hard-coded ALD = s_in + 5.5 / PRP = s_out + 5.5 of Pass 2 by an emergent read-out of the simulated coherence trajectory, whose defective span is independent of the maturation lag
equations.source_citation: Riedel-Kruse et al. (2007) Science 317:1911-1915 Figs. 2-4 (R_crit threshold model of ALD and PRP)

measurements.reference_source: Riedel-Kruse et al. (2007) Science 317:1911-1915 SOM & Morelli et al. (2009) HFSP J. 3:55-66 Eqs. 2-3 (collective period 22.18 min vs uncoupled 25.0 min)

measurements.name: effective in-phase linear stability stiffness kappa_eff = kappa * cos(Omega * tau_c)
measurements.method: linearized delayed Kuramoto stiffness kappa_eff = kappa*cos(Omega*tau_c) at tau_c=20.5 min (Omega*tau_c=5.808 rad) vs repulsive anti-phase delay tau_c=11.0 min (kappa_eff=-0.0353 min^-1)
measurements.reference_source: Morelli et al. (2009) HFSP J. 3:55-66 Eqs. 4-5 & Fig. 2 (in-phase synchronization stable iff kappa_eff = kappa*cos(Omega*tau_c) > 0)

measurements.name: Riedel-Kruse (2007) 5-regime emergent ALD/PRP vs observed Pearson r
measurements.method: correlation between emergent lattice ALD (WT, s_in=0, 4, 9) / PRP (pulse 0->9) and the observed values across 5 regimes, 5 seeds each; RMSE over the 4 perturbed regimes = 0.225 somites (max |err| 0.39)
measurements.reference_source: Riedel-Kruse, Müller & Oates (2007) Science 317:1911-1915 Figs. 2B, 3D & 4 (unit-slope ALD(s_in) = s_in + Delta_n_ALD; PRP after washout)

measurements.name: kinematic phase waves across the PSM N_w (simulated vs Morelli 2009 analytic)
measurements.method: unwrapped lateral-mean phase drop across the 6-somite-length PSM in the advected lattice with the FGF8/Wnt profile f_A=0.5 (analytic N_w = (1/S) Int (1 - c) dx = 1.609); uniform-profile control N_w = -0.025
measurements.reference_source: Morelli et al. (2009) HFSP J. 3:55-66 kinematic wave theory k = (Omega - omega(x))/v (Law 4); Soroldoni et al. (2014) Science 345:222-225 report ~1-2 waves across the zebrafish PSM

measurements.method: kappa(t) = kappa_max * u(t) * g(t) with u_ss(M) = k_ub M/(k_ub M + k_endo) (k_ub=0.08, k_endo=0.02 min^-1): M=0 gives u_ss=0.00, kappa_eff=0.0000; M=0.5 gives u_ss=0.67, kappa_eff=0.0504; WT late R=0.918

models.name: Runions et al. (2005) Leaf Venation Space-Colonization & Murray's Law
models.organism: Ginkgo biloba (open dichotomous venation) & angiosperm dicot lamina (reticulate venation)
models.math_family: Auxin Space-Colonization, Murray's Minimum-Work Vascular Law & Planar Dual Loop Nesting

equations.law_name: Murray (1926) / Price et al. (2013) Vascular Pipe-Model Conservation Law
equations.formula: r_parent^γ = ∑_{i ∈ children} r_i^γ,   r_root^γ = ∑_{leaf ∈ tips} r_leaf^γ
equations.lean_code:
def ObeysMurrayLaw (γ : Nat) : VeinTree → Prop
  | VeinTree.tip _ => True
  | VeinTree.fork r l right =>
      r ^ γ = (vein_root_radius l) ^ γ + (vein_root_radius right) ^ γ ∧
      ObeysMurrayLaw γ l ∧ ObeysMurrayLaw γ right
theorem murray_1926_tree_conservation (γ : Nat) (t : VeinTree) (h : ObeysMurrayLaw γ t) :
    (vein_root_radius t) ^ γ = sum_gamma_powers γ (vein_tip_radii t)
equations.math_family: Auxin Space-Colonization, Murray's Minimum-Work Vascular Law & Planar Dual Loop Nesting
equations.variables: r_parent, r_i: parent and daughter vein radii; γ ∈ [2, 3]: vascular scaling exponent (γ = 3 Murray cube law in minor veins -> γ = 2 Da Vinci area-preserving in major veins)
equations.role: Governs basipetal vascular radius accumulation and daughter/parent cross-sectional area ratios across Horton-Strahler orders 1-8
equations.source_citation: Murray (1926) PNAS 12:207; Runions et al. (2005) Sec. 3.5; Price, Knox & Brodribb (2013) PLoS ONE 8(12):e85420

equations.law_name: Runions et al. (2005) Eq. (2)-(3) Toussaint Relative Neighborhood Graph (RNG) Lune Law
equations.lean_code:
def in_rng_lune (d_vs d_us d_vu : Nat) : Prop := d_us < d_vs ∧ d_vu < d_vs
def rng_witness_excludes (d_vs d_us d_vu : Nat) : Bool := Nat.max d_us d_vu < d_vs
theorem runions_2005_rng_lune_iff (d_vs d_us d_vu : Nat) :
    rng_witness_excludes d_vs d_us d_vu = true ↔ in_rng_lune d_vs d_us d_vu := by
  simp [rng_witness_excludes, in_rng_lune, Nat.max_lt]
equations.math_family: Auxin Space-Colonization, Murray's Minimum-Work Vascular Law & Planar Dual Loop Nesting
equations.variables: s ∈ S: discrete auxin source; v ∈ V: vein node; V(s): Relative Neighborhood vein set; D: vein advance step; d_k: kill distance
equations.role: Attracts multiple surrounding vein tips toward a shared auxin source via empty-lune RNG neighborhoods to form closed anastomosing areole loops
equations.source_citation: Runions, Fuhrer, Lane, Federl, Rolland-Lagan & Prusinkiewicz (2005) ACM Trans. Graph. 24(3):702-711 Eq. (1)-(3)

equations.law_name: Euler-Poincaré Planar Areole Cycle Rank & Katifori (2012) Hierarchical Edge-Deletion Law
equations.lean_code:
def planar_cycle_count (edges vertices : Nat) : Nat := edges + 1 - vertices
theorem katifori_2012_tree_zero_cycles (n_edges : Nat) :
    planar_cycle_count n_edges (n_edges + 1) = 0 := by simp [planar_cycle_count]
theorem katifori_2012_edge_deletion_merges_areoles (n_edges k_bridges : Nat) (h : 1 ≤ k_bridges) :
    planar_cycle_count (n_edges + k_bridges - 1) (n_edges + 1) =
    planar_cycle_count (n_edges + k_bridges) (n_edges + 1) - 1
equations.math_family: Auxin Space-Colonization, Murray's Minimum-Work Vascular Law & Planar Dual Loop Nesting
equations.variables: V, E: planar vascular vertices and edges; L: enclosed areole count; r_j, s_j: merged subtree sizes in hierarchical loop decomposition; i_u: unweighted nesting number
equations.role: Separates open dichotomous venation (L = 0, e.g. Ginkgo biloba) from closed reticulate venation (L > 0) and quantifies hierarchical loop nesting
equations.source_citation: Katifori & Magnasco (2012) PLoS ONE 7(6):e37994; Ronellenfitsch et al. (2015) PLoS Comput. Biol. 11(12):e1004680

measurements.name: open Ginkgo venation anastomosing cycle count L = E - V + 1
measurements.method: Euler-Poincaré independent cycle rank E - V + 1 on open Voronoi space-colonization tree
measurements.reference_source: Runions et al. 2005 ACM Trans. Graph. 24(3):702-711 Sec. 3 (open venation tree)

measurements.name: Murray's cube law root-to-tip conservation ratio r_root^3 / (N_tips * r_tip^3)
measurements.method: ratio of petiole root cubic radius r_root^3 to sum of terminal veinlet cubic radii sum r_tip^3
measurements.reference_source: Murray 1926 PNAS 12:207 / Runions et al. 2005 Sec. 3.5 / Lean 4 theorem murray_1926_tree_conservation

measurements.name: open venation binary junction median daughter/parent area ratio (A_1 + A_2)/A_0
measurements.method: median (r_1^2 + r_2^2) / r_0^2 across binary bifurcations of the grown open venation tree
measurements.reference_source: Murray 1926 symmetric bifurcation 2^{1/3} = 1.2599 / Price et al. 2013 PLoS ONE e85420 Fig. 3

measurements.reference_source: Runions et al. 2005 ACM Trans. Graph. 24(3):702-711 Sec. 4 Eq. (2)-(3)

measurements.name: Horton-Strahler order 1 vs order 8 median area-ratio shift
measurements.method: decrease in median daughter/parent cross-sectional area ratio from terminal minor veins (order 1) to major midveins (order 8)
measurements.reference_source: Price, Knox & Brodribb 2013 PLoS ONE 8(12):e85420 Fig. 4 (order 1 median 1.25 -> order 8 median 1.01)
