models.name: Sapala et al. (2018) & Fu et al. (2005) ROP2-ROP6 interdigitated puzzle-shaped pavement cell lobing, Largest Empty Circle (LEC) turgor stress scaling, reduced pressurized periclinal membrane-shell and depth-resolved anticlinal wall buckling
models.organism: Arabidopsis thaliana (cotyledon & leaf epidermal pavement cells)
models.math_family: Coupled ROP2–ROP6 Cross-Inhibitory Cortical Reaction–Diffusion, Turgor-Driven Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Stress Scaling, Reduced Föppl Pressurized Periclinal Membrane-Shell & Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling

equations.law_name: Sapala et al. (2018) Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Turgor Stress Suppression Law
equations.formula: σ_max = P R_LEC / (2h);  R_LEC^2(WT) = R_0^2 ≪ R_iso^2(A) = A / π = N R_0^2  (for N ≥ 2 lobes)
equations.lean_code:
def puzzle_lec_radius_sq (r0_sq : Int) : Int := r0_sq
def isotropic_radius_sq (N r0_sq : Int) : Int := N * r0_sq
theorem sapala_2018_lec_stress_suppression (N r0_sq : Int)
    (hN : N ≥ 2) (hr0 : r0_sq > 0) :
    isotropic_radius_sq N r0_sq - puzzle_lec_radius_sq r0_sq = (N - 1) * r0_sq ∧
    2 * puzzle_lec_radius_sq r0_sq ≤ isotropic_radius_sq N r0_sq ∧
    puzzle_lec_radius_sq r0_sq < isotropic_radius_sq N r0_sq
equations.math_family: Coupled ROP2–ROP6 Cross-Inhibitory Cortical Reaction–Diffusion, Turgor-Driven Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Stress Scaling, Reduced Föppl Pressurized Periclinal Membrane-Shell & Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling
equations.variables: P: turgor pressure (MPa); h: outer periclinal cell wall thickness (um); R_LEC: radius of Largest Empty/Inscribed Circle inside cell contour (um); R_0: bounded neck half-width (um); N = A/(π R_0^2): effective lobe-unit area multiple
equations.role: Proves that puzzle-shaped interdigitation pins the Largest Empty Circle radius R_LEC near the neck half-width R_0 (~11 um) as cell area A grows 10-20x, suppressing outer periclinal wall tensile stress by >3x compared to unlobed isotropic cells
equations.source_citation: Sapala et al. (2018) eLife 7:e32794 Figs. 1-3 & Box 1

equations.law_name: Fu et al. (2005) ROP2–ROP6 Trans-Wall Complementarity & Intercellular Area Conservation Law
equations.formula: ∂U/∂t = D_u ∂²U/∂s² + (k_0 + k_a U²/(1+U²))/(1 + γ_{26} V²) (1 + α V_opp) - k_off U;  A_A(δ) + A_B(-δ) = A_0 + B_0
equations.lean_code:
def cell_A_lobe_area (A0 d_lobe : Int) : Int := A0 + d_lobe
def cell_B_neck_area (B0 d_lobe : Int) : Int := B0 - d_lobe
def cortical_rop_polarity (rop2 rop6 : Int) : Int := rop2 - rop6
theorem fu_2005_rop2_rop6_trans_wall_conservation (A0 B0 d_lobe r_hi r_lo : Int) :
    cell_A_lobe_area A0 d_lobe + cell_B_neck_area B0 d_lobe = A0 + B0 ∧
    cortical_rop_polarity r_hi r_lo + cortical_rop_polarity r_lo r_hi = 0
equations.math_family: Coupled ROP2–ROP6 Cross-Inhibitory Cortical Reaction–Diffusion, Turgor-Driven Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Stress Scaling, Reduced Föppl Pressurized Periclinal Membrane-Shell & Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling
equations.variables: U(s,t): active cortical ROP2-RIC4 concentration; V(s,t): active cortical ROP6-RIC1-KTN1 concentration; V_opp: opposing cell cortical ROP6 across shared anticlinal wall; δ_lobe: local anticlinal wall displacement
equations.role: Establishes alternating ROP2 (convex lobe outgrowth) and ROP6 (concave neck microtubule bundling) domains in antiphase across shared anticlinal walls while preserving contiguous epidermal tiling without intercellular gaps
equations.source_citation: Fu et al. (2005) Cell 120(5):687-700 Figs. 1-7; Bidhendi et al. (2019) Nature Plants 5:981-992

equations.law_name: Sapala et al. (2018) & Lin et al. (2013) ktn1 / rop2 rop4 Mutant Lobeyness & Solidity Collapse Law
equations.formula: L = P_perim / P_hull = (P_hull + k_rop A_lobe) / P_hull,  S = A_cell / (A_cell + k_rop A_indent)  ⇒  L(k_rop=0) = 1, S(k_rop=0) = 1
equations.lean_code:
def lobed_perimeter (P_hull k_rop A_lobe : Int) : Int := P_hull + k_rop * A_lobe
def lobed_hull_area (A_cell k_rop A_indent : Int) : Int := A_cell + k_rop * A_indent
theorem sapala_2018_mutant_lobeyness_collapse (P_hull A_cell k_rop A_lobe A_indent : Int)
    (hk : k_rop > 0) (hA : A_lobe > 0) :
    lobed_perimeter P_hull 0 A_lobe = P_hull ∧
    lobed_perimeter P_hull k_rop 0 = P_hull ∧
    lobed_hull_area A_cell 0 A_indent = A_cell ∧
    lobed_perimeter P_hull k_rop A_lobe > P_hull
equations.math_family: Coupled ROP2–ROP6 Cross-Inhibitory Cortical Reaction–Diffusion, Turgor-Driven Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Stress Scaling, Reduced Föppl Pressurized Periclinal Membrane-Shell & Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling
equations.variables: L = P_perim / P_hull: pavement cell lobeyness; S = A_cell / A_hull: convex solidity; k_rop: ROP2-ROP6-KTN1 mechanochemical coupling strength; A_lobe: sinusoidal lobe amplitude
equations.role: Proves that loss of ROP2/ROP4 or katanin KTN1/RIC1 microtubule severing collapses lobeyness to L -> 1 and solidity to S -> 1, causing unchecked R_LEC ~ sqrt(A/pi) growth and high periclinal wall tensile stress
equations.source_citation: Sapala et al. (2018) eLife 7:e32794 Fig. 5; Lin et al. (2013) Current Biology 23:290-297

equations.law_name: (Pass 3) Pressurized Periclinal Föppl Membrane & Inscribed-Disk Deflection Bound
equations.formula: -T ∇²z = P on Ω, z = 0 on ∂Ω;  T = T_0 + E h ε̄/(1-ν), ε̄ = ⟨½|∇z|²⟩, T_0 = P H/2;  disk: z(r) = P (R² - r²)/(4T);  z_max(Ω) ≥ P R_LEC²/(4T);  σ_m = T/h, σ_b = 6 T θ̄_edge ℓ_b / h², ℓ_b = sqrt(D/T)
equations.lean_code:
def disk_membrane_deflection_4T (P R_sq r_sq : Int) : Int := P * (R_sq - r_sq)
theorem sapala_2018_pressurized_membrane_inscribed_disk_bound (P R_sq r_sq N r0_sq : Int)
    (hP : 0 < P) (hr : 0 ≤ r_sq) (hrR : r_sq ≤ R_sq) (hN : N ≥ 2) (hr0 : 0 < r0_sq) :
    disk_membrane_deflection_4T P R_sq r_sq ≤ disk_membrane_deflection_4T P R_sq 0 ∧
    0 ≤ disk_membrane_deflection_4T P R_sq r_sq ∧
    disk_membrane_deflection_4T P (puzzle_lec_radius_sq r0_sq) 0 <
      disk_membrane_deflection_4T P (isotropic_radius_sq N r0_sq) 0
equations.math_family: Coupled ROP2–ROP6 Cross-Inhibitory Cortical Reaction–Diffusion, Turgor-Driven Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Stress Scaling, Reduced Föppl Pressurized Periclinal Membrane-Shell & Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling
equations.variables: z(x,y): out-of-plane bulge of the outer periclinal wall (um); T: uniform membrane tension (uN/um); T_0 = PH/2: pretension transmitted by the pressurised anticlinal walls of depth H; E, ν: wall Young's modulus and Poisson ratio; ε̄: mean membrane stretch; σ_m: membrane stress; σ_b: clamped-edge bending boundary-layer stress; ℓ_b: bending boundary-layer width; D = E h³/(12(1-ν²))
equations.role: Reduced (NOT finite-element) 3D periclinal shell: solved by sparse finite differences on the rasterised cell footprint with self-consistent tension and verified against the closed-form disk (z_max rel. err. < 1 %); used to TEST the Sapala et al. (2018) LEC stress proxy — shell stress tracks R_LEC (r = 0.98) but sub-linearly (fitted exponent ≈ 0.51 vs Laplace 1), giving an isotropic/WT stress ratio of ≈ 1.7 instead of the proxy's 3.32
equations.source_citation: Sapala et al. (2018) eLife 7:e32794 Fig. 3 & Box 1 (LEC stress proxy); Timoshenko & Woinowsky-Krieger (1959) Theory of Plates and Shells (uniformly loaded circular membrane)

equations.law_name: (Pass 3) Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling: Outward Monotonicity & Wavenumber Ordering
equations.formula: ∂²δ/∂s² + ∂²δ/∂ζ² = 0 on [0,L]×[0,H], δ(s,H) = δ_top(s), T_a ∂δ/∂ζ(s,0) = k_in δ(s,0);  δ̂_k(ζ) = δ̂_k(H) [k cosh(kζ) + β' sinh(kζ)]/[k cosh(kH) + β' sinh(kH)], β' = β/H;  discrete clamped mode δ_{j+2} = (2 + k²Δζ²) δ_{j+1} - δ_j, δ_0 = 0
equations.lean_code:
def depth_mode (κ a : Int) : Nat → Int
  | 0 => 0
  | 1 => a
  | n + 2 => (2 + κ) * depth_mode κ a (n + 1) - depth_mode κ a n
theorem anticlinal_depth_mode_monotone_outward (κ a : Int) (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∀ n : Nat, depth_mode κ a n < depth_mode κ a (n + 1) ∧ 0 < depth_mode κ a (n + 1)
theorem anticlinal_depth_mode_wavenumber_comparison (κ κ' a : Int)
    (hκ : 0 ≤ κ) (hκκ' : κ ≤ κ') (ha : 0 < a) :
    ∀ n : Nat, depth_mode κ a n ≤ depth_mode κ' a n ∧
      depth_mode κ a (n + 1) - depth_mode κ a n ≤ depth_mode κ' a (n + 1) - depth_mode κ' a n
equations.math_family: Coupled ROP2–ROP6 Cross-Inhibitory Cortical Reaction–Diffusion, Turgor-Driven Largest Empty Circle (LEC) Stress Scaling, Reduced Föppl Pressurized Periclinal Membrane-Shell & Depth-Resolved Anticlinal Wall Buckling
equations.variables: δ(s,ζ): lateral anticlinal wall deflection; s: arc length along the shared wall (L = 196 um); ζ: depth from inner (0) to outer (H) periclinal junction; δ_top(s): ROP2-ROP6 polarity-driven outer-face displacement; β = k_in H/T_a: dimensionless Robin stiffness of the inner face (0 = free, ∞ = clamped); κ = k²Δζ²: discrete squared wavenumber
equations.role: Resolves the Pass 2 anticlinal buckling with depth: under outer-junction forcing the k = 8 (24.5 um) lobe mode decays to 2.8 % of its outer amplitude at the inner face (β = 2, H = 15 um; e^-1 penetration 4 um), harmonics decay faster, and only depth-distributed forcing (ROP6-RIC1 microtubule bundles spanning the wall) keeps lobes through the full depth (inner/outer 0.70) — a model prediction verified against its analytic solution, not against a specimen
equations.source_citation: Fu et al. (2005) Cell 120:687-700; Bidhendi et al. (2019) Nature Plants 5:981-992; Armour et al. (2015) Plant Cell 27:2484-2500 (depth context)

models.name: Savin et al. (2011) discrete gut rod coupled to a finite-element (CST, St.Venant-Kirchhoff) dorsal-mesentery membrane with an apicobasal Pitx2 stiffness gradient
models.organism: Vertebrate midgut & dorsal mesentery (Gallus gallus, Coturnix japonica, Taeniopygia guttata, Mus musculus)
models.math_family: Discrete Elastic Rod Coupled to a Finite-Element (CST, St.Venant-Kirchhoff) Dorsal-Mesentery Membrane: Differential-Growth Buckling

equations.law_name: Savin et al. (2011) Differential Growth Strain & Surgical Mesentery Ablation Law
equations.formula: ε = (L_t - L_m) / L_m = L_t / L_m - 1;  ε = 0 ⇔ L_t = L_m (zero buckling force)
equations.lean_code:
def diff_growth_excess (L_t L_m : Int) : Int :=
  L_t - L_m
theorem savin_equal_growth_zero_strain (L : Int) :
    diff_growth_excess L L = 0 ∧
    ∀ dL : Nat, diff_growth_excess (L + Int.ofNat (dL + 1)) L = Int.ofNat (dL + 1)
equations.math_family: Discrete Elastic Rod Coupled to a Finite-Element (CST, St.Venant-Kirchhoff) Dorsal-Mesentery Membrane: Differential-Growth Buckling
equations.variables: L_t: relaxed intestinal tube length (mm); L_m: relaxed dorsal mesentery attachment length (mm); ε: differential growth strain
equations.role: Quantifies the compressive mechanical mismatch driving midgut looping and predicts complete uncoiling upon surgical mesentery dissection or zero differential growth
equations.source_citation: Savin et al. (2011) Nature 476:57-62 Fig. 1d-g & p. 58

equations.law_name: Savin et al. (2011) Cube-Law Wavelength & Loop Radius Scaling Law
equations.formula: U_tot(λ) = B_t / λ^2 + K_m λ  ⇒  ∂U_tot/∂λ = 0  ⇔  λ = c_λ (E_t I_t / (E_m h_m))^(1/3),  R = c_R (E_t I_t / (E_m h_m))^(1/3)
equations.lean_code:
def savin_euler_lagrange_residual (lam B_t K_m : Int) : Int :=
  K_m * (lam * lam * lam) - 2 * B_t
theorem savin_cube_law_stationarity (lam K_m : Int) :
    savin_euler_lagrange_residual lam (K_m * (lam * lam * lam)) (2 * K_m) = 0 := by
  simp [savin_euler_lagrange_residual, Int.mul_assoc, Int.mul_comm, Int.mul_left_comm]
equations.math_family: Discrete Elastic Rod Coupled to a Finite-Element (CST, St.Venant-Kirchhoff) Dorsal-Mesentery Membrane: Differential-Growth Buckling
equations.variables: λ: gut loop wavelength (mm); R: mean loop radius of curvature (mm); B_t = E_t I_t: gut rod bending stiffness; K_m = E_m h_m: mesenteric sheet tensile stiffness; ℓ_* = (E_t I_t / (E_m h_m))^(1/3)
equations.role: Predicts embryonic gut loop wavelength and radius across chick ontogeny (E8-E16) and across 4 vertebrate species (zebra finch, quail, chick, mouse) without free species-specific parameters
equations.source_citation: Savin et al. (2011) Nature 476:57-62 pp. 59-61, Figs. 3e-f & 4e-f

equations.law_name: Hollow Annular Gut Tube Area Moment of Inertia Factorization Law
equations.lean_code:
def savin_annular_inertia_scaled (R_t R_i : Int) : Int :=
  R_t * R_t * R_t * R_t - R_i * R_i * R_i * R_i
def savin_annular_inertia_factored (R_t R_i : Int) : Int :=
  (R_t - R_i) * (R_t + R_i) * (R_t * R_t + R_i * R_i)
theorem savin_annular_inertia_factorization (R_t R_i : Int) :
    savin_annular_inertia_scaled R_t R_i = savin_annular_inertia_factored R_t R_i ∧
    savin_annular_inertia_scaled 2 1 = 15 ∧
    savin_annular_inertia_scaled 3 1 = 80
equations.math_family: Discrete Elastic Rod Coupled to a Finite-Element (CST, St.Venant-Kirchhoff) Dorsal-Mesentery Membrane: Differential-Growth Buckling
equations.variables: R_t: outer gut tube radius (mm); R_i: inner lumen radius (mm); I_t: second moment of area (mm^4)
equations.role: Determines the quartic sensitivity of gut bending stiffness B_t = E_t I_t to outer and inner lumen radii during embryonic growth
equations.source_citation: Savin et al. (2011) Nature 476:57-62 p. 59 & Supplementary Information Sec. S2

equations.law_name: Apicobasal Pitx2 Stiffness Gradient Mean-Preservation Law (Pass 3 FE mesentery)
equations.formula: E_m(η) = E_m [1 + a (2η - 1)],  η ∈ [0,1] (dorsal root → gut edge);  E_m(η) + E_m(1-η) = 2 E_m  ⇒  ⟨E_m⟩ and ℓ_* independent of a
equations.lean_code:
def pitx2_stiffness_scaled (E0 a k n : Int) : Int :=
  E0 * (n + a * (2 * k - n))
theorem savin_pitx2_gradient_mean_preserving (E0 a k n : Int) :
    pitx2_stiffness_scaled E0 a k n + pitx2_stiffness_scaled E0 a (n - k) n = 2 * (E0 * n)
equations.math_family: Discrete Elastic Rod Coupled to a Finite-Element (CST, St.Venant-Kirchhoff) Dorsal-Mesentery Membrane: Differential-Growth Buckling
equations.variables: E_m: mean dorsal-mesentery Young's modulus (kPa); a: Pitx2 gradient amplitude (|a| < 1); η: apicobasal coordinate; k/n: discrete mesh level
equations.role: Defines the spatially varying membrane stiffness assigned to every constant-strain triangle of the FE mesentery mesh; guarantees that sweeping a changes only the spatial distribution (not the mean) of sheet stiffness, so the emergent dN/da is a genuine heterogeneity effect
equations.source_citation: Kurpios et al. (2008) PNAS 105:8499-8506 (Pitx2-dependent mesenchymal condensation of the dorsal mesentery; amplitude a is a modelling assumption)

equations.law_name: Fan-Mesentery Triangulation Euler-Characteristic Law (Pass 3 FE mesentery)
equations.formula: V = n_s n_w,  E = (n_s-1) n_w + n_s (n_w-1) + (n_s-1)(n_w-1),  F = 2 (n_s-1)(n_w-1)  ⇒  V - E + F = 1;  Ψ_e = μ_e tr(E²) + λ_e/2 tr(E)²,  E = (FᵀF - I)/2,  E_tot = Σ_e A_e h_m Ψ_e + Σ_i ½ (E_t A_t/ds_t)(|Δr_i| - ds_t)² + Σ_i ½ (B_t/ds_t³)|r_{i+1} - 2r_i + r_{i-1}|²
equations.lean_code:
def fan_mesh_vertices (ns nw : Nat) : Nat := ns * nw
def fan_mesh_triangles (ns nw : Nat) : Nat := 2 * ((ns - 1) * (nw - 1))
def fan_mesh_edges (ns nw : Nat) : Nat :=

      + fan_mesh_triangles (ns + 1) (nw + 1) = 1

equations.law_name: Schnakenberg (1979) Cubic Autocatalytic Equilibrium & Flux Conservation Law
equations.lean_code:
def schnakenberg_react_u (a u flux : Int) : Int := a - u + flux
def schnakenberg_react_v (b flux : Int) : Int := b - flux
theorem schnakenberg_equilibrium_zero_flux (a b u flux : Int) :
    schnakenberg_react_u a (a + b) b = 0 ∧
    schnakenberg_react_v b b = 0 ∧
    schnakenberg_react_u a u flux + schnakenberg_react_v b flux = a + b - u := by
  simp [schnakenberg_react_u, schnakenberg_react_v]
  omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Glycolytic Oscillations (Tri-Molecular Cubic Autocatalysis)
equations.variables: u: autocatalytic activator concentration; v: substrate/inhibitor concentration; a, b: dimensionless feed rates; γ: reaction-rate/area scale factor; d = D_v/D_u: diffusivity ratio
equations.role: Establishes the unique positive homogeneous equilibrium (u_*, v_*) = (a+b, b/(a+b)^2) with invariant cubic flux u_*^2 v_* = b and linear total mass balance R_u + R_v = a + b - u
equations.source_citation: Schnakenberg (1979) J. Theor. Biol. 81(3):389-400 Eqs. (15)-(20)

equations.law_name: Schnakenberg (1979) Exact Hopf Bifurcation Curve & Positive Jacobian Determinant Law
equations.lean_code:
def schnakenberg_scaled_trace (a b s_cubed : Int) : Int := (b - a) - s_cubed
def schnakenberg_jacobian_det (n : Nat) : Nat := n * n + 2 * n + 1
theorem schnakenberg_hopf_trace_and_det_pos (a s_cubed : Int) (n : Nat) :
    schnakenberg_scaled_trace a (a + s_cubed) s_cubed = 0 ∧
    schnakenberg_jacobian_det n ≥ 1 := by
  simp [schnakenberg_scaled_trace, schnakenberg_jacobian_det]
  omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Glycolytic Oscillations (Tri-Molecular Cubic Autocatalysis)
equations.variables: J_0: 2x2 reaction Jacobian at (u_*, v_*); s = a + b: equilibrium activator concentration; tr(J_0): Jacobian trace; det(J_0): Jacobian determinant
equations.role: Separates stable steady states from autonomous Poincaré-Bendixson limit-cycle oscillations across b - a = (a + b)^3 while proving det(J_0) = (a + b)^2 > 0 excludes fold bifurcations
equations.source_citation: Schnakenberg (1979) J. Theor. Biol. 81(3):389-400 Eqs. (21)-(24)

equations.law_name: Schnakenberg-Turing Differential-Diffusion Dispersion & Critical Ratio Law
equations.lean_code:
def schnakenberg_equal_diff_det (q : Nat) : Nat := q * q + 2 * q + 100
def schnakenberg_fourier_det (d q : Int) : Int := d * q * q - (8 * d - 10) * q + 100
theorem schnakenberg_turing_instability_and_equal_diff (q : Nat) :
    schnakenberg_equal_diff_det q ≥ 100 ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 1 0 = 100 ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 9 3 = -5 ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 18 4 = -148 := by
  refine ⟨?_, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  simp [schnakenberg_equal_diff_det]
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Glycolytic Oscillations (Tri-Molecular Cubic Autocatalysis)
equations.variables: q = k^2: squared spatial wavenumber; d = D_v/D_u: substrate-to-activator diffusivity ratio; d_c: critical Turing diffusivity ratio
equations.role: Proves equal diffusion (d = 1) is unconditionally stable at (a,b) = (0.1, 0.9) whereas d > d_c ≈ 8.5676 drives det(J(k^2)) < 0 and amplifies periodic Turing spots/stripes
equations.source_citation: Schnakenberg (1979) J. Theor. Biol. 81:389-400 & Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72

equations.law_name: Laplace–Beltrami Spherical-Harmonic Ladder & Finite Turing Band on a Hemispherical Mound (Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def sphere_laplace_eigenvalue (l : Nat) : Nat := l * (l + 1)
theorem schnakenberg_sphere_turing_band :
    sphere_laplace_eigenvalue 0 = 0 ∧
    (∀ l : Nat, sphere_laplace_eigenvalue (l + 1) = sphere_laplace_eigenvalue l + 2 * (l + 1)) ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 18 (sphere_laplace_eigenvalue 0) = 100 ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 18 (sphere_laplace_eigenvalue 1) = -96 ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 18 (sphere_laplace_eigenvalue 2) = -56 ∧
    schnakenberg_fourier_det 18 (sphere_laplace_eigenvalue 3) = 1084 := by
  refine ⟨rfl, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  intro l
  simp only [sphere_laplace_eigenvalue, Nat.mul_add, Nat.add_mul, Nat.mul_one, Nat.one_mul]
  omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Glycolytic Oscillations (Tri-Molecular Cubic Autocatalysis)
equations.variables: l: spherical-harmonic degree; R: mound radius; q_l = l(l+1)/R^2: Laplace–Beltrami eigenvalue replacing the planar k^2; q_+: upper edge of the planar Turing band; R_min: critical mound radius
equations.role: On a hemispherical Dictyostelium mound (no-flux equator) only finitely many spherical-harmonic degrees fall inside the Turing band; mound size selects the fastest-growing degree l*(R) and mounds smaller than R_min stay homogeneous — verified numerically by simulate_schnakenberg_hemisphere and the mound-radius sweep
equations.source_citation: Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72 (spherical case) & Schnakenberg (1979) kinetics; Crampin, Gaffney & Maini (1999) Bull. Math. Biol. 61:1093-1120 for the growing-stalk companion solver

equations.law_name: Extracellular Phosphodiesterase Degradation Shifts the Schnakenberg Hopf Curve (Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace (a b kappa1 s_cubed : Int) : Int :=
  kappa1 * kappa1 * kappa1 * (b - a) - s_cubed
theorem schnakenberg_pde_hopf_shift (a m kappa1 : Int) :
    schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace a (a + m) kappa1 (kappa1 * kappa1 * kappa1 * m) = 0 ∧
    schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace a (a + m) 1 m = 0 ∧
    schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace 1 9 1 1000 = -992 ∧
    schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace 1 9 5 1000 = 0 ∧
    schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace 1 9 6 1000 = 728 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · have h : a + m - a = m := by omega
    simp only [schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace, h, Int.sub_self]
  · simp only [schnakenberg_pde_scaled_trace]
    omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion & Glycolytic Oscillations (Tri-Molecular Cubic Autocatalysis)
equations.variables: κ = k_PDE/k_-1: first-order extracellular phosphodiesterase rate relative to Schnakenberg's X→A decay; k_e, K_m: Michaelis–Menten PDE rate and constant; s = a + b
equations.role: Extracellular cAMP phosphodiesterase moves the Hopf boundary — at fixed feed rates increasing PDE degradation destabilizes the focus into autonomous relaxation oscillations (κ = 4 is exactly Hopf at (a,b) = (1,9)); compared in the script against the 3-variable Martiel–Goldbeter (1987) cAMP relay with its own PDE rate k_e
equations.source_citation: Schnakenberg (1979) J. Theor. Biol. 81:389-400 Eq. (24) generalized; Martiel & Goldbeter (1987) Biophys. J. 52:807-828 (doi:10.1016/S0006-3495(87)83275-7); Gerisch & Hess (1974) PNAS 71:2118-2122 (doi:10.1073/pnas.71.5.2118)

models.math_family: 2D Gierer–Meinhardt Activator–Inhibitor Reaction–Diffusion on Curved Wing Geometry with Anisotropic Vein-Directed Diffusivity ∇·(D ∇u) and Distal-to-Proximal Boundary Gradient Switching Across Batesian Mimicry Morphs

equations.law_name: Gierer–Meinhardt Homogeneous Steady State (v₀ = u₀²) & Turing Diffusion-Driven Instability Law
equations.formula: f(u₀, v₀) = a - b u₀ + u₀²/v₀ = 0,  g(u₀, v₀) = u₀² - v₀ = 0  ⇒  u₀ = (a + 1)/b,  v₀ = u₀²,  tr(J₀) = f_u + g_v < 0,  d f_u + g_v > 0
equations.lean_code:
def gm_steady_residual_scaled (a b : Int) : Int :=
  a * b - b * (a + 1) + b
def gm_trace_scaled (a b : Int) : Int :=
  b * (10 - a) - (a + 10)
def gm_turing_drive_scaled (d a b : Int) : Int :=
  d * b * (10 - a) - (a + 10)
theorem gierer_meinhardt_steady_state_and_turing_instability (a b : Int) :
    gm_steady_residual_scaled a b = 0 ∧
    gm_trace_scaled 1 1 < 0 ∧
    gm_turing_drive_scaled 1 1 1 < 0 ∧
    gm_turing_drive_scaled 40 1 1 > 0
equations.math_family: 2D Gierer–Meinhardt Activator–Inhibitor Reaction–Diffusion on Curved Wing Geometry with Anisotropic Vein-Directed Diffusivity ∇·(D ∇u) and Distal-to-Proximal Boundary Gradient Switching Across Batesian Mimicry Morphs
equations.variables: u₀, v₀: homogeneous steady-state activator and inhibitor concentrations; a, b: Gierer–Meinhardt activator source and linear decay rates; d = D_v / D_u: inhibitor-to-activator diffusivity ratio
equations.role: Establishes the unique positive homogeneous steady state v₀ = u₀² = ((a+1)/b)² of the Gierer–Meinhardt kinetics, linear stability in the absence of diffusion (tr(J₀) < 0, d = 1), and diffusion-driven Turing instability (d f_u + g_v > 0) for d = 40
equations.source_citation: Sekimura et al. (2000) Proc. R. Soc. B 267:851-859 Eqs. (2.1)-(2.4); Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) Kybernetik 12:30-39

equations.law_name: Anisotropic Vein-Directed Diffusivity Mode Selection (Stripes vs Transverse Bands)
equations.lean_code:
def anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled (m n eps_scaled : Int) : Int :=
  100 * m * m + eps_scaled * n * n
theorem anisotropic_vein_mode_selection_switch (eps_low eps_high : Int)
    (h_low : eps_low < 100) (h_high : eps_high > 100) :
    anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled 0 1 eps_low < anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled 1 0 eps_low ∧
    anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled 1 0 eps_high < anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled 0 1 eps_high ∧
    anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled 0 1 100 = anisotropic_rayleigh_scaled 1 0 100
equations.math_family: 2D Gierer–Meinhardt Activator–Inhibitor Reaction–Diffusion on Curved Wing Geometry with Anisotropic Vein-Directed Diffusivity ∇·(D ∇u) and Distal-to-Proximal Boundary Gradient Switching Across Batesian Mimicry Morphs
equations.variables: ε = D_⊥ / D_∥: transverse-to-vein-parallel diffusivity ratio; (m, n): longitudinal and transverse eigenmode wavenumbers; Λ(m, n; ε): anisotropic elliptic operator Rayleigh quotient
equations.role: Proves that vein-aligned diffusivity (ε < 1) lowers the effective wavenumber of transverse-varying modes (0, 1) to select longitudinal vein-parallel stripes, whereas ε > 1 reverses mode ordering to select anteroposterior transverse bands (f. planemoides)
equations.source_citation: Sekimura et al. (2000) Proc. R. Soc. B 267:851-859 Section 2(b), Table 1 & Figs. 3-6; Madzvamuse et al. (2002) J. Math. Biol. 44:489-509

equations.law_name: Monotonic Melanic Wing Area Expansion Across engrailed Mimicry Thresholds
equations.formula: u_th1 ≤ u_th2  ⇒  I(u(x) > u_th2) ≤ I(u(x) > u_th1)  ∀ x ∈ Ω  ⇒  f_black(hippocoonides) < f_black(trophonius) < f_black(cenea)
equations.lean_code:
def is_melanic (u_x u_th : Int) : Int :=
  if u_x > u_th then 1 else 0
def wing_melanic_count_3pt (u_th : Int) : Int :=
  is_melanic 98 u_th + is_melanic 108 u_th + is_melanic 118 u_th
theorem monotonic_melanic_wing_expansion (u_x u_th1 u_th2 : Int)
    (h_order : u_th1 <= u_th2) :
    is_melanic u_x u_th2 <= is_melanic u_x u_th1 ∧

theorem sharon_negative_gaussian_curvature (g_yy_xx : Int) :
    marginal_metric_gaussian_curvature_lead 0 = 0 ∧
    (∀ c : Nat, marginal_metric_gaussian_curvature_lead ((c : Int) + 1) < 0) ∧
    marginal_metric_gaussian_curvature_lead (-g_yy_xx) = g_yy_xx
equations.math_family: Non-Euclidean Föppl–von Kármán Thin-Sheet Elasticity, Negative Gaussian Curvature (K < 0) & Self-Similar Multi-Generation Edge Buckling Cascades
equations.variables: K(x): intrinsic Gaussian curvature of the leaf margin metric (mm^-2); g''_yy(x): second transverse derivative of target metric; ℓ: boundary decay length (mm)
equations.role: Establishes by Gauss's Theorema Egregium that any convexly decaying marginal growth profile (g''_yy(x) > 0) induces strictly negative Gaussian curvature K(x) < 0 near the free edge, forcing out-of-plane hyperbolic buckling
equations.source_citation: Sharon et al. (2002) Nature 419:579-580; Liang & Mahadevan (2009) PNAS 106(52):22049-22054

equations.law_name: Self-Similar Multi-Generation Sub-Harmonic Wavelength Cascade & Linear Boundary Scaling Law
equations.formula: λ_m / λ_{m+1} = r_cascade ∈ [3, 5],  x_m ∝ λ_m,  λ_loc(x) = c_λ x + λ_min(t)
equations.lean_code:
def cascade_next_wavelength (r_cascade lam_m : Int) : Int :=
  r_cascade * lam_m
def local_edge_wavelength (c_lam x lam_min : Int) : Int :=
  c_lam * x + lam_min
theorem audoly_self_similar_cascade_scaling (r_cascade lam_m c_lam lam_min : Int) :
    local_edge_wavelength c_lam 0 lam_min = lam_min ∧
    cascade_next_wavelength r_cascade (cascade_next_wavelength r_cascade lam_m) =
      (r_cascade * r_cascade) * lam_m ∧
    (∀ r l : Nat, ((l : Int) + 1) < cascade_next_wavelength ((r : Int) + 2) ((l : Int) + 1))
equations.math_family: Non-Euclidean Föppl–von Kármán Thin-Sheet Elasticity, Negative Gaussian Curvature (K < 0) & Self-Similar Multi-Generation Edge Buckling Cascades
equations.variables: r_cascade: sub-harmonic period-multiplying cascade ratio; λ_m: generation-m wavelength (mm); x: inward distance from the free leaf margin (mm); λ_min(t): finite-thickness cutoff wavelength (mm)
equations.role: Proves multiplicative self-similar wavelength coarsening across buckling generations and linear growth of dominant wavelength with inward distance x from the leaf margin above the thickness cutoff λ_min ∝ t
equations.source_citation: Audoly & Boudaoud (2003) Phys. Rev. Lett. 91(8):086105; Sharon et al. (2002) Nature 419:579-580

equations.law_name: CIN/TCP-Arrested, Auxin-Boosted Marginal Growth Increment & Non-Negative Developmental Excess Metric (Pass 3)
equations.formula: dΓ_int/dt = γ_0 (1 - m),  dΓ_mar/dt = γ_0 (1 - m)(1 + β a/a_ref),  m(y,t) = σ((v_tcp t - (L - y))/w),  g_0(y,t) = ((1+Γ_mar)/(1+Γ_int))^2 - 1 ≥ 0,  m = 1 ⇒ dΓ = 0
equations.lean_code:
def marginal_growth_increment (gamma0 m_rem a_boost : Nat) : Nat :=
  gamma0 * m_rem * a_boost
theorem tcp_arrested_marginal_growth_increment (gamma0 a_boost G : Nat) :
    marginal_growth_increment gamma0 0 a_boost = 0 ∧
    (∀ m1 m2 : Nat, m1 ≤ m2 →
      marginal_growth_increment gamma0 m1 a_boost ≤ marginal_growth_increment gamma0 m2 a_boost) ∧
    (∀ m_rem R b : Nat,
      marginal_growth_increment gamma0 m_rem R ≤ marginal_growth_increment gamma0 m_rem (R + b)) ∧
    (∀ m_rem : Nat, G ≤ G + marginal_growth_increment gamma0 m_rem a_boost)
def excess_metric_numerator (g_mar g_int : Nat) : Int :=
  ((1 + g_mar) * (1 + g_mar) : Nat) - ((1 + g_int) * (1 + g_int) : Nat)
theorem developmental_excess_metric_nonneg (g_mar g_int : Nat) (h : g_int ≤ g_mar) :
    0 ≤ excess_metric_numerator g_mar g_int ∧ excess_metric_numerator g_int g_int = 0
equations.math_family: Non-Euclidean Föppl–von Kármán Thin-Sheet Elasticity, Negative Gaussian Curvature (K < 0) & Self-Similar Multi-Generation Edge Buckling Cascades
equations.variables: m(y,t): CIN/TCP maturation (growth-arrest) field in [0,1] sweeping basipetally at speed v_tcp (mm/h); Γ_int, Γ_mar: interior and marginal growth strains; a: auxin level (a.u.); β: auxin growth boost; g_0(y,t): excess metric handed to the Föppl-von Kármán solver
equations.role: Proves that TCP maturation arrests marginal growth, that a slower cin arrest front never yields less growth (excess marginal growth and K < 0 in cin), that the auxin boost keeps margin growth ≥ interior growth so the developmental excess metric g_0 is non-negative and reduces exactly to the flat Euclidean control when β a = 0
equations.source_citation: Nath, Crawford, Carpenter & Coen (2003) Science 299:1404-1407; Palatnik et al. (2003) Nature 425:257-263; Efroni et al. (2008) Plant Cell 20:2293-2306; Sharon et al. (2002) Nature 419:579-580

equations.law_name: PIN1 Up-the-Gradient Pairwise Auxin Transport Mass Conservation (Pass 3)
equations.formula: J_{i→j} = T p_i a_i exp(κ a_j) / Σ_k exp(κ a_k),  p_i = p_max c_i/(c_half + c_i),  net_{ij} = J_{i→j} - J_{j→i} = -net_{ji},  Σ_i da_i|_transport = 0
equations.lean_code:
def pin_pairwise_net_flux (f_ij f_ji : Int) : Int :=
  f_ij - f_ji
theorem pin_pairwise_transport_mass_conservation (a_i a_j f_ij f_ji : Int) :
    pin_pairwise_net_flux f_ij f_ji + pin_pairwise_net_flux f_ji f_ij = 0 ∧
    (a_i - pin_pairwise_net_flux f_ij f_ji) + (a_j + pin_pairwise_net_flux f_ij f_ji) = a_i + a_j ∧
    pin_pairwise_net_flux f_ij f_ij = 0
equations.math_family: Non-Euclidean Föppl–von Kármán Thin-Sheet Elasticity, Negative Gaussian Curvature (K < 0) & Self-Similar Multi-Generation Edge Buckling Cascades
equations.variables: a_i: auxin in cell i; p_i: CUC2-gated PIN1 level; T: transport rate; κ: up-the-gradient polarisation strength; J_{i→j}: PIN1-mediated efflux from i to j
equations.role: Establishes that the PIN1 up-the-gradient exchange used to generate auxin convergence maxima (serration tips) is antisymmetric and conserves the two-cell auxin total, hence total lattice auxin changes only through production, decay and growth dilution

equations.law_name: Turing Equal-Diffusion Negative Control (No Digit Patterning for D_u = D_v)
equations.lean_code:
def modal_trace_eq_diff (tr_J0 Dq : Int) : Int := tr_J0 - 2 * Dq
def modal_det_eq_diff (det_J0 neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq : Int) : Int :=
  det_J0 + neg_tr_Dq + Dq_sq
theorem sheth_turing_equal_diffusion_no_instability (tr_J0 det_J0 Dq neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq : Int)
    (htr : tr_J0 < 0) (hdet : det_J0 > 0)
    (hDq : Dq ≥ 0) (hterm : neg_tr_Dq ≥ 0) (hsq : Dq_sq ≥ 0) :
    modal_trace_eq_diff tr_J0 Dq < 0 ∧ modal_det_eq_diff det_J0 neg_tr_Dq Dq_sq > 0 := by
  unfold modal_trace_eq_diff modal_det_eq_diff; omega
equations.math_family: Hox-Modulated Turing Wavelength
equations.variables: tr(J_0) = f_u + g_v: homogeneous Jacobian trace; det(J_0) = f_u g_v - f_v g_u: homogeneous Jacobian determinant; Dq = D k^2: scaled diffusion wavenumber
equations.role: Proves that equal activator and inhibitor diffusivities abolish Turing instability across all spatial wavenumbers, serving as the formal negative control
equations.source_citation: Sheth et al. (2012) Science 338(6113):1476-1480 Fig. 3 & Suppl. Eqs. (S1)-(S4); Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37-72

equations.law_name: Distal Hox/Gli3 Dose Monotonic Wavenumber Scaling & Allelic Series (5 -> 14 Digits)
equations.lean_code:
def sheth_trace_J0 (fu : Int) : Int := fu - 200
def sheth_kc_sq (fu : Int) : Int := fu - 2
theorem sheth_hox_dose_monotonic_wavenumber_and_allelic_series (fu1 fu2 : Int)
    (h12 : fu1 < fu2) (h2 : fu2 < 200) :
    sheth_kc_sq fu1 < sheth_kc_sq fu2 ∧
    sheth_trace_J0 fu2 < 0 ∧
    sheth_kc_sq 27 = 5 * 5 ∧
    sheth_kc_sq 51 = 7 * 7 ∧
    sheth_kc_sq 83 = 9 * 9 ∧
    sheth_kc_sq 123 = 11 * 11 ∧
    sheth_kc_sq 198 = 14 * 14 := by
  unfold sheth_kc_sq sheth_trace_J0; omega
equations.math_family: Hox-Modulated Turing Wavelength
equations.variables: H ∈ [0, 1]: normalized distal Hoxa13 + Hoxd11-13 gene dose in Gli3-null series; f_u(H): activator self-activation rate; k_c(H): critical Turing wavenumber; N_digits = L / λ(H) = k_c(H)
equations.role: Proves that progressive genetic removal of distal Hox genes and Gli3 monotonically increases k_c^2(H), shrinking digit stripe wavelength λ(H) and increasing digit number from 5 (WT) -> 7 (Gli3-/-) -> 9 (Hoxd11-13-/-;Gli3-/-) -> 11 -> 14 (triple null) without changing autopod width L

equations.law_name: Fan-Shaped Limb Bud Proximodistal Arc Expansion & Distal Digit Mode Selection
equations.lean_code:
def in_fan_autopod_band (k_min_sq k_max_sq m r : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (k_min_sq * r * r ≤ m * m ∧ m * m ≤ k_max_sq * r * r)
theorem sheth_fan_autopod_proximodistal_mode_selection :
    in_fan_autopod_band 2 4 2 1 = true ∧
    in_fan_autopod_band 2 4 5 1 = false ∧
    in_fan_autopod_band 2 4 9 1 = false ∧
    in_fan_autopod_band 2 4 5 3 = true := by decide

equations.variables: r: proximodistal radial coordinate on the fan-shaped limb bud; m: angular digit ray mode number; [k_-^2, k_+^2]: local Turing unstable wavenumber band
equations.role: Proves why the narrow proximal zeugopod (r=1) supports only 2 skeletal condensations (radius/ulna) while excluding 5-to-14 digit modes, whereas the expanded distal autopod fan (r=3) admits the Hox-tuned digit rays
equations.source_citation: Sheth et al. (2012) Science 338(6113):1476-1480 Fig. 3D-F & Fig. 4; Newman & Frisch (1979) Science 205:662-668

equations.law_name: Digit Number = Autopod Width / Turing Wavelength on an AER-Grown Autopod (Pass 3)
equations.lean_code:
def digit_wavelengths (L lam : Nat) : Nat := L / lam
theorem sheth_growing_autopod_digit_number_law (L1 L2 L lam1 lam2 : Nat)
    (hL : L1 ≤ L2) (hlam : lam1 ≤ lam2) (hpos : 0 < lam1) :
    digit_wavelengths L1 lam1 ≤ digit_wavelengths L2 lam1 ∧
    digit_wavelengths L lam2 ≤ digit_wavelengths L lam1 ∧
    digit_wavelengths 2500 500 = 5 ∧
    digit_wavelengths 2500 357 = 7 ∧
    digit_wavelengths 2500 178 = 14 ∧
    digit_wavelengths 1365 500 = 2 := by
  unfold digit_wavelengths
  exact ⟨Nat.div_le_div_right hL, Nat.div_le_div_left hlam hpos, rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl⟩
equations.math_family: Hox-Modulated Turing Wavelength
equations.variables: L = Θ R(T) · 2500/(2π) um: final distal autopod arc set by AER-FGF8 outgrowth (R(T) from dR/dt = v(R,t)); λ(H) = 2500/k_c(H) um: Hox-tuned Turing wavelength; N: number of digit wavelengths on the rim
equations.role: Separates the two control axes of digit number on the growing autopod: AER-driven width (ablation / g_max sweep, Summerbell 1974) and Hox-driven wavelength (Sheth 2012 allelic series); the numerical growing-fan solver reports N_grow against this quasi-static law (slope < 1 = growth-induced wavelength lag)
equations.source_citation: Sheth et al. (2012) Science 338(6113):1476-1480 Figs. 2-3; Summerbell (1974) J Embryol Exp Morphol 32:651-660; Kondo & Miura (2010) Science 329:1616-1620

equations.law_name: Growth-Dilution Shift of the Turing Modal Eigenvalue on a Growing Domain (Pass 3)
equations.formula: u_t + v·∇u + (∇·v) u = D∇²u + f(u)  ⟹  J_k → J_k − g I,  σ_g(k) = σ(k) − g;  g < σ ⟹ σ_g > 0;  g ≥ σ ⟹ σ_g ≤ 0;  g = 0 (AER regression) ⟹ σ_g = σ;  449 − 195 > 0 (σ_max = 4.49, g_rim = 1.95)
equations.lean_code:
def dilution_shifted_eigenvalue (sigma g : Int) : Int := sigma - g
theorem sheth_growth_dilution_turing_threshold (sigma g : Int) :
    (g < sigma → dilution_shifted_eigenvalue sigma g > 0) ∧
    (g ≥ sigma → dilution_shifted_eigenvalue sigma g ≤ 0) ∧
    dilution_shifted_eigenvalue sigma 0 = sigma ∧
    dilution_shifted_eigenvalue 449 195 > 0 ∧
    dilution_shifted_eigenvalue 449 500 < 0 := by
  unfold dilution_shifted_eigenvalue; omega
equations.math_family: Hox-Modulated Turing Wavelength
equations.variables: g(r,t) = g_max A(t) exp(−(R−r)/l_F): AER-FGF8 kinematic area dilation rate (∇·v = g); σ(k): fixed-domain modal growth rate; σ_g(k): modal growth rate on the growing domain
equations.role: Formalizes the dilution term of the growing-domain reaction-diffusion equations: digits can condense during AER outgrowth only while σ_max exceeds the rim dilation rate, and AER regression (g → 0) restores the full Turing rate — the mechanism behind the sequential digit emergence kymograph (Panel K)

models.name: Hannezo et al. (2011) PRL & Shyer et al. (2013) Science sequential smooth-muscle mucosal buckling into ridges, zigzags, and hexagonal villi
models.organism: Vertebrate embryonic gut mucosa (Gallus gallus, Coturnix japonica, Mus musculus)
models.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán / Neo-Hookean Sequential Smooth-Muscle Mucosal Buckling (Ridges -> Zigzags -> Hexagonal Villi & Crypts)

equations.law_name: Hannezo–Shyer Mucosal Plate-on-Foundation Quartic Wavenumber Stationarity Law
equations.lean_code:
def mucosal_wavenumber_residual (q B_e K_s : Int) : Int :=
  B_e * (q * q * q * q) - K_s
def mucosal_critical_load_scaled (q B_e K_s : Int) : Int :=
  B_e * (q * q * q * q) + K_s
theorem hannezo_shyer_wavenumber_stationarity (q B_e : Int) :
    mucosal_wavenumber_residual q B_e (B_e * (q * q * q * q)) = 0 ∧
    mucosal_critical_load_scaled q B_e (B_e * (q * q * q * q)) = 2 * (B_e * (q * q * q * q))
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán / Neo-Hookean Sequential Smooth-Muscle Mucosal Buckling (Ridges -> Zigzags -> Hexagonal Villi & Crypts)
equations.variables: B_e = E_e h_e^3 / (12(1 - ν^2)): mucosal bending rigidity; K_s = E_s / H_s: mesenchymal Winkler foundation stiffness; q_*: critical buckling wavenumber; λ_*: characteristic mucosal folding wavelength
equations.role: Determines the characteristic buckling wavelength λ_* and critical compressive threshold N_c across embryonic stages (E8-E18) and vertebrate species (chick, quail, mouse)
equations.source_citation: Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2011) Phys. Rev. Lett. 107:078104 Eqs. (8)-(10); Shyer et al. (2013) Science 342:212-218 p. 214 & Supplementary Text

equations.law_name: Shyer et al. (2013) Sequential Smooth-Muscle Buckling & FK506 Ablation Hierarchy
equations.formula: Regime(Δε_x, Δε_y, α_3) = 0 (smooth, Δε_x ≤ 0) < 1 (1D ridges, Δε_x > 0, Δε_y ≤ 0) < 2 (2D zigzags, Δε_x > 0, Δε_y > 0, α_3 ≤ 0) < 3 (hexagonal villi, Δε_x > 0, Δε_y > 0, α_3 > 0)
equations.lean_code:
def shyer_buckling_regime (dex dey alpha3 : Nat) : Nat :=
  if dex == 0 then 0
  else if dey == 0 then 1
  else if alpha3 == 0 then 2
  else 3
theorem shyer_sequential_buckling_and_fk506_arrest (ex ey a3 : Nat) :
    shyer_buckling_regime 0 0 0 = 0 ∧
    shyer_buckling_regime (ex + 1) 0 0 = 1 ∧
    shyer_buckling_regime (ex + 1) (ey + 1) 0 = 2 ∧
    shyer_buckling_regime (ex + 1) (ey + 1) (a3 + 1) = 3
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán / Neo-Hookean Sequential Smooth-Muscle Mucosal Buckling (Ridges -> Zigzags -> Hexagonal Villi & Crypts)
equations.variables: Δε_x = ε_x - ε_{c,1}: circumferential smooth-muscle strain excess; Δε_y = ε_y - ε_{c,2}: longitudinal smooth-muscle strain excess; α_3: apicobasal lumen-stroma cubic asymmetry
equations.role: Governs the sequential E6 -> E8/E10 -> E13/E14 -> E16 morphological cascade and predicts the exact arrest phenotype under stage-specific FK506 smooth-muscle inhibition or surgical slitting
equations.source_citation: Shyer et al. (2013) Science 342:212-218 Figs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Hexagonal Villi Triad Wavevector Closure & Cubic Asymmetry Selection Law
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán / Neo-Hookean Sequential Smooth-Muscle Mucosal Buckling (Ridges -> Zigzags -> Hexagonal Villi & Crypts)
equations.variables: q_1, q_2, q_3: resonant hexagonal wavevector triad at 120° separation; α_3: apicobasal asymmetry coefficient; A: hexagonal mode amplitude
equations.role: Explains why biaxial compression combined with apicobasal polarity/stiffness asymmetry stabilizes a 6-fold hexagonal array of protruding villi and basal crypt invaginations
equations.source_citation: Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2011) Phys. Rev. Lett. 107:078104 p. 3; Shyer et al. (2013) Science 342:212-218 Fig. 4

equations.law_name: Tubular Circumferential Mode Quantisation on the Gut Tube (Pass 3 reduced 3D coupling)
equations.formula: K_eff = (E_s/H_s) · f_curv · f_pre,  f_curv = K_tube/K_slab (axisymmetric ring FEM = Lamé u = A r + B/r),  λ_tube = c_tube · 2π (B_e/K_eff)^(1/4),  n = round(2πR/λ_tube),  n · λ_n + (2πR mod n) = 2πR,  γ_Donnell = (E_e h_e / R²) / K_eff
equations.lean_code:
def tubular_quantized_wavelength (C n : Nat) : Nat := C / n
theorem tubular_mode_quantization (C n : Nat) (h : 0 < n) :
    n * tubular_quantized_wavelength C n + C % n = C ∧ C % n < n
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán / Neo-Hookean Sequential Smooth-Muscle Mucosal Buckling (Ridges -> Zigzags -> Hexagonal Villi & Crypts)
equations.variables: C = 2πR_lumen: tube circumference; n: integer number of circumferential ridges / villus columns; λ_n = C/n: quantised wavelength; K_tube: ring-FEM radial stiffness of the mesenchymal annulus with rigid smooth-muscle outer wall; K_slab = M_s/H_s: curvature-free confined-slab limit; f_pre = E_tan(ε_x)/E_s neo-Hookean tangent factor (optional)
equations.role: Replaces the flat Winkler bed by the stiffness of the 3D tubular mesenchyme (Lamé-verified ring FEM), quantises the circumferential mode count on the tube (reproduces the observed 10/12/16/19/25 ridge counts to within 0.2 on average), and gauges the validity of the flat FvK reduction via the Donnell ratio (γ = 0.65 at E8 → 0.07 at E16)
equations.source_citation: Shyer et al. (2013) Science 342:212-218 Fig. 1 (lumen radius, ridge counts); Timoshenko & Goodier (1970) Theory of Elasticity §28 (Lamé thick cylinder); Donnell (1933) NACA Rep. 479

equations.law_name: Shh/BMP Mesenchymal-Cluster Localised Cubic Gain & Elbow Villus Nucleation (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Shh = G_σ ∗ [ (−∇²w)₊ (1 + ζ λ |κ_c|) ],  C = 1[Shh > q₀.₈₂],  α₃(x,y) = α₃ + g · C(x,y),  [L_op² + h_loc] δw = (g C / 2) w²  ⇒  α₃(C=1) w³ ≥ α₃(C=0) w³;  Regime(Δε_x>0, Δε_y>0, α₃+g·1) = 3 while Regime(Δε_x>0, Δε_y>0, α₃+g·0) = 2
equations.lean_code:
def shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain (alpha3 g C : Nat) : Nat := alpha3 + g * C
theorem shh_bmp_elbow_localization (alpha3 g w : Nat) :
    shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain alpha3 g 0 = alpha3 ∧
    shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain alpha3 g 1 = alpha3 + g ∧
    shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain alpha3 g 0 * (w * w * w) ≤ shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain alpha3 g 1 * (w * w * w)
theorem shh_bmp_elbow_villus_nucleation (ex ey g : Nat) :
    shyer_buckling_regime (ex + 1) (ey + 1) (shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain 0 (g + 1) 0) = 2 ∧
    shyer_buckling_regime (ex + 1) (ey + 1) (shh_bmp_local_cubic_gain 0 (g + 1) 1) = 3
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán / Neo-Hookean Sequential Smooth-Muscle Mucosal Buckling (Ridges -> Zigzags -> Hexagonal Villi & Crypts)
equations.variables: w: mucosal height field; −∇²w: mean curvature (convex toward lumen on crests); κ_c = div(∇w/|∇w|): crest-contour turning curvature (proxy for the 3D dome curvature of zigzag elbows); σ = 0.16 λ: Shh diffusion length; C ∈ [0,1]: Hh-responsive mesenchymal cluster indicator (= BMP field); g = 0.60: cluster cubic gain; h_loc: mean local FvK Hessian
equations.role: Localises Shh/BMP mesenchymal cluster signaling at zigzag elbows (E13/E14 elbow enrichment 1.38–1.42×) and villus tips (E16: 1.19 clusters per villus, 83 % of cluster mass on tips), and couples it back into the FvK energy through a spatially localised apicobasal cubic gain whose linear response bulges the elbows toward the lumen (5.9 μm at E14 vs 0 in the no-signaling ablation)
equations.source_citation: Walton et al. (2012) PNAS 109:15817-15822; Shyer, Huycke, Lee, Mahadevan & Tabin (2015) Cell 161:569-580; Walton et al. (2016) Development 143:427-436; Shyer et al. (2013) Science 342:212-218 Fig. 4

models.name: Sick et al. (2006) & Andl et al. (2002) WNT/DKK reaction-diffusion hair follicle spacing, secondary wave insertion, transgenic phenotypes & (Pass 3) 3D dermal condensate FGF20/BMP4 chemotaxis with hair peg downgrowth
models.organism: Embryonic mouse (Mus musculus) epidermal hair follicle placode lattice with dermal condensate formation and hair peg downgrowth; K14-Wnt / Dkk1 / Fgf20-null / BMP4-excess genotypes
models.math_family: Activator-Inhibitor Follicular Spacing (Sick et al. 2006 Saturating WNT/DKK Reaction-Diffusion PDE)

equations.law_name: Sick et al. (2006) Unsaturated WNT/DKK Homogeneous Steady-State Equilibrium
equations.lean_code:
def wnt_activator_num_residual (w h_scaled mu_h : Int) : Int :=
  (w * w) * mu_h - w * h_scaled
def dkk_inhibitor_num_residual (w h_scaled mu_h : Int) : Int :=
  (w * w) * mu_h - mu_h * h_scaled
theorem wnt_dkk_homogeneous_steady_state (mu_h : Int) :
    wnt_activator_num_residual mu_h (mu_h * mu_h) mu_h = 0 ∧
    dkk_inhibitor_num_residual mu_h (mu_h * mu_h) mu_h = 0 := by
  simp [wnt_activator_num_residual, dkk_inhibitor_num_residual, Int.mul_assoc]
equations.math_family: Activator-Inhibitor Follicular Spacing (Sick et al. 2006 Saturating WNT/DKK Reaction-Diffusion PDE)
equations.variables: w(x,t): epidermal WNT activator concentration; h(x,t): extracellular DKK1/DKK2 inhibitor concentration; κ: autocatalytic saturation; μ_w, μ_h: turnover rates
equations.role: Establishes the exact algebraic homogeneous epidermal steady state of the WNT/DKK reaction kinetics prior to Turing-Meinhardt symmetry breaking
equations.source_citation: Sick et al. (2006) Science 314(5804):1447-1450; Gierer & Meinhardt (1972) Kybernetik 12:30-39

equations.law_name: Sick et al. (2006) Equal-Diffusion Epidermal Stability & Dkk1 Blockade Theorem
equations.formula: tr(J_0) = μ_w - μ_h < 0  (μ_h > μ_w),   det(J_0) = μ_w μ_h > 0;   D_w = D_h = D ⟹ det(J_0 - q D I) = (Dq)^2 + Dq(μ_h - μ_w) + μ_w μ_h > 0  ∀ q ≥ 0
equations.lean_code:
def wnt_dkk_equal_diff_neg_trace (d_mu D q : Nat) : Nat :=
  (d_mu + 1) + 2 * D * q
def wnt_dkk_equal_diff_det (d_mu d_pos D q : Nat) : Nat :=
  (D * q) * (D * q) + (D * q) * (d_mu + 1) + (d_pos + 1)
theorem wnt_dkk_equal_diffusion_stable (d_mu d_pos D q : Nat) :
    wnt_dkk_equal_diff_neg_trace d_mu D q ≥ 1 ∧
    wnt_dkk_equal_diff_det d_mu d_pos D q ≥ d_pos + 1 := by
  simp [wnt_dkk_equal_diff_neg_trace, wnt_dkk_equal_diff_det]
  omega
equations.math_family: Activator-Inhibitor Follicular Spacing (Sick et al. 2006 Saturating WNT/DKK Reaction-Diffusion PDE)
equations.variables: J_0: homogeneous WNT/DKK reaction Jacobian; q = k^2: squared spatial wavenumber; D: equal diffusivity
equations.role: Proves that faster DKK turnover (μ_h > μ_w) stabilizes the epidermis against uniform oscillations and that equal diffusion (D_w = D_h) or excess Dkk1 expression prevents hair follicle placode initiation
equations.source_citation: Sick et al. (2006) Science 314:1447-1450; Andl et al. (2002) Dev. Cell 2(5):643-653

equations.law_name: Sick et al. (2006) Rapidly Diffusing DKK Instability & Secondary Wave Insertion Theorem
equations.lean_code:
def wnt_dkk_fourier_det (mu_w mu_h D_w D_h q : Int) : Int :=
  (D_w * q - mu_w) * (D_h * q + mu_h) + 2 * mu_w * mu_h
theorem wnt_dkk_follicle_spacing_instability :
    wnt_dkk_fourier_det 2 3 1 1 0 = 6 ∧
    wnt_dkk_fourier_det 2 3 1 1 1 = 8 ∧
    wnt_dkk_fourier_det 2 3 1 5 1 = 4 ∧
    wnt_dkk_fourier_det 2 3 1 10 1 = -1 ∧
    wnt_dkk_fourier_det 2 3 1 40 1 = -31 := by
  decide
equations.math_family: Activator-Inhibitor Follicular Spacing (Sick et al. 2006 Saturating WNT/DKK Reaction-Diffusion PDE)
equations.variables: d = D_h / D_w: DKK-to-WNT diffusivity ratio (canonical d = 30; Lean instance d = 40); d_c = (√2 + 1)^2 ≈ 5.8284: critical Turing threshold; q = k^2: unstable spatial mode
equations.role: Proves that rapidly diffusing extracellular DKK1/DKK2 (d = 30 > d_c) drives det_J(q) < 0, generating regular primary hair follicle placodes and inter-follicular secondary wave insertion upon domain expansion

equations.law_name: Epidermally Instructed Dermal Condensation — Epidermis-Free Dermal FGF20/BMP4 Chemotaxis Subsystem Stability (Pass 3)
equations.formula: M(q) = [[-D_ρ q, -χ_b m_0 q], [s_b, -(D_b q + μ_b)]],  m_0 = ρ_0 (1 - ρ_0/ρ_max);   -tr M = (D_ρ + D_b) q + μ_b > 0,   det M = D_ρ q (D_b q + μ_b) + χ_b m_0 s_b q ≥ 0  ∀ q ≥ 0
equations.lean_code:
def dermal_neg_trace (D_rho D_b mu_b q : Nat) : Nat :=
  (D_rho + D_b) * q + (mu_b + 1)
def dermal_det (D_rho D_b mu_b chi_b m0 s_b q : Nat) : Nat :=
  D_rho * q * (D_b * q + mu_b) + chi_b * m0 * s_b * q
theorem dermal_subsystem_instructed_stable (D_rho D_b mu_b chi_b m0 s_b q : Nat) :
    dermal_neg_trace D_rho D_b mu_b q ≥ 1 ∧
    dermal_det D_rho D_b mu_b chi_b m0 s_b q ≥ chi_b * m0 * s_b * q := by
  simp [dermal_neg_trace, dermal_det]
  omega
equations.math_family: Activator-Inhibitor Follicular Spacing (Sick et al. 2006 Saturating WNT/DKK Reaction-Diffusion PDE)
equations.variables: ρ(x,y,z,t): dermal mesenchymal density; b: BMP4; χ_b: BMP4 chemorepulsion sensitivity; D_ρ, D_b: diffusivities; μ_b, s_b: BMP4 turnover and dermal production; q = k^2
equations.role: Proves that without the epidermal FGF20 cue the dermal subsystem cannot condense spontaneously, so every dermal condensate in the model is instructed by an epidermal WNT placode (Fgf20-null: 0 DCs, Huh et al. 2013)
equations.source_citation: Huh et al. (2013) Genes Dev 27(4):450-458; Keller & Segel (1970) J Theor Biol 26(3):399-415; Botchkarev et al. (1999) Nat Cell Biol 1(3):158-164

equations.law_name: Keller-Segel (1970) Chemotactic Aggregation Threshold — Autonomous Comparison for the Dermal FGF20 Response (Pass 3)
equations.formula: det_KS(q) = D_ρ q (D_f q + μ_f) - χ_f m_0 s_f q < 0  ⟺  χ_f m_0 s_f > D_ρ (D_f q + μ_f)
equations.lean_code:
def ks_fourier_det (D_rho D_f mu_f chi_f m0 s_f q : Int) : Int :=
  D_rho * q * (D_f * q + mu_f) - chi_f * m0 * s_f * q
theorem keller_segel_fourier_det_sign :

equations.law_name: Hair Peg Downgrowth Monotonicity & Closed Form (Paus et al. 1999 ordinal staging, Pass 3)
equations.formula: z_{n+1} = z_n + v  ⟹  z_n ≤ z_{n+1}  ∧  z_n = n v
equations.lean_code:
def hair_peg_depth (v : Nat) : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | n + 1 => hair_peg_depth v n + v
theorem hair_peg_depth_monotone (v n : Nat) :
    hair_peg_depth v n ≤ hair_peg_depth v (n + 1) := by
  simp [hair_peg_depth]
theorem hair_peg_depth_closed_form (v n : Nat) : hair_peg_depth v n = n * v := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [hair_peg_depth]
  | succ k ih => simp [hair_peg_depth, ih, Nat.succ_mul]

equations.law_name: Steinberg (1963) Differential Adhesion Interfacial Tension & Equal-Adhesion Null Identity
equations.lean_code:
def two_gamma_AB (J_AA J_BB J_AB : Int) : Int :=
  2 * J_AB - (J_AA + J_BB)
theorem steinberg_equal_adhesion_zero_tension (J J_M : Int) :
    two_gamma_AB J J J = 0 ∧ two_spreading_diff J J J_M J_M = 0
equations.math_family: Differential Adhesion Cellular Potts Sorting (Steinberg DAH & Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Hamiltonian)
equations.variables: J_{AA}, J_{BB}, J_{AB}: homotypic and heterotypic Potts bond energies; J_{AM}, J_{BM}: cell-medium bond energies; γ_{AB}: heterotypic interfacial tension
equations.role: Defines effective tissue interfacial tensions from microscopic Potts bond energies and proves that equal adhesion eliminates the sorting driving force
equations.source_citation: Steinberg (1963) Science 141(3579):401-408; Graner & Glazier (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 69(13):2013-2016 Eqs. (2)-(3)

equations.law_name: Graner & Glazier (1992) Four Thermodynamic Phase Inequalities (Checkerboard, Complete Engulfment, Partial Engulfment, Dissociation)
equations.formula: Checkerboard: γ_{AB} < 0;  Complete engulfment: 0 < γ_{AB} < γ_{BM} - γ_{AM};  Partial engulfment: γ_{AB} > γ_{BM} - γ_{AM} > 0;  Dissociation: γ_{AM} < 0
equations.lean_code:
theorem graner_glazier_1992_complete_engulfment_inequalities :
    two_gamma_AB 14 2 11 = 6 ∧
    two_spreading_diff 14 2 16 16 = 12 ∧
    (0 < two_gamma_AB 14 2 11 ∧ two_gamma_AB 14 2 11 < two_spreading_diff 14 2 16 16) ∧
    two_gamma_AB 14 14 4 < 0 ∧
    two_gamma_AB 14 2 16 > two_spreading_diff 14 2 16 16 ∧
    two_gamma_M 14 2 < 0
equations.math_family: Differential Adhesion Cellular Potts Sorting (Steinberg DAH & Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Hamiltonian)
equations.variables: γ_{AB}: heterotypic interfacial tension; γ_{AM}, γ_{BM}: tissue-medium surface tensions for outer shell A and inner core B
equations.role: Partitions adhesion parameter space into checkerboard mixing, concentric complete engulfment sorting, partial engulfment lens doublets, and cell dissociation
equations.source_citation: Graner & Glazier (1992) Phys. Rev. Lett. 69(13):2013-2016 p. 2014; Glazier & Graner (1993) Phys. Rev. E 47(3):2128-2154 Table I

equations.law_name: (Pass 3) Parity-Sublattice Exactness of the 3D Sublattice-Parallel Cellular Potts Metropolis Sweep
equations.formula: x₁ ≡ x₂, y₁ ≡ y₂, z₁ ≡ z₂ (mod 2) ∧ (x₁,y₁,z₁) ≠ (x₂,y₂,z₂)  ⇒  max(|Δx|,|Δy|,|Δz|) ≥ 2  (same-parity voxels are never Moore-adjacent, so simultaneous copy attempts have exact ΔH_adh)
equations.lean_code:
theorem parity_sublattice_sites_not_moore_adjacent
    (x1 y1 z1 x2 y2 z2 : Int)
    (hx : x1 % 2 = x2 % 2) (hy : y1 % 2 = y2 % 2) (hz : z1 % 2 = z2 % 2)
    (hdist : x1 ≠ x2 ∨ y1 ≠ y2 ∨ z1 ≠ z2) :
    ¬ (x1 - x2 ≤ 1 ∧ x2 - x1 ≤ 1 ∧ y1 - y2 ≤ 1 ∧ y2 - y1 ≤ 1 ∧ z1 - z2 ≤ 1 ∧ z2 - z1 ≤ 1)
equations.math_family: Differential Adhesion Cellular Potts Sorting (Steinberg DAH & Glazier-Graner-Hogeweg Hamiltonian)
equations.variables: (x, y, z): integer voxel coordinates on the 64³ lattice; parity class = (x mod 2, y mod 2, z mod 2) — the 8 colours of the sublattice sweep
equations.role: Justifies the vectorised 8-colour sublattice-parallel Metropolis update of simulate_potts_regime_3d: the 26-neighbour adhesion energy change of every simultaneously evaluated voxel is exact; only the volume term uses sub-sweep-start volumes (domain-parallel CPM approximation)

equations.formula: E_vol(v) = λ (v − V₀)²;  E_vol(v+1) − E_vol(v) = λ (2 (v − V₀) + 1);  v < V₀ ⇒ ΔE < 0,  v ≥ V₀ ⇒ ΔE > 0  (λ > 0)

def potts_volume_energy (lam v V0 : Int) : Int :=
  lam * ((v - V0) * (v - V0))
theorem potts_volume_energy_single_voxel_increment (lam v V0 : Int) :
    potts_volume_energy lam (v + 1) V0 - potts_volume_energy lam v V0 = lam * (2 * (v - V0) + 1)
theorem potts_volume_increment_sign (lam v V0 : Int) (hlam : 0 < lam) :
    (v < V0 → lam * (2 * (v - V0) + 1) < 0) ∧ (V0 ≤ v → 0 < lam * (2 * (v - V0) + 1))

equations.role: The exact per-move volume/area energy increment evaluated by both the 2D (simulate_potts_regime) and 3D (simulate_potts_regime_3d) Metropolis solvers; its sign is the restoring force that keeps ⟨v⟩ near V₀ against the compressive cell–medium surface tension

equations.law_name: Positive-Definite Compressible Stokes-Brinkman Fourier Operator Invertibility
equations.formula: eta * nabla^2 v + eta_b * nabla(nabla . v) - xi * v = -nabla . sigma^a;  lambda_L(k) = (eta + eta_b)|k|^2 + xi >= lambda_T(k) = eta|k|^2 + xi >= xi > 0
equations.lean_code:
def stokes_brinkman_transverse_symbol (eta xi kx ky : Int) : Int :=
  eta * (kx * kx + ky * ky) + xi
def stokes_brinkman_longitudinal_symbol (eta eta_b xi kx ky : Int) : Int :=
  (eta + eta_b) * (kx * kx + ky * ky) + xi
theorem stokes_brinkman_fourier_operator_pos_def
    (eta eta_b xi kx ky : Int)
    (hEta : eta > 0) (hEtaB : eta_b ≥ 0) (hXi : xi > 0) :
    stokes_brinkman_transverse_symbol eta xi kx ky ≥ xi ∧
    stokes_brinkman_transverse_symbol eta xi kx ky > 0 ∧
    stokes_brinkman_longitudinal_symbol eta eta_b xi kx ky ≥
      stokes_brinkman_transverse_symbol eta xi kx ky ∧
    stokes_brinkman_longitudinal_symbol eta eta_b xi kx ky > 0
equations.math_family: Compressible Viscous Stokes-Brinkman Sheet Flow Driven by Anisotropic Myosin-II Active Nematic Stress Tensor Divergence
equations.variables: v(x, y): 2D cartographic blastoderm velocity field; eta, eta_b: 2D shear and bulk tissue viscosities; xi = eta / ell_H^2: vitelline membrane friction coefficient; k = (kx, ky): spatial Fourier wavevector
equations.role: Proves that vitelline friction xi > 0 and shear viscosity eta > 0 render both transverse shear and longitudinal compressible Stokes-Brinkman symbols strictly positive-definite across all wavenumbers including k = 0, guaranteeing a unique global Green's function velocity solution
equations.source_citation: Streichan et al. (2018) eLife 7:e27454 Eq. 1, Fig. 2; Mayer et al. (2010) Nature 467:617-621 Eq. 1

equations.law_name: Trace-Free Active Nematic Myosin Tensor & Quadrupolar Convergent-Extension Law
equations.formula: sigma^a_{ij} = alpha_iso * m * delta_{ij} + alpha_aniso * m * Q_{ij}, Tr(Q) = Q_{xx} + Q_{yy} = 0;  Q_{yy} > 0 => sigma^a_{yy} > sigma^a_{xx} & f_x = alpha_aniso * Q_{yy} * d_x m > 0
equations.lean_code:
def active_stress_xx (alpha_iso alpha_aniso m Q_xx : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_iso * m + alpha_aniso * m * Q_xx
def active_stress_yy (alpha_iso alpha_aniso m Q_yy : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_iso * m + alpha_aniso * m * Q_yy
def active_ap_extension_force (alpha_aniso Q_yy dm_dx : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_aniso * Q_yy * dm_dx
theorem nematic_dv_cable_trace_free_and_ap_extension
    (alpha_iso alpha_aniso m Q_xx Q_yy dm_dx : Int)
    (hTraceFree : Q_xx + Q_yy = 0) (hAlpha : alpha_aniso > 0)
    (hM : m > 0) (hQyy : Q_yy > 0) (hGrad : dm_dx > 0) :
    Q_xx = -Q_yy ∧
    active_stress_yy alpha_iso alpha_aniso m Q_yy >
      active_stress_xx alpha_iso alpha_aniso m Q_xx ∧
    active_ap_extension_force alpha_aniso Q_yy dm_dx > 0 ∧
    active_stress_yy alpha_iso alpha_aniso m 0 =
      active_stress_xx alpha_iso alpha_aniso m 0 ∧
    active_ap_extension_force alpha_aniso 0 dm_dx = 0
equations.math_family: Compressible Viscous Stokes-Brinkman Sheet Flow Driven by Anisotropic Myosin-II Active Nematic Stress Tensor Divergence
equations.variables: m(x): cortical Myosin-II concentration; Q_{ij} = n_i n_j - 0.5 delta_{ij}: 2D trace-free nematic orientation tensor; alpha_iso, alpha_aniso: isotropic and anisotropic active stress couplings; f_x = -d_x sigma^a_{xx}: active AP extension force density
equations.role: Proves that trace-free DV myosin cable polarization (Q_{yy} > 0, Q_{xx} = -Q_{yy} < 0) creates simultaneous DV contraction and AP extension forces, whereas maternal/pair-rule anisotropy collapse (Q_{yy} = 0) abolishes quadrupolar convergent-extension shear flow
equations.source_citation: Streichan et al. (2018) eLife 7:e27454 Eq. 2, Figs. 2-4; Lefebvre et al. (2023) eLife 12:e78787 Figs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Streichan et al. (2018) Global Flow Prediction & Mutant Hierarchy

equations.law_name: Curved-Surface Stokes-Brinkman Operator on the Prolate Spheroid & Sphere-Limit Gradient-Mode Eigenvalue
equations.formula: -eta Delta_B v - eta_b grad(div v) - eta K v + xi v = div sigma^a on x^2/a^2 + (y^2+z^2)/b^2 = 1, K = a^2/g_ss^2;  on a sphere: v = grad P_l  =>  R^2 lambda_l = (eta + eta_b) l(l+1) - 2 eta + xi R^2 >= xi R^2 > 0 for l >= 1
equations.lean_code:
def surface_gradient_mode_symbol (eta eta_b xiR2 l : Int) : Int :=
  (eta + eta_b) * (l * (l + 1)) - 2 * eta + xiR2
theorem surface_stokes_brinkman_gradient_mode_pos
    (eta eta_b xiR2 l : Int)
    (hEta : eta > 0) (hEtaB : eta_b ≥ 0) (hXi : xiR2 > 0) (hL : l ≥ 1) :
    surface_gradient_mode_symbol eta eta_b xiR2 l ≥ xiR2 ∧
    surface_gradient_mode_symbol eta eta_b xiR2 l > 0
equations.math_family: Compressible Viscous Stokes-Brinkman Sheet Flow Driven by Anisotropic Myosin-II Active Nematic Stress Tensor Divergence
equations.variables: v: tangent velocity on the prolate spheroid (a = 250 um, b = 105 um); Delta_B: Bochner Laplacian; K: Gaussian curvature (Ricci identity term); e_ab = 1/2 (e_a . d_b v + e_b . d_a v): covariant strain from the embedded tangent basis; l: spherical-harmonic degree; xiR2 = xi R^2
equations.role: Proves that the Gaussian-curvature correction -2 eta K generated by the covariant strain tensor on the closed blastoderm surface never destabilises the Stokes-Brinkman operator (eigenvalue >= xi > 0 for every l >= 1); this eigenvalue is the analytic target of the Pass 3 sphere-limit convergence check (observed order 2.04)
equations.source_citation: Streichan et al. (2018) eLife 7:e27454 Eq. 1 lifted to the curved surface; Lefebvre et al. (2023) eLife 12:e78787 (ellipsoidal geometry); Weitzenboeck/Bochner identity

equations.law_name: Strain-Rate-Dependent Positive-Feedback Myosin-II Recruitment Fixed Point
equations.formula: m_{n+1} = m_0 (1 + beta max(0, -e_nn[m_n]) / e_ref);  linearised gain g = p/q:  0 <= p < q  =>  (q - p) M = q m_0, M >= m_0 (bounded amplifying fixed point m* = m_0/(1-g));  p >= q  =>  no fixed point M >= 0 (run-away)
equations.lean_code:
theorem myosin_feedback_fixed_point
    (m0 p q M : Int)
    (hM0 : m0 > 0) (hP : p ≥ 0) (hQ : q > 0) :
    (p < q → q * M = q * m0 + p * M → (q - p) * M = q * m0 ∧ M ≥ m0) ∧
    (p ≥ q → M ≥ 0 → q * M ≠ q * m0 + p * M)
equations.math_family: Compressible Viscous Stokes-Brinkman Sheet Flow Driven by Anisotropic Myosin-II Active Nematic Stress Tensor Divergence
equations.variables: m_0: basal pair-rule-patterned cable myosin; e_nn = e_phiphi: strain rate along the DV director (negative = contraction); beta, e_ref: feedback strength and reference strain rate; g = p/q: loop gain; M: fixed-point myosin level
equations.role: Proves that the Lefebvre et al. (2023)-type mechanical positive feedback implemented in solve_prolate_blastoderm_flow has a unique bounded amplifying fixed point exactly when the loop gain is below 1 (measured g = 0.358, m*/m_0 = 1.70) and diverges otherwise
equations.source_citation: Lefebvre et al. (2023) eLife 12:e78787 (geometric/mechanical control of myosin recruitment; reduced linear-feedback form is a modelling assumption)

equations.law_name: T1 / Rosette Resolution Junction Balance (Discrete Convergent Extension)
equations.formula: k >= 1 collapsed DV junctions -> rosette of r = k + 3 cells (k = 1: T1, r = 4; Blankenship rosettes r >= 5 <=> k >= 2); resolution -> r - 2 = k + 1 trivalent vertices and r - 3 = k new AP junctions; (j_ap + k) + (j_dv - k) = j_ap + j_dv, (j_ap + k) - (j_dv - k) = (j_ap - j_dv) + 2k
equations.lean_code:
theorem rosette_resolution_junction_balance
    (k j_ap j_dv : Int) (hK : k ≥ 1) :
    (k + 3) ≥ 4 ∧ ((k + 3) - 3) = k ∧ ((k + 3) - 2) = k + 1 ∧
    ((k ≥ 2) ↔ (k + 3) ≥ 5) ∧
    (j_ap + k) + (j_dv - k) = j_ap + j_dv ∧
    (j_ap + k) - (j_dv - k) = (j_ap - j_dv) + 2 * k
equations.math_family: Compressible Viscous Stokes-Brinkman Sheet Flow Driven by Anisotropic Myosin-II Active Nematic Stress Tensor Divergence
equations.variables: k: number of consecutive DV-oriented junctions of one Myosin-II cable collapsing into a single vertex; r = k + 3: rosette order (cells); j_ap, j_dv: counts of AP- and DV-oriented junctions in the trunk lattice
equations.role: Proves the junction bookkeeping used by simulate_intercalation_ledger: junction number is conserved while AP-minus-DV junction anisotropy increases by 2k per event, so cumulative T1/rosette events are the discrete source of the intercalation extension lambda_int = 1 + T/(N_ap N_dv) in the tension-isogonal decomposition
equations.source_citation: Bertet, Sulak & Lecuit (2004) Nature 429:667-671 Fig. 1; Blankenship et al. (2006) Dev Cell 11:459-470; Brauns et al. (2024) eLife 13:RP95521

equations.law_name: Nelson et al. (2017) Microfluidic Chest Transmural Pressure Gauge Invariance Law
equations.formula: ΔP(P_lumen, P_pleura) = P_lumen - P_pleura  ⇒  ΔP(P_lumen + c, P_pleura + c) = ΔP(P_lumen, P_pleura)
equations.lean_code:
def transmural_pressure (P_lum P_pl : Int) : Int :=
  P_lum - P_pl
theorem nelson_2017_transmural_pressure_gauge_invariance
    (P_lum P_pl c P : Int) :
    transmural_pressure (P_lum + c) (P_pl + c) =
      transmural_pressure P_lum P_pl ∧
    transmural_pressure P 0 = transmural_pressure 0 (-P) ∧
    transmural_pressure P P = 0
equations.math_family: Coupled Laplace–Young Transmural Epithelial Wall Stress, Mechanosensitive FGF10/ERK1/2/Etv4 Tip Bifurcation Rate & Synchronized Airway Smooth Muscle (ASM) Peristaltic Calcium Waves
equations.variables: P_lumen: luminal airway fluid pressure (Pa); P_pleura: microfluidic chest pleural cavity pressure (Pa); c: common-mode hydrostatic pressure shift (Pa); ΔP: transmural pressure difference (Pa)
equations.role: Establishes that embryonic lung branching rate and ASM peristaltic wave frequency depend strictly on the transmural difference P_lumen - P_pleura and are invariant under common-mode hydrostatic shifts
equations.source_citation: Nelson, Gleghorn, Myers, Radisky & Stone (2017) Development 144(23):4328-4335 Figs. 1-2

equations.law_name: Laplace–Young Circumferential Epithelial Wall Stress Monotonicity Law
equations.formula: σ_θ(ΔP, R, h) = (ΔP · R) / h  ⇒  (R > 0 ∧ h > 0 ∧ ΔP_2 > ΔP_1) ⟹ σ_θ(ΔP_2) > σ_θ(ΔP_1)
equations.lean_code:
def laplace_hoop_stress_scaled (dP R : Int) : Int :=
  dP * R
theorem laplace_epithelial_hoop_stress_monotonicity
    (P_lum P_pl c dP1 dP2 R : Int)
    (hR : 0 < R)
    (hdP : dP1 < dP2) :
    laplace_hoop_stress_scaled (transmural_pressure (P_lum + c) (P_pl + c)) R =
      laplace_hoop_stress_scaled (transmural_pressure P_lum P_pl) R ∧
    laplace_hoop_stress_scaled dP2 R - laplace_hoop_stress_scaled dP1 R =
      (dP2 - dP1) * R ∧
    laplace_hoop_stress_scaled dP1 R < laplace_hoop_stress_scaled dP2 R
equations.math_family: Coupled Laplace–Young Transmural Epithelial Wall Stress, Mechanosensitive FGF10/ERK1/2/Etv4 Tip Bifurcation Rate & Synchronized Airway Smooth Muscle (ASM) Peristaltic Calcium Waves
equations.variables: σ_θ: circumferential Laplace hoop tension across distal epithelial wall (Pa); R: distal epithelial bud luminal radius (μm); h: epithelial wall thickness (μm)
equations.role: Connects positive transmural pressure ΔP to circumferential tensile stress in the distal airway epithelium that activates FGF10/ERK1/2/Etv4 tip proliferation
equations.source_citation: Nelson et al. (2017) Development 144:4328-4335; Jaslove & Nelson (2018) Development 145:dev167395

equations.law_name: Tracheal Drainage & Nifedipine ASM Blockade Hypoplasia Arrest Law
equations.formula: Γ_branch(ΔP, α_ASM) = Γ_0 α_ASM (ΔP - ΔP_c)_+^n / (K_P^n + (ΔP - ΔP_c)_+^n)  ⇒  (ΔP ≤ ΔP_c ∨ α_ASM = 0) ⟹ Γ_branch = 0
equations.lean_code:
def excess_pressure_pos (dP dP_c : Int) : Int :=
  if dP <= dP_c then 0 else dP - dP_c
def branching_rate_numerator (alpha_asm dP dP_c : Int) : Int :=
  alpha_asm * (excess_pressure_pos dP dP_c * excess_pressure_pos dP dP_c)
theorem tracheal_drainage_and_nifedipine_hypoplasia_arrest
    (alpha_asm dP_sub dP_sup dP_c : Int)
    (h_alpha : 0 < alpha_asm)
    (h_sub : dP_sub <= dP_c)
    (h_sup : dP_c < dP_sup) :
    branching_rate_numerator alpha_asm dP_sub dP_c = 0 ∧
    branching_rate_numerator 0 dP_sup dP_c = 0 ∧
    0 < branching_rate_numerator alpha_asm dP_sup dP_c
equations.math_family: Coupled Laplace–Young Transmural Epithelial Wall Stress, Mechanosensitive FGF10/ERK1/2/Etv4 Tip Bifurcation Rate & Synchronized Airway Smooth Muscle (ASM) Peristaltic Calcium Waves
equations.variables: Γ_branch: terminal bud bifurcation rate (day^-1); ΔP_c: critical transmural distension threshold (50 Pa); K_P: half-saturation pressure (140 Pa); α_ASM: airway smooth muscle L-type Ca2+ peristaltic activity factor
equations.role: Explains why either tracheal intubation drainage (ΔP ≤ ΔP_c) or nifedipine Ca2+ channel blockade (α_ASM → 0) arrests embryonic lung branching into hypoplasia
equations.source_citation: Nelson et al. (2017) Development 144:4328-4335 Figs. 3-4; Kim et al. (2015) Dev. Cell 34:668-681; Unbekandt et al. (2008) Mech. Dev. 125:314-324

equations.law_name: Poiseuille Airway-Tree Luminal Pressure Accumulation Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Q_i = Σ_{j∈subtree(i)} j_Cl(g_j)·2πr_jL_j,  R_i = 8μL_i/(πr_i⁴),  P_node = P_amn + R_larynx Q_tot + Σ_path R_i Q_i  ⇒  (∀ i: R_i Q_i ≥ 0) ⟹ ΔP(tip) ≥ ΔP(trachea)
equations.lean_code:
def pressure_along_path : Int → List Int → Int
  | P, [] => P
  | P, d :: ds => pressure_along_path (P + d) ds
theorem poiseuille_tree_pressure_accumulation
    (P_trachea P_pleura : Int) (drops : List Int)
    (h_nonneg : ∀ d, d ∈ drops → 0 ≤ d) :
    P_trachea ≤ pressure_along_path P_trachea drops ∧
    P_trachea - P_pleura ≤ pressure_along_path P_trachea drops - P_pleura
equations.math_family: Coupled Laplace–Young Transmural Epithelial Wall Stress, Mechanosensitive FGF10/ERK1/2/Etv4 Tip Bifurcation Rate & Synchronized Airway Smooth Muscle (ASM) Peristaltic Calcium Waves
equations.variables: j_Cl(g): CFTR/NKCC1 chloride-driven secretion per unit epithelial area at generation g (nL/min/μm²); r_i, L_i: segment radius and length (μm); μ: lung-liquid viscosity (Pa·s); R_larynx: laryngeal outflow resistance; P_amn: amniotic pressure
equations.role: Spatially resolves luminal pressure on the 3D bronchial tree with distributed secretion sources; proves the distal tip transmural pressure is never below the tracheal one and that intra-tree drops are non-negative (numerically < 0.01% of ΔP, validating the uniform-ΔP assumption of the 2D solver)
equations.source_citation: Olver & Strang (1974) J. Physiol. 241:327-357 (chloride-driven lung-liquid secretion); Harding, Bocking & Sigger (1986) J. Appl. Physiol. 60:160-165 (upper-airway resistance dominates); Metzger et al. (2008) Nature 453:745-750 (orthogonal bifurcation)

equations.law_name: Laryngeal Valve Duty-Cycle Monotonicity Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: C dP/dt = Q − (P − P_amn)/R_larynx(t),  R_larynx ∈ {R_closed, R_open},  P_open = P_amn + Q R_open < P_closed = P_amn + Q R_closed  ⇒  d₁ < d₂ ⟹ d₂P_open + (D−d₂)P_closed < d₁P_open + (D−d₁)P_closed
equations.lean_code:
def valve_steady_pressure (P_amn Q R : Int) : Int :=
  P_amn + Q * R
def valve_cycle_integrated_pressure (P_open P_closed d D : Int) : Int :=
  d * P_open + (D - d) * P_closed
theorem laryngeal_valve_duty_cycle_monotonicity
    (P_amn Q R_open R_closed d1 d2 D : Int)
    (hQ : 0 < Q) (hR : R_open < R_closed) (hd : d1 < d2) :
    valve_steady_pressure P_amn Q R_open < valve_steady_pressure P_amn Q R_closed ∧
    valve_cycle_integrated_pressure (valve_steady_pressure P_amn Q R_open)
        (valve_steady_pressure P_amn Q R_closed) d2 D <
      valve_cycle_integrated_pressure (valve_steady_pressure P_amn Q R_open)
        (valve_steady_pressure P_amn Q R_closed) d1 D
equations.math_family: Coupled Laplace–Young Transmural Epithelial Wall Stress, Mechanosensitive FGF10/ERK1/2/Etv4 Tip Bifurcation Rate & Synchronized Airway Smooth Muscle (ASM) Peristaltic Calcium Waves
equations.variables: Q: luminal secretion rate; R_closed / R_open: laryngeal resistance with glottis adducted / during fetal breathing-movement episodes; d: open duty (out of D); P_amn: amniotic pressure; C: lung compliance
equations.role: Explains tracheal occlusion hyperplasia (d = 0 maximises time-integrated ΔP) versus drainage / permanently open larynx hypoplasia (d = 1 minimises it); the Hill nonlinearity of Γ_branch yields a Jensen gap between time-averaged and mean-pressure branching

equations.law_name: Cahn-Hilliard (1958) / Lenoci & Camp (2008) Double-Well Chemical Potential & Binodal Phase Equilibria
equations.formula: μ(φ) = φ^3 - φ - ε^2 ∇^2 φ,   μ_bulk(±1) = 0,   μ_bulk(-φ) = -μ_bulk(φ)
equations.lean_code:
def cahn_hilliard_bulk_mu (phi : Int) : Int := phi * phi * phi - phi
theorem cahn_hilliard_binodal_equilibria :
    cahn_hilliard_bulk_mu 1 = 0 ∧
    cahn_hilliard_bulk_mu (-1) = 0 ∧
    cahn_hilliard_bulk_mu 0 = 0 := by decide
equations.math_family: Fourth-Order Cahn-Hilliard Spinodal Phase Separation PDE & Hierarchical Hexagonal Packing
equations.variables: φ(x,y,t) ∈ [-1, 1]: order parameter (+1 silica wall, -1 LCPA droplet pore); ε: interfacial thickness parameter

equations.law_name: Fourth-Order Cahn-Hilliard Spinodal Dispersion & Wavelength Selection Law
equations.lean_code:
def cahn_hilliard_dispersion (M alpha eps_sq q : Int) : Int :=
  M * q * (alpha - eps_sq * q)
theorem cahn_hilliard_mass_conservation_zero_mode (M alpha eps_sq : Int) :
    cahn_hilliard_dispersion M alpha eps_sq 0 = 0 := by simp [cahn_hilliard_dispersion]
theorem cahn_hilliard_spinodal_band_selection :
    cahn_hilliard_dispersion 1 4 1 2 = 4 ∧
    cahn_hilliard_dispersion 1 4 1 4 = 0 ∧
    cahn_hilliard_dispersion 1 (-2) 1 1 = -3 := by decide

equations.variables: M: mobility; φ_0: mean composition; α = 1 - 3 φ_0^2: spinodal instability drive; q = k^2: squared wavenumber; k_c: fastest-growing wavenumber
equations.role: Selects the characteristic pore spacing λ_c = 2π/k_c inside the spinodal (|φ_0| < 1/√3) while guaranteeing exact mass conservation (σ(0)=0) and stability outside the spinodal
equations.source_citation: Lenoci & Camp (2008) Langmuir 24(1):217-223 Section 2; Sumper (2002) Science 295:2430

equations.law_name: Sumper (2002) Hierarchical LCPA Droplet Subdivision & Centered Hexagonal Packing Law

def centered_hexagonal_droplets (R : Nat) : Nat := 1 + 3 * R * (R + 1)
theorem sumper_2002_hierarchical_hex_packing (s0 ratio : Nat) :
    sumper_tier_scale s0 ratio 2 = ratio * (ratio * s0) ∧
    centered_hexagonal_droplets 1 = 7 ∧
    centered_hexagonal_droplets 2 = 19 := by
  simp [sumper_tier_scale, centered_hexagonal_droplets]

equations.law_name: Furukawa (1992) Directional (Centrifugal) Quench: Stability Ahead of the Advancing Front
equations.formula: a(r,t) = tanh((R0 + v t - r)/w);  ahead of the front a = -1:  σ(k) = M k^2 (-1 - ε^2 k^2) < 0  ∀ k ≠ 0;  behind it a = +1 (spinodal)
equations.lean_code:
theorem directional_quench_stable_ahead_of_front
    (M eps_sq q : Int) (hM : 0 < M) (hq : 0 < q) (he : 0 ≤ eps_sq) :
    cahn_hilliard_dispersion M (-1) eps_sq q < 0 := by
  unfold cahn_hilliard_dispersion
  have hMq : 0 < M * q := Int.mul_pos hM hq
  have heq : 0 ≤ eps_sq * q := Int.mul_nonneg he (Int.le_of_lt hq)
  have hneg : -1 - eps_sq * q < 0 := by omega
  have := Int.mul_lt_mul_of_pos_left hneg hMq
  simpa using this
equations.math_family: Fourth-Order Cahn-Hilliard Spinodal Phase Separation PDE & Hierarchical Hexagonal Packing
equations.variables: R0: initial quench radius; v: centrifugal front speed (px/time); w: front width; a(r,t) ∈ [-1, 1]: local quench drive; q = k^2
equations.role: Couples the Cahn-Hilliard equation to the radially advancing silica-precipitation front: the mixture is linearly stable until the front passes, after which demixing proceeds; slow fronts (Pe = v/(λ_c σ_max) ≲ 0.1) select radial, bifurcating costae lamellae, fast fronts concentric lamellae
equations.source_citation: Furukawa H (1992) Physica A 180:128-155; Schmid & Volcani (1983) J. Phycol. 19:387 (centrifugal valve silicification); Sumper (2002) Science 295:2430

equations.law_name: Lagging Silica-Precipitation Front: Frozen Region Inside the Quenched Disc & Irreversible Solidification
equations.formula: R(t) = R0 + v t,  R_s(t) = R(t) - lag;  0 < lag ∧ 0 < R_s(t1) ⟹ R_s(t1) < R(t1);  t1 ≤ t2 ⟹ R(t1) ≤ R(t2) ∧ R_s(t1) ≤ R_s(t2)
equations.lean_code:
def quench_front_radius (R0 v t : Nat) : Nat := R0 + v * t
def solidification_radius (R0 v lag t : Nat) : Nat := quench_front_radius R0 v t - lag
theorem frozen_front_monotone_irreversible (R0 v lag t1 t2 : Nat)
    (hlag : 0 < lag) (hsolid : 0 < solidification_radius R0 v lag t1) (ht : t1 ≤ t2) :
    solidification_radius R0 v lag t1 < quench_front_radius R0 v t1 ∧
    quench_front_radius R0 v t1 ≤ quench_front_radius R0 v t2 ∧
    solidification_radius R0 v lag t1 ≤ solidification_radius R0 v lag t2 := by
  unfold solidification_radius quench_front_radius at *
  have hv : v * t1 ≤ v * t2 := Nat.mul_le_mul_left v ht
  omega

equations.variables: lag = 1.0 λ_c: distance between quench and precipitation fronts; frozen pixels: zero mobility, value held, leaked mass re-projected onto mobile pixels (exact total conservation)
equations.role: Guarantees the model never freezes un-quenched mixture and that silica precipitation is irreversible; the same frozen-wall mechanism confines tiers 2-3 of the explicit 3-stage 512x512 single-domain quench to the unsolidified chambers of the previous tier
