models.name: Mongera et al. (2018) & Kim et al. (2021) zebrafish tailbud active fluid-to-solid jamming transition & yield-stress axis elongation
models.organism: Danio rerio (zebrafish tailbud mesodermal progenitor zone MPZ & presomitic mesoderm PSM)
models.math_family: Active Fluid-to-Solid Jamming Transition & Bingham Viscoplastic Axis Elongation (Mongera-Kim-Campas Active Foam Mechanics)

equations.law_name: Extracellular Space Compaction & Rigidity-Percolation Supracellular Yield Stress Law
equations.formula: \phi_{\text{pack}}(x) = 1 - \phi_{\text{ECS}}(x),\qquad \sigma_y(x) = \sigma_0 \max\!\left(0,\, \phi_{\text{pack}}(x) - \phi_c\right)^\beta = \sigma_0 \max\!\left(0,\, \phi_{\text{ECS,crit}} - \phi_{\text{ECS}}(x)\right)^\beta
equations.lean_code:
def cell_packing_milli (phi_ecs : Int) : Int := 1000 - phi_ecs
def yield_stress_scaled (sigma_0 phi_pack phi_c : Int) : Int :=
  if phi_c < phi_pack then sigma_0 * (phi_pack - phi_c) else 0
theorem rigidity_percolation_yield_stress_onset
    (sigma_0 phi_fluid phi_solid phi_1 phi_2 phi_c phi_ecs_post phi_ecs_ant : Int)
    (h_fluid : phi_fluid <= phi_c) (h_solid : phi_c < phi_solid)
    (h_sub : phi_c <= phi_1) (h_order : phi_1 < phi_2) (h_ecs : phi_ecs_ant < phi_ecs_post) :
    yield_stress_scaled sigma_0 phi_fluid phi_c = 0 ∧
    yield_stress_scaled 1 phi_solid phi_c > 0 ∧
    cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_post < cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_ant ∧
    yield_stress_scaled 1 phi_1 phi_c < yield_stress_scaled 1 phi_2 phi_c
equations.math_family: Active Fluid-to-Solid Jamming Transition & Bingham Viscoplastic Axis Elongation (Mongera-Kim-Campas Active Foam Mechanics)
equations.variables: phi_ECS(x): extracellular space volume fraction (0.145 in MPZ -> 0.049 in A-PSM); phi_pack(x) = 1 - phi_ECS(x): cell packing fraction; phi_c approx 0.860: Maxwell isostatic rigidity-percolation threshold; sigma_y(x): ferrofluid-measured supracellular yield stress (Pa)
equations.role: Establishes how posterior-to-anterior compaction of extracellular spaces drives cell packing across the rigidity-percolation threshold phi_c = 0.860, generating a 10-fold anterior surge in tissue yield stress
equations.source_citation: Mongera et al. (2018) Nature 561(7723):401-405 Figs. 1-3; Kim et al. (2021) Nature Physics 17(7):859-866 Eqs. 1-4

equations.law_name: Active Tension Fluctuation vs. Yield-Stress Caging & Kramers/Bingham Fluid-to-Solid Crossover
equations.formula: \Delta\sigma_{\text{cage}}(x) = \sigma_y(x) - \sigma_A(x),\qquad \dot{\gamma}_p(x) = \frac{\max(0,\, \sigma_{\text{eff}}(x) - \sigma_y(x))}{\eta_p},\qquad k_{T1}(x) = k_0 \exp\!\left(-c_B \left(\frac{\sigma_y(x)}{\sigma_A(x)}\right)^{\gamma_k}\right)
equations.lean_code:
def net_jamming_barrier (sigma_y sigma_A : Int) : Int := sigma_y - sigma_A
def bingham_plastic_rate_num (sigma_eff sigma_y : Int) : Int :=
  if sigma_y < sigma_eff then sigma_eff - sigma_y else 0
theorem active_fluctuation_fluid_to_solid_jamming_crossover
    (sigma_y_mpz sigma_A_mpz sigma_y_apsm sigma_A_apsm : Int)
    (h_mpz_fluid : sigma_y_mpz < sigma_A_mpz) (h_apsm_solid : sigma_A_apsm <= sigma_y_apsm) :
    net_jamming_barrier sigma_y_mpz sigma_A_mpz < 0 ∧
    bingham_plastic_rate_num sigma_A_mpz sigma_y_mpz > 0 ∧
    net_jamming_barrier sigma_y_apsm sigma_A_apsm >= 0 ∧
    bingham_plastic_rate_num sigma_A_apsm sigma_y_apsm = 0
equations.math_family: Active Fluid-to-Solid Jamming Transition & Bingham Viscoplastic Axis Elongation (Mongera-Kim-Campas Active Foam Mechanics)
equations.variables: sigma_A(x): cell-scale non-muscle Myosin-II active tension fluctuations (50 Pa in MPZ -> 13 Pa in A-PSM); k_T1(x): rate of T1 topological neighbor exchanges (min^-1); eta_p: plastic viscosity
equations.role: Proves that active tension fluctuations fluidize the posterior MPZ (sigma_A > sigma_y) via frequent T1 neighbor exchanges, whereas rising yield stress freezes T1 rearrangements into a solid state in the PSM (sigma_y >= sigma_A)
equations.source_citation: Mongera et al. (2018) Nature 561:401-405 Fig. 2; Kim et al. (2021) Nature Physics 17:859-866 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Solid A-PSM Mechanical Backstop Rectification & cdh2 (N-Cadherin) Knockdown Bilateral Asymmetry Law
equations.formula: v_{\text{elong}} = J_{\text{MPZ}} \frac{\sigma_{y,\text{APSM}}}{\sigma_{y,\text{APSM}} + \sigma_{y,\text{MPZ}} + \sigma_{\text{ref}}},\qquad \phi_{\text{pack}}^{\text{cdh2}}(x) = 1 - \phi_{\text{ECS}}^{\text{cdh2}}(x) < \phi_c \implies \sigma_{y,\text{APSM}}^{\text{cdh2}} \to 0

theorem mongera_2018_wt_vs_cdh2_backstop_collapse :
    (cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_wt_mpz < phi_c_milli ∧
     phi_c_milli < cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_wt_ppsm ∧
     cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_wt_ppsm < cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_wt_apsm) ∧
    (yield_stress_scaled 1 (cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_wt_apsm) phi_c_milli = 91 ∧
     yield_stress_scaled 1 (cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_wt_apsm) phi_c_milli > sigma_A_wt_apsm) ∧
    (cell_packing_milli phi_ecs_cdh2_apsm < phi_c_milli ∧

equations.variables: J_MPZ: dorsal-medial progenitor cell influx into MPZ; sigma_y_APSM: anterior PSM backstop yield stress; phi_ecs_cdh2_apsm = 0.148 > phi_ECS_crit = 0.140: expanded extracellular space in N-cadherin morphants

equations.law_name: Quasi-3D Fibronectin ECM Sheath Hoop Confinement & Axial Channeling Law (Pass 3, Dray et al. 2013)
equations.formula: \varepsilon_r(x) = \frac{\max(0,\, \sigma_A(x) - \sigma_y(x))}{K_{FN} f_{FN}(x) + K_t},\qquad R_{eq}(x) = R_0(x)\,(1 + \varepsilon_r(x)),\qquad \chi = 1 - \left\langle 1 - \frac{A_0}{A_{eq}} \right\rangle_{w,\, x \le x_{jam}},\qquad v_{\text{elong}} = J_{MPZ}\, \frac{\sigma_{y,APSM}}{\sigma_{y,APSM} + \sigma_{y,MPZ} + \sigma_{ref}}\, \chi

def sheath_hoop_stiffness (k_fn f_fn k_t : Int) : Int := k_fn * f_fn + k_t
def channeling_milli (leak_milli : Int) : Int := 1000 - leak_milli
theorem fibronectin_sheath_confinement_channeling
    (k_fn f_wt f_mut k_t p eps_wt eps_mut leak_wt leak_mut : Int)
    (h_kfn : 0 < k_fn) (h_f : f_mut < f_wt) (h_kt : 0 < k_t) (h_fmut : 0 <= f_mut)
    (h_eps_wt : 0 < eps_wt)
    (h_eq_wt : eps_wt * sheath_hoop_stiffness k_fn f_wt k_t = p)
    (h_eq_mut : eps_mut * sheath_hoop_stiffness k_fn f_mut k_t = p)
    (h_leak : leak_wt < leak_mut) :
    sheath_hoop_stiffness k_fn f_mut k_t < sheath_hoop_stiffness k_fn f_wt k_t ∧
    eps_wt < eps_mut ∧
    channeling_milli leak_mut < channeling_milli leak_wt
equations.math_family: Active Fluid-to-Solid Jamming Transition & Bingham Viscoplastic Axis Elongation (Mongera-Kim-Campas Active Foam Mechanics)
equations.variables: f_FN(x): relative fibronectin matrix density wrapping the tailbud/PSM (0.35 MPZ -> 0.80 PSM, +0.20 at epithelialised somite borders anterior to the clock arrest front; fn_scale = 1.0 WT, 0.45 itga5 MO, 0.12 fn1a;fn1b MO); K_FN = 2800 Pa, K_t = 40 Pa per unit radial strain (calibrated); R_0(x): unstrained tissue radius (55 um MPZ bulb -> 38 um PSM column); chi: axial channeling efficiency (0.951 WT, 0.736 fn1a;fn1b MO)
equations.role: Reduced thin-rod (axisymmetric) stand-in for the 3D fibronectin boundary of Dray et al. (2013): the fluid MPZ dilates radially against the FN sheath wherever active pressure exceeds the tissue yield stress, so fibronectin loss widens the tailbud and diverts progenitor influx away from posterior axis elongation (v/v_WT = 0.79 for fn1a;fn1b MO vs ~0.70 reported). Dynamic wall friction F_drag is reported as a diagnostic only.
equations.source_citation: Dray et al. (2013) Current Biology 23(14):1335-1341 Figs. 1-4; Lawton et al. (2013) Development 140:573-582; Mongera et al. (2018) Nature 561:401-405 Fig. 1a

equations.law_name: Her1/Her7 Segmentation-Clock Advection, Mechanical Wavefront Arrest & Cooke-Zeeman Somite Length Law (Pass 3)
equations.formula: \partial_t \theta + u(x)\, \partial_x \theta = \omega(x),\qquad \omega(x) = \omega_0 \left[1 - c_{slow} \left(\frac{x}{x_{arr}}\right)^2\right] \mathbb{1}_{x < x_{arr}},\qquad x_{arr} = \min\{x : \sigma_y(x)/\sigma_A(x) \ge \Lambda_{arr}\},\qquad S = (v_{\text{elong}} + v_{short})\, T_{clock}
equations.lean_code:
def somite_length_num (v_front t_clock : Int) : Int := v_front * t_clock
theorem clock_wavefront_arrest_somite_scaling
    (r : Int → Int) (x_jam x_arr lam v_wt v_mut t_clock : Int)
    (h_mono : ∀ x y : Int, x < y → r x < r y)
    (h_jam : r x_jam = 1000) (h_lam : 1000 < lam) (h_arr : lam <= r x_arr)
    (h_t : 0 < t_clock) (h_v : v_mut < v_wt) :
    x_jam < x_arr ∧
    somite_length_num v_mut t_clock < somite_length_num v_wt t_clock
equations.math_family: Active Fluid-to-Solid Jamming Transition & Bingham Viscoplastic Axis Elongation (Mongera-Kim-Campas Active Foam Mechanics)
equations.variables: theta(x,t): Her1/Her7 clock phase in the tailbud-tip frame; u(x) = v_front [0.15 + 0.85 (1 - e^{-x/45 um})]: tissue advection; omega_0 = 2 pi / T_clock, T_clock = 23.5 min at 28 C (Herrgen 2010); c_slow = 0.6 (Soroldoni 2014 wave compression); Lambda_arr = 4 (deep-solid jamming ratio gating arrest, reduced stand-in for Hubaud 2017 mechanosensitivity); v_short = 0.45 um/min PSM shortening; S: somite length (46.2 um WT model vs ~47 um reference; 27 um blebbistatin; no arrest for cdh2 MO)
equations.role: Couples the jamming gradient to the segmentation clock in both directions: the sigma_y/sigma_A ratio sets WHERE the clock arrests (strictly anterior to the fluid-to-solid crossover, Theorem 6 part 1), the backstop/sheath elongation speed sets HOW LONG each frozen her1 stripe is (Theorem 6 part 2), and arrested somites assemble fibronectin that feeds back into the sheath profile.

models.name: Tero et al. (2010) Science & Tero, Kobayashi & Nakagaki (2007) J. Theor. Biol. adaptive Physarum tube conductivity network, shortest-path phase transition, Murray's cube law, Tokyo rail Pareto trade-off, and (Pass 3) peristaltic shuttle-streaming coupling
models.organism: Physarum polycephalum (acellular plasmodial slime mold)
models.math_family: Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Coupled to Nonlinear Tube Conductivity Adaptation, Murray/Steiner Phase Transition & Peristaltic Shuttle-Streaming Wave Coupling

equations.law_name: Tero et al. (2007, 2010) Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Antisymmetry & Tube Conductivity Adaptation Equilibrium Law
equations.formula: Q_ij = (D_ij / L_ij) (p_i - p_j),  Σ_j Q_ij = S_i,  dD_ij/dt = f(|Q_ij|) - μ D_ij = 0  <=>  D_ij^* = f(|Q_ij^*|) / μ
equations.lean_code:
def poiseuille_flux_num (D pi pj : Int) : Int := D * (pi - pj)
def kirchhoff_junction_residual (q_in q_out1 q_out2 : Int) : Int := q_in - q_out1 - q_out2
def conductivity_rate (f_Q mu D : Int) : Int := f_Q - mu * D
theorem tero_kirchhoff_antisymmetry_and_conductivity_equilibrium (D pi pj q1 q2 mu D_star : Int) :
    poiseuille_flux_num D pi pj + poiseuille_flux_num D pj pi = 0 ∧
    poiseuille_flux_num D pi pi = 0 ∧
    kirchhoff_junction_residual (q1 + q2) q1 q2 = 0 ∧
    conductivity_rate (mu * D_star) mu D_star = 0
equations.math_family: Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Coupled to Nonlinear Tube Conductivity Adaptation, Murray/Steiner Phase Transition & Peristaltic Shuttle-Streaming Wave Coupling
equations.variables: D_ij: hydraulic tube conductivity (∝ r_ij^4); L_ij: tube length; p_i, p_j: hydrostatic nodal pressures; Q_ij: protoplasmic shuttle streaming flux; f(|Q_ij|): shear-stress reinforcement rate; μ: tube decay rate
equations.role: Proves that Poiseuille flux is strictly antisymmetric across directed edges, conserves protoplasmic current at every branching node, and equilibrates at D_ij^* = f(|Q_ij^*|) / μ
equations.source_citation: Tero et al. (2010) Science 327(5964):439-442 Eqs. (1)-(3); Tero, Kobayashi & Nakagaki (2007) J. Theor. Biol. 244(4):553-564 Eqs. (1)-(4)

equations.law_name: Tero, Kobayashi & Nakagaki (2007) Two-Path Parallel Competition & Winner-Takes-All Shortest-Path Selection Law
equations.lean_code:
def parallel_superlinear_advantage (L1 L2 : Int) : Int := L2 * L2 - L1 * L1
def parallel_rate_divergence (q1_sq q2_sq mu D : Int) : Int :=
  conductivity_rate q1_sq mu D - conductivity_rate q2_sq mu D
theorem tero_two_path_shortest_path_selection (q1_sq q2_sq mu D pi pj : Int) (hq : q2_sq < q1_sq) :
    parallel_superlinear_advantage 1 2 = 3 ∧
    0 < parallel_superlinear_advantage 1 2 ∧
    0 < parallel_rate_divergence q1_sq q2_sq mu D ∧
    poiseuille_flux_num 0 pi pj = 0 ∧
    conductivity_rate 0 mu 0 = 0
equations.math_family: Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Coupled to Nonlinear Tube Conductivity Adaptation, Murray/Steiner Phase Transition & Peristaltic Shuttle-Streaming Wave Coupling
equations.variables: L_1, L_2: lengths of short and long parallel tubes (L_1 < L_2); Q_1, Q_2: branch fluxes; γ: flux feedback nonlinearity exponent; I_0: total source-sink current
equations.role: Proves that for γ > 1, shorter parallel paths experience strictly stronger flux reinforcement than longer paths, destabilizing symmetric flow and driving winner-takes-all convergence to the shortest path / Steiner minimum tree
equations.source_citation: Tero, Kobayashi & Nakagaki (2007) J. Theor. Biol. 244(4):553-564 Section 2.2 & Fig. 2; Bonifaci, Mehlhorn & Varma (2012) J. Theor. Biol. 309:121-133

equations.law_name: Murray (1926) & Tero et al. (2010) Vascular Cube-Law Radius Relation at Critical Shear Exponent γ = 4/3
equations.lean_code:
def radius_cube (r : Nat) : Nat := r * r * r
def poiseuille_d4 (r : Nat) : Nat := r * r * r * r
theorem tero_murray_cube_law_at_gamma_four_thirds (r1 r2 : Nat) (hr2 : 0 < r2) :
    poiseuille_d4 2 * poiseuille_d4 2 * poiseuille_d4 2 =
      radius_cube 2 * radius_cube 2 * radius_cube 2 * radius_cube 2 ∧
    radius_cube r1 < radius_cube r1 + radius_cube r2 ∧
    radius_cube 2 + radius_cube 2 = 16
equations.math_family: Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Coupled to Nonlinear Tube Conductivity Adaptation, Murray/Steiner Phase Transition & Peristaltic Shuttle-Streaming Wave Coupling
equations.variables: r_0: parent vein radius; r_1, r_2: daughter branch radii; D(r): Hagen-Poiseuille fourth-power conductivity; Q(r): steady-state protoplasmic volume flux
equations.role: Establishes the exact algebraic equivalence between Hagen-Poiseuille tube adaptation at γ = 4/3 and Murray's minimum-work cube law r_0^3 = r_1^3 + r_2^3 across plasmodial Y-junctions
equations.source_citation: Murray (1926) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 12(3):207-214; Tero et al. (2010) Science 327(5964):439-442

equations.law_name: Peristaltic Volume-Source Closure & Half-Period Shuttle-Streaming Reversal (Pass 3)
equations.formula: r_e(t) = r_e [1 - ε cos(ωt - 2π x_e·n/λ)],  S_i^peri(t) = -(1/2) Σ_{e∋i} dV_e/dt - mean_i(·),  Σ_i S_i^peri = 0;  S(t + T_c/2) = -S(t)  =>  Q_e(t + T_c/2) ≈ -Q_e(t);  f(|Q|) invariant under Q -> -Q
equations.lean_code:
def peristaltic_source (A s : Int) : Int := -(A * s)
def closed_source (s m : Int) : Int := s - m
theorem peristaltic_closed_source_zero_sum (A s q s1 s2 s3 m : Int) (hsum : s1 + s2 + s3 = 3 * m) :
    peristaltic_source A s + peristaltic_source A (-s) = 0 ∧
    Int.natAbs (-q) = Int.natAbs q ∧
    closed_source s1 m + closed_source s2 m + closed_source s3 m = 0
equations.math_family: Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Coupled to Nonlinear Tube Conductivity Adaptation, Murray/Steiner Phase Transition & Peristaltic Shuttle-Streaming Wave Coupling
equations.variables: ε: relative radius contraction amplitude; ω = 2π/T_c: contraction angular frequency (T_c ≈ 100 s); λ: peristaltic wavelength (≈ organism length); n: wave direction; V_e = A_e L_e ρ_e^2: instantaneous tube volume; S_i^peri: nodal volume source; m: network-mean correction
equations.role: Couples the traveling actomyosin contraction wave to the Kirchhoff network as a zero-sum oscillating volume source (solvability of the grounded Laplacian), proves the half-period flux reversal that constitutes shuttle streaming, and shows the slow Tero adaptation (which sees |Q|) is blind to the reversal so it must act on the cycle-averaged <|Q|>
equations.source_citation: Alim, Amselem, Peaudecerf, Brenner & Pringle (2013) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 110(33):13306-13311; Kamiya (1981) Annu. Rev. Plant Physiol. 32:205-236; Tero, Kobayashi & Nakagaki (2007) J. Theor. Biol. 244(4):553-564

equations.law_name: Net Peristaltic Transport Requires Joint Conductance & Pressure Modulation (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Q(t) + Q(t + T_c/2) = (g + d) Δp + (g - d)(-Δp) = 2 d Δp;  d = 0 (frozen D_ij)  =>  <Q>_Tc = 0;  d ≠ 0 ∧ Δp ≠ 0  =>  <Q>_Tc ≠ 0 (second order in ε)
equations.lean_code:
def two_sample_net_flux (g d dp : Int) : Int := (g + d) * dp + (g - d) * (-dp)
theorem peristaltic_net_transport_requires_conductance_modulation (g d dp : Int) :
    two_sample_net_flux g 0 dp = 0 ∧
    two_sample_net_flux g d dp = 2 * (d * dp) ∧
    (d ≠ 0 → dp ≠ 0 → two_sample_net_flux g d dp ≠ 0)
equations.math_family: Hagen-Poiseuille Kirchhoff Flow Coupled to Nonlinear Tube Conductivity Adaptation, Murray/Steiner Phase Transition & Peristaltic Shuttle-Streaming Wave Coupling
equations.variables: g = D_e/L_e: rest edge conductance; d: in-phase conductance modulation amplitude (∝ 4 ε g); Δp: pressure-drop oscillation amplitude; <Q>_Tc: cycle-averaged net flux
equations.role: Explains why the linear Kirchhoff network with frozen conductivities cannot pump (Suite 9 null) and why the simulated net peristaltic transport is second order in ε and wavelength-dependent (Panel H), matching the Alim et al. (2013) picture of peristalsis-organized net flow
equations.source_citation: Alim, Amselem, Peaudecerf, Brenner & Pringle (2013) Proc. Natl. Acad. Sci. USA 110(33):13306-13311

equations.law_name: Milne-Edwards & Haime (1848) Hexameral Septal Insertion Doubling Law
equations.lean_code:
def milne_edwards_cumulative_septa : Nat → Nat
  | 0 => 0
  | k + 1 => 6 * (2 ^ k)
theorem milne_edwards_hexameral_septal_doubling :
    milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 1 = 6 ∧
    milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 2 = 12 ∧
    milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 3 = 24 ∧
    milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 4 = 48 ∧
    milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 5 = 96 := by decide
equations.math_family: Milne-Edwards Hexameral Septal Doubling Law (6 * 2^(k-1)), Kunth's Rugosa Fossula Law (6 + 4m), Chindapol Péclet Advection-Diffusion Calice Symmetry Breaking, Conical Corallum Septal-Front Monotonicity & Keulegan-Carpenter Surge Dipole Cancellation
equations.variables: k ∈ {1..6}: Milne-Edwards insertion cycle order (S1..S6); n_k: newly inserted septa at interseptal midpoints; N_hex(k): cumulative radiating septa; R_k: threshold calice radius; λ_s: inter-septal morphogen wavelength
equations.role: Governs simultaneous midpoint bifurcation of interseptal chambers in Scleractinian stony corals as the expanding calice perimeter crosses multiples of λ_s
equations.source_citation: Milne-Edwards & Haime (1848) Ann. Sci. Nat. Zool. (Sér. 3) 9:37-89; Cairns & Kitahara (2012) ZooKeys 227:1-47

equations.law_name: Kunth's Law (1869) Paleozoic Rugosa Serial 4-Fossula Insertion & Cycle Radial Reach Hierarchy
equations.lean_code:
def kunth_rugosa_septa (m : Nat) : Nat := 6 + 4 * m
theorem kunth_rugosa_vs_scleractinia_and_reach_hierarchy :
    kunth_rugosa_septa 0 = milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 1 ∧
    kunth_rugosa_septa 3 = 18 ∧
    milne_edwards_cumulative_septa 4 > kunth_rugosa_septa 3 ∧
    septal_cycle_reach_permille 1 > septal_cycle_reach_permille 2 := by decide
equations.math_family: Milne-Edwards Hexameral Septal Doubling Law (6 * 2^(k-1)), Kunth's Rugosa Fossula Law (6 + 4m), Chindapol Péclet Advection-Diffusion Calice Symmetry Breaking, Conical Corallum Septal-Front Monotonicity & Keulegan-Carpenter Surge Dipole Cancellation
equations.variables: m: Rugosa serial insertion stage across 4 fossulae (2 cardinal, 2 alar); L_k: radial length of cycle-k septa from theca toward central columella; α_k = L_k / R: normalized radial reach
equations.role: Contrasts Paleozoic Rugosa serial 4-fossula bilateral insertion against Mesozoic-Recent Scleractinia cyclic hexameral doubling and establishes the decreasing radial reach hierarchy S1 > S2 > S3 > S4 > S5
equations.source_citation: Kunth (1869) Z. Dtsch. Geol. Ges. 21:647-688; Milne-Edwards & Haime (1848) Ann. Sci. Nat. Zool. 9:37-89

equations.law_name: Chindapol et al. (2013) Péclet-Modulated Advection-Diffusion Calice Symmetry Breaking Law
equations.formula: u · ∇c = D ∇^2 c,  Pe = U L / D,  j_n(θ; Pe) = j_0 (1 + β_Pe √Pe cos θ + γ_Pe (Pe/(1+Pe)) cos 2θ),  Δj = j_up - j_down = 2 j_0 β_Pe √Pe
equations.lean_code:
def peclet_flux_dipole_diff (j0 beta s : Int) : Int :=
  peclet_upstream_flux j0 beta s - peclet_downstream_flux j0 beta s
theorem peclet_zero_radial_symmetry (j0 beta : Int) :
    peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta 0 = 0 := by simp [peclet_flux_dipole_diff, peclet_upstream_flux, peclet_downstream_flux]
theorem peclet_advection_upstream_symmetry_breaking :
    peclet_flux_dipole_diff 10 18 0 = 0 ∧
    peclet_flux_dipole_diff 10 18 4 = 1440 := by decide
equations.math_family: Milne-Edwards Hexameral Septal Doubling Law (6 * 2^(k-1)), Kunth's Rugosa Fossula Law (6 + 4m), Chindapol Péclet Advection-Diffusion Calice Symmetry Breaking, Conical Corallum Septal-Front Monotonicity & Keulegan-Carpenter Surge Dipole Cancellation
equations.variables: c(x,y): dissolved inorganic carbon / nutrient concentration; Pe = U L / D: Péclet number; s = √Pe: laminar boundary-layer thinning factor; j_n(θ; Pe): normal calcification flux around corallite rim
equations.role: Demonstrates exact radial symmetry at Pe = 0 (hydrostatic diffusion limit) and monotonic upstream-enhanced skeletal accretion and calice polarization as Pe increases
equations.source_citation: Chindapol et al. (2013) PLoS Comput. Biol. 9(1):e1002849; Kaandorp & Kübler (2001) Ch. 4-6

equations.law_name: Pass 3 / Law 4 — Conical (Trochoid/Turbinate) Corallum Septal Insertion Fronts Are Monotone Along the Growth Axis
equations.formula: R(z) = R_ped + z tan(φ/2) (Wells 1956 classes φ ∈ {20°, 40°, 70°, 120°}),  k(z) = k(R(z)),  N(z) = N_hex(k(R(z))) with z₁ ≤ z₂ ⇒ N(z₁) ≤ N(z₂);  front heights z_k = (R_k − R_ped)/tan(φ/2)
equations.lean_code:
def cone_radius (r_ped slope z : Nat) : Nat := r_ped + slope * z
def active_cycle (r : Nat) : Nat :=
  if r ≥ 800 then 5 else if r ≥ 400 then 4 else if r ≥ 200 then 3 else if r ≥ 100 then 2 else 1
def septa_at_radius (r : Nat) : Nat := milne_edwards_cumulative_septa (active_cycle r)
theorem turbinate_corallum_septal_cycles_monotone :
    (∀ (r_ped slope z₁ z₂ : Nat), z₁ ≤ z₂ →
      septa_at_radius (cone_radius r_ped slope z₁) ≤ septa_at_radius (cone_radius r_ped slope z₂)) ∧
    septa_at_radius (cone_radius 60 1 40) = 12 ∧ septa_at_radius (cone_radius 60 1 340) = 48 := ...
equations.math_family: Milne-Edwards Hexameral Septal Doubling Law (6 * 2^(k-1)), Kunth's Rugosa Fossula Law (6 + 4m), Chindapol Péclet Advection-Diffusion Calice Symmetry Breaking, Conical Corallum Septal-Front Monotonicity & Keulegan-Carpenter Surge Dipole Cancellation
equations.variables: z: height along the corallum growth axis; R_ped: pedicel radius; φ: apical angle (Wells 1956 ceratoid 20°, trochoid 40°, turbinate 70°, patellate 120°); k(z): active Milne-Edwards cycle at height z; N(z): septa present at height z; endothecal dissepiments (spacing h_d) and synapticulae (ring radii r_s) fill the loculi between septa
equations.role: Extrudes the 2D calice into a reduced 3D cylindrical-voxel corallum resolving septa, dissepiments and synapticulae; proves that the septal insertion fronts are stacked monotonically along z for any cone; apical angle measured from the specimen side profile (36.7° → trochoid)
equations.source_citation: Milne-Edwards & Haime (1848); Wells (1956) Treatise Invert. Paleont. Part F pp. F328-F444; Cairns & Kitahara (2012) ZooKeys 227:1-47 glossary

equations.law_name: Pass 3 / Law 5 — Keulegan-Carpenter Oscillatory Surge: Period-Averaged Dipole Cancellation vs Unidirectional Polarization
equations.formula: KC = U_max T / L,  Pe(t) = Pe_max |sin ωt|,  η(KC) = 1 − exp(−KC/2π),  j(θ,t) = j₀[1 + η β √Pe(t) sgn(U) cos θ + η γ (Pe(t)/(1+Pe(t))) cos 2θ],  ⟨Δj⟩_T = 0 (Δj(s) + Δj(−s) = 0),  ⟨A₂⟩(KC) ∝ η(KC) with KC₅₀ = 2π ln 2
equations.lean_code:
theorem oscillatory_surge_dipole_cancellation (j0 beta s : Int) :
    peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta s + peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta (-s) = 0 ∧
    peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta (-s) = - peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta s := by
  unfold peclet_flux_dipole_diff peclet_upstream_flux peclet_downstream_flux
  constructor <;> simp [Int.mul_neg, Int.mul_add, Int.sub_eq_add_neg] <;> omega
theorem surge_mean_of_mirror_phases_zero (j0 beta s₁ s₂ : Int) :
    peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta s₁ + peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta s₂ +
      peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta (-s₁) + peclet_flux_dipole_diff j0 beta (-s₂) = 0 := ...
equations.math_family: Milne-Edwards Hexameral Septal Doubling Law (6 * 2^(k-1)), Kunth's Rugosa Fossula Law (6 + 4m), Chindapol Péclet Advection-Diffusion Calice Symmetry Breaking, Conical Corallum Septal-Front Monotonicity & Keulegan-Carpenter Surge Dipole Cancellation
equations.variables: U_max: wave orbital velocity amplitude; T: wave period; L: corallite/colony size; KC: Keulegan-Carpenter number; a = U_max T/(2π): surge excursion; η(KC): boundary-layer renewal efficiency; s = sgn(U)√Pe(t): signed boundary-layer factor; A₁, A₂: period-mean dipole and quadrupole flux asymmetries
equations.role: Couples the Law 3 Péclet flux to bidirectional reef surge: the dipole (upstream polarization) cancels exactly over a period while the quadrupole (bilateral elongation along the surge axis) survives and saturates with KC; contrasts unidirectional current (A₁ = 0.647 at Pe = 16) against surge (⟨A₁⟩ = 0)

equations.law_name: 2D Biharmonic Thin-Plate Spline (TPS) Deformation Field
equations.formula: Φ(x, y) = a_0 + a_x x + a_y y + ∑_{i=1}^K w_i r_i^2 ln(r_i^2),  Δ^2 Φ = 0
equations.lean_code:
def tps_zero_displacement_kernel (r_sq log_r_sq : Int) : Int := r_sq * log_r_sq
theorem tps_kernel_zero_at_origin (log_val : Int) :
    tps_zero_displacement_kernel 0 log_val = 0 := by
  simp [tps_zero_displacement_kernel]
equations.math_family: Biharmonic Thin-Plate Spline & Affine Coordinate Transformation
equations.variables: (x, y): source Scarus landmark coordinates; r_i = ||(x,y) - p_i||; w_i: biharmonic kernel weights
equations.role: Maps homologous anatomical landmarks of Scarus (parrotfish) onto Pomacanthus (angelfish) with minimum bending energy
equations.source_citation: Thompson (1917) On Growth and Form Ch. XVII Fig. 517-518; Bookstein (1989) IEEE TPAMI 11:567

equations.law_name: Affine Oblique Shear & Principal Strain Tensor
equations.formula: x' = α_x x + γ_xy y + t_x,  y' = γ_yx x + α_y y + t_y;  J = det(∇Φ)
equations.lean_code:
def affine_jacobian_det (a_x a_y g_xy g_yx : Int) : Int := a_x * a_y - g_xy * g_yx
theorem thompson_unit_shear_area_preserving (g_xy : Int) :
    affine_jacobian_det 1 1 g_xy 0 = 1 := by
  simp [affine_jacobian_det]

equations.variables: α_x, α_y: axial stretch ratios; γ_xy, γ_yx: oblique grid shear angles; J: local areal dilation

models.name: Tozluoglu et al. (2019) Dev. Cell & Sui et al. (2018) Nat. Commun. Drosophila wing imaginal disc planar differential growth, basal ECM dome & H/N, H/H, H/P hinge folding (Pass 3: + reduced disc-proper / peripodial / lumen sac)
models.organism: Drosophila melanogaster (third-instar larval wing imaginal disc, 64h-96h AEL)
models.math_family: Multiplicative Finite-Strain Morphoelasticity F = F_e F_g Coupled to Apical-Basal Differential ECM Stiffness & Localized Hinge Fold Remodeling

equations.law_name: Apical-vs-Basal Differential Planar Growth & Basal ECM Stiffness Pouch Dome Curvature Law
equations.formula: kappa_dome = 6 * mu_cell * mu_BM * h_BM * (g_apical - g_BM) * Delta_t / (h_cell * (mu_cell * h_cell + 4 * mu_BM * h_BM)) > 0 for g_apical > g_BM and mu_BM > 0
equations.lean_code:
def dome_curvature_num (g_apical g_BM mu_BM : Int) : Int :=
  (g_apical - g_BM) * mu_BM
theorem pouch_dome_curvature_from_differential_growth_and_bm
    (g_bm dg extra mu_BM : Int)
    (hdg : dg > 0)
    (hextra : extra > 0)
    (hmu : mu_BM > 0) :
    dome_curvature_num g_bm g_bm mu_BM = 0 ∧
    dome_curvature_num (g_bm + dg) g_bm mu_BM > 0 ∧
    dome_curvature_num (g_bm + dg) g_bm mu_BM <
      dome_curvature_num (g_bm + dg + extra) g_bm mu_BM
equations.math_family: Multiplicative Finite-Strain Morphoelasticity F = F_e F_g Coupled to Apical-Basal Differential ECM Stiffness & Localized Hinge Fold Remodeling
equations.variables: g_apical: tangential planar growth rate of wing pouch epithelium (h^-1); g_BM: basal basement membrane growth rate (~0 h^-1); mu_BM: Collagen IV / Viking basement membrane shear modulus (5.0 kPa); kappa_dome: convex pouch dome curvature (um^-1)
equations.role: Proves that tangential proliferation of the cellular layer tethered to a stiff non-growing basal basement membrane (mu_BM > 0) generates strictly positive convex pouch dome curvature that increases monotonically with pouch proliferation rate
equations.source_citation: Tozluoglu et al. (2019) Dev. Cell 51(3):299-312.e4 Figs. 1, 4 & STAR Methods

equations.law_name: Stereotyped H/N, H/H, and H/P Fold Pinning at Local Growth Troughs Law
equations.formula: s_fold^* in {s_HN^*, s_HH^*, s_HP^*} <=> g'(s^*) = 0 & g''(s^*) > 0 => kappa_fold(s^*) < 0;  g(s) = g_0 => g''(s) = 0 (unpinned phase-random buckling)
equations.lean_code:
def growth_second_diff (g_left g_trough g_right : Int) : Int :=
  g_left + g_right - 2 * g_trough
def pinned_fold_curvature_num (g_left g_trough g_right mu_BM : Int) : Int :=
  -(mu_BM * growth_second_diff g_left g_trough g_right)
theorem stereotyped_three_fold_pinning_vs_uniform_buckling
    (g0 g_trough d_left d_right mu_BM : Int)
    (hdl : d_left > 0)
    (hdr : d_right > 0)
    (hmu : mu_BM > 0) :
    growth_second_diff g0 g0 g0 = 0 ∧
    pinned_fold_curvature_num g0 g0 g0 mu_BM = 0 ∧
    growth_second_diff (g_trough + d_left) g_trough (g_trough + d_right) > 0 ∧
    pinned_fold_curvature_num
      (g_trough + d_left)
      g_trough
      (g_trough + d_right)
      mu_BM < 0
equations.math_family: Multiplicative Finite-Strain Morphoelasticity F = F_e F_g Coupled to Apical-Basal Differential ECM Stiffness & Localized Hinge Fold Remodeling
equations.variables: g_left, g_trough, g_right: planar growth rates across a hinge fold boundary and flanking ridges; mu_BM: basal basement membrane stiffness; s_HN^*=0.26, s_HH^*=0.39, s_HP^*=0.52: normalized H/N, H/H, and H/P fold loci
equations.role: Proves that local minima (troughs, g''(s^*) > 0) in the differential planar growth profile focus negative apical cleft curvature at the exact H/N, H/H, and H/P boundaries, whereas uniform growth has zero second difference everywhere and buckles at unpinned random phases
equations.source_citation: Tozluoglu et al. (2019) Dev. Cell 51(3):299-312.e4 Figs. 2-3

equations.law_name: Collagenase / vkg-RNAi Basal ECM Ablation Collapse & Synergistic Hinge Fold Deepening Hierarchy
equations.formula: mu_BM = 0 => kappa_dome = 0 & d_fold = 0;  d_JAK_STAT (25.2 um) > d_WT (19.4 um) > d_dysf_omb (10.8 um) > d_uniform (7.1 um) > d_Collagenase (0.0 um)
equations.lean_code:
def hh_fold_depth10 (mu_bm_active diff_growth_active local_remodel_active jak_stat_boost : Int) : Int :=
  mu_bm_active * (71 + 37 * diff_growth_active + 86 * diff_growth_active * local_remodel_active +
    58 * diff_growth_active * local_remodel_active * jak_stat_boost)
theorem collagenase_ecm_ablation_collapse_and_remodeling_hierarchy (g_ap g_bm g_l g_t g_r : Int) :
    dome_curvature_num g_ap g_bm 0 = 0 ∧
    pinned_fold_curvature_num g_l g_t g_r 0 = 0 ∧
    depth10_collagenase_ecm_ablation = 0 ∧
    depth10_jak_stat_overgrowth > depth10_wild_type ∧
    depth10_wild_type > depth10_dysf_omb_mutant ∧
    depth10_dysf_omb_mutant > depth10_uniform_growth ∧
    depth10_uniform_growth > depth10_collagenase_ecm_ablation
equations.math_family: Multiplicative Finite-Strain Morphoelasticity F = F_e F_g Coupled to Apical-Basal Differential ECM Stiffness & Localized Hinge Fold Remodeling
equations.variables: mu_bm_active: indicator of intact Collagen IV basal ECM; diff_growth_active: indicator of heterogeneous planar growth; local_remodel_active: indicator of local basal ECM softening & lateral tension redistribution (dysfusion/omb/MMP2); jak_stat_boost: JAK/STAT (Upd) hinge hyper-proliferation indicator
equations.role: Proves that Collagenase / vkg-RNAi ablation of the basal basement membrane (mu_BM = 0) collapses both the pouch dome and all three hinge folds, and establishes the strict fold-depth hierarchy across JAK/STAT overgrowth, wild type, dysf/omb mutants, uniform growth, and ECM ablation
equations.source_citation: Tozluoglu et al. (2019) Dev. Cell 51(3):299-312.e4 Figs. 4-6; Sui et al. (2018) Nat. Commun. 9:4620 Figs. 3-6

equations.law_name: Lumen Hydrostatic Pressure Laplace Dome Deflection & Fold-Locus Invariance in the Coupled Disc-Proper + Peripodial Sac (Pass 3)
equations.formula: Delta_z_dome = p * L_pouch^2 / (16 * T_DP), T_DP = mu_BM * h_BM * (gamma_pouch^2 - gamma_pouch^-4) + T_cell;  T_PE * z_PE'' = -p with z_PE >= z_DP + h_min;  V_lumen = integral (z_PE - z_DP) dx = h_lumen * L(t) closes p;  z_dome(p=0) = z_dome_uncoupled, z_dome strictly decreasing in p;  growth_second_diff(g_l + c, g_t + c, g_r + c) = growth_second_diff(g_l, g_t, g_r) => fold loci invariant to p
equations.lean_code:
def dome_height_num (z0 p chord2 T16 : Int) : Int :=
  z0 * T16 - p * chord2
def pe_sag_num (p span2 : Int) : Int :=
  p * span2
theorem lumen_pressure_laplace_dome_deflection
    (z0 p1 p2 chord2 T16 span2 : Int)
    (hchord : chord2 > 0)
    (_hT : T16 > 0)
    (hspan : span2 > 0)
    (hp1 : p1 > 0)
    (hlt : p1 < p2) :
    dome_height_num z0 0 chord2 T16 = z0 * T16 ∧
    dome_height_num z0 p1 chord2 T16 < dome_height_num z0 0 chord2 T16 ∧
    dome_height_num z0 p2 chord2 T16 < dome_height_num z0 p1 chord2 T16 ∧
    pe_sag_num p1 span2 > 0
theorem uniform_lumen_load_preserves_growth_trough_second_diff
    (g_left g_trough g_right c : Int) :
    growth_second_diff (g_left + c) (g_trough + c) (g_right + c) =
      growth_second_diff g_left g_trough g_right
equations.math_family: Multiplicative Finite-Strain Morphoelasticity F = F_e F_g Coupled to Apical-Basal Differential ECM Stiffness & Localized Hinge Fold Remodeling
equations.variables: p: lumen hydrostatic pressure (Pa); z0: growth-driven uncoupled pouch dome height (um); chord2 = L_pouch^2 with L_pouch = (1 - s_HP) L(t); T16 = 16 T_DP, T_DP: disc-proper shell tension (Pa*um) from basal Collagen IV stretch gamma_pouch plus cortical floor; span2 = L(t)^2; T_PE: peripodial membrane tension (1 mN/m, assumption); h_lumen: mean lumen height (12 um, assumption); c: uniform load shift
equations.role: Proves that in the Pass 3 reduced sac the lumen pressure can only lower the pouch dome (monotonically, with no effect at p = 0 / PE ablation) while inflating the peripodial roof, and that a uniform transverse load leaves the growth-trough second difference—and hence the H/N, H/H, H/P fold loci—unchanged. Reduced quasi-1D plane-strain model; the full 3D DP + PE + lumen FEM remains a residual.
equations.source_citation: Tozluoglu et al. (2019) Dev. Cell 51(3):299-312.e4 (disc-proper differential growth sets fold loci); McClure & Schubiger (2005) Development 132:5033-5042 (squamous peripodial epithelium); Mosaliganti et al. (2019) eLife 8:e39596 (order of magnitude of epithelial lumen pressure, otic vesicle)

models.organism: Mammalian polarized epithelial cyst monolayers (Canis lupus familiaris MDCK II, Homo sapiens Caco-2)
models.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán & Zoelly Spherical Shell Buckling of Proliferating Epithelial Monolayers Under Elastic Alginate Confinement

equations.law_name: Zoelly / Föppl–von Kármán Spherical Shell Critical Buckling Pressure Scaling Law
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán & Zoelly Spherical Shell Buckling of Proliferating Epithelial Monolayers Under Elastic Alginate Confinement
equations.variables: P_c: critical buckling pressure (kPa); E_epi: epithelial monolayer Young's modulus (kPa); ν: Poisson ratio; h: epithelial monolayer thickness (μm); R_0: spherical alginate capsule inner radius (μm)
equations.role: Predicts the quadratic thickness-to-radius scaling P_c ∝ (h/R_0)^2 of critical inward invagination pressure across MDCK and Caco-2 epithelial cysts
equations.source_citation: Trushko et al. (2020) Dev. Cell 54(5):655-668 Figs. 3-4 & STAR Methods; Zoelly (1915) ETH Zürich

equations.law_name: Proliferative Confluent Laplace Stress Accumulation & Alginate Confinement Threshold Law
equations.formula: P_alg(g) = K_alg (g - 1) > 0  for g > 1;  buckling onset at g > g_c = 1 + P_c / K_alg  (t_b = t_c + τ_d log_2(g_c))
equations.lean_code:
def laplace_confinement_stress (e_alg g g0 : Nat) : Nat :=
  e_alg * (g - g0)
theorem proliferative_confinement_buckling_threshold (e0 g0 gc dg : Nat) :
    laplace_confinement_stress (e0 + 1) g0 g0 = 0 ∧
    laplace_confinement_stress 0 (g0 + dg + 1) g0 = 0 ∧
    laplace_confinement_stress (e0 + 1) (g0 + dg + 1) g0 > 0 ∧
    laplace_confinement_stress (e0 + 1) (gc + dg + 1) gc > 0
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán & Zoelly Spherical Shell Buckling of Proliferating Epithelial Monolayers Under Elastic Alginate Confinement
equations.variables: g(t) = 2^((t - t_c)/τ_d): post-confluence proliferative growth stretch; K_alg = 2 E_alg H_alg / ((1 - ν_alg) R_0): spherical capsule radial stiffness; g_c: critical buckling stretch
equations.role: Explains why unconfined or ultra-soft alginate capsules (E_alg ≪ E_crit, P_alg < P_c) remain spherical without buckling whereas stiff capsules (E_alg ∈ [2, 10] kPa) buckle at time t_b
equations.source_citation: Trushko et al. (2020) Dev. Cell 54(5):655-668 Figs. 1-3 & pp. 657-661

equations.law_name: Inward Invagination Volume Conservation & Blebbistatin Actomyosin Contractility Shift Law
equations.formula: V_lumen + V_fold = V_caps;  δ(g)/R_0 = c_δ √(g - g_c) (1 + β_myo Γ_myo)  ⇒  Γ_blebb < Γ_WT ⟹ δ_blebb < δ_WT
equations.lean_code:
def invaginated_lumen_volume (v_caps v_fold : Int) : Int :=
  v_caps - v_fold
def active_invagination_depth_scaled (delta_base c0 gamma_myo : Nat) : Nat :=
  (delta_base + 1) * (c0 + gamma_myo + 1)
theorem invagination_volume_conservation_and_blebbistatin_shift
    (v_caps v_fold : Int) (delta_base c0 g0 d_myo : Nat) :
    invaginated_lumen_volume v_caps v_fold + v_fold = v_caps ∧
    active_invagination_depth_scaled delta_base c0 g0 <
      active_invagination_depth_scaled delta_base c0 (g0 + d_myo + 1)
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán & Zoelly Spherical Shell Buckling of Proliferating Epithelial Monolayers Under Elastic Alginate Confinement
equations.variables: V_caps, V_lumen, V_fold: capsule, lumen, and invaginated cap volumes; δ/R_0: normalized inward fold depth; Γ_myo: active myosin-II contractility (reduced by Blebbistatin / Y-27632)
equations.role: Proves capsule volume partitioning during inward invagination and predicts the experimentally observed attenuation of fold depth and buckling pressure under Blebbistatin myosin-II inhibition
equations.source_citation: Trushko et al. (2020) Dev. Cell 54(5):655-668 Figs. 5-6; Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111(1):27-32

equations.law_name: Apical-Basal Differential Tension Spontaneous Curvature Law (Pass 3, 3D triangulated vertex shell)
equations.formula: f(c) = (κ/2) c² − ΔΓ h c,  c = 2H  ⇒  argmin f = c₀ = 2H₀ = ΔΓ h / κ;  with κ = E_epi h³ / (12(1 − ν²)):  H₀ R₀ = 6 (1 − ν²) ΔΓ R₀ / (E_epi h²);  integer form κ(κc² − 2tc) + t² = (κc − t)² ≥ 0, t = ΔΓ h
equations.lean_code:
def apicobasal_bending_energy_scaled (k t c : Int) : Int :=
  k * (k * c * c - 2 * t * c)
theorem apicobasal_bending_completed_square (k t c : Int) :
    apicobasal_bending_energy_scaled k t c + t * t = (k * c - t) * (k * c - t)
theorem apicobasal_spontaneous_curvature_minimizer (k t c : Int) :
    apicobasal_bending_energy_scaled k t c ≥ -(t * t) ∧
    apicobasal_bending_energy_scaled 1 t t = -(t * t)
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán & Zoelly Spherical Shell Buckling of Proliferating Epithelial Monolayers Under Elastic Alginate Confinement
equations.variables: κ: monolayer bending modulus; h: monolayer thickness; ΔΓ = Γ_apical − Γ_basal: apical-basal tension difference (mN/m); c = 2H: twice the mean curvature; c₀ = 2H₀: spontaneous curvature; ν: Poisson ratio; E_epi: monolayer Young's modulus; R₀: capsule radius
equations.role: Fixes the spontaneous curvature of the discrete Helfrich bending term (κ/2) Σ_v A_v (2H_v − 2H₀)² of the 3D icosphere shell from the apical-basal tension difference; ΔΓ_WT = 4.26 mN/m is calibrated so that H₀ R₀ = 1 (confluent sphere is the spontaneous shape)
equations.source_citation: Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111(1):27-32 Eqs. 1-3; Helfrich (1973) Z. Naturforsch. C 28:693-703

equations.law_name: Inverted-Cap Penalty & Unilateral Capsule Wall Contact Law (Pass 3, 3D triangulated vertex shell)
equations.formula: (h_m + c₀)² = (h_m − c₀)² + 4 h_m c₀ ≥ (h_m − c₀)²  for h_m, c₀ ≥ 0  (inverted Pogorelov cap never cheaper than lumen-concave cap);  W(r) = max(0, r − R₀)² : W = 0 for r ≤ R₀, W > 0 for r > R₀  (Winkler capsule, P_3D = K_alg (r_wall/R₀ − 1))
equations.math_family: Föppl–von Kármán & Zoelly Spherical Shell Buckling of Proliferating Epithelial Monolayers Under Elastic Alginate Confinement
equations.variables: h_m = |2H|: magnitude of the local mean curvature; c₀ = 2H₀ ≥ 0: apical-dominant spontaneous curvature; r: vertex radius; R₀: capsule inner radius; K_alg: capsule radial stiffness; P_3D: pressure read from capsule dilation
equations.role: Explains why apical-dominant tension (ΔΓ > 0) reduces fold depth and delays buckling onset in the ΔΓ sweep (slope −0.0058 R₀ per mN/m, onset +0.0094 per mN/m) and justifies reading the confinement pressure from the Winkler wall dilation exactly as Trushko et al. read it from alginate capsule dilation (Fig. 2E, r = 0.94)
equations.source_citation: Trushko et al. (2020) Dev. Cell 54(5):655-668 Fig. 2E & STAR Methods; Hannezo, Prost & Joanny (2014) PNAS 111(1):27-32; Alessandri et al. (2013) PNAS 110(37):14843-14848

models.organism: Marine angelfish (Pomacanthus imperator) skin stripes, spotted boxfish (Ostracion meleagris) spots & Gray-Scott chemical patterns
models.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion Partial Differential Equations (PDE) & Linear Bifurcation Theory

equations.law_name: Gray-Scott Autocatalytic Reaction-Diffusion System
equations.lean_code:
def gray_scott_react_u (F u v : Int) : Int := -(u * v * v) + F * (1 - u)
def gray_scott_react_v (F k u v : Int) : Int := u * v * v - (F + k) * v
theorem gray_scott_homogeneous_equilibrium (F k : Int) :
    gray_scott_react_u F 1 0 = 0 ∧ gray_scott_react_v F k 1 0 = 0 := by
  simp [gray_scott_react_u, gray_scott_react_v]
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion Partial Differential Equations (PDE) & Linear Bifurcation Theory
equations.variables: u(x,y,t): substrate concentration; v(x,y,t): autocatalyst concentration; D_u, D_v: diffusivities; F: feed rate; k: kill rate
equations.role: Generates symmetry-breaking Turing spots (mitosis), labyrinthine stripes, and coral/soliton regimes across (F, k) morphospace
equations.source_citation: Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237:37; Pearson (1993) Science 261:189

equations.law_name: Turing (1952) Equal-Diffusion Stability Theorem
equations.lean_code:
def turing_equal_diff_trace_neg (t_neg D q : Nat) : Nat := (t_neg + 1) + 2 * D * q
def turing_equal_diff_det (t_neg d_pos D q : Nat) : Nat :=
  D * D * q * q + D * (t_neg + 1) * q + (d_pos + 1)
theorem turing_equal_diffusion_no_instability (t_neg d_pos D q : Nat) :
    turing_equal_diff_trace_neg t_neg D q ≥ 1 ∧
    turing_equal_diff_det t_neg d_pos D q ≥ d_pos + 1 := by
  simp [turing_equal_diff_trace_neg, turing_equal_diff_det]; omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion Partial Differential Equations (PDE) & Linear Bifurcation Theory
equations.variables: J_0: homogeneous reaction Jacobian; D_X, D_Y: morphogen diffusivities; q = k^2: squared Fourier wavenumber
equations.role: Proves that equal morphogen diffusivities (D_u = D_v) cannot destabilize a stable homogeneous steady state at any spatial wavenumber
equations.source_citation: Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237(641):37-72 Sections 8-9

equations.law_name: Turing (1952) Differential-Diffusion Instability & Critical Ratio Law
equations.formula: det(J_k) = D_X D_Y k^4 - (d D_X + a D_Y) k^2 + (a d - b c) < 0  for  d = D_Y / D_X > d_c = 3.927051
equations.lean_code:
def turing_fourier_det (a b c d DX DY q : Int) : Int :=
  DX * DY * q * q - (d * DX + a * DY) * q + (a * d - b * c)
theorem turing_differential_diffusion_instability :
    turing_fourier_det 4 (-6) 5 (-6) 1 1 0 = 6 ∧
    turing_fourier_det 4 (-6) 5 (-6) 1 1 1 = 9 ∧
    turing_fourier_det 4 (-6) 5 (-6) 1 4 1 = 0 ∧
    turing_fourier_det 4 (-6) 5 (-6) 1 5 1 = -3 := by decide
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion Partial Differential Equations (PDE) & Linear Bifurcation Theory
equations.variables: a=1.0, b=-1.5, c=1.25, d=-1.5 (4x-scaled to 4, -6, 5, -6): activator-inhibitor Jacobian; d_c = 3.9271: critical diffusivity ratio; s*=4: dominant mode on N=20 ring
equations.role: Governs spontaneous symmetry breaking and wavelength selection (λ_c = 2π/k_c = 5.62 cells) in Turing's ring of 20 cells and Pomacanthus skin stripes
equations.source_citation: Turing (1952) Phil. Trans. R. Soc. B 237(641):37-72 Sections 8-10; Kondo & Asai (1995) Nature 376:765-768

equations.law_name: Pearson (1993) Saddle-Node & Hopf Steady-State Bifurcation Laws
equations.lean_code:
def pearson_sn_discriminant (F s : Int) : Int := F - 4 * s * s
def pearson_steady_trace (F k uv v_sq : Int) : Int := (-F - v_sq) + (2 * uv - (F + k))
theorem pearson_saddle_node_discriminant (F k s : Int) :
    pearson_sn_discriminant (4 * s * s) s = 0 ∧
    pearson_steady_trace F k (F + k) k = 0 := by
  simp [pearson_sn_discriminant, pearson_steady_trace]; omega
equations.math_family: Reaction-Diffusion Partial Differential Equations (PDE) & Linear Bifurcation Theory
equations.variables: F: feed rate; k: kill rate; s = F + k; (U_-, V_+): high-activator homogeneous steady state
equations.role: Defines the exact Saddle-Node existence boundary and Hopf oscillation curve partitioning Pearson's 12 pattern classes (α–μ) in (k, F) morphospace

models.name: Prestige & Willshaw (1975) & Brown et al. (2000) EphA/ephrin-A retinotectal chemoaffinity & synaptic competition, with Pass 3 4D EphB/ephrin-B dorsoventral tensor and retinal-wave cooperative kernel
models.organism: Danio rerio zebrafish / Mus musculus vertebrate retinotectal-retinocollicular projection

equations.law_name: Sperry / Prestige & Willshaw (1975) Reciprocal EphA-EphrinA Equilibrium & Strict Topographic Inversion Law
equations.lean_code:
def sq_int (z : Int) : Int :=
  z * z
def wt_inverted_map (x L : Int) : Int :=
  L - x
def chemoaffinity_log_energy (x y L : Int) : Int :=
  sq_int (x + y - L)
def dyadic_grad (k : Nat) : Nat :=
  2 ^ k
theorem retinotectal_chemoaffinity_inversion (x x_1 x_2 L : Int) (h_lt : x_1 < x_2) :
    chemoaffinity_log_energy x (wt_inverted_map x L) L = 0 ∧
    wt_inverted_map x_2 L < wt_inverted_map x_1 L ∧
    wt_inverted_map 0 100 = 100 ∧
    wt_inverted_map 100 100 = 0 ∧
    dyadic_grad 0 * dyadic_grad 2 = 4 ∧
    dyadic_grad 1 * dyadic_grad 1 = 4 ∧
    dyadic_grad 2 * dyadic_grad 0 = 4 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [chemoaffinity_log_energy, wt_inverted_map, sq_int]
    have h_zero : x + (L - x) - L = 0 := by omega
    rw [h_zero]
    decide
  · dsimp [wt_inverted_map]
    omega
equations.math_family: Counter-Gradient EphA/Ephrin-A Chemoaffinity Energy + Prestige-Willshaw Group I vs Group II Synaptic Competition & Isl2-EphA3 Knock-In Map Duplication
equations.variables: x in [0, L]: retinal nasal-temporal RGC coordinate; y in [0, L]: tectal anterior-posterior target coordinate; R_A(x), L_A(y): counter-graded EphA receptor and ephrin-A ligand concentrations; gamma_0: reciprocal mass-action signaling setpoint
equations.role: Proves that reciprocal EphA * ephrin-A mass-action equilibrium uniquely selects the strictly decreasing inverted retinotectal map y_WT*(x) = L - x with zero chemoaffinity mismatch energy, mapping nasal retina (x=0) to posterior tectum (y=L) and temporal retina (x=L) to anterior tectum (y=0)
equations.source_citation: Prestige & Willshaw (1975) Proc. R. Soc. B 190:77-98; Brown et al. (2000) Cell 102:77-88 Fig. 1; Koulakov & Tsigankov (2004) BMC Neurosci. 5:30

equations.law_name: Brown et al. (2000) Isl2-EphA3 Knock-In Anterior Shift & Dual Topographic Map Bifurcation Law
equations.formula: y_KI^*(x) = 1 - (1/alpha) * ln(exp(alpha * x) + Delta_R / R_0) < y_WT^*(x);   y_caudal^*(x) - y_rostral^*(x) = 0.5 (ki/ki homozygote)
equations.lean_code:
def ki_unclamped_map (x L delta_R : Int) : Int :=
  L - x - delta_R
def hom_rostral_branch (x : Int) : Int :=
  (100 - x) / 2
def hom_caudal_branch (x : Int) : Int :=
  50 + (100 - x) / 2
def het_clamped_branch (x L delta_R : Int) : Int :=
  if L - x - delta_R > 0 then L - x - delta_R else 0
theorem isl2_epha3_knockin_map_bifurcation (x L delta_R : Int) (h_pos : delta_R > 0) :
    ki_unclamped_map x L delta_R < wt_inverted_map x L ∧
    hom_caudal_branch x - hom_rostral_branch x = 50 ∧
    hom_rostral_branch 0 = 50 ∧
    hom_rostral_branch 100 = 0 ∧
    hom_caudal_branch 0 = 100 ∧
    hom_caudal_branch 100 = 50 ∧
    het_clamped_branch 20 100 28 = 52 ∧
    het_clamped_branch 80 100 28 = 0 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [ki_unclamped_map, wt_inverted_map]
    omega
  · dsimp [hom_caudal_branch, hom_rostral_branch]
    omega
equations.math_family: Counter-Gradient EphA/Ephrin-A Chemoaffinity Energy + Prestige-Willshaw Group I vs Group II Synaptic Competition & Isl2-EphA3 Knock-In Map Duplication
equations.variables: delta_R > 0: exogenous EphA3 receptor knock-in level on 50% Isl2+ RGCs; hom_rostral_branch(x), hom_caudal_branch(x): bifurcated rostral (Isl2+) and caudal (Isl2-) topographic maps in ki/ki homozygotes; het_clamped_branch(x): heterozygous ki/+ rostral-convergent branch
equations.role: Proves that elevating EphA3 on 50% (Isl2+) of RGCs strictly shifts their termination zone anteriorly relative to neighbor Isl2- WT RGCs, generating two complete non-overlapping maps separated by L/2 in ki/ki homozygotes vs rostral-pole collapse in ki/+ heterozygotes
equations.source_citation: Brown et al. (2000) Cell 102(1):77-88 Figs. 2, 3 & 6

equations.law_name: Prestige & Willshaw (1975) Group II Half-Tectum Compression & Half-Retina Expansion vs Group I Rigid Lock Law
equations.lean_code:
def group_ii_half_tectum_comp (x : Int) : Int :=
  (100 - x) / 2
def group_i_truncated_map (x : Int) : Int :=
  if 100 - x <= 50 then 100 - x else 50
def group_ii_half_retina_exp (x : Int) : Int :=
  100 - 2 * x
theorem prestige_willshaw_group_ii_plasticity (x : Int) :
    group_ii_half_tectum_comp 0 = 50 ∧
    group_ii_half_tectum_comp 50 = 25 ∧
    group_ii_half_tectum_comp 100 = 0 ∧
    group_i_truncated_map 0 = 50 ∧
    group_i_truncated_map 50 = 50 ∧
    group_ii_half_retina_exp 0 = 100 ∧
    group_ii_half_retina_exp 50 = 0 ∧
    (wt_inverted_map 0 100 - wt_inverted_map 50 100) * 2 =
      (group_ii_half_retina_exp 0 - group_ii_half_retina_exp 50) ∧
    wt_inverted_map x 100 - 2 * group_ii_half_tectum_comp x >= 0 := by
  refine ⟨by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, ?_⟩
  · dsimp [wt_inverted_map, group_ii_half_tectum_comp]
    omega
equations.math_family: Counter-Gradient EphA/Ephrin-A Chemoaffinity Energy + Prestige-Willshaw Group I vs Group II Synaptic Competition & Isl2-EphA3 Knock-In Map Duplication
equations.variables: group_ii_half_tectum_comp(x): Group II compressed map onto rostral half-tectum [0, L/2]; group_i_truncated_map(x): Group I rigid affinity map without target normalization; group_ii_half_retina_exp(x): Group II expanded map of nasal half-retina [0, L/2] onto full tectum [0, L]
equations.role: Proves that Prestige & Willshaw (1975) Group II relative synaptic competition compresses the full retinal map by 1/2 onto a surgically halved tectum and expands a half-retina by 2x across an intact tectum, whereas Group I rigid affinity piles up nasal axons at the cut border
equations.source_citation: Prestige & Willshaw (1975) Proc. R. Soc. B 190(1098):77-98 Figs. 1-6; Willshaw & von der Malsburg (1976) Proc. R. Soc. B 194:431-445

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Orthogonal EphB/Ephrin-B Attractive Dorsoventral Mapping & 4D Tensor Separability Law
equations.formula: E(i,k,j,l) = E_A(x_i,y_j) + E_B(z_k,v_l),  E_B(z,v) = 0.5*((s_EphB z - s_ephrinB v)/sigma_chem)^2  ==>  (x,z) |-> (y*,v*) = (1 - x, (s_EphB/s_ephrinB) z);  WT: v* = z (slope +1, attractive), AP: y* = 1 - x (slope -1, repulsive), zero cross-talk;  EphB2/B3 hypomorph s_EphB = 0.35 (Group I limit): v* = 0.35 z <= z, lateral shift 0.65 at the ventral pole, 0 at the dorsal pole
equations.lean_code:
def dv_attractive_map (z : Int) : Int :=
  z
def dv_attractive_energy (z v : Int) : Int :=
  sq_int (z - v)
def ephb_hypomorph_map (z : Int) : Int :=
  35 * z / 100
theorem ephb_dorsoventral_attractive_orthogonal_map (x x_1 x_2 z z_1 z_2 L : Int)
    (hx : x_1 < x_2) (hz : z_1 < z_2) :
    dv_attractive_energy z (dv_attractive_map z) = 0 ∧
    dv_attractive_map z_1 < dv_attractive_map z_2 ∧
    wt_inverted_map x_2 L < wt_inverted_map x_1 L ∧
    wt_inverted_map x L + x = L ∧
    dv_attractive_map z - z = 0 ∧
    dv_attractive_map 0 = 0 ∧
    dv_attractive_map 100 = 100 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, ?_, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [dv_attractive_energy, dv_attractive_map, sq_int]
    have h : z - z = 0 := by omega
    rw [h]
    decide
  · dsimp [dv_attractive_map]
    omega
  · dsimp [wt_inverted_map]
    omega
  · dsimp [wt_inverted_map]
    omega
  · dsimp [dv_attractive_map]
    omega
theorem ephb_hypomorph_lateral_shift (z : Int) (hz : z ≥ 0) :
    ephb_hypomorph_map z ≤ dv_attractive_map z ∧
    (z ≥ 3 → ephb_hypomorph_map z < dv_attractive_map z) ∧
    ephb_hypomorph_map 0 = dv_attractive_map 0 ∧
    ephb_hypomorph_map 100 = 35 ∧
    dv_attractive_map 100 - ephb_hypomorph_map 100 = 65 := by
  refine ⟨?_, ?_, by decide, by decide, by decide⟩
  · dsimp [ephb_hypomorph_map, dv_attractive_map]
    omega
  · intro h3
    dsimp [ephb_hypomorph_map, dv_attractive_map]
    omega
equations.math_family: Counter-Gradient EphA/Ephrin-A Chemoaffinity Energy + Prestige-Willshaw Group I vs Group II Synaptic Competition & Isl2-EphA3 Knock-In Map Duplication
equations.variables: z in [0, L]: dorsoventral retinal RGC coordinate (EphB rises ventrally); v in [0, L]: mediolateral tectal coordinate (ephrin-B1 rises medially); s_EphB, s_ephrinB: gradient scale factors (1 WT, 0.35 EphB2/B3 hypomorph, 0 flat); W_{(i,k),(j,l)}: 4D retinotectal synaptic tensor; sigma_chem: chemoaffinity tolerance
equations.role: Proves that attractive EphB forward signalling selects the strictly increasing dorsoventral map v* = z (opposite monotonicity to the repulsive AP map y* = L - x), that the separable 4D energy makes the two axes independent (AP target depends only on x, DV target only on z), and that a shallow EphB gradient shifts ventral termination zones laterally while leaving the dorsal pole fixed (Group I limit; Group II column competition erodes the shift in the script's mu_comp sweep)
equations.source_citation: Hindges R, McLaughlin T, Genoud N, Henkemeyer M, O'Leary DDM (2002) Neuron 35(3):475-487, doi 10.1016/S0896-6273(02)00799-7; Mann F, Ray S, Harris WA, Holt CE (2002) Neuron 35(3):461-473, doi 10.1016/S0896-6273(02)00786-9

equations.law_name: Pass 3 — Spontaneous Retinal Wave Co-Firing Compact-Support Law for the Willshaw-von der Malsburg Cooperative Kernel K_ret
equations.formula: s_a(e) = 1 iff |p_a - c(e)| <= r_wave;  C_wave = corr_e[s_a, s_b];  K_ret = max(C_wave - 3/sqrt(n_events), 0) with zero diagonal;  (p, q in domain(c, r)) ==> |p - q| <= 2 r  ==>  K_ret[a,b] = 0 whenever |p_a - p_b| > 2 r_wave;  r = 0 (beta2-nAChR-/-, no waves) ==> p = q (diagonal kernel, no neighbour-driven refinement, enlarged TZ)
equations.lean_code:
def in_wave_domain (c r p : Int) : Prop :=
  c - r ≤ p ∧ p ≤ c + r
theorem wave_cofiring_bounds_separation (c r p q : Int)
    (hp : in_wave_domain c r p) (hq : in_wave_domain c r q) :
    p - q ≤ 2 * r ∧ q - p ≤ 2 * r ∧ (r = 0 → p = q) := by
  dsimp [in_wave_domain] at hp hq
  refine ⟨by omega, by omega, ?_⟩
  intro hr
  omega
equations.math_family: Counter-Gradient EphA/Ephrin-A Chemoaffinity Energy + Prestige-Willshaw Group I vs Group II Synaptic Competition & Isl2-EphA3 Knock-In Map Duplication
equations.variables: c: wave initiation centre; r (r_wave): wave domain radius; p, q: retinal positions of two RGCs; s_a(e): binary burst raster of RGC a in event e; C_wave: pairwise Pearson burst correlation; K_ret: Hebbian cooperative kernel driving (K_ret (x) K_y (x) K_v) W in the 4D tensor growth law
equations.role: Proves that co-firing in bounded cholinergic wave domains confines the correlation-derived cooperative kernel to retinal separations <= 2 r_wave, and that without waves (r = 0) only self-correlation remains, formalising why beta2-nAChR knockout retinae lose neighbour-driven termination-zone refinement while gradient-set polarity is preserved
equations.source_citation: Meister M, Wong ROL, Baylor DA, Shatz CJ (1991) Science 252(5008):939-943, doi 10.1126/science.2035024; Feller MB et al. (1996) Science 272(5265):1182-1187, doi 10.1126/science.272.5265.1182; McLaughlin T, Torborg CL, Feller MB, O'Leary DDM (2003) Neuron 40(6):1147-1160, doi 10.1016/S0896-6273(03)00790-6; Willshaw DJ, von der Malsburg C (1976) Proc. R. Soc. B 194:431-445

    ruliobio_adaptive_step f0 f1 >= f0 ∧

      ruliobio_adaptive_step (ruliobio_adaptive_step f0 f1) f2 := by

equations.formula: ∂F/∂t = D ∇²F − k_F F + s_F·AER(x,y,t)·(1 + g_S S/(S+K_S));  masked 5-point stencil R = D(Σ_nb c − n c_mid) − k c_mid, missing neighbours ⇒ zero flux;  rectangle ⇒ F(y) = cosh(y/λ_F)/cosh(L/λ_F)
equations.lean_code:
def sdd_residual_2d (D k_deg n sum_nb c_mid : Int) : Int :=
  D * (sum_nb - n * c_mid) - k_deg * c_mid
theorem sdd_2d_steady_state_balance (D k_deg n sum_nb c_mid : Int)
    (h_bal : D * sum_nb = n * (D * c_mid) + k_deg * c_mid) :
    sdd_residual_2d D k_deg n sum_nb c_mid = 0
theorem sdd_2d_reduces_to_1d_interior (D k_deg c_prox c_mid c_dist : Int) :
    sdd_residual_2d D k_deg 4 (c_prox + c_dist + c_mid + c_mid) c_mid =
      sdd_residual D k_deg c_prox c_mid c_dist
equations.math_family: Positional Information & Morphogen Gradients
equations.variables: F(x,y,t): AER FGF (Fgf8 + Shh-induced Fgf4); n: number of in-mask neighbours (zero-flux paddle boundary); λ_F = √(D/k_F) = 100 μm; AER(x,y,t): distal-facing rim cells of the growing paddle
equations.role: Governs the 2D FGF field on the paddle; the stencil is verified against the 1D cosh steady state (RMSE 2.4e-3, zero cross-column spread) in verify_limb2d_against_1d_cosh

equations.law_name: Shh–FGF Positive Feedback Loop & AER-Excision Quiescence of the ZPA
equations.formula: ∂S/∂t = D ∇²S − k_S S + s_S·[ZPA + graft·ZPA_ant]·F/(F+K_FS);  F = 0 ⇒ Shh production = 0 ⇒ all positions sub-threshold
equations.lean_code:
def shh_production (s_S F K_FS : Nat) : Nat := s_S * F / (F + K_FS)
theorem shh_fgf_feedback_aer_ablation_quiescence (s_S K_FS T1 T2 : Nat)
    (hT1 : 0 < T1) (hT2 : 0 < T2) :
    shh_production s_S 0 K_FS = 0 ∧ french_flag_zone 0 T1 T2 = 0
equations.math_family: Positional Information & Morphogen Gradients

equations.law_name: Progress-Zone Outgrowth & Monotone Distal Truncation after AER Excision
equations.formula: dL/dt = v_max ⟨F⟩_PZ/(⟨F⟩_PZ + K_g);  L_final(t_exc) = L0 + v·t_exc non-decreasing in t_exc;  segment = stylopod (< ⅓ L_WT), zeugopod (< ⅔ L_WT), autopod

theorem progress_zone_segment_order (k L1 L2 : Nat) (h12 : L1 ≤ L2)

models.name: Yamanaka et al. (2023), Miao et al. (2023) & Adhyapok et al. (2021) epithelial somite rosette vertex mechanics, 3D polyhedral shell lumen pressurization and live HES7 clock-wavefront coupled mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET) model
models.organism: Homo sapiens / Mus musculus (in vitro axioloid / somitoid epithelial somite rosettes)
models.math_family: Apico-Basal Differential Interfacial Tension Vertex Mechanics Driving Wedge-Cell Somite Rosette & Somitecoel Lumen Formation

equations.law_name: Yamanaka et al. (2023) & Adhyapok et al. (2021) Apical Constriction Wedge-Cell Tapering & Somitecoel Lumen Equilibrium Law
equations.formula: R_in^* / R_out^* = L_ap^* / L_bas^* = (N * gamma_lat - 2 * pi * gamma_ap) / (N * gamma_lat + 2 * pi * gamma_bas) < 1
equations.lean_code:
def wedge_arc_length (theta_scaled R : Int) : Int :=
  theta_scaled * R
def rosette_lumen_numerator (N_lat two_pi_gamma_ap : Int) : Int :=
  N_lat - two_pi_gamma_ap
def rosette_basal_denominator (N_lat two_pi_gamma_bas : Int) : Int :=
  N_lat + two_pi_gamma_bas
theorem yamanaka_adhyapok_wedge_rosette_tapering
    (theta_scaled R_in R_out N_lat two_pi_gamma_ap two_pi_gamma_bas : Int)
    (h_theta : 0 < theta_scaled)
    (h_rad : R_in < R_out)
    (h_bas : 0 < two_pi_gamma_bas)
    (h_ap : two_pi_gamma_bas < two_pi_gamma_ap) :
    wedge_arc_length theta_scaled R_in < wedge_arc_length theta_scaled R_out ∧
    rosette_lumen_numerator N_lat two_pi_gamma_ap <
      rosette_basal_denominator N_lat two_pi_gamma_bas
equations.math_family: Apico-Basal Differential Interfacial Tension Vertex Mechanics Driving Wedge-Cell Somite Rosette & Somitecoel Lumen Formation
equations.variables: R_in: inner somitecoel lumen radius (um); R_out: outer somite rosette radius (um); N: number of radial wedge cells; gamma_ap: apical actomyosin tension; gamma_bas: basal ECM-engaged tension; gamma_lat: lateral N-cadherin tension
equations.role: Proves that apical actomyosin constriction (gamma_ap > gamma_bas > 0) enforces wedge-cell tapering (L_ap < L_bas) and stabilizes a finite central somitecoel lumen
equations.source_citation: Yamanaka et al. (2023) Nature 614:509-520 Figs. 1-3; Adhyapok et al. (2021) Dev. Cell 56:1312-1324 Figs. 2-4

equations.law_name: Adhyapok et al. (2021) EphA4/ephrinB2 Inter-Somite Cleft Boundary Sorting Energy Barrier Law
equations.formula: Delta_E_cleft = L_cleft * (2 * gamma_het - (gamma_ant + gamma_post)) > 0  when 2 * gamma_het > gamma_ant + gamma_post
equations.lean_code:
def eph_cleft_sorting_energy (L_cleft gamma_het gamma_ant gamma_post : Int) : Int :=
  L_cleft * (2 * gamma_het - (gamma_ant + gamma_post))
theorem adhyapok_2021_eph_ephrin_cleft_sorting_barrier
    (L_cleft gamma_het gamma_het_kd gamma_ant gamma_post : Int)
    (h_len : 0 < L_cleft)
    (h_rep : gamma_ant + gamma_post < 2 * gamma_het)
    (h_kd : 2 * gamma_het_kd = gamma_ant + gamma_post) :
    0 < eph_cleft_sorting_energy L_cleft gamma_het gamma_ant gamma_post ∧
    eph_cleft_sorting_energy L_cleft gamma_het_kd gamma_ant gamma_post = 0
equations.math_family: Apico-Basal Differential Interfacial Tension Vertex Mechanics Driving Wedge-Cell Somite Rosette & Somitecoel Lumen Formation
equations.variables: L_cleft: inter-somitic boundary contact length (um); gamma_het: heterotypic EphA4-ephrinB2 interfacial tension; gamma_ant, gamma_post: homotypic intra-somite cell-cell tensions
equations.role: Establishes that heterotypic EphA4/ephrinB2 repulsion (2*gamma_het > gamma_ant + gamma_post) creates a positive energy barrier that drives physical somite cleft separation
equations.source_citation: Adhyapok et al. (2021) Dev. Cell 56:1312-1324 Figs. 1-3; Yamanaka et al. (2023) Nature 614:509-520 Fig. 2

equations.law_name: Yamanaka et al. (2023) & Miao et al. (2023) Y-27632 ROCK Inhibition & Minus-Matrigel Curvature Collapse Law
equations.formula: gamma_ap = gamma_bas  =>  Delta_gamma_{ap-bas} = gamma_ap - gamma_bas = 0
equations.lean_code:
def apico_basal_tension_diff (gamma_ap gamma_bas : Int) : Int :=
  gamma_ap - gamma_bas
theorem yamanaka_2023_rock_inhibition_curvature_collapse
    (N_lat gamma_ap_wt gamma_bas : Int)
    (h_wt : gamma_bas < gamma_ap_wt) :
    apico_basal_tension_diff gamma_bas gamma_bas = 0 ∧
    0 < apico_basal_tension_diff gamma_ap_wt gamma_bas ∧
    rosette_lumen_numerator N_lat gamma_ap_wt <
      rosette_lumen_numerator N_lat gamma_bas
equations.math_family: Apico-Basal Differential Interfacial Tension Vertex Mechanics Driving Wedge-Cell Somite Rosette & Somitecoel Lumen Formation
equations.variables: gamma_ap_wt: wild-type apical actomyosin tension under RhoA/ROCK activation; gamma_bas: basal ECM tension; N_lat: lateral N-cadherin adhesion term N*gamma_lat
equations.role: Proves that ROCK inhibition (Y-27632) or absence of Matrigel ECM abolishes the apico-basal tension differential and dilates the somitecoel lumen relative to wild-type MET rosettes
equations.source_citation: Yamanaka et al. (2023) Nature 614:509-520 Fig. 3; Miao et al. (2023) Nature 614:500-508 Fig. 4

equations.law_name: Yamanaka et al. (2023) 3D Polyhedral Shell Somitecoel Lumen Pressurization Law
equations.formula: rho_3D = R_in / R_out = (Lambda - 4 pi gamma_ap + 2 pi P R_in) / (Lambda + 4 pi gamma_bas);  rho_3D < 1 iff 2 pi P R_in < 4 pi (gamma_ap + gamma_bas)
equations.lean_code:
def shell_lumen_numerator (Lam four_pi_gamma_ap two_pi_P_Rin : Int) : Int :=
  Lam - four_pi_gamma_ap + two_pi_P_Rin
def shell_basal_denominator (Lam four_pi_gamma_bas : Int) : Int :=
  Lam + four_pi_gamma_bas
theorem yamanaka_2023_shell_lumen_pressurization
    (Lam four_pi_gamma_ap four_pi_gamma_bas two_pi_P_Rin : Int)
    (h_P : 0 < two_pi_P_Rin)
    (h_bas : 0 < four_pi_gamma_bas)
    (h_ap : 0 < four_pi_gamma_ap) :
    shell_lumen_numerator Lam four_pi_gamma_ap 0 <
      shell_lumen_numerator Lam four_pi_gamma_ap two_pi_P_Rin ∧
    (shell_lumen_numerator Lam four_pi_gamma_ap two_pi_P_Rin <
        shell_basal_denominator Lam four_pi_gamma_bas ↔
      two_pi_P_Rin < four_pi_gamma_ap + four_pi_gamma_bas) ∧
    shell_lumen_numerator Lam four_pi_gamma_ap 0 <
      shell_basal_denominator Lam four_pi_gamma_bas
equations.math_family: Apico-Basal Differential Interfacial Tension Vertex Mechanics Driving Wedge-Cell Somite Rosette & Somitecoel Lumen Formation
equations.variables: Lambda = gamma_lat * (total angular lateral edge length) / 2 for the N_3D-cell spherical Voronoi shell; gamma_ap, gamma_bas: apical and basal face tensions; P: somitecoel lumen pressure (gamma_lat / um); R_in: lumen radius
equations.role: Proves that lumen pressure strictly dilates the 3D somitecoel equilibrium and that the closed-shell condition is the two-surface Laplace bound P < 2 (gamma_ap + gamma_bas) / R_in; the discrete 2 N_3D-DOF polyhedral relaxation reproduces the closed form to < 1e-3
equations.source_citation: Yamanaka et al. (2023) Nature 614:509-520 Figs. 2-3 (somitecoel lumen); Gomez-Galvez et al. (2018) Nat Commun 9:2960 (polyhedral/scutoid shell geometry)

equations.law_name: Lewis (2003) / Cooke & Zeeman (1976) HES7 Clock-Wavefront Arrest & Tension Maturation Gradient Law
equations.formula: S = v * T_HES7 ;  gamma(t) = gamma_base + k * (t - t_arrest) ;  t_ant < t_post <= t  =>  gamma_ant(t) > gamma_post(t)
equations.lean_code:
def segment_length (v T : Int) : Int :=
  v * T
def cell_age (t t_arrest : Int) : Int :=
  t - t_arrest
def tension_ramp (gamma_base k age : Int) : Int :=
  gamma_base + k * age
theorem hes7_wavefront_arrest_tension_gradient
    (v T_short T_long t t_ant t_post gamma_base k : Int)
    (h_v : 0 < v)
    (h_T : T_short < T_long)
    (h_order : t_ant < t_post)
    (h_t : t_post ≤ t)
    (h_k : 0 < k) :
    segment_length v T_short < segment_length v T_long ∧
    (0 ≤ cell_age t t_post ∧ cell_age t t_post < cell_age t t_ant) ∧
    tension_ramp gamma_base k (cell_age t t_post) <
      tension_ramp gamma_base k (cell_age t t_ant)
equations.math_family: Apico-Basal Differential Interfacial Tension Vertex Mechanics Driving Wedge-Cell Somite Rosette & Somitecoel Lumen Formation
equations.variables: v: determination wavefront speed (um/h); T: HES7 clock period (h); t_arrest: wavefront passage time of a cell; k: linearised RhoA/ROCK (or EphA4/ephrinB2) tension ramp slope; gamma_base: pre-MET baseline tension
equations.role: Proves the clock-and-wavefront segment-length law S = v T and the anterior-to-posterior MET maturation gradient that the live HES7 -> MESP2/RIPPLY2 -> tension coupling feeds into the vertex rosette solver
equations.source_citation: Lewis (2003) Curr Biol 13:1398-1408; Cooke & Zeeman (1976) J Theor Biol 58:455-476; Diaz-Cuadros et al. (2020) Nature 580:113-118; Matsuda et al. (2020) Nature 580:124-129; Yamanaka et al. (2023) Nature 614:509-520 Fig. 4

equations.law_name: Parabolic Radial Compression Stress Center Peak & Margin Vanishing Law
equations.lean_code:
def radial_compression_stress (kappa R r : Int) : Int :=
  kappa * (R * R - r * r)
def radial_stress_nat (kappa r_sq_diff : Nat) : Nat :=
  kappa * r_sq_diff
theorem parabolic_radial_stress_center_peak_and_edge_zero (kappa R : Int) (k0 r0 gap : Nat) :
    radial_compression_stress kappa R R = 0 ∧
    radial_compression_stress kappa R 0 = kappa * (R * R) ∧
    radial_stress_nat (k0 + 1) ((r0 + 1) + (gap + 1)) >
      radial_stress_nat (k0 + 1) (gap + 1)
equations.math_family: Hertzian Rod-on-Substrate Radial Compression Stress & Critical Verticalization Instability (P(r) = (1/2) ζ g (R^2 - r^2) ≥ P_c(L_cell))

equations.law_name: Critical Verticalization Radius Onset & RbmA Friction-Loss Control Law

def verticalization_front_sq (R_sq R_c_sq : Nat) : Nat :=

equations.lean_code:
def junction_tension_vertical (Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda : Int) : Int :=
  Lambda_0 + Delta_Lambda
def junction_tension_horizontal (Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda : Int) : Int :=
  Lambda_0 - Delta_Lambda
def t1_quartet_energy_change (Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda l_0 : Int) : Int :=
  (junction_tension_horizontal Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda -
   junction_tension_vertical Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda) * l_0
theorem zajac_bertet_polarized_t1_energy_drop
    (Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda l_0 : Int)
    (hAniso : Delta_Lambda > 0) (hLen : l_0 > 0) :
    junction_tension_vertical Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda >
      junction_tension_horizontal Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda ∧
    t1_quartet_energy_change Lambda_0 Delta_Lambda l_0 < 0 ∧
    t1_quartet_energy_change Lambda_0 0 l_0 = 0

equations.variables: theta: junction angle relative to mediolateral (ML, x) axis; J_0, Delta_J: isotropic and anisotropic adhesion coefficients; Lambda_0, Delta_Lambda: isotropic and Myosin II planar-polarized line tensions; l_0: junction length resolved across a 4-way T1 vertex
equations.role: Proves that planar-polarized mediolateral adhesion / Myosin II enrichment (Delta_Lambda > 0) elevates vertical AP-facing junction tension above horizontal ML junction tension and drives a strictly negative interfacial energy drop across vertical-to-horizontal T1 neighbor exchanges
